title: renv::remove() uninstalls R packages from global .libPath()
description:
I was trying to remove a package from my `renv.lock` file using `renv::remove()`. Note that I do not use renv for anything other than recording packages so that the project can be used elsehwere. I never `renv::activate()`. 

After running `renv::remove()` the package wasn't removed from the renv.lock file but it was uninstalled globally. 

If the `library = NULL` arugment (default) is used and the global user path is being used and in an interactive session it might make sense to prompt the user if thats the behavior they want

title: renv_description_read(package=) silently reads the working-directory DESCRIPTION when the package isn't found
description:
### Summary

`renv_description_read(package = X)` does not fail when package `X` cannot be found on the library paths. Instead it silently falls back to reading the DESCRIPTION in the **current working directory** (typically the active project's own DESCRIPTION).

### Mechanism

In `renv_description_read()` (`R/description.R`):

```r
# if given a package name, construct path to that package
path <- path %||% renv_package_find_impl(package, compat = TRUE)

# normalize non-absolute paths
if (!renv_path_absolute(path))
  path <- renv_path_normalize(path)

# if 'path' refers to a directory, try to resolve the DESCRIPTION file
if (dir.exists(path)) {
  components <- c(path, if (nzchar(subdir %||% "")) subdir, "DESCRIPTION")
  path <- paste(components, collapse = "/")
}
```

When the package is not installed, `renv_package_find_impl()` returns `""`. The empty string is not absolute, so `renv_path_normalize("")` resolves it to the working directory; `dir.exists()` is then `TRUE`, and the code reads `<cwd>/DESCRIPTION`. Callers reasonably expect either the requested package's DESCRIPTION or an error, not the project's DESCRIPTION.

### Impact

This was the root cause behind the CI failures investigated in #2324. The dependency-graph "supplement" step in `renv_graph_resolve()` called `renv_description_read(package = pkg)` to recover non-standard fields; for a not-yet-installed package it received the *project's* DESCRIPTION and leaked its `Imports` into the resolved record, manufacturing a dependency cycle that silently failed the install.

That specific call site was fixed in #2324 (only reads genuinely-installed packages, via `renv_package_find()`), but the underlying `renv_description_read()` fallback remains a footgun for any other caller that passes `package =` for a package that may not be installed.

### Suggested fix

When `package` is supplied and `renv_package_find_impl()` returns `""` (not found), error out (or return an error/`NULL` consistently) rather than falling back to the working directory. The `path`-supplied case can retain existing behavior.

title: renv shared cache on workbench - installing wrong package
description: We've got a workbench server with a shared renv cache, and have had repeated reports of users seeing renv installing the wrong package when instructed to install styler (R 4.4.0)... (we've seen it point at different wrong packages at different times, but the issue always seems to happen when trying to install styler... I can't work out why that might be) To fix it we tried renv::purge("styler"), but it didn't help, however, manually removing the styler package from the cache directory does seems to work. Unfortunately, after a few days/weeks/months the issue reappears. Our guess is maybe some cache write concurrency issues might be occurring and we're wondering whether moving to a user level caching approach may be the best solution... Not sure this counts fully as a code issue for renv, but wondered if it's something you've encountered before and if you have any guidance? Happy to share more details if required

title: `renv::dependencies` does not search dependencies in imported box modules or sourced scripts
description:
This issue is related to [my post on the Posit forum](https://forum.posit.co/t/how-can-i-automatically-detect-all-dependencies-of-a-qmd-file/213143).

I made a [minimal reproducible example](https://github.com/ekatko1/reprex-renv-recursive-dependencies) with a test.

To summarise, I would like a way to extract dependencies recursively from .qmd files since not all dependencies present in the repository are needed to render a quarto document. When rendering the document using GitHub Actions workflow, installing all unneeded dependencies using would waste time and CPU cycles (caching can mitigate this over some time, but nevertheless adds bloat).

title: Dependencies are taken from most recent version and not from lock-file.
description:
I have in my `renv.lock` an older version of `selectr` specified (0.5-1), which had a dependency on `stringr`, whereas the newest version 0.6-0 (eg the version on CRAN) has no dependency on `stringr`.

When I run `renv::restore` using the lock file, it fails to detect the dependency on `stringr`, therefore the installation fails (no package called `stringr`, as it happens that `stringr` happened to be scheduled to be installed after `selectr`).

I would expect that the dependencies are taken from the locked-version and not the most current ones.

This happens on `renv` 1.2.3.

title: regression in 1.2.0: installing from cellar ignores dependencies
description: I have R packages in my `renv` cellar. I've used this feature successfully for several years now. Starting with `renv` 1.2.0 (and still present in 1.2.3) when using `renv::install` or `renv::use` to install a package from the cellar, none of the dependencies are installed, which obviously causes problems.

title: Detect ragg from yaml header/chunk options?
description:
If you have a quarto document with:

```yaml
knitr:
    opts_chunk: 
      dev: "ragg_png"
```

in the header, knitr will use ragg for rendering the graphics. This works without having to place`library(ragg)` in the document.
Deploying on Connect doesn't work without adding `library(ragg)`, as `ragg` doesn't get discovered and not listed among the required dependencies.
I don't know if it's possible/a good idea to discover this from the yaml header and/or individual code chunk options

title: Question: what is the right way to handle libraries like dbplyr that are never called directly
description:
I'm looking for some advice on how to handle libraries that are required by my project but are never called directly. I think the dbplyr library is a good example:

https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/#usage

> Note that you don’t actually need to load dbplyr with [library(dbplyr)](https://dbplyr.tidyverse.org/); dplyr automatically loads it for you when it sees you working with a database. Database connections are coordinated by the DBI package. Learn more at https://dbi.r-dbi.org/

**app.R**

```R
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), ":memory:")
copy_to(con, mtcars)

mtcars2 <- tbl(con, "mtcars")
mtcars2
```

Set up renv:

```R
renv::init()
renv::snapshot()
renv::restore()
```

How do I ensure that RM will always install `dbplyr`? For my specific use case, I'm trying to deploy an application to Posit Connect. So I need to make sure that Posit Connect picks up `dbplyr` and installs it.

title: RStudio error opening R projects using renv when updating to R 4.6.0
description:
Hi,

This is my first time doing a bug report on github, so many apologies if this is wrong, or in the wrong place! Happy to be corrected or redirected.

I think this is an error in the interaction between RStudio and renv so again apologies if this is the wrong place for it - I wasn't sure which side was best placed to look into it!

When updating to R 4.6.0, I and several of my colleagues became unable to open R projects that use renv in RStudio. RStudio threw an error on starting R, saying variously that "the R session failed to start", or that "RStudio can't establish a connection to R. This usually indicates one of the following: 1) The R session is taking an unusually long time to start, perhaps because of slow operations in startup scripts or slow network drive access. 2) RStudio is unable to communicate with R over a local network port, possibly because of firewall restrictions or anti-virus software". Mine actually failed to render the error message, so I can't tell you exactly what the error message was for my exact setup.

As part of troubleshooting I reinstalled RStudio. I found I could successfully open an R project in RStudio if I first deleted the .Rprofile file. The only line in .Rprofile was source("renv/activate.R"). This ran fine once I had the project open, including installing renv, but did take a little time. Once I had run this line in a given project, I was able to restore the .Rprofile file and open and close the project without error.

My conclusion from this was that as a result of updating to R 4.6.0 and/or reinstalling RStudio, I needed to re-install renv for each project. This was being done by source("renv/activate.R") in .Rprofile when starting R, but took too long and timed out so RStudio threw an error.

The workaround of deleting .Rprofile, opening the project, running source("renv/activate.R"), and then restoring .Rprofile worked for all of my projects, but is obviously not ideal since other users won't know to do this, and I still needed to do it when cloning a new repo.

To reproduce:
 - install RStudio and R 4.6.0 (and check that RStudio is using the R 4.6.0)
 - try to open an R project that contains source("renv/activate.R") in .Rprofile (and the renv/activate.R script)
      - this could be an existing R project, or new R project made by cloning a version control repo, I had the same issue with both

Thank you! And again, happy to be redirected if this is something that the RStudio team should deal with.

title: `record()` writes fewer fields than `snapshot()` for the same installed package
description:
`renv::record("<pkg>")` doesn't write all of the new fields that were added in #2059 like `renv::snapshot()` does — only `Package`, `Version`, `Source`, `Repository`. Fields like `Hash`, `Requirements`, and the dependency lists (`Depends`, `Imports`, `Suggests`, `LinkingTo`) are dropped. 

Originally surfaced in rstudio/rsconnect#1319.                                
   
### Repro

Adding this test to `tests/testthat/test-record.R` reproduces it:             
 
```r                                                                          
test_that("record() writes the same fields as snapshot() for an installed
package", {                                                                   
 
  renv_tests_scope("breakfast")                                               
  init()                                                                      
 
  lockfile <- renv_lockfile_read("renv.lock")                                 
  snap_record <- renv_lockfile_records(lockfile)$breakfast                    
                                                                              
  record("breakfast")                                                         
                                                                              
  lockfile <- renv_lockfile_read("renv.lock")
  rec_record <- renv_lockfile_records(lockfile)$breakfast
                                                                              
  expect_setequal(names(rec_record), names(snap_record))
                                                                              
})              
```

Returns:   
```                                                                           
FAILURE: 'test-record.R:80:3' ---------------------
Expected `names(rec_record)` to have the same values as `names(snap_record)`.
Actual:   "Package", "Version", "Source", "Repository"
Expected: "Package", "Version", "Source", "Type", "Depends", "Suggests",      
          "Repository", "License", "Description", ...
Absent:   "Type", "Depends", "Suggests", "License", "Description", "Title",   
          "Author", "Maintainer", "Config/Needs/protein"
```                                                                           

It looks (to Claude) like `record()` and `snapshot()` build records via completely different code paths and never converge:

* `snapshot()` → `renv_snapshot_description()` (`R/snapshot.R:715`) reads the installed package's DESCRIPTION and (for v2, `R/snapshot.R:815`) keeps   essentially every field except a small `ignore` list. For v1 it also computes   `Hash` and a `Requirements` list.
* `record()` → `renv_remotes_resolve(spec, latest = TRUE)` (`R/record.R:36`).    For a CRAN/repository spec that lands in `renv_remotes_resolve_repository()`  (`R/remotes.R:463`), which returns only: `list(Package, Version, Source = "Repository", Repository)` `renv_lockfile_modify()` (`R/lockfile.R:241`) then slots that minimal list straight into the lockfile with no enrichment from the installed DESCRIPTION.

title: `renv::vulns()` reporting all packages instead of only packages with known vulnerabilities
description:
Recently, `renv::vulns()` started returning all queried packages, even those with no reported vulnerabilities on Posit Package Manager.

According to PPM, [curl 7.1.0](https://packagemanager.posit.co/client/#/repos/cran/packages/curl/overview) has no known vulnerabilities, but the package information is returned when calling `renv::vulns()`, contradicting the documentation.

To reproduce:

```r
dput(renv::vulns(c("curl==7.1.0"), repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest"))
```

Output:

```r
list(list(name = "curl", version = "7.1.0", type = "R", source_id = 1L, 
    repo_id = 2L, licenses = list("MIT + file LICENSE"), license_types = list(
        "MIT"), blocked = FALSE))
```

title: graph: memoize per-version crandb DESCRIPTION lookups
description:
## Context

After #2279, `renv_graph_description_crandb` (`R/graph.R:298`) is the primary fallback for resolving `Depends`/`Imports`/`LinkingTo` of any lockfile-pinned version that is not present in the configured repositories — most notably when restoring against `packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest`, which only indexes the newest version of each package.

Each call hits `https://crandb.r-pkg.org/<package>/<version>` synchronously, with no caching. For a large lockfile this can mean dozens of sequential HTTP requests on the hot path of `renv::restore()`.

## Proposal

Reuse the already-memoized `/all` endpoint helper at `renv_available_packages_crandb_query` (`R/available-packages.R:642`), which fetches the full version history for a package once and caches it under scope `crandb-history`. The graph helper can:

1. Call `renv_available_packages_crandb_query(package)` to get the cached version map.
2. Filter to the requested version in-process and convert via `renv_graph_description_crandb_convert`.
3. Fall back to the per-version endpoint only if the `/all` response doesn't contain the requested version (shouldn't happen for valid pinned versions, but worth keeping as a safety net).

Net effect: one request per package instead of one per `(package, version)` pair, with caching shared across the resolver.

## Notes

- The existing per-version endpoint helper should probably stay around for the edge case above; the change is to *try the memoized path first*.
- No behavior change expected — same DESCRIPTION fields returned, just sourced from a different endpoint with caching.

title: snapshot() not respecting DESCRIPTION's Remotes packages
description:
I have a project set up with snapshot.type = "explicit" and snapshot.dev = TRUE. In my DESCRIPTION file I have a GitHub package that needs to be installed, so it's under the `Remotes:` field.

I can install it in my library with `renv::install("user/repo")`. But when I do `renv::snapshot()`, it doesn't get added to the lockfile.
If I move the package to Depends/Imports/Suggests, and then do a snapshot, then it does get added (it's incorrect to do so, but I was just testing).

Is renv not meant to work for this case?

title: Allow/forcing project package to be included in renv.lock
description:
I'm developing a shiny app contained within a package, and want to deploy the shiny app to shinyapps.io via {rsconnect}. In order for the deployment to be successful, all the dependencies of the package and the package itself need to be listed in the renv.lock file, so it can be installed.

Currently, `renv::snapshot()` automatically prunes the "root" package from the lockfile, and I've tried many hacky ways to overcome it. Even if I add a `R/deps.R` that loads the package, {renv} is smart enough to ignore it. If I manually add it with `renv::record("user/repo")`, when I then call `renv::snapshot()` the package gets removed from the lockfile.

This is a problem because the package itself does need to be in renv so that the remote server (shinyapps.io) will know to install this package.

I could not find any flag, parameter, or workaround. Is it possible to do this, or would you consider adding such a mechanism?

title: When pak is enabled restore fails to remove unused dependencies
description:
My renv.lock only lists renv as a dependency:

```
  "Packages": {
    "renv": {
...
```

My renv library contains tidyverse, drc and all their dependencies (a lot).

In my project neither tidyverse nor drc are used anymore at this point.

```
r$> renv::status()
No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

This seems already wrong to me, there are tons of installed dependencies that are unrequired:

```
r$> renv::dependencies()
Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
                                   Source Package Require Version   Dev
1 /Users/carlos/Desktop/Scratch/renv.lock    renv                 FALSE
```

Now I add to some file:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(drc)
```

so that:

```
r$> renv::status()

The following package(s) are in an inconsistent state:

 package        installed recorded used
 abind          y         n        y   
 askpass        y         n        y   
 backports      y         n        y   
 base64enc      y         n        y   
 bit            y         n        y   
 bit64          y         n        y   
...
```

At this point `renv::restore(clean = TRUE)` does nothing at all.

Perhaps I'm misunderstanding how all this should work but AFAIU:

- Before adding the `library(...)` lines `status` should have said that there were installed and unused dependencies and `restore(clean = TRUE)` should have removed them.

- After adding the `library(...)` lines the output of `status` is fine but `restore(clean = TRUE)` still does nothing.

Both behaviors seem wrong to me, according to the lock file all the installed dependencies has to be removed. More so in the first scenario where even the inferred dependencies were nil.

The documentation of `restore` clearly states:

> If clean = TRUE, restore() will additionally delete any packages in the project library that don't appear in the lockfile.

title: `renv` (v1.2.2) computes dependency graph from repository-provided requirements rather than individual package requirements
description:
Pointing to https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest as the repo and then trying to restore `ggplot2` v3.5.2 alongside `ggiraph` v0.9.0 and `ggstats` v0.10.0 forces a repair to `ggplot2` v4.0.3 seemingly because the more recent versions of `ggiraph` and `ggstats` require `ggplot2 (>= 4.0.0)`.

If I point to https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2025-09-11 instead (the day before the publication of `ggplot2 v4.0.0`, and thus before `ggiraph` and `ggstats` updated their requirements) seems to do the trick modulo some package downgrades.

I can send a minimal reproducible example if necessary.

title: renv::install() fails: GitHub remotes in DESCRIPTION not fully resolved
description:
I'm trying to install the latest packages in a package-project I'm working in, created with older renvs.

{renv} 1.1.8 was working fine, {renv} 1.2.1 and the latest dev version do not.
The project uses a private package hosted on GitHub, say {privatepackage}.
{privatepackage} is specified as an Import, with a Remotes entry in the DESCRIPTION.

The bare `renv::install()` fails with the following error:

> Error in `record$Package`:
> ! object of type 'closure' is not subsettable
>     ▆
>  1. └─renv::install()
>  2.   └─renv:::renv_graph_init(packages, records = records, project = project) at renv/R/install.R:240:3
>  3.     └─renv:::renv_graph_resolve(remote, envir, records = records, fields = fields) at renv/R/graph.R:32:5

The error happens at these lines:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/f3ed0f26d2ad6df90288596414c86d007dc6e84f/R/graph.R#L102-L104

Debugging, after L104 `record` is still a function.
To get the actual resolved record I should call `record()()`.
Weirdly there are no recursive dependencies in the lockfile.

The package alone installs fine with `renv::install("privateorg/privatepackage")`.
Plain new project, I just copied the older renv.lock.

# Reprex

Create a package ex-nihilo with a single GitHub dependency:
``` r
dir <- tempfile("renv-test")
dir.create(dir)

desc <- 'Package: renv-reprex
Title: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case)
Version: 0.0.0.9000

    person("First", "Last", , "first.last@example.com", role = c("aut", "cre"))
Description: What the package does (one paragraph).
License: `use_mit_license()`, `use_gpl3_license()` or friends to pick a
    license
Imports:
    skeleton
Remotes:
    skeleton=kevinushey/skeleton
Encoding: UTF-8
Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE)
RoxygenNote: 7.0.0'

writeLines(desc, file.path(dir, "DESCRIPTION"))

renv::init(project = dir, bare = TRUE)
#> - Using 'explicit' snapshot type. Please see `?renv::snapshot` for more details.
#> 
#> - The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.
renv::install(project = dir)
#> Error in `record$Package`:
#> ! object of type 'closure' is not subsettable

title: Feature request: `purge()` many packages and their symlinks
description:
The global cache is great, but I often find myself wanting to start from scratch for one reason or another, particularly confirming reproducibility. `purge()` is limited in three main ways for this

* `purge()` only accepts one package at a time. I can get around this with `lapply()` + `dependencies()`
* Usually, when I want this approach, it is precisely this workflow: purge all packages in the cache that this project uses. Again, I can combine it with `dependencies()` to meet that need, but ideally this would be streamlined with a new argument like `purge_project`
* `purge()` does not remove symlinks. I think that could make sense as a default but I would like it if we could optionally remove the symlinks in the project, too. This would practically be limited to the project's symlinks and would still result in broken symlinks from any other project that used those packages from the cache.

Ideally, I would also be able to completely purge the entire cache (regardless of package and R version, project, etc) with something like `purge_all`.

Currently you can do this by just deleting the folder

```r
# Retrieve the root cache path
cache_path <- renv::paths$root()

# Delete the entire cache directory recursively
unlink(cache_path, recursive = TRUE)   
```

but again, it would be nice to streamline this for reproducibility checks or other issues.

title: renv::install() crashes on packages not in any configured repo
description:
## Description

`renv::install()` crashes with a `vapply` error when any dependency in the project cannot be found in the configured repositories.

## Minimal reproducible example

```r
dir <- tempfile("renv-test")
dir.create(dir)
writeLines("library(thispackagedoesnotexist)", file.path(dir, "script.R"))
renv::init(project = dir, bare = TRUE)
renv::install(project = dir)
#> Error in vapply(x, f, ..., FUN.VALUE = character(1)) : 
#>   values must be length 1,
#>   but FUN(X[[2]]) result is length 0
```

## Traceback

```
5: renv::install(project = dir)
4: renv_install_report(descriptions[needed], library = library)
3: renv_pretty_print_records("The following package(s) will be installed:",
       records, ...)
2: map_chr(records, renv_record_format_short)
1: vapply(x, f, ..., FUN.VALUE = character(1))
```

## Cause

`renv_record_format_short()` returns a zero-length character when a package record has missing fields (e.g. no `Version`). This happens when a package is detected as a dependency but cannot be resolved in any configured repository.

The function should handle missing/NULL fields gracefully — e.g. by returning a placeholder like `"pkgname [unknown version]"` — rather than producing a zero-length result that breaks `vapply`.

## Workaround

```r
assignInNamespace("renv_record_format_short", function(record) {
  tryCatch(
    paste(record$Package %||% "???", record$Version %||% "???"),
    error = function(e) "???"
  )
}, ns = "renv")
```

## Environment

- renv 1.2.0
- R 4.5.3
- macOS 26.3.1 (aarch64)

## Previous reports

Same crash pattern, reported and fixed before but keeps regressing:

- #138 (renv 0.6.0)
- #193 (renv 0.7.0)
- #966 (renv 0.15.4)

title: restore / update /install failures with Gitlab URL
description:
Hello! Im excited to take advantage of the new version of renv and parallel downloads. We have internal packages stored in gitlab and noticed an error when restoring:

```
Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y
Error in is.null(field) || is.na(field) : 
  'length = 39' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
Traceback (most recent calls last):
6: renv::restore(
     prompt = prompt,
     clean = clean,
     exclude = exclude,
     repos = repos
   ) 
5: records <- renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile, rebuild, strict) at restore.R#208
4: descriptions <- renv_graph_init(packages, records = lockrecords, project = project) at restore.R#237
3: deps <- renv_graph_resolve(remote, envir, records = records, fields = fields) at graph.R#32
2: deps <- renv_graph_deps(desc, fields = fields) at graph.R#167
1: value <- renv_description_parse_field(desc[[field]]) at graph.R#414
```

I dont have a reprex, im not sure how i'd do that for gitlab easily but After debugging i think the root cause: When a GitLab package has `RemoteSubdir: ""`  in the lockfile, the DESCRIPTION file URL is constructed incorrectly in two places:                                
                                                                                                
  - R/graph.R line 352 (used during restore())                                                  
  - R/remotes.R line 883 (used during install()/update())                                       
  
``` 
  parts <- c(subdir, "DESCRIPTION")                                                             
  descpath <- URLencode(paste(parts, collapse = "/"), reserved = TRUE)                          
```
                  
  When subdir is "", this produces "/DESCRIPTION" which URL-encodes to `%2FDESCRIPTION`, resulting in an invalid URL like:
  `.../repository/files/%2FDESCRIPTION/raw?ref=HEAD`                                          
                                                  
The download silently fails, then a secondary crash occurs in renv_description_parse_field()  (line 95) because the lockfile's list-valued Imports field gets merged into the empty description, and `is.null(field) || is.na(field)` can't handle a list of length > 1.            
                                                                                                
Possible fix: Filter empty subdir before building the path (consistent with how R/description.R line 17 already handles it):
                                                                                                
before (broken)
```
  parts <- c(subdir, "DESCRIPTION")                                                             
```   
after (fixed)
```                                                                               
  parts <- c(if (nzchar(subdir %||% "")) subdir, "DESCRIPTION")
```                                                                                                
  This or a similar change could be applied in both `renv_graph_description_gitlab()` in graph.R and                  
  `renv_remotes_resolve_gitlab()` in remotes.R.                                                   
                                              
I temporarily deleted the `Subdir` field below in the lockfile and everything went smooth with restore/update/snapshot.  Maybe this is already fixed?

```
{
      "VignetteBuilder": "knitr",
      "Config/testthat/edition": "3",
      "Config/testthat/parallel": "true",
      "Author": "Me",
      "Maintainer": "Me",
      "RemoteType": "gitlab",
      "RemoteHost": "gitlab.host.com",
      "RemoteUsername": "blah",
      "RemoteRepo": "blah",
      "RemoteRef": "main",
      "RemoteSubdir": <THIS EMPTY "" LINE DELETED>
      "RemoteSha": "d01d28dfe66116e36fa107df26ddea6d9cea0b28"
    },
```

title: renv_ppm_transform generates invalid opensuse157 identifier for SLES 15 SP7
description:
## Problem

On SLES 15 SP7, `renv_ppm_transform()` constructs a PPM repository URL using the distribution identifier `opensuse157`. However, Posit Package Manager does not recognize this identifier — the highest supported is `opensuse156` (which covers both SP6 and SP7).

This causes all package downloads to fail with curl error code 22 (HTTP 404):

```
renv was unable to query available packages from the following repositories:
- # https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/opensuse157/latest/src/contrib --------
error downloading '…/PACKAGES.rds' [error code 22]
error downloading '…/PACKAGES.gz' [error code 22]
error downloading '…/PACKAGES' [error code 22]
```

## Root Cause

renv reads `/etc/os-release`, detects SLES 15.7, and naively maps the version to the PPM identifier `opensuse157`. But PPM bundles SP7 under the `opensuse156` identifier since the binaries are compatible.

The PPM `/status` endpoint (`https://packagemanager.posit.co/__api__/status`) lists valid distribution identifiers, and `opensuse157` is not among them.

## Suggested Fix

A few options (not mutually exclusive):

1. **Query the PPM status endpoint** to validate the constructed identifier against PPM's actual supported distributions, and fall back to the closest supported version.
2. **Maintain a mapping** of OS versions to PPM identifiers that accounts for cases where PPM bundles multiple SPs under one identifier.
3. **Fall back gracefully** — if the constructed binary URL returns 404, retry with source packages or the next-lower identifier.

## Workaround

Users can manually set the repository URL:
```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/opensuse156/latest"))
```

## Related

A corresponding issue has been filed against Posit Package Manager to add `opensuse157` as a valid route.

...

title: Local Libraries Missing in Upgrade from 1.1.4 to 1.1.7

Executing our tests afterwards, we found that all our libraries that had been installed from local libraries, were no longer installed. Is this a bug or a feature? All that was present was the header showing that the new version of R had been detected as 4.5.2 (required to update MASS) and then the details of the renv and MASS packages. So it looks like most of the libraries disappeared in the upgrade. Output of snapshot is Running update yielded I'm guessing this only updates what's in the lock file, so if there are lots of libraries missing from the lock file, then update won't re-populate them. title: Suggest renv::hydrate() when packages are used but not installed
description:
I just migrated to a new laptop and I'm setting up everything from scratch for the first time in a very long time. For repos where I was working alone and did a poor job snapshotting my library state I'm getting a lot of:
```
The following packages are used in this project, but not installed:

	ggplot2, htmlwidgets, [...]

Use `renv::restore()` to restore the packages recorded in the lockfile.
Use `renv::status()` afterwards to re-assess the project state.
```

Looking for a solution I came across renv::hydrate() which was mentioned in [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/647#issuecomment-780136241) as the solution to my state. Wouldn't it make sense to suggest this workflow when the user is in this state?

title: ```renv::restore()``` ```the$platform$VERSION_ID``` is a non-character object
description:
**Problem Description**
I've been trying to set up RStan in a Docker image using renv. However, renv::restore() fails when building the image with this error message: ```Error in startsWith(the$platform$VERSION_ID, version) non-character object(s)```

**What I've Tried**
- The build succeeds when I exclude RStan from the .R and renv.lock files.
- The build succeeds with RStan included in the .R and renv.lock files if I either modify the$platform$VERSION_ID -- which is NULL -- when running the container interactively or if I modify /etc/os-release via the Dockerfile.

**How to Reproduce**
I've put together a [minimal example](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24216883/renv_issue.zip) to reproduce this error. (Note in the Docker file that I've been encountering another, though I think unrelated issue which requires me to manually install some RStan dependencies before calling renv::restore().)

title: renv::lockfile not exported from namespace renv
description:
I was attempting to follow [this example](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/lockfile-api.html), but `lockfile()` doesn't appear to be exported from `renv`. I checked `NAMESPACE` in the current `main` branch and it only exports functions like `lockfile_create()`, `lockfile_modify()`, etc. 

Unless I'm missing something, I believe either `lockfile()` is missing from `NAMESPACE` or that the documentation example is incorrect or outdated. I confirmed I am using `renv` version 1.1.5, which is the same version that appears in the header of the documentation example above.

title: Feature Request: Clarify `.renvignore` Messaging when `.renvignore` is used.
description:
When running `renv::snapshot()`, I see the note:

```
NOTE: Dependency discovery took 31 seconds during snapshot.
Consider using .renvignore to ignore files, or switching to explicit snapshots.
See ?renv::dependencies for more information.
```

However, I already have a .`renvignore` file in place. The message makes it look like `renv` isn’t aware of it, even though it is being used. This can be confusing — it suggests I haven’t configured `.renvignore` when in fact I have so the messaging does not reassure the user that the file is being used the only thing they can go off of is the discovery time, which is less than ideal. 

If a `.renvignore` file is detected then perhaps the note could read:

```
NOTE: Dependency discovery took 22 seconds during snapshot using current .renvignore specifications.
Consider modifying .renvignore or switching to explicit snapshots.
See ?renv::dependencies for more information.
```

title: `renv::snapshot()` records repository URL despite `repos = c()` argument
description:
Hi,

our team is using a private package repository where authentification works with a token that is passed within the repository URL.
Hence it is undesirable in our case that `renv::snapshot()` records repository URLs since those contain private tokens, and the renv.lock file is supposed to be shared.

We used the workaround to pass `renv::snapshot(repos = c())` which avoided recording of URLs. But with recent versions of renv or R (I don't know exactly which one) the behavior changed, and URLs are now recorded regardless.
Every package in renv.lock contains a "Repository:" entry with the URL.

Is there any way to create renv.lock files that do not contain URLs?

Thanks!

title: Not able to query repos using the new setup instruction from Posit Package Manager
description: I have a new laptop and recently had WSL set up with Ubuntu 24.04. I've been using Posit Package Manager in other environments with `renv` before and had not had issues. [renv 1.1.5] > renv::install("remotes") renv was unable to query available packages from the following repositories: - # https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/__linux__/noble/4.5/src/contrib -------- error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/__linux__/noble/4.5/src/contrib/PACKAGES.rds' [error code 22] error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/__linux__/noble/4.5/src/contrib/PACKAGES.gz' [error code 22] error downloading 'https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/__linux__/noble/4.5/src/contrib/PACKAGES' [error code 22] Error: package 'remotes' is not available Traceback (most recent calls last): 12: renv::install("remotes") 11: renv_retrieve_impl(packages) 10: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl_one(package)) 9: renv_retrieve_impl_one(package) 8: withCallingHandlers(renv_available_packages_latest(package), error = function(err) stopf("package '%s' is not available", package)) 7: renv_available_packages_latest(package) 6: stopf("package '%s' is not available", package) 5: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.) 4: .handleSimpleError(function (err) { ... }, "package 'remotes' is not available", base::quote(NULL)) 3: h(simpleError(msg, call)) 2: stopf("package '%s' is not available", package) 1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.) ``` But I can install packages using `install.packages()` when `renv` is not activated. title: `renv::sysreqs()` fails with if a package is not found on crandb
description:
Using this lockfile, `renv::sysreqs()` errors with `Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : subscript out of bounds`. The error comes from this line 


https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/fea901478b1fd6f8fcb845bbff2f013743d65655/R/sysreqs.R#L124


The reason is that getting system requirement for the package tagger seems to fail so the entry in `records` is not a list, but a character vector with the text of the error. `"error downloading 'https://crandb.r-pkg.org/tagger' [error code 22]"`

My guess is that errors should be filtered out or the `renv_sysreqs_crandb_impl_one` function should check for errors and return a list with the error or something like that here: 

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/fea901478b1fd6f8fcb845bbff2f013743d65655/R/sysreqs.R#L188-L193

title: More flexible Python discovery for renv::use_python
description:
Recently I have been investigating best practices for deploying reticulated content to Posit Connect. One of the things I have been trying to decide on is the best way to create virtual environments that are used by Reticulate and Renv.

Reticulate has the `reticulate::virtualenv_create` function:

```R
reticulate::virtualenv_create(envname = "./.venv", python = "3.11")
```

What I like about `reticulate::virtualenv_create` Is that it will do a good job finding a Python interpreter in your system that matches your request. In my example above, any Python interpreter using 3.11.

Renv has a similar function `renv::use_python`. When I pass only the major and minor version of Python, it fails to find an interpreter.

```R
> system2("ls", "-la /opt/python")
total 0
drwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 51 Oct 17 17:18 .
drwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 20 Oct 17 17:18 ..
drwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 41 Oct 17 17:15 3.11.13
drwxr-xr-x. 1 root root 41 Oct 17 17:15 3.12.11
lrwxrwxrwx. 1 root root 19 Oct 17 17:16 default -> /opt/python/3.12.11
drwxr-xr-x. 7 root root 98 Oct 17 17:19 jupyter

> renv::use_python(python = "3.11", name = "./.venv")
Error: '3.11' does not refer to a valid python interpreter
```

If I pass the absolute path to the Python interpreter, it works as desired.

```R
> renv::use_python(python = "/opt/python/3.11.13/bin/python", name = "./.venv")
- Creating virtual environment '.venv' ... Done!
- Updating Python packages ... Done!
- Lockfile written to "~/tmp/ret-test/renv.lock".
- Activated Python 3.11.13 [virtualenv; .venv]
```

Would it be possible to change the `renv::use_python` function so that with only passing the major or minor Python version, it can discover the interpreter to create the virtual environment with?

cc @t-kalinowski

title: `lockfile_validate()` does not check whether {jsonvalidate} is installed
description:
```r renv::lockfile_validate() ``` results in 
Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘jsonvalidate’
when jsonvalidate is not installed. A slightly more graceful exit would be appreciated, it does not have to be as sophisticated as `rlang::check_installed()`.

title: embed and deps when global cache not found
description:
In the docs, I see "inspects the dependencies" and think that it will identify packages that are needed for that script. However, it seems to not do much in this case.

`~/tmp/quux.R`

```r
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(collapse)

data.table(a = pi) |>
  mutate(b = a * 2)
```

```r
renv::embed("~/tmp/quux.R")
# [1] TRUE
```

This results in the following being prepended to the file.

```r
renv::use(
  renv = "renv@1.1.4"
)
```

Given that `renv` otherwise can determine deps fairly easily with

```r
renv::dependencies("~/tmp/quux.R")
# Finding R package dependencies ... Done!

# 1 /Users/r2/tmp/quux.R   collapse                 FALSE

# 3 /Users/r2/tmp/quux.R      dplyr                 FALSE
# 4 /Users/r2/tmp/quux.R       renv                 FALSE
```

I expected something like either of the following:

```r
renv::use(
  renv = "renv@1.1.4",
  data.table = "data.table@1.17.8",
  dplyr = "dplyr@1.1.4",
  collapse = "collapse@2.1.2"
)

renv::use(
  renv = "renv@1.1.4",
  data.table = "data.table",
  dplyr = "dplyr",
  collapse = "collapse"
)
```

Granted, it's not difficult for me to manually edit that portion of the file, but it seems like the utility/purpose of `embed()` is not working for me here. What am I missing and/or doing wrong?

title: hydrate() repeatedly attempts to install already-installed packages on macOS with Apple Silicon
description:
Problem
renv::hydrate() continuously reports packages as "not available locally" and attempts to reinstall them, even though:

The packages are successfully installed and loadable
renv::status() reports "No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state"
renv::restore() reports "The library is already synchronized with the lockfile"
The packages exist in the project library and work normally

Environment

renv version: 1.1.5
R version: 4.5.1 (2025-06-13)
Platform: aarch64-apple-darwin20 (Apple Silicon)
OS: macOS Sonoma 14.5

Reproducible Example
```
# Despite packages being installed and working:
library(Hmisc)    # Loads successfully
library(ggpmisc)  # Loads successfully

# And renv showing everything is fine:
renv::status()    # Returns: "No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state"
renv::restore()   # Returns: "The library is already synchronized with the lockfile"

# hydrate() still thinks they're missing:
renv::hydrate()
# Output:
# The following packages are used in this project, but not available locally:
# - Hmisc
# - ggpmisc
# renv will attempt to download and install these packages.
# [Installs packages that are already installed]

# This happens repeatedly, no matter how many times you run it
renv::hydrate()  # Same "missing" message
renv::hydrate()  # Same "missing" message
```

Investigation Details

Packages ARE present in project library:

```
file.exists("~/R_Projects/.../renv/library/macos/R-4.5/aarch64-apple-darwin20/Hmisc")
# [1] TRUE
file.exists("~/R_Projects/.../renv/library/macos/R-4.5/aarch64-apple-darwin20/ggpmisc")
# [1] TRUE
```

Packages are properly detected as dependencies:
```
deps <- renv::dependencies()
unique(deps[deps$Package == "Hmisc", "Source"])
# Shows 6 .Rmd files using Hmisc
unique(deps[deps$Package == "ggpmisc", "Source"])  
# Shows 7 .Rmd files using ggpmisc
```

Other renv functions work correctly:

```
renv::install() correctly identifies packages as already installed
renv::snapshot() works normally
renv::restore() correctly identifies library as synchronized
```

Expected Behavior
hydrate() should recognize that packages linked from cache are already available and not repeatedly attempt to install them.
Actual Behavior
hydrate() continuously reports the same packages as missing and reinstalls them from cache every time it's run, despite them being present and functional.
Additional Context

Packages are installed as symlinks from cache: "OK [linked from cache]"
Issue persists across R session restarts
Only affects hydrate() - all other renv functions work correctly
The packages load and function normally despite hydrate's complaints

renv::install("shinychat", repos = "https://posit-dev.r-universe.dev")

This works great locally, but fails to deploy correctly because the repository used to install `shinychat` is not recorded in the `renv.lock` file.

title: feat: list cached packages
description:
I have a scenario where I would like to list the packages that are cached as well as which versions for all R installs on my machine. 

It would be great if there was an renv function that assisted with this. The best I've come up with is below—though I think a named list with versions would likely be better.

Is this a correct way of finding cached R packages for an install?

```r
list_cached_pkgs <- function() {
  # get the cache path
  cache_path <- renv::paths$cache()

  # get the cached packages
  cached_pkgs <- list.dirs(cache_path, recursive = FALSE)

  # get the version of the packages
  pkg_versions <- list.dirs(cached_pkgs, recursive = FALSE) |>
    gsub(paste0(cache_path, "/"), "", x = _) |>
    strsplit("/")

  # extract packages and versions
  pkgs <- vapply(pkg_versions, `[`, character(1), 1)
  vers <- vapply(pkg_versions, `[`, character(1), 2)

  # create data.frame
  data.frame(package = pkgs, version = vers)
}
```

> Sys.setenv("RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY" = file.path(".", "renv2"))

> renv::paths$library()
[1] "./renv2/windows/R-4.5/x86_64-w64-mingw32"

> dir(renv::paths$library())
character(0)

> renv::install("tinytest")
The following package(s) will be installed:
- tinytest [1.4.1]
These packages will be installed into "~/reprex/renv/library/windows/R-4.5/x86_64-w64-mingw32".

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: Y

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing tinytest ...                       OK [copied from cache in 1.6s]
Successfully installed 1 package in 1.6 seconds.

> dir(renv::paths$library())
character(0)
```

I know that [in documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/paths.html#customising-individual-paths) it's recommended to set this variable in some startup file, however it seems that it's rather mandatory in case of `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY`.

For comparison `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` has effect even if set later.
```r
> renv::paths$cache()
[1] "...\\AppData\\Local/R/cache/R/renv/cache/v5/windows/R-4.5/x86_64-w64-mingw32"
> length(dir(renv::paths$cache()))
[1] 135

> Sys.setenv("RENV_PATHS_CACHE" = "~/cache2")

> renv::paths$cache()
[1] "~/cache2/v5/windows/R-4.5/x86_64-w64-mingw32"

> length(dir(renv::paths$cache()))
[1] 0

> renv::install("checkmate")
...
- Installing backports ...                      OK [installed binary and cached in 1.3s]
- Installing checkmate ...                      OK [installed binary and cached in 1.2s]

> length(dir(renv::paths$cache()))
[1] 2
```

I've checked that underneath `paths$library()` calls `renv_bootstrap_library_root` function, that takes `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` into account, while others rely rather on `.libPaths()`, that are not updated to account for the current value of `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY`.

I'm not sure what is the desired behaviour, but even if `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY` is supposed to be set only during startup, than at least `paths$library()` should also ignore it, and maybe it should be stated clearly in the documentation.





In addition it can even be more surprising with `status`. Starting with an empty project:
```r
> renv::init()

> Sys.setenv("RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY" = file.path(".", "renv2"))

> renv::paths$library()
[1] "./renv2/windows/R-4.5/x86_64-w64-mingw32"

> renv::status()
There are no packages installed in the project library.
Use `renv::restore()` to install the packages defined in lockfile.

> renv::restore()
- The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.
```
We receive contradictory information - `status` says that there are no packages installed, while `restore` that library is synchronized.

Underneath it could be attributed to `renv_status_check_initialized` function, that checks if library exists. It could be "fixed" just by creating directory, even empty one.
```r
> dir.create(renv::paths$library(), recursive = TRUE)

> renv::status()
No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

title: Issue installing package binaries
description:
Recently my organisation has been increasing IT security and various users have reported spontaneously receiving the same errors when rebuilding package caches for existing projects. 

I believe the issue arises due to the following:https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/1e065e1eb7325a301614c7eddfaf6c7216bf62ca/R/package.R#L496

It appears that the `oldpath` is temporarily getting locked, and therefore failing to rename the path to `newpath`. I assume it could be a virus scanner which is something you've mentioned before: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/649#issuecomment-780021418.

I've since locally forked `renv` and simply added a basic retry which appears to resolve the issue. E.g.:
```R
if (!file.rename(oldpath, newpath)) {
    for (i in 1:100) {
        print("# Issuing with copying/renaming, retrying ...")
        Sys.sleep(2)
        test <- file.rename(oldpath, newpath)
        if (test) break
    }
} else {
    print("# No issue copying/renaming.")
}
```

I'm hoping that a fix could be implemented that attempts the retry?

Apologies for the lack of a repex, it certainly seems something internal to our organisation and it's difficult to reproduce locally let alone creating a repex.

- Confirming this occurs across various versions of `renv` (certainly the latest version)
- We're on Windows 11
- Warning & Error we receive:
```R
Error in normalizePath(path.expand(path), winslash, mustWork) : 
  path[1]="C:/XXXX/RtmpAtrUsG/renv-package-new-5868558c675d/Matrix": The system cannot find the file specified

title: Suggestion: Consistent Code Block Markup in Vignettes for Accessibility and Usability
description:
Today, while exploring renv profiles in the vignettes, I noticed some inconsistency in the formatting of code examples that could be polished for better accessibility and user experience.

For instance, this code block is formatted with `{r}` markup, which provides syntax highlighting and enables easy copying to the clipboard - a great plus for usability:  
<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/f732223c9114e6f45ce164fba842687b355d7354/vignettes/profiles.Rmd#L105-L107>

However, this one uses plain ` ``` ` markup without a language specifier, lacking the syntax highlighting and clipboard functionality that come with attaching `{r}` or at least ` ```r `:  
<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/f732223c9114e6f45ce164fba842687b355d7354/vignettes/profiles.Rmd#L41-L43>

I also noticed that RMarkdown chunks are not evaluated by default in `vignettes/profiles.Rmd`, which makes complete sense for static documentation:  
<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/f732223c9114e6f45ce164fba842687b355d7354/vignettes/profiles.Rmd#L12>

Additionally, I’ve observed that similar documentation files in the `renv` repository may be affected by this inconsistency in code block markup. The full extent of this across all vignettes and documentation is yet to be checked, but it appears to be a recurring pattern in at least some other files.

I understand this is a small detail and likely an oversight, but consistent use of language-specific markup (e.g., `{r}` or ````r) across all code blocks could improve accessibility by ensuring syntax highlighting is applied uniformly.

title: Windows path conflict: %localappdata%/R/cache/R/renv/index
description:
A colleague recently ran into an issue installing packages in an renv managed environment on Windows 11. They reported that the following error was produced for any package installation, but for this particular output we were attempting to install workflowr:

```
> install.packages("workflowr")
# Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
Warning: failed to create directory at path 'C:\Users\user\AppData\Local/R/cache/R/renv/index/R-4.2/x86_64-w64-mingw32/available-packages'
Warning in entry[[key]] : wrong arguments for subsetting an environment
Warning: failed to create directory at path 'C:\Users\user\AppData\Local/R/cache/R/renv/index/R-4.2/x86_64-w64-mingw32/available-packages'
Warning in file.path(repo, "src/contrib/Archive", Package) :
  object 'Package' not found
Error: failed to retrieve package ''
```

We found that this was because the directory `C:\Users\user\AppData\Local/R/cache/R/renv` already contained an `INDEX` file typical of R package structure, and since Windows treats paths as case-insensitive, the intermediate directory `index` couldn't be created. After renaming the resident file to `_INDEX` all installations proceeded without issue.

title: `dependencies()` is scanning strings
description:
`renv::dependencies()` appears to be scanning character strings for required packages. It seems that this can trigger errors when the string has content like

```r
eqn <- "\\o"
eqn <- "\o"
```

The first line is ok, but the second will cause `renv::dependencies()` to error out. I assume that scanning character strings may be helpful for people doing string manipulation  to automate the execution of some code. However, this seems like a rather specialized use case that deserves the option to selectively ignore. Perhaps scanning of strings could be selectively ignored per file or simply entirely toggled?

title: Bioconductor dependencies picked up for empty biocviews
description:
For version 0.1.2 nestcolor https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nestcolor/index.html mistakenly included the entry in description

`Biocviews:`

This causes `renv` to activate Bioconductor in the lock file despite no actual Bioconductor dependencies being used. It seems like this should only happen if a package includes at least one dependency in the `Biocviews` field. 

For a reprex, add a file with library(nestcolor) and use `renv::checkout("https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2024-08-14")` to see that Bioconductor dependencies get installed.

title: Clarity on how {renv} uses the site-library
description:
Apologies if (i) this has been discussed already or (ii) if there's a setting somewhere that help manage this (but I've looked and can't readily find any).

To describe my confusion, let's use a hypothetical machine on which:
* R and R's core libraries are installed at `/usr/local/lib/R/library`.
* Some additional site-wide packages have been installed at `/usr/local/lib/R/site-library`.

I believe that setup closely aligns with quite a few installations, but in general any 'core-library' and 'site-library' set should work the same.

Let's also assume that {renv} has **never** been used on this machine. There is no {renv} cache or {renv}-managed package library yet.

## Scenario 1

I'm given a `{renv.lock}` file from which I decide to `renv::restore()` the project. This lock file includes the {somepkg} v1.2.3 dependency. It just so happens that {somepkg} v1.2.3 is installed in the site-library. When `restore()` is running, two things happen (amongst others):
1. The core-library is linked via {renv}'s sandbox.
2. {somepkg} v1.2.3 is downloaded, compiled, and installed.

In step 2, the site-library version of {somepkg} v1.2.3 was ignored, and {renv} favored fetching a fresh copy from CRAN (or whatever repo) instead. I suppose that makes sense in an effort to maximize consistency and isolation, _but_ ...

## Scenario 2

Before being given the above `renv.lock` file, I do some other development and happen to create a project that depends on {somepkg} v1.2.3, which again happens to be installed in the site-library. When I `renv::init()` the project, {renv} doesn't download {somepkg} v1.2.3, but rather it copies from the site-library.

Later, I'm given that `renv.lock` file from above. When I now `restore()` that project, {renv} decides to use the cached version of {somepkg} v1.2.3, which was copied from the site-library on account of the other project I created above.

That is to say, by virtue of Scenario 2 simply `init()`ing a (completely unrelated) project, we now have an alternative outcome in the two scenarios, where they have different 'sources' of {somepkg} v1.2.3 installed into {renv}'s cache.

## Question

Since Scenario 2 is actually quite common (at least for me and amongst my colleagues), I don't quite understand why in Scenario 1 {renv} doesn't copy from site-library during the `restore()`. My confusion has some practicality: I have a few Docker workflows and there are a handful of patterns from which to choose (some of which -- but not all -- are similar to those described in the {renv} docs on Docker).

In one particular use case, I base some images off of the `rocker/tidyverse` family, but find when I then inject the {renv} bootstrapping files I still need to install much of the {tidyverse} (at least during the first layer build). In cases where the `rocker/tidyverse` image already contains exactly the correct package versions (installed in the site-library), I'd much rather just copy those to the {renv} cache. I've developed a workaround to achieve this (basically just a forced variant of Scenario 2), but workarounds don't feel great and yet I can't really find a compelling reason why this one wouldn't work, since on a local/development/interactive machine, Scenario 2 is indeed the most common anyhow.

Again, apologies if this isn't the correct venue for clarity, though I think it'd be useful during a `restore` if there was an option to say, "I trust the existing site-library, let's just use that as if we had run an `init()` on some other project anyhow".

title: Out of date version leading to MD5 mismatch error.
description:
I used `pak` to install `this.path (2.7.0)` and `renv` was alerting me to MD5 issues. 
From `sessioninfo::session_info()`:
```
─ Session info ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 setting  value
 version  R version 4.5.0 (2025-04-11 ucrt)
 os       Windows 11 x64 (build 26100)
 system   x86_64, mingw32
 ui       RStudio
...
─ Packages ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 ! package     * version date (UTC) lib source
...
 D this.path     2.7.0   2025-04-10 [1] RSPM (R 4.5.0)
D ── DLL MD5 mismatch, broken installation.
```

I investigated since presumably the same version 2.7.0 should give the same files. The offending DLL (`this_path_reg_ptrs.dll`) was only slightly different (2 timestamps and a checksum when diffed against the CRAN version using Ghidra version comparison tool).

https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/windows/contrib/4.5/this.path_2.7.0.zip with md5 `c84...8fe`
vs
https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/this.path_2.7.0.tar.gz with md5 `140b...a87`

I noticed the CRAN versions timestamp (IN the DLL itself) was today 24 June 2025 whereas the RSPM timestamp was 23 May 2025.
Could it be that RSPM just hasn't updated fast enough? It's strange though that it's exactly the same version but different files. Seemed like something worth mentioning on the issue tracker here. 

Note that I already posted this issue [here](https://github.com/cran4linux/rspm/issues/34) but it was the wrong place. If there's somewhere else I should be posting it let me know. Thanks.

title: [Feature Request] Compress R packages and Unpack to Set Directory for Later Use?
description:
Hello,

Thanks for the great package.

I'd like to request the ability to compress all the R packages into some archive file and then for renv to be able to later unzip this archive to some set directory, then use the set directory.

I know this is a peculiar request, but it's a very helpful feature for in high performance computing contexts and I imagine in any case where one is doing massively distributed computing. 

Let's say that someone stores their R studio project (with renv enabled) on a networked drive. Then as more and more systems try to access the networked drive to do their computations, this can dramatically increase the i/o load on the networked drive--presumably both because (1) the way `renv` starts-up by default is heavy on the i/o and (2) regardless of `renv`, loading many R packages into memory is inherently a high i/o load--such that everything is brought to a halt. 

If it were possible to archive the R packages, then to ask renv to unpack it to system's local drive (as opposed to the network drive), it would be really helpful. Additionally, the reason why I'd like to request this feature of `renv` as opposed to attempting a custom `tar/dar` script solution is to ensure both the correctness and reproducibility of the archiving and decompressing.

title: Feature Request: Centralized Caching for Python Virtual Environments to Improve Performance and Portability
description:
FEATURE REQUEST (and discussion for existing solutions)

**Problem Description:**

Currently, `renv` manages Python virtual environments in one of two main ways:

1.  **Project-Local:** Created within the project directory (e.g., `renv/python/virtualenvs/myenv`). This is great for encapsulation and `renv::restore()` recreating the environment easily. However, when developing R packages, tools like `devtools::check()` copy the entire project, including this potentially large Python environment. This can lead to extremely long check times, significantly slowing down the development iteration cycle.
2.  **External/Pre-existing:** Using `renv::use_python(python = "/path/to/venv/bin/python")`. This avoids the copying issue during `devtools::check()` as the environment is outside the project. However, it often leads to absolute paths being recorded or implied, which harms reproducibility across different machines or for different users, as the path to the Python environment might not be the same.

This situation presents a trade-off: either slow checks or less portable/reproducible Python environment setups.

The way `renv` handles R package caching is a great model: R packages are stored in a central cache and linked into project libraries. This provides both efficiency (no copying, shared resources) and reproducibility.

**Desired Behavior / Feature Request:**

I would like to request a feature (or inquire if a similar mechanism already exists) where `renv` can manage Python virtual environments in a way analogous to its R package caching:

1.  **Centralized Storage:** `renv` creates/manages Python virtual environments in a location *outside* the project directory (e.g., in the global `renv` cache directory or a user-configurable Python environment cache).
2.  **Project-Specific Referencing:** The `renv.lock` file would reference this Python environment using a project-specific, non-absolute identifier. This could be the environment name (if unique resolution is possible), a hash, a project ID, or similar.
3.  **Automatic Linking/Activation:** During `renv::init()`, `renv::restore()`, or `renv::use_python()`, `renv` would ensure that the project is configured to use the correct centrally cached Python environment. This might involve `reticulate` configuration or perhaps even symlinking (if feasible and robust across platforms for Python venvs).
4.  **No Copying During Checks:** Because the Python environment's files would reside outside the project directory being copied by `devtools::check()`, the check process would remain fast.
5.  **Reproducibility:** The `renv.lock` would enable `renv` to recreate or locate the correct, centrally managed Python environment on a different machine or for a different user without relying on hardcoded absolute paths.

**Benefits:**

*   **Performance:** Significantly speeds up `devtools::check()` and similar operations for projects with Python dependencies.
*   **Reproducibility:** Enhances reproducibility for Python environments across different systems, similar to R packages.
*   **Disk Space:** Potentially saves disk space if multiple projects can share common Python base environments or packages (though Python venvs are typically more isolated than R package libraries).
*   **Consistency:** Aligns the management philosophy of Python environments more closely with R packages within `renv`.

**Current Workarounds and Their Limitations:**

*   **Project-local venv + `.Rbuildignore`:** Adding `renv/python/` to `.Rbuildignore` keeps the built package tarball small but does *not* speed up `devtools::check()` as it operates on the source tree before `.Rbuildignore` is applied.
*   **External venv with absolute/user-specific paths:** Requires manual setup and path adjustments on new systems, making it less portable.

**Questions for the `renv` Team:**

1.  Is managing Python virtual environments in a centralized cache, referenced by a project-specific ID, a feature that has been considered or is on the roadmap?
2.  Are there existing, perhaps less documented, ways to configure `renv` and `reticulate` to achieve a similar outcome (centralized Python venv without absolute paths in `renv.lock` and without being copied during checks)?
3.  Given the nature of Python virtual environments (which are often less "relocatable" than individual R packages), what are the potential challenges or design considerations for such a feature?

Thank you for developing `renv` and for considering this request. I believe such a feature would greatly benefit R developers working on projects with substantial Python dependencies, particularly in the context of package development.

title: [Feature request] Support uv level dependency specification in comments
description:
The `renv` package is being used by shinylive to automatically determine dependencies for a Shiny app in either `app.R` or `server.R`/`ui.R`. However, when custom repositories serving R WASM packages are required by organizations, there are some slight dependency hiccups that occur as the package can't be found.

The ask is to move toward implementing support for `uv` level [script dependency headings](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/scripts/#declaring-script-dependencies) allowing us to specify remote dependencies

```r
# /// script
# dependencies = [
#     package_name == 0.1.5
# ]
# [tool.sources]
# package_name = { web = "https://website.com/custom-repo" }
# ///
```

title: disabling bioconductor
description:
This is a little hard to make a reprex for as I can't find a public package manager snapshot which replicates our set up.

Currently our snapshot of packages includes both CRAN and BioConductor packages; we do not separate them into two images.  However this behaviour seems to cause some odd behaviours in renv.

If a package `biocViews:` in its description then the following behaviour seems to occur

1) when running `renv::checkout(<snapshot from our manager>)` renv will sometimes (not always, it seems a little inconsistent) install Bioconductor packages from Bioconductor (the urls packaged with renv); this can mean that a package of a greater version than is on our snapshot ends up being installed
2) Whether 1 happens or not, BiocVersion will be added to the snapshot, and the repos will include all the Bioconductor sources found in ` renv:::renv_bioconductor_repos()`. 

Some exploration indicates that I can disable this by adding `options(renv.bioconductor.repos = c("<my snapshot>"))` in my RProfile, basically overwriting renv's default bioconductor behaviour.

I think this could be classed as a bug; renv should ideally check my ppm image to see if a bioconductor package is available before checking Bioconductor. I think it would be good to actively disable this behaviour entirely without needing to specify my snapshot in the profile.

title: renv doesn't create symlink to packages in system libraries.
description:
I am trying to create a wrapper script around renv with the aim to facilitate the use of renv on our HPC infrastructure. The cluster runs entirely on the rocky8 OS and has heterogeneous (mostly) intel hardware architecture. 

These are my findings so far:
1) When a centrally installed hardware specific R installation (aka R module) is used and `renv::init()` is called the `.cache/R/renv/sandbox/R-<version>/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/<hash>` contains (as desired) symlinks to packages installed in the library of this R module. In this case, the path is unique for different installations of R.
2) When `renv::install()` installs a new package it is installed in the `.cache/R/renv/cache` directory. A first issue is that this install path is not unique per hardware architecture. This can lead to potential issues when linking from various projects to packages in this cache directory.
3) When calling `renv::install()` on a package that is already available in the R module library, then I would expect that renv can pick this up and creates a symlink link to the package in this library, similar to how it worked for `renv::init()`. 

The issue: this doesn't happen.
I have tried setting both the `renv.config.cache.symlinks=TRUE` and `renv.cache.linkable=TRUE` and have added the available R module libraries to the RENV_PATHS_CACHE variable before running `renv::install()`. 

```bash
export RENV_CACHE_DIRS="${XDG_CACHE_HOME}/R/renv;${EBROOTR}/lib/R/library"
export PACKAGE_LIST="<package1>,<package2>,...,<packageX>"
export PROJECT_DIR="/path/to/r-project/"
```

```R
options(renv.config.cache.symlinks = TRUE, renv.cache.linkable = TRUE); 
Sys.setenv(RENV_PATHS_CACHE = Sys.getenv("RENV_CACHE_DIRS")); 
renv::activate(Sys.getenv("PROJECT_DIR"))
renv::install(packages=strsplit(Sys.getenv("PACKAGE_LIST"), ",")[[1]], project=Sys.getenv("PROJECT_DIR"), lock=TRUE)
```

When attempting to install a package (e.g. `RColorBrewer`) this way `renv::install()` crashes with the following traceback.

```R
In dir.create(rownames(info), recursive = TRUE) :
  cannot create dir '/apps/rocky8/icelake/2022b/software/R/4.2.2-foss-2022b/lib64/R/library/.renv', reason 'Permission denied'
Traceback (most recent calls last):
12: renv::install(packages = strsplit(Sys.getenv("PACKAGE_LIST"), ",")[[1]], project = Sys.getenv("PROJECT_DIR"), lock = TRUE)
11: renv_install_impl(records)
10: renv_install_staged(records)
9: enumerate(targets, renv_file_move, overwrite = TRUE)
8: lapply(idx, callback)
7: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
6: f(n[[i]], x[[i]], ...)
5: renv_file_preface(source, target, overwrite)
4: renv_file_backup(target)
3: renv_file_move(path, tempfile)
2: stopf(text, source, target)
1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
Execution halted
```

When digging a bit deeper into the source code of install.R:
`renv_install_staged(records)` first calls `renv_install_default(records)` on line 314 which in turn calls `renv_install_package`. If I understood correctly, this method will attempt to create symlinks to a staged library if possible. 
After installing or linking the packages, "packages are migrated into the true library". This attempts to make a hidden `.renv` folder in the R module library which then fails due to obvious write permissions on a centrally installed R library. 
```R
  # migrate packages into true library
  library <- nth(libpaths, 1L)
  sources <- list.files(templib, full.names = TRUE)
  targets <- file.path(library, basename(sources))
  names(targets) <- sources
  enumerate(targets, renv_file_move, overwrite = TRUE)
```
My question is, what is the purpose of migrating these packages? and is there a way to circumvent this?
perhaps I'm missing something obvious.

title: renv::init() is not installing packages from user/system library
description:
We have discovered a bug in `renv::init()` of `renv@1.1.x` or a change in expected behvior from `renv@1.0.x` for a specific set of circumstances. 
1. A package is installed in the User (or System) Library
2. The same package is not in the `renv` cache.

It appears that `hydrate()` in `renv@1.1.x` is not properly linking packages into the project library. `init()` and `hydrate()` do not show any errors or warnings. This change in behavior happened between 1.0.11 and 1.1.0.

### Reprex:

Start with an empty project. WIth one source file.

```R
## source.R
library(dplyr)
```

To show what is expected behavior, let's use `renv@1.0.11`

```R
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_version("renv", version = "1.0.11")
.rs.restartR()

# Ensure that `dplyr` is in the User (or System) Library
install.packages("dplyr")

# Clear `dplyr` from renv cache
renv::purge("dplyr")

renv::init()

renv::status()
# No issues found
```

Now, we reset our project to its original pre-renv state.

```R
renv::deactivate()
unlink("renv", recursive = TRUE)
file.remove("renv.lock")

.rs.restartR()

renv::purge("dplyr")
```

Then we install the latest renv and initialize.

```R
install.packages("renv")
packageVersion("renv")
# [1] ‘1.1.2’

renv::init()

renv::status()
# The following package(s) are used in this project, but are not installed:
# - dplyr
```

### hydrate() is not working as it used to

```R
# renv 1.0.11
> renv::purge("dplyr")
The following packages will be purged from the cache:
- dplyr 1.1.4 [Hash: fedd9d00c2944ff00a0e2696ccf048ec]

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y

- Removed 1 package from the cache.
> renv::hydrate()
The following packages were discovered:

# ~/Library/R/arm64/4.4/library ----------------------------------------------
- dplyr   1.1.4

They will be linked into the project library.

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y

- Linking packages into the project library ... Done!
- Hydrated 1 packages in 53 milliseconds.
> renv::status()
No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

```R
# renv 1.1.2
> renv::hydrate()
The following packages were discovered:

# ~/Library/R/arm64/4.4/library ----------------------------------------------
- dplyr   1.1.4

They will be linked into the project library.

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y

- Linking packages into the project library ... Done!
- Hydrated 1 packages in 3 milliseconds.
> renv::status()
The following package(s) are used in this project, but are not installed:
- dplyr

See `?renv::status` for advice on resolving these issues.
```

We took a look inside `hydrate()` and further into `renv_hydrate_link_packages()` and found the following difference:

```R
# renv 1.0.11
Browse[1]> cached
$dplyr
[1] TRUE

# renv 1.1.2
Browse[1]> cached
$dplyr
[1] FALSE
```

       "rpm", ~stop("don't know how to check sysreqs on this system"))
1: stop("don't know how to check sysreqs on this system")
```

And 

```r
> renv::sysreqs()
Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
Error in case(nzchar(Sys.which("dpkg")) ~ "deb", nzchar(Sys.which("rpm")) ~  : 
  don't know how to check sysreqs on this system
```

To workaround, I did 

```r
options(renv.config.sysreqs.check = FALSE)
```

and then seemingly everything was fine again.

Is that options setting my only or recommended option for use on Arch Linux?

title: renv doesn't persist between RStudio sessions
description:
BUG REPORT: There seems to be a problem when using renv with a different base version of R to the one it was created with. RStudio / renv does not recognise the packages are already installed, and I have to reinstall them all each time I open the project.

I have an RStudio project that uses renv. I recently upgraded my core R version, and had to reinstall the packages from the original lockfile. Now each time I open the project I get this message:
```
Using R 4.4.2 (lockfile was generated with R 4.3.1)
- Project {my_project} loaded. [renv 1.0.11]
- One or more packages recorded in the lockfile are not installed.
- Use `renv::status()` for more details.
```
When I explore my_project/renv/library... I see all the packages duly sitting there.

I sought help for this on the [Posit forum](https://forum.posit.co/t/renv-doesnt-persist-between-rstudio-sessions/196971) but there is no solution.

title: renv doesn't capture additional repos from `install.packages(..., repos = "<repo>")`
description:
I think this might be a regression as this was apparently implemented in #1175

If you installed a package via `install.packages(..., repos = "<repo>")` then `<repo>` isn't captured anywhere in the lock file and the lock file is thus not able to be restored. 

Code to reproduce:

```R

# Set repo where most recent version of renv is available from, but not too recent so we can install newer packages
options(repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2025-02-08")

install.packages("renv")
renv::init()   # and then Restart R

# Ensure correct url is stored in the initial lock file
options(repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2025-02-08")
renv::snapshot()

# data.table v1.17.0 was released on Feb 22, 2025 so won't be availabel in the 8th Feb snapshot used above
# May need to adjust environment variables to not link to an already installed/cached version
install.packages("data.table", repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2025-03-03" )
# insert a `library(data.table)` somewhere for R env to pick it up
renv::snapshot()
```
