#> - StanHeaders   [repo: CRAN -> Stan; ver: 2.32.9 -> 2.35.0.9000]
```

All the items listed under `Stan` here were initially installed from CRAN and recorded in `renv.lock` as such, but `renv::update()` attempts to replace these with development versions from R-Universe. I was wondering if this is unexpected behavior, or if this is simply a case where "Updates will only be checked from the same source" actually means CRAN (or CRAN-like repo) vs. GitHub with no way to distinguish between different sources in `getOption("repos")`.

title: Behavior of `renv::install(prompt = FALSE)` when `options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE)`
description:
I have, perhaps lazily, fallen into the habit of using `renv:install(prompt = FALSE)` when packaging up shiny apps for deployment. This works great with base `renv` as it goes through, finds, and installs all packages used in the directory. My reason for doing things this way is due to non-negotiable company anti-virus software, I can't actually use R when `renv` is active as many package `.dll`s get flagged. However, to "easily" deploy applications on our shiny server or test w/ Docker, `renv` makes life easier. So, though I'm quite sure this not best practice, I have to refrain from using renv until development is complete and simply use it as a deployment tool.

Recently, I have seen a VAST difference in Docker build times and shiny server deployment when using `options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE)` and would like to go in that direction. However, I have noticed that `renv:install(prompt = FALSE)` fails when `pak` is enabled on a couple of different levels.

```r
renv::deactivate(clean = TRUE)
# restart R
renv::activate()
# restart R

renv::install(prompt = FALSE)
```

Firstly, I am prompted whether I want to install `pak` or not. This is not a huge deal but does not agree with the `prompt = FALSE` argument.

```r
The following package(s) will be installed:
- pak [0.7.2]
These packages will be installed into "~/path/to/app/renv/library/macos/R-4.4/x86_64-apple-darwin20".


Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]:
```

Secondly, and more importantly, I get this error which I presume is just the way `pak` is set up to work:

```r
# Installing packages ----------------------------------------
- Installing pak ...                            OK [linked from cache]
Successfully installed 1 package in 23 milliseconds.
Error: 
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `find_package_root(path = root)`:
! Could not find R package in `/path/to/app` or its parent directories.
Type .Last.error to see the more details.
Traceback (most recent calls last):
6: renv::install(prompt = FALSE)
5: renv_pak_install(packages, libpaths, project)
4: pak$local_install_dev_deps(root = project, lib = lib)
3: remote(function(...) {
       get("local_install_dev_deps_make_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...)
   }, list(root = root, lib = lib, upgrade = upgrade, start = start, 
       dependencies = dependencies, loaded = loaded_packages(lib)))
2: err$throw(res$error)
1: base::stop(cond)
```

However, if I:


```r
renv::dependencies() |>
    getElement("Package") |>
    unique() |>
    renv::install(prompt = FALSE)
```

I'm still prompted:

```
Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
                                                              
→ Will update 1 package.
→ The package (103.96 kB) is cached.
+ KernSmooth 2.23-22 → 2.23-24 

? Do you want to continue (Y/n)
```

But then things work after I `Y`:

```
ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg (103.96 kB) is cached
✔ Got KernSmooth 2.23-24 (x86_64-apple-darwin20) (104.06 kB)
✔ Installed KernSmooth 2.23-24  (62ms)                
✔ 19 pkgs + 93 deps: kept 111, upd 1, dld 1 (104.06 kB) [40s]
```

After which point I `renv::snapshot()`. 

However, if I simply `renv::activate()`, restart, and then `renv::snapshot()`, that seems to find and install packages just fine using the prompts hence the issue.

title: Dependency discovery can't handle complex `eval` chunk options
description:
Let's say you have the following nonsensical chunk:

`````rmd
```{r}
#| eval = c(1, 2)
x <- LETTERS
x <- letters
x <- stringi::stri_rand_lipsum()
```
`````

If you save it as "foo.rmd" and run `rmarkdown::render("foo.rmd")` you will note that it works correctly, demonstrating that this uses valid syntax.

However, if you run `renv::dependencies()`:
```
Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
[1] Source  Package Require Version Dev
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
Warning message:
In if (value %in% c("TRUE", "True", "true", "T", "1")) TRUE else if (value %in%  :
  the condition has length > 1
```

Specifically this happens because when we reach the following line, `value` is a vector of `c(1, 2)`, and so the `if` gets a length-2 argument: 
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/568e8cc0a7344b7dc54c5a928c153937af61a999/R/truthy.R#L20

 3: h(simpleError(msg, call))
 2: stopf("package '%s' is not available", package)
 1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
```

However, I still don't understand why this issue arise (as BiocManager is in cache) and how I can make sure that will not happen again.

1) Why does the app has to connect to an external repo if it has everything stored in cache?
2) Why does it only affect applications making use of BioConductor libraries (I tend to incriminate BiocManager, not BioConductor itself).
3) Would it be possible to specify more than one URL for the repositories defined in the renv.lock file? It would be something like this :

```
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": ["https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest",  "https://cloud.r-project.org"]
      }

```

Many thanks for your help.
Regards.

title: `ppm.enabled` in settings vs. config
description:
The documentation implies that the config and settings `ppm.enabled` options operate similarly. However a recent use case brought up some questions about the difference between these two options. Here is the scenario:

- Repo is set to a specific, older CRAN snapshot
- Package version from the specified CRAN snapshot is *earlier* than the default package version from P3M (according to the version of R being used in the session)
- Windows OS
	
For example, from R 4.3.2, the following code:
```
renv::install("dplyr", repos = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2023-03-01")
```

Results in 
```
# Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
- Downloading dplyr from P3M ...                OK [1.5 Mb in 2.1s]
Successfully downloaded 1 package in 2.3 seconds.
The following package(s) will be installed:
- dplyr [1.1.4]
```

As opposed to downloading dplyr 1.1.0 from the 2023-03-01 snapshot. 
I have found that if I set config ppm.enabled = FALSE and settings ppm.enabled = TRUE, I *think* I am able to avoid {renv} from reaching out to P3M, while keeping other benefits of PPM being enabled. 

Is this the expected behavior/the recommended configuration for sticking to just the specified repos? If so, is there a way to update the documentation so these 2 options can be more easily distinguished?

Thanks very much in advance for your help!

title: Some packages that need compilation will incur in an error with R 4.4.0
description:

This doesn't happen when installing the same packages without using renv (but using R 4.4.0) or when using renv and R 4.3.3, hence why I believe it to be a problem related to renv and R 4.4.0.

title: renv::restore() is not reliable on Windows; calls make and other Linux utilities
description:
We want to use renv on Windows, but have encountered an issue running renv::restore() on the lockfile generated by migrating from packrat. Specifically, renv::restore() fails because 1: It asks for things like make and g++ on Windows machines, without installing these dependencies itself.

I've worked around this problem by using renv::init() instead, however we need to be able to rely on renv::restore() because we don't want the packages to update when we reproduce old run throughs of code. This was only an option because I was working on a new run through.

Occurs: Running renv::restore() on the new lockfile after migrating from packrat to renv.
renv::restore() does not work for restoring some libraries on windows machines. Specifically the sys library, from the renv.lock file

title: {gitcreds}
Allow renv::restore to help updating packages when restore fails
description:
After updating to R 4.4 I just spent 20 minutes repeating the following procedure to restore an old project:

* renv::restore()
* renv::update("packagethatcausedproblems")
* renv::record("packagethatcausedproblems")
* rinse and repeat

Could we have `restore(and_try_updating_to_make_it_work=TRUE)` handle this itself? (With a better argument name obviously)

There is no need for a human to be at the helm to do the above routine repetatively for a period of time. Of course there are perfectly valid reasons why more or less blindly updating arbitrary packages isn't a good idea, but I imagine, for probably a large majority of projects, package versions that are no longer installable can be safely updated as the prefered solution instead of troubleshooting installation of old versions.

Halfway through I tried `renv::update()` to just update all packages, (and risking rebuilding packages not in cache), but this didnt fix things, still had to go back to update individual packages and repeat. This is also not an ideal solution as you now update everything and not just the ones that are causing a problem.

title: Do not hang renv activation script if communication with the repository does not work
description:
Today when I started the R session it hung and I wondered what was going on. After trying a few things, I realized that p3m was not working properly and I could not install the package using pak, etc.
I solved the problem by deleting all renv-related files and installing the package from the CRAN 0-cloud mirror using pak.

Perhaps the current script does not have some kind of communication timeout with the repository, which is not very ideal since the R session cannot be started unless it is prevented from reading the Rprofile.

title: `renv::install()` sometimes doesn't like `glue::glue()` double curly brace escapes
description:
Hello there!

Since version 1.0.0 (I think) `renv` appears to have a problem with the use of `{{}}` in `glue::glue()` expressions where there is a variable to be evaluated inside the escaped braces. (A use case for these is when dynamically building {cli} formatted messages).

### Reprex (using {renv} 1.0.7)

```R
writeLines("Imports:\n\tglue\n\tcli", con = "DESCRIPTION")

# This will cause issues
writeLines("foo <- 'world'\nbar <- glue::glue('Hello {{{foo}}}')", con = "foo.R")

# This will cause issues - this is the "real" use case with a cli class
writeLines("foo <- 'world'\nbar <- glue::glue('Hello {{.strong {foo}}}')", con = "bar.R")

# This will not cause issues
writeLines("foo <- 'world'\nbar <- glue::glue('Hello {foo}')", con = "baz.R")

# This will not cause issues
writeLines("foo <- 'world'\nbar <- glue::glue('Hello {{world}}')", con = "ham.R")

renv::install()
```
```
WARNING: One or more problems were discovered while enumerating dependencies.

# /home/pbbgss/projects/foo/bar.R --------------------------------------------
Error: <text>:1:4: unexpected '}'
1: foo}
       ^

# /home/pbbgss/projects/foo/foo.R --------------------------------------------
Error: <text>:1:4: unexpected '}'
1: foo}
       ^

Please see `?renv::dependencies` for more information.
```

The warning isn't triggered on {renv} 0.15.4 but I haven't tested everything in between

title: clean() doesn't remove packages from older versions of R
description: Having upgraded R, run `snapshot()` and reinstalled all the relevant packages, I've now got packages in both `renv/library/R-4.3` and `renv/library/R-4.4`. I ran `renv::clean()` expecting it to remove the packages in R-4.3 (since those versions are indeed no longer used). But it doesn't do that. Maybe it should?

title: renv / install.packages ignore requested repo
description:
`arrow` currently has an issue when the Mac version has heavily restricted capabilities. The recommended solution is to download from https://apache.r-universe.dev. However, if I use

`install.packages("arrow", repos = "https://apache.r-universe.dev")`

from within a renv-enabled project, `install.packages` keeps using the cran version. This persisted after deleting the package and using `renv::purge("arrow")`. The only way I could finally get the r-universe version installed was to close the project, install `arrow` when renv was not loaded, and then go back to the project and install `arrow` again. 

The expected behavior is that renv honors a requested repo.

title: "Package libcurl was not found" during Github action setup-renv on Ubuntu
description:
When setting up github actions to test on push, the workflow fails on the setup-renv step when trying to use `ubuntu-latest` as the OS. I get the following message:

```
Package libcurl was not found in the pkg-config search path.
Perhaps you should add the directory containing `libcurl.pc'
to the PKG_CONFIG_PATH environment variable
No package 'libcurl' found
```

I do not get this when I use `macos-latest` as the OS, but I was hoping to use Ubuntu. Note that I tried to add Ubuntu dependencies as a separate step before `setup-r` but that did not work:

```
- name: Install ubuntu deps
        run: sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
          git-core \
          libssl-dev \
          libcurl4-gnutls-dev \
          curl \
          libsodium-dev \
          libxml2-dev
```

Here is my full yaml for the github workflow:

```
name: Testing R

on:
  pull_request
    
env:
  RENV_PATHS_ROOT: ~/.cache/R/renv
  R_HOME: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/Current/Resources
  

jobs:
  tests:
    runs-on: macos-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2
      - name: Cache R environment setup
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ${{ env.R_HOME }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-r-setup-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-r-setup-

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2
      - name: Cache packages
        uses: actions/cache@v1
        with:
          path: ${{ env.RENV_PATHS_ROOT }}
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-renv-${{ hashFiles('**/renv.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-renv-
      - name: Restore packages
        shell: Rscript {0}
        run: |
          if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("renv")
          renv::restore()
      - name: Install testing dependencies
        run: Rscript -e "install.packages(c('testthat', 'here'))"
      - name: Run tests
        run: Rscript -e "source('tests/testthat.R')"
```

title: `renv::restore()` doesn't use RemoteSHA recorded in the lockfile when running in Docker container
description:
Hi @kevinushey and renv dev team,
We're using `renv::restore` as part of our Docker build process and just discovered that when `renv::restore` runs while building the Docker image it's not respecting the RemoteSHA recorded in the lockfile for github dependencies, and is rather using the most recent commit. title: Addition of `renv.lock` schema
Result of `renv::update(lock = TRUE)` differs from `renv::update(lock = FALSE); renv::snapshot()`
description:
renv 1.0.6 introduced a `lock` parameter to  `renv::update()` via https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/3c136470935e32175bcfa401a5387591e469f083, implementing https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1849 (thanks again!).

I just tested this new parameter for the first time and noticed it suffers from a similar issue as https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1828:

When I run (in a project using renv's **explicit** snapshot type)

```r
renv::update(prompt = FALSE, lock = TRUE)
```

it produces the following output

```
- Checking for updated packages ... Done!
The following package(s) will be updated:

# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- spatial   [7.3-15 -> 7.3-17]

The following package(s) will be installed:
- spatial [7.3-17]
These packages will be installed into "~/Arbeit/ZDA/Git/zdaarau/fokus_reports/input/renv/library/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu".

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing spatial ...                        OK [linked from cache]
Successfully installed 1 package in 16 milliseconds.
- Lockfile written to "~/Arbeit/ZDA/Git/zdaarau/fokus_reports/input/renv/renv.lock".
```

and renv writes the following lines to my project's `renv.lock`

```json
    "spatial": {
      "Package": "spatial",
      "Version": "7.3-17",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "RSPM",
      "Requirements": [
        "R",
        "graphics",
        "stats",
        "utils"
      ],
      "Hash": "1229a01b4ec059e9f2396724f2ec9010"
    },
```

although package `spatial` is neither a direct, nor indirect project dependency, i.e. it is not listed in my project's `DESCRIPTION` file, nor is it a required dependency of any other listed package. This results in the project being "out-of-sync" (until I manually revert the lockfile addition above). `renv::status()` at this point outputs

```
The following package(s) are in an inconsistent state:

 package installed recorded used
 spatial y         y        n   

See ?renv::status() for advice on resolving these issues.
```

---

When I OTOH run

```r
renv::update(prompt = FALSE)
renv::snapshot(prompt = FALSE)
```

it produces the following output (which is exactly the same as above)

```
- Checking for updated packages ... Done!
The following package(s) will be updated:

# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- spatial   [7.3-15 -> 7.3-17]

The following package(s) will be installed:
- spatial [7.3-17]
These packages will be installed into "~/Arbeit/ZDA/Git/zdaarau/fokus_reports/input/renv/library/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu".

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing spatial ...                        OK [linked from cache]
Successfully installed 1 package in 16 milliseconds.
```

```
- Lockfile written to "~/Arbeit/ZDA/Git/zdaarau/fokus_reports/input/renv/renv.lock".
```

but renv ***does not alter my project's lockfile*** and everything is fine afterwards.

---

The project I'm testing this with is public, you can reproduce the above with

```sh
git clone https://gitlab.com/zdaarau/fokus_reports.git
cd fokus_reports/input/
R
```

and then

```r
renv::restore()
```

After this, the project should be in consistent state and running either `renv::update(prompt = FALSE, lock = TRUE)` or `renv::update(prompt = FALSE); renv::snapshot(prompt = FALSE)` should reproduce what I reported above.

title: could not find function "heredoc" in renv 1.0.6 activate script
description:
I believe there is a critical bug in renv 1.0.6. When writing the corresponding renv/activate.R script it contains
```
    fmt <- heredoc("
      renv %1$s was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv %2$s.
      - Use `renv::record(\"%3$s\")` to record renv %1$s in the lockfile.
      - Use `renv::restore(packages = \"renv\")` to install renv %2$s into the project library.
    ")
```
in lines 842+. This fails with an error when the R session starts and the renv version installed is not 1.0.6, because heredoc is not found (it is an unexported function of renv, renv:::heredoc works).

```
Error in heredoc("\n      renv %1$s was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv %2$s.\n      - Use `renv::record(\"%3$s\")` to record renv %1$s in the lockfile.\n      - Use `renv::restore(packages = \"renv\")` to install renv %2$s into the project library.\n    ") :

```

title: Feature request: add `upgrade` parameter to `renv::install()`
description:
Currently `renv::install()` always installs the latest version of dependencies. Sometimes it is desirable to install packages without upgrading installed dependencies, like `remotes::install_cran("renv", upgrade = "never")`.

Can an `upgrade` parameter be added to `renv::install()` so that it functions like `remotes::install_*`?

title: GitHub Action fails when using development version of renv (1.0.5.9000)
description:
To resolve #1869, I upgraded to the development version of renv (1.0.5.9000). Some GitHub Actions using renv are now failing with an error:

```
2024-04-08T16:38:43.0699010Z Error in heredoc("\n      renv %1$s was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv %2$s.\n      - Use `renv::record(\"%3$s\")` to record renv %1$s in the lockfile.\n      - Use `renv::restore(packages = \"renv\")` to install renv %2$s into the project library.\n    ") : 
2024-04-08T16:38:43.0784300Z   could not find function "heredoc"
2024-04-08T16:38:43.0788230Z Calls: source ... renv_bootstrap_load -> renv_bootstrap_validate_version
2024-04-08T16:38:43.0789610Z Execution halted
2024-04-08T16:38:43.0813430Z ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

(see https://github.com/jabenninghoff/rdev/pull/197 for full details)

This appears to be occurring because renv is not loaded when `renv_bootstrap_validate_version()` is called from `renv/activate.R`. I was unable to reproduce the issue locally, but it is reliably failing for my `missing-deps.yaml` and `lint.yaml` actions.

title: `renv::install` fails to install from GitHub when using `curl` 8.7.1
description:
`renv::install` fails to install from GitHub when using `curl` 8.7.1 on macOS.

To reproduce, create a new project in RStudio on macOS in a new directory, selecting "Use renv with this project" and install the latest version of `curl` using `brew install curl`.

Running:

```r
Sys.setenv(PATH = paste0("/opt/homebrew/opt/curl/bin:", Sys.getenv("PATH")))
renv::install("eddelbuettel/digest")
```

Will fail with an error:

```
Error: failed to resolve remote 'eddelbuettel/digest' -- error downloading 'https://api.github.com/repos/eddelbuettel/digest/contents/DESCRIPTION?ref=ebd25a4bd18f3c5ee786a463cb01d629162cc8f1' [error code 26]
```

A trace shows the call is failing on `renv_remotes_resolve_github_description`. Setting `options(renv.download.trace = TRUE)` fails to provide any additional information.

```
> traceback()
15: stop(simpleError(message = message, call = e$call))
14: h(simpleError(msg, call))
13: .handleSimpleError(function (e) 
    {
        fmt <- "failed to resolve remote '%s'"
        prefix <- sprintf(fmt, spec)
        message <- paste(prefix, e$message, sep = " -- ")
        stop(simpleError(message = message, call = e$call))
    }, "error downloading 'https://api.github.com/repos/eddelbuettel/digest/contents/DESCRIPTION?ref=ebd25a4bd18f3c5ee786a463cb01d629162cc8f1' [error code 26]", 
        base::quote(NULL))
12: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
11: stopf("error downloading '%s' [%s]", url, msg, call. = FALSE)
10: renv_download_error(url, "error code %i", status)
9: download(url, destfile = destfile, type = "github", quiet = TRUE, 
       headers = headers)
8: renv_remotes_resolve_github_description(url, host, user, repo, 
       subdir, sha)
7: renv_remotes_resolve_github(remote)
6: renv_remotes_resolve_impl(spec, latest)
5: withCallingHandlers(renv_remotes_resolve_impl(spec, latest), 
       error = error)
4: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
3: lapply(x, f, ...)
2: map(packages, renv_remotes_resolve)
1: renv::install("eddelbuettel/digest")
```

Notes:

- The `PATH` command is for `arm64` macs, the `curl` path will be different for `x86_64`.
- I discovered this issue when GitHub Actions started failing after the release of [macOS-12/20240329.1](https://github.com/actions/runner-images/releases/tag/macOS-12%2F20240329.1), which updates curl from 8.6.0 to 8.7.1
- This will cause any GitHub Action that runs `renv::install` to fail, although `renv::restore` still works
- On the Windows runner, which uses `curl` 8.4.0, `renv::install` succeeds
- See https://github.com/jabenninghoff/jbplot/pull/49 for more detail

title: library path is inside cache and not the project
description:
Hi @kevinushey,

When I call renv inside a golem Shiny App, it creates an renv folder inside the project with .gitignore, activate.R, settings.json. There is no library inside with all my packages. With `.libPaths()` I found out it is saving this directory to:

'/home/myUser/.cache/R/renv/library/myAppName/...'. 

I would expect `.libPaths()` to change to my project directory once I initiate renv `renv::init()`.

When I call renv outside a golem shiny App it works as intended. I wonder what behaviour of renv or interaction between golem and renv is causing this?

title: Factor our configuration resolution mechanism to a separate package so others can use it
description:
In my limited understanding, {renv} has a sophisticated configuration resolution mechanism:

**user-level configs**

Uses R options in the form of `renv.config.<name>`, or `RENV_CONFIG_<NAME>⁠` (with resolving conflicts), e.g. in `.Rprofile` or `.Renviron`. These can be accessed in session with `renv::config`.

**project-local settings**

Allows two ways of specifying option defaults with resolving conflicts (e.g. in `.Rprofile`):

```r
options(renv.settings = list(snapshot.type = "all"))
options(renv.settings.snapshot.type = "all")
```
These can be accessed and changed in session with `renv::settings` and are persistent within `renv/settings.json`


The configuration options are well documented leveraging R's helpfile mechanism. I believe resolving project-local and user-level configurations is a very generic functionality for R packages, and many packages have opted to implement their own, using various file formats, heuristics and logic, creating friction for users and maintenance burden for developers. I myself have experimented before (since people have [long asked to allow configuring {styler} with a config file](https://github.com/r-lib/styler/issues/319)), creating a prototype [{fallback}](https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/fallback) that tackles the problem in an even more general way. However, I abandoned that approach due to a lack of time. But I don't think we need to re-invent the wheel for every package anew, it would be great to have a standard way of resolving configuration on a  user and project level. 

Hence, I was wondering if you'd consider exposing the config resolution mechanism of {renv} in a separate package so other package developers (or even just R users) could use it.

title: renv install linking from cache only
description:
Hello,
I have a general question about the initialization of a new project using `renv`.

This is a sample case:
I create a new renv project with `renv::init`
I need to install tidyverse, I use `renv::install("tidyvese")` (Tidiverse was already installed before with all the dependencies at the time of installation, and is available in the cache).
`renv` repopulates the project folder with the requested packages and relative dependencies. Some packages are linked from the cache since they are already available. Some others might have changed over time; therefore, they are not linked from the cache but built from source or installed as binaries.
```
...
- Installing gplots ...                         OK [linked from cache]
- Installing ROCR ...                           OK [linked from cache]
- Installing Rtsne ...                          OK [built from source and cached in 23s]
- Installing scattermore ...                    OK [built from source and cached in 5.9s]
...
```

The question is:
Can I install only the version of the packages already available in the cache and avoid installing a newer version?
Is there a specific argument in `renv::install()` or a different `renv::` command?
Should I just copy the renv folder from an old project and use that one in the new project?
Does it make sense to copy only from the cache to avoid installation of multiple newer versions of dependencies packages?
Should I install only the version of the packages already available in the cache and avoid installing a newer version?

title: renv looks for specific library version instead of general one
description:
The problem is also visible here <https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1834> but in a different context.

Sticking with the `sodium` and `libsodium` mentioned in the liked issue.
On https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sodium/index.html the system requirements mention `libsodium (>= 1.0.3)` but I get the error

```R
libsodium.so.23: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

when `libsodium@1.0.19` is installed. Checking which `libsodium` version still has `libsodium.so.23` the web tells me `libsodium@1.0.18`. When I use this version the installation goes through.

I experience the same problem when e.g. installing `sf` which requires GDAL / PROJ. Detailed information are in the sf issue https://github.com/r-spatial/sf/issues/2360. Picking only the PROJ issue, they mentioned on https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sf/index.html that `PROJ (>= 4.8.0)` is required, but when installing with `PROJ 4.9.2` present I get

```sh
libproj.so.15: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

because this version comes with

```sh
libproj.a
libproj.so
libproj.so.9
libproj.so.9.1.0
```

updating to `PROJ 8.2.1` I get the same error because this version comes with

```sh
libproj.a
libproj.so
libproj.so.22
libproj.so.22.2.1
```

Only when searching online which PROJ version ships `libproj.so.15` and using that version the error goes away.
So I am wondering how I should know beforehand which system dependency versions are actually required and why `renv` picks the very specific version lib instead of the `.so` file (without the version), because obviously the package authors didn't specify such a narrow version requirement.

title: problem with renv parsing .qmd file when using shortcode in a R source block
description:
Take this example 

````markdown
---
title: test
format: html
---

Demoing how to write shortcode for including file: use 


```r 
{{{< include _demo.R >}}}
```

to include the content of `_content.qmd` inside this qmd source. 

````

This will give a warning about parsing 
````
WARNING: One or more problems were discovered while enumerating dependencies.

C:/Users/chris/Documents/DEV_R/renv/test.qmd
--------------------------------------------

ERROR 1: <text>:2:4: '<' inattendu(e)
1: 
2: {{{<
      ^

Please see `?renv::dependencies` for more information.
````

Looking into **renv** internal functions, I believe this is because there is a trailing space after `` ```r  `` and this will trigger the inline R pattern. 

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/84126c74d2e0d62212c06c50e3e8f2e3ef0ebf6e/R/dependencies.R#L936

This will match new line too, and so matched the raw source with class `r`

I wonder why not using your `md` pattern inline code `renv:::renv_knitr_patterns()$md$inline.code`, 
```r
> renv:::renv_knitr_patterns()$md$inline.code
[1] "(?<!(^|\n)``)`r[ #]([^`]+)\\s*`"
```

though I believe it would need to be updated to match knitr's internal one 
````r
knitr:::all_patterns$md$inline.code
[1] "(?<!(^``))(?<!(\n``))`r[ #]([^`]+)\\s*`"
````

I don't think you can do `(?<!(^|\n)``)`  - I got this issue when trying
````
'lookbehind assertion is not fixed length' at '(?<!(^| )``)`r[ #]([^`]+)\s*`'
````

title: `renv::install` from cellar regression
description:
For context my `R` environment is behind a firewall, so I don't have access to the outside internet. However, I do have access to a mirror of CRAN.

I use the very convenient `renv` cellar to store in-house packages as well as a handful of external packages that rely on external dependencies. For the latter, I have to do the build outside of the firewall and then place them in the cellar for later use.

___

What I found is that `renv::install` recognizes the package in my cellar, and says it will be installed from there. Then, for some reason it goes to CRAN and downloads the tarball from there and installs _that_ one, instead of mine in the cellar. This is a problem because my tarball has all the source dependencies bundled, per: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/reference/create_package_with_all_dependencies.html

```R
Sys.setenv(ARROW_S3="ON", ARROW_DEPENDENCY_SOURCE="BUNDLED", ARROW_OFFLINE_BUILD="true")
renv::install("arrow@15.0.1", repos = NULL, prompt = FALSE)
# - Package arrow [15.0.1] will be installed from the cellar.
# # Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
# - Downloading arrow from Repository ...         OK [4.2 Mb in 1.3s]
# Successfully downloaded 1 package in 4.5 seconds.
# 
# The following package(s) will be installed:
# - arrow [15.0.1]
# These packages will be installed into "/mnt/code/renv/library/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu".
# 
# # Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
# - Installing arrow ...                          OK [built from source and cached in 26m]
# Successfully installed 1 package in 26 minutes.
```

I know it says it was successful, but if you run `arrow::arrow_info()` I see that it did not install all the optional dependencies, like S3 support which is included in my bundle.

I attempted to prevent `renv` from accessing CRAN (my mirror):
```R
options(repos = NULL)
Sys.setenv(ARROW_S3="ON", ARROW_DEPENDENCY_SOURCE="BUNDLED", ARROW_OFFLINE_BUILD="true")
renv::install("arrow@15.0.1", repos = NULL, prompt = FALSE)
# - Package arrow [15.0.1] will be installed from the cellar.
# # Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
# Warning: failed to find source for 'arrow 15.0.1' in package repositories
# Error: failed to retrieve package 'arrow@15.0.1'
```

Another thing I tried to do was use the `renv` shim of `install.packages`. This used to work for me but had some odd behavior this time:
```R
install.packages(file.path(renv::paths$root(), "cellar", "arrow", "arrow_15.0.1.tar.gz"), repos = NULL, type = "source")
# or
install.packages("/mnt/imported/data/renv/cellar/arrow/arrow_15.0.1.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

# 15.
# stop(simpleError(message = message, call = e$call)) at remotes.R#57
# 14.
# h(simpleError(msg, call))
# 13.
# .handleSimpleError(function (e)
# {
# fmt <- "failed to resolve remote '%s'"
# prefix <- sprintf(fmt, spec) ...
# 12.
# stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.) at utils-format.R#3
# 11.
# stopf("failed to parse remote spec '%s'", spec) at remotes.R#324
# 10.
# renv_remotes_parse(spec) at remotes.R#71
# 9.
# renv_remotes_resolve_impl(spec, latest) at remotes.R#62
# 8.
# withCallingHandlers(renv_remotes_resolve_impl(spec, latest),
# error = error) at remotes.R#62
# 7.
# FUN(X[[i]], ...)
# 6.
# lapply(x, f, ...) at utils-map.R#57
# 5.
# map(packages, renv_remotes_resolve) at install.R#166
# 4.
# renv::install("/mnt/imported/data/renv/cellar/arrow/arrow_15.0.1.tar.gz",
# repos = NULL, type = "source")

I had a partial success by downgrading to `renv` 0.17.3 (this was arbitrary, I didn't try in-between version).

The issue here was that for some reason the package did not end up moving to my cache, it just installed directly to my project folder. 

Happy to try troubleshooting anything else.

description: I wondered whether the [recently introduced param `lock` in `install()`](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/41a4d4dbea1297a2f45ae1327321c8a043ffeb6a) could also be added to `update()`, allowing the `renv.lock` lockfile to be updated automatically after successful update of the requested packages. It would be be a convenient feature for users of renv's `"explicit"` [snapshot type](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/snapshot.html#snapshot-types).

title: should `init()` gitignore the project's `.Renviron` ?
description:
Let's imagine that a project wants to store secrets in a project-level `.Renviron` file as discussed [here](https://do4ds.com/chapters/sec1/1-3-data-access.html#env-vars). Are there any `renv` functions that gitignore the project-level `.Renviron` file so that the secrets it contains don't get commited by accident?

If there aren't any functions that do this as a file-system side-effect, would it make sense to do this on the user's behalf, perhaps through a safety-oriented default that can be changed by the user as needed (e.g., `renv::init(ignore_renviron = TRUE)`)?

To unpack this idea  bit more, I don't see any guardrails to prevent leaking secrets stored in a project-level `.Renviron`. Here's some pseudo-code for project setup steps that I could imagine folks would follow:

```
# instantiate a project
usethis::create_project("foo_bar_baz")

# set up renv
renv::init()

# set project-level secrets as environment variables while in the project session
usethis::edit_r_environ(scope = "project")

# remember to gitignore `.Renviron` but share secrets with team via some other safe means
# maybe run `usethis::edit_gitignore()` or directly editing `.gitignore`
# if secrets nevertheless get committed, panic and `git reset --hard HEAD`
```

title: Can pak be enabled with renv and still use the global package cache as an install source?
description:
## Intro

I'm setting up an R environment to be used in notebooks in a Databricks workspace. I have currently identified a workflow that enables persisting a global package cache so that libraries need not be installed from source every time a user spins up compute and starts working in an R Notebook. 

## Workflow
The workflow is loosely:
1. set up a directory and subdirectories in DBFS for the global package cache
2. one-time install of all relevant packages after setting requisite environment variables, calling `renv:init()`, `renv:install()`, and `renv::snapshot()`
3. in a separate notebook, setting relevant environment variables and calling `renv::restore()`

This works well enough to get around the build-from-source workflow, but I've encountered situations where `renv::restore()` might still take 10+ minutes to restore an environment from lockfile, even when it is simply copying packages. This might be a Databricks issue (?).

I also know that with `options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE)`, the restoration can be faster since it builds from source in parallel. This also takes about 10-15m.

## My Question
The core question I have is if `pak` can copy from a global package cache in parallel to set up the environment? At current, if it is enabled, it only rebuilds from source, and after having a look through the `renv` and `pak` documentation I haven't found a definitive answer.

Thanks for your help!

I am new to renv:: and think this sounds like it could be really useful for helping make our code more reproducible.

However, I've run into an issue that I don't know whether it is me or the code...

title: `renv_cache_init` assumes that the cache only consists of one path
description:
This part

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/be4dc4e387ca0f177d750d2418e7a0816a110a11/R/cache.R#L24-L31

assumes that the cache consists of at most one path. If there are multiple caches then you get an error:
```r
if (renv_path_within(cache, getwd())) {
  error: the condition has length > 1
```

[Here](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/compare/main...vandenman:renv:fix_multiple_cache_error) is a proposed solution. I'd be happy to open a PR, but I also noticed that the unit tests for multiple caches are skipped: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/be4dc4e387ca0f177d750d2418e7a0816a110a11/tests/testthat/test-cache.R#L230

Is there a particular reason for skipping these tests? I'd be happy to figure out what goes on there and fix them.

title: `upgrade` doesn't update `activate.R` in 1.0.5
description:
Hi @kevinushey, thanks as always for the amazing `renv` package! I tried using `renv::upgrade` to go from 1.0.4 to 1.0.5 this morning and encountered this issue:

```R
# no renv.lock

> renv::upgrade()
A new version of the renv package will be installed:

# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- renv   [* -> 1.0.5]

This project will use the newly-installed version of renv.

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing renv ...                           OK [linked from cache]
- Lockfile written to "/mnt/code/renv.lock".
- Updating activate script

Restarting R session...

renv 1.0.5 was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv 1.0.4.
- Use `renv::record("renv@1.0.5")` to record renv 1.0.5 in the lockfile.
- Use `renv::restore(packages = "renv")` to install renv 1.0.4 into the project library.
- Project '/mnt/code' loaded. [renv 1.0.5]
- The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.


# with renv.lock and status up to date

> renv::upgrade()
A new version of the renv package will be installed:

# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- renv   [1.0.4 -> 1.0.5]

This project will use the newly-installed version of renv.

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: y

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing renv ...                           OK [linked from cache]
- Lockfile written to "/mnt/code/renv.lock".
- Updating activate script

Restarting R session...

# at this point I received this RStudio error/popup/modal
# (Error: Save File) Error occurred during transmission (OK)

renv 1.0.5 was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv 1.0.4.
- Use `renv::record("renv@1.0.5")` to record renv 1.0.5 in the lockfile.
- Use `renv::restore(packages = "renv")` to install renv 1.0.4 into the project library.
- Project '/mnt/code' loaded. [renv 1.0.5]
```

The fix was very simple. I just ran `renv::activate()` and it then changed the one line in `renv/activate.R` to reflect the new version number. Then I ran `renv::snapshot()` to cleanup the `renv` record, but this latter behavior is not new to 1.0.5, I've always needed to do that.

title: Use a package within .Rprofile ?
description:
Hello,
I'm using the `box` package in most of my projects along with `testthat`and `covr` packages in CI/CD workflows. To make these work together, it's very convenient to have absolute file paths when using `box::use`, this is easily done with the help of `here::here()`and this can be set with an option.

As result my `.Rprofile` looks like this :
```
source("renv/activate.R")
options(box.path = here::here())
```

`here` is being listed by `renv::dependencies()` and hence is in my lock file.

My issue is when I try to `renv::restore(clean = TRUE)` in a workflow. My basic understanding (still onboarding with `renv`...) is that it looks like it's not yet restored the library and reads the `.Rprofile` file first, hence not finding the package, resulting in this error :
```
# Bootstrapping renv 1.0.3 ---------------------------------------------------
- Downloading renv ... OK
- Installing renv  ... OK

- One or more packages recorded in the lockfile are not installed.
- Use `renv::status()` for more details.
Error: Error in loadNamespace(x) : there is no package called ‘here’
Calls: options ... loadNamespace -> withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> doWithOneRestart
Execution halted
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```

If I remove the options line from my `.Rprofile` file, it restores successfully.

Is there a trick of some sort to make this work ? 
One obvious alternative solution would be to not set the option but instead do something like
`box::use(here::here("folder", "file"))` every time I use `box::use` ? I'm of course not fond of this.

title: GDAL cannot be found when using {renv} on Mac
description:
Hi {renv} folks - I am trying to trace an issue with using packages like {terra} and {raster} for a project using {renv} across Windows and Mac. On the windows side, everything works great. But on my M2 MacBook Pro (RStudio, {renv}, other packages, and OS up to date), the same code does not run. title: Ignore comparing package version number at R start
description:
Hello,
Is it possible to hide/ignore that the project is out of sync? I receive the following message at the start of R.
```
The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.
```
This is okay. However, when working in parallel at an HPC, the message is repeated on the screen; e.g.:
```
.NCores <- 50
c1 <- snow::makeSOCKcluster(.NCores)
future::plan(cluster, workers = c1, gc = TRUE)
# here the message appears 50 times, for each core
```

Is it possible to ignore this warning using something like `options()`? 

Alternatively is it possible to disable comparing between versions of installed packages and their versions on the lock file at R startup altogether (this may make R start faster especially if there are many packages installed in the project)? 

Thanks

title: Result of `renv::install(lock = TRUE)` differs from `renv::install(lock = FALSE); renv::snapshot()`
description:
I'm using renv with its `"explicit"` [snapshot type](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html#snapshot-type) and just tested the new `lock` argument for `renv::install()` introduced in renv 1.0.4.

I noticed that when I install a new package[^rsvg] using

```r
renv::install("rsvg", lock = TRUE)
```

renv writes the following lines to my project's `renv.lock`:

```json
    "rsvg": {
      "Package": "rsvg",
      "Version": "2.6.0",
      "OS_type": null,
      "NeedsCompilation": "yes",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Path": "/home/salim/.cache/R/renv/cache/v5/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/rsvg/2.6.0/7aaf92c4adddc8a85696ae7f0123a725/rsvg"
    },
```

When installing the same package using

```r
renv::install("rsvg", lock = FALSE)
renv::snapshot()
```

OTOH, renv writes these lines to the `renv.lock`:

```json
    "rsvg": {
      "Package": "rsvg",
      "Version": "2.6.0",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "RSPM",
      "Hash": "7aaf92c4adddc8a85696ae7f0123a725"
    },
```

I guess this isn't supposed to be the intended behaviour, no?

I was first delighted by the new `lock` argument since it'd give a better UX for renv's explicit snapshot type, but I really don't wanna write local filesystem paths to an renv project's lock file shared with others...

[^rsvg]: For the sake of simplicity, I use [rsvg](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rsvg/index.html) here, a package without any further R package dependencies. In both cases, `rsvg` was added to the project's `DESCRIPTION` file before installing it.

title: renv.lock git conflict
description:
I abandoned renv a while ago and wrote a more streamlined replacement that we use in the lab, but periodically check in on the project to see what's new.

A major reason for the change was version controlling the single renv.lock across multiple users.  Turns out it was very frequently in conflict, meaning the first thing you had to do when starting work on a project was deal with that.  To avoid that mess, we would just avoid updating the lock file and/or package library which of course defeats the purpose.

The solution which was very simple and works very well is for each user to have their own lock file:  <user>.renv.lock.   Then you can always keep yours updated and adopt some or all of another user's package library at will.

I would recommend this change to renv.  It can probably be implemented with a few non-breaking changes to your code.

Also, although I understand some of the advantages, I find JSON offensive to read.  Occasionally this is necessary to do so we keep the minimum essential data in our version of the lock file as a .tsv.

title: FR: make recovering from OS upgrades less painful by identifying when library was built under a different OS
description:
## Description
In the case where a team is undergoing an OS upgrade, the project-level library established via `renv` must be rebuilt. Currently, there is not an easy way for users to know that their library was built under a different OS.

To recover from an OS upgrade, a user will need to rebuild the cache for every renv project using a script similar to: 

```R 
# Delete the existing libraries
unlink("renv/library", recursive=TRUE)

# Restart R session
.rs.restartR()

# Re-install libraries
renv::restore(rebuild = TRUE)

```

This is not well-documented, requires a user to perform this individually for every project, and its not possible to inspect a renv project to determine if it has been rebuilt to the new OS or not.


## Suggested Approach
Similar to how `renv::status()` will notify if a lockfile was built per a different version of R, `renv::status()` should identify if the library cache was built against a different OS.  


## Impact
This work becomes very important as RHEL7 reaches EOL. We are coaching a large number of customers through OS upgrades and the renv rebuild actions put a significant burden on users.

title: `renv::restore()` fails for packages hosted on a GitHub Enterprise server when `gitcreds` is installed
description:
## Steps to recreate the issue

```r
renv::install(c("gitcreds", "remotes"))
remotes::install_github(repo = "REPO/PACKAGE",  host = "GHE_SERVER_URL/api/v3")
renv::snapshot(type="all")
renv::rebuild("PACKAGE")
```

This fails with an error like:

```
Error: error downloading 'https://GHE_SERVER_URL/api/v3/repos/REPO/PACKAGE/tarball/COMMIT_SHA' [curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 401]
```

Apologies that I can't give a real GHE server to make this fully reproducible.

However if `gitcreds` is not installed it works.

## Possible Solution

It looks like the call to `gitcreds::gitcreds_get()` is always using the default github.com url:

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/e7c23eae4b8fd726391607c2fa5ac854c88b6397/R/download.R#L546-L548

Is there a way to pass down the `RemoteHost` in `renv.lock` to give `gitcreds` a shot at finding the right PAT?

Alternatively, is there a way to shut off authenticating altogether which will be fine as long as I'm using public repos?

title: Dependency not checked when filenames only differ in their extension
description:
Hi Kevin,

With two similarly named files in a project, say filename.Rmd and filename.R, renv::dependencies() (and hence renv::status()) appears to fail to notice the file with the ".R" extension. Contributing factors may have been that the filename.R used to be called something else, and at some point the code in filename.R had an error in it. So the full sequence of steps to get into trouble and then recover in my case was:

1. install and renv sync various packages successfully into filename.Rmd and somethingelse.R.
2. rename somethingelse.R to filename.R and then add package B to filename.R and leave filename.R with a code error
3. renv::status() reports that package A (used in filename.R) is installed and recorded but not used, and says nothing about package B (used in filename.R, installed, and not recorded).  
4. guess this might be a filename clash issue and rename filename.R to filename2.R
5. renv now reports code error in filename2.R and still reports renv status as above
6. fix code error in filename2.R. renv::status now reports everything as expected: package A is not mentioned (because it is installed, recorded and used), and package B is installed, used and not recorded. renv::snapshot and all is well.

I have not reproduced this behaviour without the contributing factors, but could do so if that would help.

Kind regards,
Alex

title: Create a mechanism for easily "correcting" a package installation
description:
Before `restore()` is complete, I often run into issues with environment restoration on new computers.

The easiest resolution is often to install a new version of troublesome packages, or install them from a new location (i.e. RSPM instead of GitHub, etc.).

However, then it is tricky to update the `renv.lock` file so that the "successful" package installation is used (and not discarded on the next `restore()`).

The natural way a user might want to do this is as an argument to install, e.g. an argument `lock=TRUE` to suggest that the install should immediately be written to the lockfile (with any upgraded / installed dependencies).

```
renv::install("package", lock=TRUE)
```

This is possible today:

```
renv::snapshot(packages="package", update=TRUE)
```

However, it uses the `snapshot()` verb, which is counter-intuitive, because I am thinking about _correcting_ an install / the lockfile, not creating a new lockfile.

title: Rstudio namespace polluting loaded renv
description:
Hi all,

First off, thank you for developing such an excellent tool.

I work with a data science team and we've have been setting up a system of shared renv projects that can be loaded for reproducibility when running R scripts and markdown (Rmd) files from Rstudio. At the top of these files, we want to load an renv project from our shared filesystem so the scripts can executed consistently by anyone on the team.

My team has been hitting problems related to packages are getting loaded into the global namespace when opening files prior to loading our renv projects. This isn't unexpected, and is actually a [known behavior](https://community.rstudio.com/t/prevent-rstudio-from-loading-namespaces-at-startup/158442), but these namespace packages are persisting after loading an renv project with `renv::load`. This leads to package version mismatches that result in errors, since packages in the default library may conflict with versions in the renv.

Here are some steps to reproduce the issue:
- Have a version of a package installed in the default package library, e.g. `rmarkdown@2.22`
- Create an renv project containing a different version of that package, e.g. `rmarkdown@2.25`
- Create a basic Rmd file with the following contents
````
```{r include=True}
renv::load(<path to renv project>)
library(rmarkdown)
sessionInfo()
```
````
- Start a new session in Rstudio
- Open the the Rmd created above. Prior to executing the Rmd file, note how packages are loaded into the "loaded via a namespace (and not attached)" section when running `sessionInfo()`
- Finally, execute the Rmd file. Note how the `sessionInfo()` output shows how the default package is still in the namespace, in this case `rmarkdown@2.22`. I would expect it to be the version from the renv project, specifically `rmarkdown@2.25`

Further, running `packageVersion('rmarkdown')` after loading the renv project will also return `"2.22"`.

To me, this behavior is not expected. We've worked around it by turning off Rstudio's diagnostics tools that run when a file is opened and thus preventing those packages from getting into the namespace prior to the renv load, but that's obviously not ideal because we miss out on features like syntax checking in Rstudio.

On the surface, the issue looks similar to this recently closed one: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1671

However, I tried with the development version of renv as instructed in the issue above (installed with `renv::install("rstudio/renv")`) and am still hitting the namespace collision.

Am I misunderstanding the role of `renv::load`? Or do you expect the prior namespace to be retained when loading an renv project?

I've attached an extensive diagnostic log from a real-world example of this procedure. Please not that I had to redact some file paths and names.

[renv_namespace_diagnostics.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/14117905/renv_namespace_diagnostics.txt)

Thanks!

title: Support {R} denoting R code chunks
description:
Currently, `renv` doesn't support using `{R}` to denote R code chunks. This can cause inconsistent behavior since `rmarkdown` and RStudio both see those as valid R code chunks and correctly interpret and run them using R. The outcome of this behavior is that `library` statements made in these  `{R}` blocks are not correctly parsed by `renv::dependencies()`, causing eventual failures during publishing and reproducibility checks since those package details will not be captured in the `renv.lock` file. This also results in these packages not being updated when `renv::update()` is run. 

At least these places need updating:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ae73cfcde5b9799f807634e14f780516f1193088/R/dependencies.R#L817
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ae73cfcde5b9799f807634e14f780516f1193088/R/dependencies.R#L908

Thanks!

title: Cannot `R CMD build` renv-based package having vignettes
description:
Hi. Thank you for your hard work on this incredibly useful package!

I've been trying to run `R CMD build <pkg>` command on a package having some vignettes within.
Every time the command fails on the vignette building step with the following error (R@4.3.1 - but for lower version it's the same, renv@1.0.3):

```
$ R CMD build .
* checking for file ‘./DESCRIPTION’ ... OK
* preparing ‘checkpkg’:
* checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... OK
* installing the package to build vignettes
      -----------------------------------
# Bootstrapping renv 1.0.3 ---------------------------------------------------
- Downloading renv ... OK
- Installing renv  ... OK

- None of the packages recorded in the lockfile are currently installed.
ERROR: dependency ‘magrittr’ is not available for package ‘checkpkg’
* removing ‘/tmp/RtmpNCKMdZ/Rinst99e0500257ef/checkpkg’
      -----------------------------------
ERROR: package installation failed
```

The missing `magrittr package`:
- is included in Imports section of DESCRIPTION file,
- is installed and added via `renv::snapshot` to renv.lock file.

After short investigation I found the reason is `hash` added to the project library which is based on its path.
Because of that:
1. The original project library is `<lib-path>/project-<hash1>/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`
2. When `R CMD build <project>` is run, the project is copied to `/tmp/<tmp-path>`.
3. Further commands are run from within `/tmp/<tmp-path>`. Because of different project path this line https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/inst/resources/activate.R#L766 will compute different hash, so the project library becomes `<lib-path>/project-<hash2>/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu` where none of the dependencies is installed.

We can easily overcome the issue by setting up `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT_ASIS=TRUE` (see: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/inst/resources/activate.R#L761) in order to stop adding the hash to the library, but I guess this is not expected setup.

Could you please take a look at the issue? Thank you.

title: Undefined `catch` function in `activate.R`
description:
# Description

Hello 👋 . I've noticed a strange error when trying to bootstrap renv from a custom repo.

When renv attempts to bootstap itself during start up, it first does some checks to determine which repo it should use. I have a custom repo defined in `renv.lock`, and the default CRAN URL doesn't work on our company network. In `activate.R` the `renv_json_read` function references a `catch` function which doesn't seem to be defined at this point. It looks like this function comes from `R/utils.R`, but at this point during the bootstrap, that isn't available.

Consequently, the bootstrap process fails. I'm able to workaround by setting `renv.repos.cran`, so that the code path never touches the undefined `catch`, but it seems like this is a bug that prevents bootstrapping against a non-standard repo defined in the lock file (if you don't have access to CRAN!).

I guess the fix could be to just use a standard `tryCatch` in `activate.R` instead 🤷 ... Actually, I just tried replacing it with `tryCatch(..., error = identity)`, and now it's complaining that the `read` function is also undefined (another one from `R/utils.R`). Would it be sufficient to copy the definition to `activate.R`?

title: renv::status() displaying incomplete information about inconsistencies
description:
When I have some packages that are installed but not recorded, and some other packages that are installed AND recorded but an inconsistent version, renv::status() is only showing me the former and not displaying the latter.

# Reprex

Create a directory with `script.R`:
```
library(data.table) 
print(data.table(foo = 1:3, bar = 4:6))
```

In the directory, run:
```
% R
> renv::init()
- Linking packages into the project library ... Done!
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- data.table   [* -> 1.14.8]
- renv         [* -> 1.0.3]

The version of R recorded in the lockfile will be updated:
- R            [* -> 4.2.3]

- Lockfile written to "~/scratchpad/renv-masking-reprex/renv.lock".
- renv activated -- please restart the R session.
[ctrl-D]
% R
> renv::install("data.table@1.14.6")
[installs]
> renv::status()
```

As expected:

```
The following package(s) are out of sync [lockfile -> library]:
# CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
- data.table   [1.14.8 -> 1.14.6]
See ?renv::status() for advice on resolving these issues.
```

Now, edit script.R:
```
library(data.table)
print(data.table(foo = 1:3, bar = 4:6))
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy, colour = class)) + geom_point()
```

```
% R
> renv::status()
The following package(s) are missing:

 package installed recorded used
 ggplot2 n         n        y   

See ?renv::status() for advice on resolving these issues.
```

No information is given about data.table's discrepancy anymore.

This can lead to some unexpected behavior if you run `renv::restore()` or `renv::snapshot()` in a more realistic scenario, expecting it only to affect packages listed by `renv::status()`. (Thankfully, those functions will prompt you with the full list of things they're about to change, so a keen eye will reveal what's going on.)

title: renv fails when HTTPUserAgent is improperly set
description:
I encountered this issue when using the rstudio binary builds of R on Debian unstable, which is not an officially supported platform. As such this is a bit niche and might not be worth addressing.

The result is the equivalent of running `options(HTTPUserAgent = character(0))` (see rstudio/r-builds#196 for background).

In this case, every attempt to run `install()` with renv 1.0.3 fails with:

``` r
options(HTTPUserAgent = character(0))
renv::install("tidyverse")
#> Error in if (!grepl("renv", agent)) {: argument is of length zero
```

<sup>Created on 2024-01-09 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

This is because of this internal function:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/de3af61f7e1d69f0f8320ec7251a7340e740f233/R/http.R#L2-L5

The fix could be to set `agent` to NULL if it is equal to `character(0)`. However, feel free to close this since it's probably not a likely scenario that others will run into unless they are using the rstudio R binaries on Debian testing or unstable.

title: `renv` does not respect enterprise or user repository configuration
description:
## Description

Depending on how `renv` is started in a project, it overrides the repository configuration in different ways by modifying the named `CRAN` repository and/or removing all other configured repositories. This happens in both an enterprise environment where a `repos.conf` or `rsession.conf` file is used as well as a local environment where the Package Management settings pane in RStudio is used. The problem appears in all tested versions of R on a variety of operating systems. Only renv 1.0.3 was tested. Below is documentation of the problem across two different enterprise environments. While testing, it was determined that using `renv` inside of a `reprex::reprex()` call did not reproduce these results.

```{bash}

#> # R Session Configuration File
#> # repository
#> r-cran-repos=https://rspm.example.com/prod-cran/__linux__/jammy/latest/

options("repos")
#> $repos

#>                                     Example

#> attr(,"RStudio")
#> [1] TRUE

title: Bootstrapping fails when `renv` is installed via `actions/setup-r-dependencies`
description:
### Background

Our testing setup in [Rhino](https://github.com/Appsilon/rhino) includes a GitHub Actions workflow which initializes a `renv` project and pushes it to a branch. When we subsequently try to run this project, `renv` fails to bootstrap (install itself). The problem seems to stem from the fact that we install `renv` via `actions/setup-r-dependencies` in our workflow.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a fresh GitHub repository and push a `.github/workflows/renv-test.yml` file with content as follows:

```yml
on: push
jobs:
  main:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install R
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          # Speeds up the workflow; does not affect the results.
          # Caching (enabled by default) seems to have no effect either.
          use-public-rspm: true

      - name: Install renv (broken)
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2
        with:
          packages: renv

      # - name: Install renv (working)
      #   shell: Rscript {0}
      #   run: install.packages("renv")

      - name: Init renv
        shell: Rscript {0}
        run: renv::init()

      - name: Debug
        run: head renv/activate.R

      - name: Force renv bootstrap
        run: rm -r renv/library

      - name: Say hi
        shell: Rscript {0}
        run: message("Hi!")
```

### Problem

The "Say hi" step fails with the following output:

```
# Bootstrapping renv 1.0.3 [sha: 1.0.3] --------------------------------------
- Downloading renv ... FAILED
Error: Error in h(simpleError(msg, call)) : failed to download:
All download methods failed
Calls: source ... bootstrap -> withCallingHandlers -> renv_bootstrap_download
Execution halted
Error: Process completed with exit code 1.
```

### Expected behavior

After removing `renv/library`, `renv` should bootstrap without issues when running `Rscript` in the "Say hi" step and the whole workflow should succeed.

### Notes

Installing `renv` with `install.packages()` instead of `actions/setup-r-dependencies` resolves the problem. It can be tested by uncommenting the "Install renv (working)" step.

The "Debug" step gives us a hint to the cause of the issue. After installation with `actions/setup-r-dependencies` the `renv/activate.R` file starts with:
```
attr(version, "sha") <- "1.0.3"
```
Setting the attribute to `NULL` instead (as happens when using `install.packages()`) fixes the problem:
```
attr(version, "sha") <- NULL
```

Our workflow uses a fixed version (v2) of `actions/setup-r-dependencies` and the latest CRAN version of `renv`. It stopped working somewhere between 2023-07-06 (last successful run) and 2023-07-24 (first failure) without any relevant changes in the repo. This led me to believe that some `renv` update introduced the problem and that's why I decided to report it here and not in `r-lib/actions` repo.

title: Feature request: Make renv::status() check configurabe for dev dependencies
description:
Hey everyone,

In my workflow, I snapshot development dependencies into the lockfile using `renv::snapshot(type = "explicit, dev = TRUE)`. Whenever I open the project, I get the message, that the project is out of sync. I think this is because `renv::status()` shows that there are several packages that are installed and recorded but not used, as expected. 
When I run `renv::status(dev = TRUE)` , it correctly returns that the lockfile is up to date.

Would it be a possibility to make the default for the `dev` argument of `renv::status()` configurable, similar to what I can do with the settings for `snapshot.type`? This could prevent quite some confusion, as e.g. code reviewers or colleagues do not necessarily immediately know why the message is shown.

Reprex:
``` r
devtools::create("newpackage", open = TRUE)
renv::init(bare = TRUE)
renv::install("usethis", prompt = FALSE)
usethis::use_package("usethis", type = "Suggests")
renv::snapshot(type = "explicit", dev = TRUE, prompt = FALSE)
renv::status()
#> The following package(s) are in an inconsistent state:
#> ...
renv::status(dev = TRUE)
#> No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

Maybe related to #1019 

Thank for the consideration!
Martin

title: "Do you want to proceed" prompt for installing BiocManager after activation doesn't render properly in Rstudio
description: ## Steps to reproduce 1. Create a directory, e.g. `renv_bioc_reprex` 2. Create the following files in that directory: `renv_bioc_reprex/script.R`: ``` x <- data.frame(x=1:5, y=factor(letters[1:5], levels=letters[1:8]), row.names=letters[1:5]) y <- data.frame(z=3:7, y=factor(letters[3:7], levels=letters[1:8]), row.names=letters[3:7]) BiocGenerics::combine(x,y) ``` `renv.lock`: ``` { "R": { "Version": "4.2.2", "Repositories": [ { "Name": "CRAN", "URL": "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest" } ] }, "Bioconductor": { "Version": "3.16" }, "Packages": { "BiocGenerics": { "Package": "BiocGenerics", "Version": "0.44.0", "Source": "Bioconductor", "Requirements": [ "R", "graphics", "methods", "stats", "utils" ], "Hash": "0de19224c2cd94f48fbc0d0bc663ce3b" }, "BiocManager": { "Package": "BiocManager", "Version": "1.30.19", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Requirements": [ "utils" ], "Hash": "726b3bc83ff8e0c35c7efdb74a462b0d" }, "BiocVersion": { "Package": "BiocVersion", "Version": "3.16.0", "Source": "Bioconductor", "Requirements": [ "R" ], "Hash": "44c5824508b9a10e52dbb505c34fa880" }, "renv": { "Package": "renv", "Version": "1.0.3", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Requirements": [ "utils" ], "Hash": "41b847654f567341725473431dd0d5ab" } } } ``` (this was generated by simply running `renv::init()`, but the bug happens when activating, not init-ing) 3. Create and open an Rstudio project in that directory (if in a setup affected by https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/13922) 4. In Rstudio, run `renv::activate()` 5. See expected messages that BiocManager will be installed, followed by what looks like the standard command prompt. 6. Attempt to run any R command--it turns out that a "Y" or "N" is expected, but the prompt for such only appears *after* trying to run a command. (See screenshots below.) ## Repro 1 ### System details - MacOS Sonoma 14.0 (23A344) - RStudio Desktop 2023.09.1+494 - renv 1.0.3 - R 4.2.3 or 4.3.1 ## Repro 2 ### System details - Linux CentOS 7 - RStudio Server 2022.12.0 build 353 - renv 1.0.3 - R 4.2.2 ![renv-bug-1](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/assets/106110177/c3264d57-7c8c-4682-bdce-a86bd1ede7c2) ![renv-bug-2](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/assets/106110177/94c8a2a8-b343-4048-a518-6f1baf8de0bb)

title: Packages needing compilation fail within an renv project, but succeed outside of one.
description:
I've cloned an Rproject that uses renv and it is failing to restore a package (cluster) due to not locating gcc and gfortran.

I've done diagnostics and have found that in Rstudio with the renv project loaded, Sys.which("gfortran") gives different results than outside of an renv project.

Outside renv: "/opt/homebrew/bin/gfortran" (which is correct, and matches the location when I check which gfortran in terminal. Inside the renv project, I get an empty string: ""

How is renv able to affect my system paths like this? Per the help for Sys.which(), "This is an interface to the system command which". Or where in the Rproj/renv settings are paths set that overrule system paths?

title: Package installation fails at dependency level when using an older PPM CRAN snapshot
description:
As of {renv} 1.0.0, following `renv::init()` with `restart = FALSE`, `renv::install()` tries to pull more recent versions of dependencies that are not available in the snapshot.
I will caveat this by stating that I am having trouble reproducing this error 100% of the time, but thought it would be worth reporting. When it does occur, it seems that the correct version of the requested package is retrieved, but the failure is on the dependencies. Specifically, {renv} will attempt to pull a more recent version of a dependency than is available in the snapshot (e.g. {cli} 3.6.1 instead of 3.6.0 in the example below). 

example code:

```r
options(repos = c("CRAN" = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2023-03-01"))
renv::init( 
  bare = TRUE,
  restart = FALSE
)
renv::install("purrr")
```

results in: 
```
# Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
- Downloading purrr from CRAN ...               OK [file is up to date]
Warning: failed to find binary for 'cli 3.6.1' in package repositories
Warning: failed to find source for 'cli 3.6.1' in package repositories
Error: failed to retrieve package 'cli@3.6.1'
```
I do have {cli} 3.6.1 installed to my regular R library outside of {renv}, so my best guess is that {renv} may be looking there for version information. If I downgrade that to {cli} 3.6.0, then I get a failure later on for {vctrs}, when it's looking for 0.6.3 (matching my regular R library) but snapshot version is 0.5.2.

Ideally I can keep using `restart=FALSE` as part of our use case. Could this be a bug or is there a setting that could be used to help counter this behavior?

Thanks very much in advance for any help you can provide!

title: user profile is ignored if autoloader is disabled
description:
I noticed that if autoloader is disabled the user profile `~/.Rprofile` is not sourced even if `RENV_CONFIG_USER_PROFILE` is set to `TRUE`.

## Steps to reproduce this:
1. Create `~/.Rprofile` with the following line: `cat("~/.Rprofile is executed\n")`
2. Add the following lines to `~/.Renviron`:
```
RENV_CONFIG_USER_PROFILE=TRUE
RENV_CONFIG_AUTOLOADER_ENABLED=FALSE
```
3. Create renv in an empty folder:
```
R -e "renv::init()"
```
4. Launch R


## Expected result
`~/.Rprofile is executed` in the stdout

## Actual result
`~/.Rprofile` is ignored

title: Should `install()` respect the `ignored.packages` setting?
description:
I am setting [`ignored.packages`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html#ignored-packages) to make ‘renv’ ignore a package that’s used in a project. The reason is that this package gets loaded (from the global library) *before* the renv gets activated (consequently, the package is only referred to in the project’s `.Rprofile`, nowhere else).

This seems to work insofar as `renv::status()` and `renv::snapshot()` ignore that package.

However, `renv::dependencies()` still lists it, and `renv::install()` still attempts to install it. For me, this seems to defeat the purpose of the setting. Is this an oversight, or is this working as intended?

If so, is there a way of making ‘renv’ *truly* ignore a package, and not attempt to install it?

 (`renv::settings$ignored.packages()` includes the package, so it was definitely set correctly.)

title: Default snapshotting behaviour breaks RStudio's `devtools::load_all()` keyboard shortcut
description:
Within a package development environment, {renv} does not typically snapshot a package like {devtools}. Unfortunately, this seems to break RStudio's `devtools::load_all()` keyboard shortcut (i.e. nothing happens). I was able to fix the problem with the following steps,

1. Configure renv to capture all packages in the project library, `renv::settings$snapshot.type("all")`
2. Snapshot packages, `renv::snapshot()`
3. Restart R session

A month or so ago I opened a related issue under the rstudio/rstudio repo, https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/13727.

title: [BUG] `renv::restore()` fails under v1.0.3 but is successful using v0.17.3
description: I am running `renv::restore()` as part of the following `docker_build` command: `docker build -f Dockerfile_base --progress=plain -t golem.test.project_base .` where `Dockerfile_base` is: ``` FROM rocker/verse:4.2.2 RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/R/etc/ /usr/lib/R/etc/ RUN echo "options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE, repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cran.rstudio.com/'), download.file.method = 'libcurl', Ncpus = 4)" | tee /usr/local/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site | tee /usr/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site RUN R -e 'install.packages(c("renv","remotes"))' COPY renv.lock renv.lock RUN R -e 'renv::restore()' ``` this results in the following error: I have attempted fix by changing `Dockerfile_base` to force an install of renv version 0.17.3 to: ``` FROM rocker/verse:4.2.2 RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/R/etc/ /usr/lib/R/etc/ RUN echo "options(renv.config.pak.enabled = TRUE, repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cran.rstudio.com/'), download.file.method = 'libcurl', Ncpus = 4)" | tee /usr/local/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site | tee /usr/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site RUN R -e 'install.packages("remotes")' RUN R -e 'remotes::install_version("renv", version = "0.17.3")' COPY renv.lock renv.lock RUN R -e 'renv::restore()' ``` which results in a successful build when using the `docker build` command. I believe this might relate to [this bug](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/issues/330) and is affecting [golem package](https://github.com/ThinkR-open/dockerfiler/issues/66) upstream. I have attached my `renv.lock` file as [renv.lock.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/13183016/renv.lock.txt) so that i can upload it here. Thank you for any help. Please let me know if any addition information is needed.
