title: Failing to install old package versions on Windows with MitM proxy gives unhelpful error message
description:
See #1624

Trying to install an old package on such a system does not give a helpful error message:

```r
renv::install("lintr@2.0.1")
#> # Downloading packages -----------------------------------------------
#> Warning: failed to find binary for 'lintr 2.0.1' in package repositories
#> Warning: failed to find source for 'lintr 2.0.1' in package repositories
#> Error: failed to retrieve package 'lintr@2.0.1'
```

(The `"repos"` option is set to `"https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2023-10-05"`, if that matters. Unfortunately I don't have Windows with MitM proxy handy any more, so I cant try out a more minimal version of this.)

Tracing this through the debugger ultimately shows that the following fails:
```r
renv:::renv_download_impl(
  url = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2023-10-05/src/contrib/Archive/lintr/lintr_2.0.1.tar.gz",
  destfile = "test.txt", type = NULL, request = "HEAD", headers = character(0))
#> <simpleWarning: curl: (35) schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: Unknown error (0x80092012) - Die Sperrfunktion konnte keine Sperrpr�fung f�r das Zertifikat durchf�hren.>
```

Running `C:\Windows\System32\curl.exe "https://google.com"` gives the same error message, so this is ultimately because the system's `curl` is broken here.

#1624 already solved this problem, and the workaround is already built into `renv`:
```r
Sys.setenv("R_LIBCURL_SSL_REVOKE_BEST_EFFORT" = "T")
```
It would be helpful if the error message could inform the user about this option here; I only found this option by going through the source code.

It would be even nicer if downloading source-versions of old packages could work in a more robust way, maybe using a different download method as fallback? Downloading up-to-date packages also seems to work with no issues, after all.

title: Request: function to compare lockfiles
description:
I would be interested in having a function that would be able to take two lockfiles and present a report of packages that are added, removed, upgraded, and downgraded. 

I _believe_ that the functionality exists in `renv::snapshot()` here:

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/4b11818ca81897f10bf1def73db6b69c9fd1af0f/R/snapshot.R#L226-L228

My motivation for this is that I currently use [`capture.output()` on `renv::snapshot()`](https://github.com/carpentries/vise/blob/90b34c1b5f916789b82522b9f53f9306a74b28e2/R/update.R#L44-L65) to extract the report that's generated from the above code. It would be really nice if I could 
do away with that step and just compare two lockfiles.

I could imagine something like this:

```r
lock1 <- renv::lockfile_read("/path/to/first/lockfile")
lock2 <- renv::lockfile_read("/path/to/second/lockfile")
renv::lockfile_diff(lock1, lock2)
```

title: Renv installation fails with dependency only available in Archive
description:
Hello! Thanks for the great package 🎉 

## Description of Issue

I'm looking for some guidance on how `renv` handles dependencies stored in the archive of a repo. Specifically we are using Artifactory, and have a package `ABC` that isn't available at `/src/contrib` on the repo, it's only available at `/src/contrib/Archive`. This file doesn't appear in the `PACKAGES` index for the repo.

From checking through the `renv` source, it seems that `renv` uses this `PACKAGES` index exclusively to determine what is available on the repo. This means that `renv::install("ABC", repos="artifactory.example.com/repo")` fails with `Error: package 'ABC' is not available`.

If I do `renv::install("ABC@0.1.2", repos="artifactory.example.com/repo")` (i.e. requesting the specific version that is in the archive. Then this succeeds. From checking the source, this seems to be because specific version installations elicit an additional `renv` heuristic check in the `/Archive` location.

So that's good, that we can explicitly fetch the package. However, what I don't know how to handle is when I try to install a package `MainPackage` that depends on the archived package `ABC`. In this situation, when I run `renv::install("MainPackage", repos="artifactory.example.com/repo")`, `renv` goes to fetch the package dependencies and in the end errors with `Error: package 'ABC' is not available`.

It looks to me that during the dependency fetching, `renv` is only consulting the `PACKAGES` index, and therefore doesn't know that the `ABC` package is available in the archive.

## Questions

1. Is this a bug with our repo? i.e. Should the archived package appear in the `PACKAGES` index somehow? (I should note that the same package is available on public CRAN, and on CRAN it also doesn't appear in the `PACKAGES` index, which makes me think that this is not the case. However, I'm relatively new to the R eco system, so def wouldn't put it past myself simply having completely the wrong end of the stick about how these things _should_ be working!)
2. Should `renv` be looking further afield to determine the available packages on a repo? I've noticed while exploring this issue that cranlike repos provide an `archive.rds` file available at `/src/contrib/Meta/archive.rds`, should `renv` also consult this and add the data to its list of index DB's when determining what packages are available?
3. If the answer to 2 is "no", then should `renv` also be performing its own archive heuristic check (i.e. looking in `/Archive`) for packages that don't appear in it's index DB's?

Thank you for any insight you can shed on this 🙏 . `renv` is great!

How to init a fully isolated renv?
description:

What I want is a fully isolated renv that does not see the system-level installed libraries. How does one do that? title: question on renv 0.12.5 using default user library as local package source
description:
I have a situation where two users are trying to both do a renv::restore(clean=TRUE) having wiped out their renv cache and doing this in a fresh git clone. For one user, their renv::restore works and all the lines say "OK [built from source]" but for the other user, they have occasional lines of "OK [copied local binary]" and end up with weird Rcpp linking issues.

Details are lme4@1.1-25 which has a copied local binary of minqa@1.2.4 and ends up with the error of 

function 'Rcpp_precious_remove' not provided by package 'Rcpp'

which it is not in Rcpp@1.0.5

Literally everything _SEEMS_ the same for these two users - except however their DEFAULT library which would be under ~/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.6/

I'm wondering if potentially (based on the comments on https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/636) if potentially renv is finding a compatible (meaning package+version) if minqa there for one user and not the other and for one it copies it over and for the other it builds from source.

That is, does renv 0.12.5 make use of the default user library?

description:
Hello, 

I have looked at the other Azure DevOps issues (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues?q=DevOps) and I am still unable to resolve my specific issue. Most of the other threads don't show exactly how people were able to resolve their problem.  

So here is what I have at the moment. In my renv.lock file the entry gets generated for our internal package like the below. 

```

title: `renv` does not detect Red Hat 9 as compatible with `rhel9` binaries served by Posit Package Manager
description:
`renv`'s function `renv_ppm_platform` does not properly detect Red Hat 9 in a manner compatible with Posit Package Manager, and also cannot detect Rocky Linux, which is compatible with RHEL9 binaries.

`renv` detects the distribution by reading `/etc/os-release`. In RHEL9, that file looks something like:

```
NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
VERSION="9.2 (Plow)"
ID="rhel"
ID_LIKE="fedora"
VERSION_ID="9.2"
PLATFORM_ID="platform:el9"
PRETTY_NAME="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 (Plow)"
ANSI_COLOR="0;31"
LOGO="fedora-logo-icon"
CPE_NAME="cpe:/o:redhat:enterprise_linux:9::baseos"
HOME_URL="https://www.redhat.com/"
DOCUMENTATION_URL="https://access.redhat.com/documentation/en-us/red_hat_enterprise_linux/9"
BUG_REPORT_URL="https://bugzilla.redhat.com/"

REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9"
REDHAT_BUGZILLA_PRODUCT_VERSION=9.2
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT="Red Hat Enterprise Linux"
REDHAT_SUPPORT_PRODUCT_VERSION="9.2"
```

When `renv` detects `rhel` in the `ID`, it returns `"centos"` concatenated with a substring of `VERSION_ID`. In this case, it would return `centos9`.

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/36e1b5192fbc9f380dd4fffc6ee837856d5d3e75/R/ppm.R#L199-L207

For Red Hat 9, Posit Package Manager now serves binaries using the `rhel9` substring, not `centos9` (e.g. `https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/rhel9/latest`). (See https://packagemanager.posit.co/client/#/repos/cran/setup?distribution=redhat-9)

title: `renv_ppm_platform()` should detect Rocky Linux as Red Hat.
description:
Rocky Linux is "designed to be 100% bug-for-bug compatible with Red Hat Enterprise Linux". However, `renv` (via `renv_ppm_platform()`) does not detect it as RHEL-compatible, so `renv_ppm_transform()` transforms Package Manager URLs (even those using compatible RHEL9 binaries) to source package URLs.

You can currently work around this by setting the `RENV_PPM_PLATFORM` environment variable, but it would be better if it worked out of the box.

title: Best practices for using renv and Posit Connect to manage and deploy R projects
description:
Hello,

we are using renv and Posit Connect to manage and deploy our R projects. I have a question about the best practices for using these tools together, and also about the future plans of Posit regarding their package management tools.

As far as I understand, renv and Posit Connect both use lock files to record the R version and the package dependencies for a project. However, they use different formats: renv uses renv.lock and RStudio Connect uses manifest.json. The renv documentation recommends committing both files to version control, but I am worried about the potential inconsistencies and conflicts that might arise if they are not updated in sync.

Is there a way to avoid duplicating the information in these lock files? For example, can manifest.json reference renv.lock instead of listing the packages separately? Or can Posit Connect use renv.lock directly instead of generating manifest.json?

Another issue is that Posit Connect seems to use Packrat, another package management tool, for its deployment process. This adds another layer of complexity (and maybe confusion). How can I ensure that the environment on RStudio Connect matches the one on my local machine using renv?

I would appreciate any guidance or suggestions on how to build a good workflow here to avoid unnecessary problems. Thank you.

Also, is Posit planning to switch from packrat to renv internally for its deployment process? If so, when can we expect this change to happen? If not, what are the reasons for keeping Packrat as the default tool?

Thank you!

title: renv::restore() failing to download packages - potentially due to differences in R versions
description:
Hi,

I have a laptop where I conducted all of my statistical analysis 2 years ago. It has R version 4.0.3; hence, Bioconductor is limited to version 3.12 and Biocmanager 1.30.10. I stopped working on it and migrated to a desktop, which is running R 4.2.0 (Bioconductor 3.15.2 and Biocmanager 1.30.19). I had to re-run an analysis, and it gave me slightly different results comparing both systems. This is the moment I realized I needed renv.

Now, I installed renv on both machines, and I am trying to "migrate" the laptop scripts to the desktop. When trying to run `renv::restore()` on my desktop, using a lock.file for a specific project from the laptop, renv can't install the packages. This is what I did:

1. created a new folder and a project in R (on my desktop)
2. ran `renv::init()`
3. ran `renv::restore(lockfile = "backup_renv.lock")`
4. Console is asking if I want to install BiocManager [1.30.22]. I say "Yes", but this is already a red flag as this version does not match my lock.file
5. Console then shows all packages in the lock.file and proceeds to install them.
6. A few get installed, but a bunch have these errors:
```
Warning: failed to find binary for 'ggrepel 0.9.1' in package repositories

It seems that R is ok-ish regarding backward compatibility, but Bioconductor is not ok at all running older versions unless you have older R as well.

Does this make sense or am I doing something wrong?

title: Option to disable installing packages with `--with-keep.source`
description:
Recently, `renv` changed the way packages are installed by adding with `--with-keep.source` installation option. I have created a related (solved) issue here: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1688.

While the problems that arose in this issue are fixed from our side, we are now running into related problems that also arise due to the installation option `--with-keep.source`.
A side effect of keeping all the sources is that the size of serialized functions becomes much larger. 

If I e.g. save the `ggplot2::ggplot` function when installing ggplot2 without source, the function has 1.76 KB, wheres when I install the package with the sources, the serialized `ggplot2::ggplot` function has 1.65 MB, a factor of around **1000**. 

I believe that the culprit here is `attributes(attributes(ggplot2::ggplot)$srcref)$srcfile$original$lines`, which is a large character vector containing the sources.

It would be great if one could disable the `--with-keep.source` flag. In light of the above issue, might it also make sense to not set this option by default?

I see these reported occasionally after the renv activation during an R session start, and after operations like `renv::restore()`:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/assets/141234056/48119108-17ae-4596-a91c-985c20afdf2d)

Using `options(warn=2)` I managed to track this down to renv_available_packages_success being passed an empty `db` parameter:

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/assets/141234056/aa9dbf11-fa8f-4f37-b82b-9f7996794579)

Looking down the stack this is because our CRAN server for our local packages doesn't cache any binaries - so it returns an empty string for PACKAGES for https://cran.OurCo.app/cran/bin/windows/contrib/4.3

We can change this behaviour in our CRAN server - it can return 404 instead I guess.. although then I suspect we will see warnings about the file being missing... Or maybe we could add a dummy `zzzUnicorn` binary entry...

But I thought I'd also check with renv whether this is a situation you want to handle without this warning (or with a more specific message/warning)

title: Updating to Mac OSX Sonoma causes RStudio to hang because of non-responsiveness of R in repos using renv with many dependencies
description:
It looks like `source` ing _renv/activate.R_ can take up to a minute. The reason appears to be that cached packages are no longer available and so `renv` detects that the lockfile and the repo dependencies are out of sync. 
Installing the now missing packages anew and snapshotting appears to have mostly fixed the issue. The R session is still responding unusually slowly from time to time but things appear to be mostly resolved. 

Cataloging this just in case anyone else encounters it!

title: Binary package with RemoteSubdir and other remote fields set will always result in Git clone
description:
Hello,

I'm trying to use `renv` with a `miniCRAN` repository. This repository contains a few GitHub packages, and similar to r-universe I added a few Remote fields to the `DESCRIPTION` and an automatically generated package lock file to make sure packages can be updated if only the Git hash changes.

This seems to work mostly well, except for one package which resides in a sub directory of a GitHub hosted repository. For this package the binary package is ignored and a checkout is performed instead. To simplify things, here is a minimal lock file that generates the error:

```json
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "4.3.1",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "patRoonDeps",
        "URL": "https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps"
      }
    ]
  },
    "Packages": {
      "splashR": {
      "Package": "splashR",
      "Version": "0.0.4",
      "Repository": "https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps",
      "Source": "patRoonDeps",
      "RemoteType": "patRoonDeps",
      "RemoteSha": "174fbf289a0357535f9bacda282b9a2dbb7807cc",
      "RemoteUrl": "https://github.com/berlinguyinca/spectra-hash",
      "RemoteRef": "master",
      "RemoteUsername": "berlinguyinca",
      "RemoteRepo": "spectra-hash",
      "RemoteSubdir": "splashR"
    }
  }
}
```

The `DESCRIPTION` on the miniCRAN repository has the following lines:

```
RemoteType: patRoonDeps
RemoteSha: 174fbf289a0357535f9bacda282b9a2dbb7807cc
RemoteUrl: https://github.com/berlinguyinca/spectra-hash
RemoteRef: master
RemoteUsername: berlinguyinca
RemoteRepo: spectra-hash
RemoteSubdir: splashR
```

To test it:

```R
renv::init(bare=T)
renv::restore(lockfile = "bug.lock")
```

And the output (the test is done with an empty cache by setting RENV_PATHS_ROOT to a temporary directory):

```
> renv::restore(lockfile = "bug.lock")
The following package(s) will be updated:

# https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps -----------------------------------
- splashR   [* -> berlinguyinca/spectra-hash:splashR]

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: 
# Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
- Querying repositories for available binary packages ... Done!
- Downloading splashR from https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps ... OK [575.6 Kb in 0.34s]
- Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
renv was unable to query available packages from the following repositories:
- # https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps/src/contrib -----------------------
error downloading 'https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps/src/contrib/PACKAGES.rds' [curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404]
error downloading 'https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps/src/contrib/PACKAGES.gz' [curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404]
error downloading 'https://rickhelmus.github.io/patRoonDeps/src/contrib/PACKAGES' [curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404]


- Cloning 'https://github.com/berlinguyinca/spectra-hash' ... OK [cloned repository in 13 seconds]
- Downloading digest from patRoonDeps ...       OK [201.4 Kb in 0.23s]
Successfully downloaded 2 packages in 16 seconds.

# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing digest ...                         OK [installed binary and cached in 0.34s]
- Installing splashR ...                        OK [built from source and cached in 1.4s]
The dependency tree was repaired during package installation:
- digest  [0.6.33]
- splashR [berlinguyinca/spectra-hash:splashR]
Call `renv::snapshot()` to capture these dependencies in the lockfile.
```

From what I could gather it seems that `renv_description_read_impl` is trying to use the `subdir` to locate the `DESCRIPTION` file also for the binary package, which then fails and the installation process then proceeds with a Git checkout (where the subdir actually makes sense).

Thanks,
Rick

title: Unable to install historical binaries on macOS
description:
## Description
When using `renv` with [P3M](https://packagemanager.posit.co/) on macOS older versions of packages are installed from source.

Based on the [renv 1.0.0 blog post](https://posit.co/blog/renv-1-0-0/) and [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1343#issue-1726287923) I understood that P3M should provide binaries of older versions of packages:

> _Fortunately, this shouldn't be necessary with PPM; **if you try to install an archived package, PPM will quietly give you a binary from the last snapshot that had binaries available for that package**._ ([source](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1343#issue-1726287923))

> MRAN integration is now disabled by default, pending the upcoming shutdown of Microsoft’s MRAN service. **Users who require binaries of older R packages on Windows + macOS can consider using the instance of CRAN mirrored by the [Posit Public Package Manager](https://packagemanager.posit.co/) (#1343)**. ([source](https://posit.co/blog/renv-1-0-0/))


## Repro script

The repro script uses `duckplyr` as an example, version `0.2.0` is installed from `source` when using the latest P3M CRAN snapshot. The 0.2.0 binary is available for the `2023-09-13` P3M CRAN snapshot - my understanding was that because a binary is available in an older snapshot, then the installation of duckplyr 0.2.0 should use that binary.

Am I understanding this correctly?

```r
options(renv.settings.use.cache = FALSE) # don't use cache to show how package is installed
project_directory <- withr::local_tempdir()

withr::with_dir(
  new = project_directory,
  code = {
    renv::init(restart = FALSE)
    
    message("Installing duckplyr@0.2.0 from https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest")
    # installs from source
    renv::install(
      "duckplyr@0.2.0", 
      prompt = FALSE
    ) 
    
    message("Installing duckplyr@0.2.0 from P3M snapshot")
    # installs binary
    renv::install(
      "duckplyr@0.2.0", 
      prompt = FALSE,
      repos = c(
        "CRAN" = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2023-09-13"
        )
    )
  }
)

```

title: Renv does not respect == dependency in the import file
description:
While trying to install an internal package from an internal repo, it seems that renv will ignore the dependency and will try to install the latest version from CRAN.



We have developed an internal package (called internal_package) which we publish on our internal repo at https://internal.site/repo/. We also have a dependency on an external package (e.g. paws) which we would like to be fixed for very valid reasons. 

In the DESCRIPTION file of the internal_package, we fix the dependency using the == operator for Imports and the archived versions of the package are found on our internal repo (see below).

In renv.lock, our internal repo is defined before CRAN and works just fine.

However, the _issue_ is that if we try to install our internal package using renv::install('internal_package') then the internal package is retrieved from the internal repo and then a call is made to CRAN for v0.4.0 (latest) of paws. If we restrict the repo list to just the internal repo using the repos parameter, then the correct version if used.

The expected behaviour, would be for the specific version to be installed from the internal repo, without having to specify the repo.

Thank you,
A

  "R": {
    "Version": "4.1.0",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "INTERNAL_REPO",
        "URL": "https://internal.site/repo"
      },
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "http://cran.rstudio.com"

}

title: `renv::install` does not respect version bounds in the `DESCRIPTION` file of subdependencies
description:
`renv::install` respects version requirements if I explicitly install a package with `>= version` in its DESCRIPTION file. But if a dependency of a package has `>= version` in the `DESCRIPTION` file, this is not respected.

In the example below, I first install [`BayesFactor`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=BayesFactor) directly. There `renv::install` correctly realizes it needs to update `Matrix` to satisfy the requirements of the dependency [`MatrixModels`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=MatrixModels).

Next, I install a package that has `BayesFactor` as a dependency ([vandenman/tempRenvPkg](https://github.com/vandenman/tempRenvPkg/blob/master/DESCRIPTION)). There `renv::install` does not update `Matrix`, which ultimately causes the installation of `BayesFactor` to fail with the error:
```r
Error in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]) : 
  namespace ‘Matrix’ 1.5-4.1 is already loaded, but >= 1.6.0 is required`
```

Below is the example code.
```r
renv::init(bare = TRUE)

packageVersion("renv")
# [1] ‘1.0.3’

packageVersion("Matrix") # version shipped with R-4.3.1

renv::install("BayesFactor")

title: Package installation with `renv::restore()` is broken
description:
Hey, thanks for your work on the renv package!

I have noticed  that calling `renv::restore()` can install packages incorrectly.
This is with R 4.3.1 and  renv 1.0.0
I have created an example repository with a workflow that illustrates this behavior [here](https://github.com/sebffischer/zzz/actions/runs/6173720354/job/16756711475).

This workflow essentially runs:

```r
library(mlr3)
LearnerClassifRpart$new()$train
```
twice, once after installing mlr3 using `renv::restore()` and once using `install.packages("mlr3")` and the output is different.
(The code in the workflow is `lrn("classif.rpart")$train`, which is equivalent to the above `LearnerClassifRpart$new()$train`).

In the relevant package (https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3) for which the installation via renv fails, we have some "magic" in the `./R/zzz.R` file, which "leanifies" R6 classes (see: https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3misc/blob/main/R/leanify.R and https://github.com/mlr-org/mlr3/blob/dfa917ea8afd074b632547242cd853005b4e2a76/R/zzz.R#L96)
This walks over all R6 classes and puts the class methods as functions into the `mlr3` namespace and then replaces the method in the class with a call to the function from the namespace.

E.g. the public `$train` method from the `Learner` R6 class (from which `LearnerClassifRpart` inherits) is put into the mlr3 namespace as 
```r
.__Learner__train = function(self, private, super, task, row_ids) {
      task = assert_task(as_task(task))
      assert_learnable(task, self)
      row_ids = assert_row_ids(row_ids, null.ok = TRUE)
      ... (the actual content of the function)
}
```

The method in the R6 class is then replaced with a call to the above function:

``` r
library(mlr3)
lrn("regr.rpart")$train
#> function (task, row_ids = NULL) 
#> .__Learner__train(self = self, private = private, super = super, 
#>     task = task, row_ids = row_ids)
#> <environment: 0x55a424ab3230>
```

When installing packages using `renv::restore()` this leanification is not applied and the output of `lrn("classif.rpart")$train` is not as expected, but what should be the content of `.__Learner__train`.

```r
function(task, row_ids = NULL) {
      task = assert_task(as_task(task))
      assert_learnable(task, self)
      row_ids = assert_row_ids(row_ids, null.ok = TRUE)
      ... (the actual content of the function)
    }
```

If this is not an issue with renv but a dependency, please let me know and I will transfer the issue.

title: "The project is out-of-sync" message appears when using a second named repository
description:
Using the latest GitHub version of renv (dba0079), I'm trying to add a second named repository to the lockfile for Stan-related stuff, [following the instructions here](https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/). (This is possibly related to #1550.)

However, it seems that when there are two repositories in the lockfile, like this:

```
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "Stan",
        "URL": "https://mc-stan.org/r-packages"
      },
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest"
      }
    ]
```

…I get this error, even though `renv::status()` says everything is fine and stable:

```
- The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.
```

Here's a reproducible example (starting from a new empty project)

```r
# Start a new renv library
renv::init()

# Add Stan's repo as a valid source
repos <- c(Stan = "https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/", CRAN = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest")
options(repos = repos)

# Install cmdstanr; it will come from the Stan repo; all other dependencies will come from CRAN/RSPM
install.packages("cmdstanr")

# Save to lockfile
renv::snapshot()

# Make sure everything is good
renv::status()
#> No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.

# RESTART R SESSION

#> Restarting R session...
#> 
#> - Project '~/Desktop/renv-testing' loaded. [renv 1.0.2.9000; sha: dba0079]
#> - The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.

# It says it's out of sync there ↑
# But if I run renv::status() again, all is well
renv::status()
#> No issues found -- the project is in a consistent state.
```

If I remove the Stan repository and only use one repository entry in the lockfile and install {cmdstanr} like this:

```r
install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://mc-stan.org/r-packages/", getOption("repos")))
```

…and then snapshot, I get this message, which is to be expected, since it comes from an unknown-to-renv repository:

```
The following package(s) were installed from an unknown source:
- cmdstanr [0.6.1]
renv may be unable to restore these packages in the future.
Consider reinstalling these packages from a known source (e.g. CRAN).
```

BUT when I restart R, I don't get the "The project is out-of-sync". That message only appears if the Stan repository is included in the lockfile.

Hey there,

Was going through the process of [setting up renv to work with R in Databricks](https://docs.databricks.com/en/sparkr/renv.html#id3) via Notebooks + RStudio Server and the lack of an automated `.Rprofile` sourcing mechanism in the context of Databricks Notebooks and the ephemeral compute makes the global cache very important and a little confusing to set and change the path (to a non ephemeral DBFS path).

When I install packages from `renv` I get the following:
`These packages will be installed into "/local_disk0/.ephemeral_nfs/envs/rEnv-6e7151e7-3792-4219-ae69-7dec6aaa5672".`
This is _fine_, I assume -- a local ephemeral copy of the packages, symlinked to the global cache. Am slightly confused that none of the paths at `renv::paths$*` (i.e. library, sandbox, etc.) give me this path but it's fine.

I also understand we can _access_ and set our `renv` global cache path with these commands: 
```
>  renv::paths$cache()
"/Workspace/Repos/kunal.mishra@interwellhealth.com/data-predictive-analytics/v5/R-4.2/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"

> Sys.setenv(RENV_PATHS_CACHE = here::here()) # here::here() = /Workspace/Repos/kunal.mishra@interwellhealth.com/data-predictive-analytics

> # Change not reflected:
>  renv::paths$cache()
"/Workspace/Repos/kunal.mishra@interwellhealth.com/data-predictive-analytics/v5/R-4.2/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
```
But when an R session is already running, is there a way to set the cache path? Or even alter the path to which our project's library is saved? Right now, the global package cache is persisting on the DBFS (good), but I wonder if that's the default behavior or something that occurred because I did a `setwd(here::here())` at some point earlier and the cache ended up in that working directory due to that. 

If there's not a way, a possible addition here could be a function for refreshing or setting the cache path that works _with_ the environment variable (like `sparklyr::spark_home_set()`) that refreshes the output of `renv::paths$cache()` as well.

title: Explicit mode and suggested packages
description:
`renv::init()` installs packages in `Suggests`. Which is the right thing to do, probably.

But these packages are not added to `renv.lock`, and if the project/package is copied to a new user/location, they are not restored.

Should they be added to the lock file? Should they be restored?

Is there a way to install them manually?

title: Feature Request: support arbitrary pip install arguments
description:
I have a project where `numpy` needs to be installed from source to avoid issues with R and Python being linked to different versions of (Open)BLAS. To do this, I add `--no-binary=numpy` to the requirements.txt file.

However, `renv::snapshot` overwrites this portion of the requirements file and `renv::restore` does not provide a means of specifying additional arguments to `pip install`.

It would be nice if there was a way to do this, perhaps as a new `pip_args` argument to `renv::restore`.

title: Silently allow pre-existing library if it contains preinstalled renv with the same version
description:
We deploy R containerized as a command line tool, and we have moved the renv libary to a location inside the container using RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY.

This means that the first time you run renv::init() , it works as fine, it installs itself into the library and sets up renv.lock and renv and .Rprofile.

When I restart R, and by that elaunching the container, the library is again empty so it starts by downloading renv, (and does so every single time we launch R in the project)

To help this, we preinstall renv into RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY in the docker image so that its there when it revisits a project with a renv setup. This worked find in renv <1.0.0, but now it complains when it finds renv preinstalled in the project library.

So now renv [prompts you what to do](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/R/init.R#L224) if you try to `renv::init()` a project that has an already existing library.

If possible, could renv silently accept the presence of the renv package already installed in the project library? (By checking that its the only package in the libary, and that it has the right version)?

I have written up a proposal for a solution where `renv_init_action_conflict_library()` checks for these exact things and returns "init" if this is the case.

description:
Found the error when trying to upload a Shiny App to our own server. 

```{r}
# Use any existing Shiny app (with renv), or use the example app created by Rstudio:
# File > New Project > New Directory > Shiny Application > [tick "use renv with this project"]

# Bundle app
appDir = getwd()
appFiles <- rsconnect:::bundleFiles(appDir)
appMetadata <- rsconnect:::appMetadata(appDir, appFiles, isShinyappsServer = FALSE)
bundlePath <- rsconnect:::bundleApp("test", appDir, appFiles, appMetadata)

# Extract to get manifest.json
dir.create("packed")
system(paste0('tar xzf ', bundlePath,' -C ', "packed"))

converted_lockfile <- renv:::renv_lockfile_from_manifest("packed/manifest.json")

# Returns: Error: C stack usage <stack limit> is too close to the limit
renv::lockfile_write(converted_lockfile)

# The issue seems to be with the class/attributes stored in R$Version:
original_lockfile <- renv::lockfile_read("packed/renv.lock")
all.equal(original_lockfile, converted_lockfile)

modified_lockfile  <- converted_lockfile
modified_lockfile$R$Version <- as.character(converted_lockfile$R$Version)
all.equal(modified_lockfile, original_lockfile)

renv::lockfile_write(modified_lockfile) # Runs fine
```

This invalid value (1) is the default for the `menu` call in `renv_init_type`:

<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ac7126d7b2856a39012d6079689861b18c07c5b7/R/init.R#L344-L358>

And `menu` returns that default as is:

<https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ac7126d7b2856a39012d6079689861b18c07c5b7/R/utils.R#L190-L193>

     cancel = "Cancel and resolve the situation another way."
   )
 
-  choice <- menu(choices, title, default = "continue")
+  choice <- menu(choices, title, default = 2)
   switch(choice,
     activate = { activate(project = project); TRUE },
     continue = FALSE,
diff --git a/R/utils.R b/R/utils.R
index b67f5f14c..6be63ec67 100644
--- a/R/utils.R
+++ b/R/utils.R
@@ -189,7 +189,7 @@ menu <- function(choices, title, default = 1L) {
 
   if (!interactive()) {
     writef(c("Not interactive. Will:", choices[[default]]))
-    return(default)
+    return(names(choices)[default])
   }
 
   idx <- tryCatch(
```

I'm not sure whether the intention is for "implicit" to be the default even when a `DESCRIPTION` file is present. If that's the case, then `renv_init_type` would also need to be updated to pass `default = 2`.

---

For any others hitting into this, I think the easiest workaround is to sidestep the menu by setting `snapshot.type` (e.g., `init(settings = list("snapshot.type" = "explicit"))`).

title: profile specific ignore setting
description:
Let's suppose the following file structure

```
.
├── renv
│   └── ...
├── basic
│   ├── run.R
│   └── scripts
│       ├── foo.R
│       └── bar.R
└── extra
    ├── run.R
    └── scripts/
        └── baz.R
```

I would like to have two renv profiles: "all" (all dirs included) and let's say "basic" (just "basic" dir). Is there a way to _tell_ the "basic" profile to ignore dirs? Or from different angle: is there a way to specify `.renvignore` file to be applied / ignored for certain profiles? I was also looking for a way to register a callbacks on activate / deactivete (here: add/remove `.renvignore` file) but no success.

Often, if I install each dependency individually, and then try installing the main package again, it will work. Since I've just installed all the deps, I should just be able to run `renv::install('geojsonio')` to do that. But, alas, I get:

```
# Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
- Installing urltools ...                       OK [linked from cache in 1.5s]
- Installing httpcode ...                       OK [linked from cache in 1.0s]
...
- Installing s2 ...                             OK [linked from cache in 1.9s]
- Installing units ...                          OK [linked from cache in 1.7s]
- Installing sf ...                             OK [linked from cache in 19s]
- Installing V8 ...                             OK [linked from cache in 2.0s]
- Installing geojsonio ...                      FAILED
```

It seems like if one of the installations fails, all are rewound? 

It's easy enough to run

```r
renv::install(tools::package_dependencies("geojsonio")[[1]])
```

but I think it would be preferable if the installed deps just stuck around despite the failure.

title: Converting Checkpoint to renv
description:
This summer Microsoft sopped daily mirrors of CRAN on MRAN.  The source code I was working with building our base containers used checkpoints of MRAN.  I want to convert these over to renv.

It seems like an obvious solution, but when trying to do it there were several issues.  I am posting here as others may have a similar problems.

I installed renv in an active container and activated the project.  So far so good, however when I go to load/snapshot libraries it doesn't seem to know about the system libraries.  If I deactivate renv, then snapshot it gives an option to use system paths (option 2), but it crawls a huge number of dependencies.  I have twenty libraries that I installed with checkpoint.

description:
``` r

title: Skip packages loaded with `devtools::load_all(".")` when running `renv::install()` ?
description:
I bundle all my work into packages, and use `devtools::load_all(".")` to load the package, instead of building and installing the package. `renv` seems to have some conflicting opinions on this...

`renv::install()` fails with an error:

```
> renv::install()
# Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
Warning: failed to find binary for 'rtraining 0.8.20' in package repositories
Warning: failed to find source for 'rtraining 0.8.20' in package repositories
Error: failed to retrieve package 'rtraining@0.8.20'
Traceback (most recent calls last):
8: renv::install()
7: retrieve(packages)
6: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
5: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
4: renv_retrieve_unknown_source(record)
3: renv_retrieve_repos(record)
2: stopf("failed to retrieve package '%s'", renv_record_format_remote(record))
1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
```

As a workaround, running Build > Install in RStudio fixes the issue.

However, `renv::clean()` reports the package as installed but not used:

```
> renv::clean()
- No stale package locks were found.
- No temporary directories were found in the project library.
The following packages are installed in the project library,
but appear to be no longer used in your project.
- rtraining
These packages will be removed.

Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]:
```

`renv::clean()` is working as I expect, however I'd ideally like `renv::install()` to either skip the local package as `renv::clean()` does, or provide an option to continue installation and/or skip installation of specific packages. Could this functionality be added to renv?

title: Feature request: `dependencies()` to scan `NAMESPACE` files
description:
At present, `dependencies()` will perform a static analysis of R files. I find this very useful during development as a mechanism to help build the Imports section of a package's DESCRIPTION file; e.g.:
```r
package_imports <- renv::dependencies("R/")$Package
purrr::walk(package_imports, usethis::use_package, type = "Imports", min_version = TRUE)
```
The only problem is the static analysis skips the NAMESPACE file, which itself is based on roxygen2 tags, and includes some imports. For example, I might have the tag `#' @importFrom foo bar`, yielding the NAMESPACE entry:
```
importFrom(foo, bar)
```
It'd be useful if `dependencies()` also read the NAMESPACE file to identify additional packages.

FWIW, there's a base `parseNamespaceFile()` function, which can be run (here from within the nascent package's root) like so:
```r
parseNamespaceFile("packagename", "..")
```
One would still need to know how to deal with the various outputs -- each type corresponding to each unique NAMESPACE directive, but fortunately new NAMESPACE directives don't come around too often :-)

This is the call stack leading up to the error:

      renv_bootstrap_run(version, libpath) at activate.R#1007

title: Errors using `renv` with RMarkdown
description:
I have an RMarkdown file in an R Project that reproduces all of the analyses for a manuscript. Originally, I had a section in the RMarkdown file where required packages were installed (if needed) and loaded, but I am trying to switch over to `renv` for package management. I used `renv::init()` to set up my project to use `renv`, installed and loaded all the packages I needed using my normal script for doing so, and used `renv::snapshot()` to update my lockfile. 

Then, I was imagining I could just use `renv::restore()` in place of my original package loading section in my RMarkdown file. 

While I am able to run individual chunks from the RMarkdown file in the console successfully, and I also seem to be able to render the RMarkdown file from the console successfully, when I try to Knit to HTML using the RStudio IDE, which is typically how I knit, I now get an error from my first chunk of code that suggests `renv::restore()` is not successfully allowing RMarkdown to access the packages:

```
Error in `ggplot()`:
! could not find function "ggplot"
Execution halted
```

Any idea why this is happening and how to fix it? My ideal is that anyone can load the GitHub repo with this R Project, and immediately knit the RMarkdown file to HTML (ideally using the button, rather than code, to make it easy for new R users) without any problems, without having to do anything extra. This was the case when the RMarkdown file installed/loaded packages correctly, so I'm hoping to make it the case using `renv` too, for maximum reproducibility!

title: Activation considerably slower since 1.0.0 if renv version used in project is not installed globally
description:
renv version 0.17.3 has a relativley fast `source('renv/activate.R')` (after the env was set up with `restore()` before), even if not the same renv version that is used in a specific project is globally installed. If my project uses renv version 1.0.0, the same command very slow if the same version of renv is not available in the global R package library. For https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit, it took ~ 1s on my labtop if my project used 0.17.3 and around 30s with version 1.0.0 if renv is not installed globally.

**reprex**
```bash
# do this outside RStudio to avoid RENV_PROJECT and other env variables to interfere
# ------------------ setup -------------------- 
git clone https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit
cd precommit
# verify that relevant commit was only renv version change
git show 981cb1b29c5b028906e1a965ce0ab961f3164d0f
git reset 981cb1b29c5b028906e1a965ce0ab961f3164d0f~1 --hard

# -------------  with renv verion 1.0.0 recorded in lockfile -------------- 

Rscript -e "if (rlang::is_installed('renv')) remove.packages('renv')"
Rscript -e "source('renv/activate.R'); renv::restore()"

# after I restored the renv, this is now very slow
Rscript -e "system.time(source('renv/activate.R'))"
Rscript -e "if (rlang::is_installed('renv')) remove.packages('renv')"


# -------------- with renv version 0.17.3 in lockfile  ---------- 
git reset 981cb1b29c5b028906e1a965ce0ab961f3164d0f --hard
Rscript -e "source('renv/activate.R'); renv::restore()"

# after I restored the renv, this is fast
Rscript -e "system.time(source('renv/activate.R'))"
Rscript -e "if (rlang::is_installed('renv')) remove.packages('renv')"
```
I noted that I could disable the sandbox, as a warning message suggest, which is apparently responsible for nearly all the overhead according to the docs and my experiments. It's not clear what side effect disabling the sandbox has for my use case, which is a read-only, non-interactive usage of renv to run an R script as a pre-commit hook (https://pre-commit.com/). Since every hook invokes a shell process which invokes `Rscript` which has to load renv, while the user waits to see all hooks pass after `git commit`, a delay of even a few seconds is already a lot (on top of the slow R Startup). I know this is maybe a bit of special case, but also everytime someone opens RStudio with a renv, a startup time of 20s on top of RStudio + R is not very convenient.

Looking at GitHub issues, I found that the dev version of renv allows for profiling the sandboxing, which I (see below in _Details_). This did not help me to figure out how to use `renvignore` or other workarounds to decrease the timing. Maybe you can suggest guidance for this?


I also tried to change the `snapshot.type` to `all`, which also brought a little speed-up, but for my use case, I actually would like to skip discovery as well since I only want a read-only, light way of using the currently installed state of the renv library. To my knowledge, there is no such API in renv and I don't want to fiddle with `.LibPaths()` and friends myself I think.

Thanks for working on renv, it's great to see how it has matured and gained many features over the last few years.

title: `renv::init` ignores interactive snapshot type
description:
Hi,

we're trying to use the `renv::init` function using the *explicit* snapshot type (only capturing the dependencies as declared in the DESCRIPTION).
It looks like the snapshot type is ignored when submitted interactively as opposed to setting it in advance.

---

Our workflow was as follows: (in a new package without any dependencies):

1. setup a package without dependencies (using `usethis::create_package()`)
2. add a function using `tibble` package ( `use_r("tibble.R")`) without adding `tibble` as package dependency to DESCRIPTION
3. run `renv::init() ` interactively
```
renv::init()
#> This project contains a DESCRIPTION file.
#> Which files should renv use for dependency discovery in this project? 
#>   
#> 1: Use only the DESCRIPTION file. (explicit mode)
#> 2: Use all files in this project. (implicit mode)
#> 
#> Selection: 1
#> 
#> - Using 'explicit' snapshot type. Please see `?renv::snapshot` for more details.
#> 
#> - Linking packages into the project library ... Done!
#>   The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:
#>   
#>   # CRAN -----------------------------------------------------------------------
#> - cli         [* -> 3.6.1]
#> - glue        [* -> 1.6.2]
#> - lifecycle   [* -> 1.0.3]
#> - magrittr    [* -> 2.0.3]
#> - renv        [* -> 1.0.0]
#> - rlang       [* -> 1.1.1]
#> - vctrs       [* -> 0.6.3]
#> 
#> # RSPM -----------------------------------------------------------------------
#> - fansi       [* -> 1.0.4]
#> - pillar      [* -> 1.9.0]
#> - pkgconfig   [* -> 2.0.3]
#> - tibble      [* -> 3.2.1]
#> - utf8        [* -> 1.2.3]
#> 
#> The version of R recorded in the lockfile will be updated:
#>   - R           [* -> 4.3.1]
#> 
#> - Lockfile written to '~/cstepper/justfortesting/renvtestr/renv.lock'.
#> 
#> Restarting R session...
#> 
#> - Project '~/cstepper/justfortesting/renvtestr' loaded. [renv 1.0.0]

It looks like all package dependencies from `tibble` are written to the `renv.lock` (as we assume is "implicit" mode, not "explicit"). Also, in `renv/settings.json` snapshot type "implicit" is defined, not "explicit" as chosen interactively.

In contrast, when manually setting the type before `renv::init()` it seems to work as expected:

```

Any ideas?

title: `renv::status()` not usable on uninitialized projects
description:
Hi,
we use `renv` for dependency management in our package setup (for CI/CD purposes, i.e. `restoring` within docker containers).

Our setup is: 
- using only dependencies as declared in DESCRIPTION file
- defining renv settings
  `renv::settings$snapshot.type(value = "explicit")` --> writing a `renv/settings.json`
- creating a snapshot (with type "explicit" as defined in settings.json file)
  `renv::snapshot()`

(see [test package](https://github.com/cstepper/renvtestr))

Each time we add new functions etc. we used to use `renv::status()` to check if our lockfile is up to date (comparing against the currently set libraries, e.g. default `.libPaths()`). 
If not, we took a new snapshot to update the lockfile.

With the new version of `renv`, this does not work any longer, as `renv::status()` is exiting without comparing the lockfile with the library; it exits before checking as `renv_status_check_initialized` returns `FALSE` 

(due to the missing projlib object: 
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ba90043f58c2d8f6ee807512da1287fd750dd887/R/status.R#L122
)

``` r
# check status of renv.lock against currently set libraries 
# (for checking if all packages are up to date)
(lb = .libPaths())
#> [1] "/home/christoph/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/4.3"
#> [2] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"                    
#> [3] "/usr/lib/R/site-library"                          
#> [4] "/usr/lib/R/library"

st = renv::status(library = lb)
#> This project does not appear to be using renv.
#> Use renv::init() to initialize the project.

str(st)
#> List of 3
#>  $ library     :List of 1
#>   ..$ Packages: Named list()
#>  $ lockfile    :List of 1
#>   ..$ Packages: Named list()
#>  $ synchronized: logi FALSE
```

<sup>Created on 2023-07-28 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

Is this on purpose? Do we need to initialize the package in all cases, even if we just want to use `renv` in the described setup?
Any workarounds?

Thanks for consideration.

title: `renv=1.0.0` fails on `box` installation
description:
### Error description

`renv=1.0.0` checks if package installed from a binary [can be loaded](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blame/main/R/install.R#L660) (happens on Linux). `box` on the other hand is not intended to be loaded using `library` and throws an error that blocks installation.

## Steps to reproduce:
1. Initialize `renv` in project:
```r
remotes::install_version("renv", version = "1.0.0")
renv::init()
```
2. Try to install `box` :
```r
renv::install("box", rebuild = TRUE)
#> # Downloading packages -------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> - Downloading box from RSPM ...                 OK [file is up to date]
#> 
#> The following package(s) will be installed:
#> 
#> - box [1.1.3]
#> 
#> These packages will be installed into "~/tmp_projects/renv_box/renv/library/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu".
#> 
#> # Installing packages --------------------------------------------------------
#> 
#> - Installing box ...                            FAILED
#> Error: error testing if 'box' can be loaded [error code 1]
#> /opt/R/4.3.1/lib/R/bin/R --vanilla -s -f '/tmp/Rtmp0Oh8zr/renv-install-67f1e5c0ac0fa'
#> ================================================================================
#> 
#> NULL
#> Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘box’:
#>  .onAttach failed in attachNamespace() for 'box', details:
#>   call: library(box)
#>   error: the ‘box’ package is not supposed to be attached!
#> 
#> Please consult the user guide at `vignette("box", package = "box")`.
#> Execution halted
```

## Available workarounds

Setting option `--no-test-load`:
```r
withr::with_options(
    list(install.opts = "--no-test-load"),
    renv::install("box", rebuild = TRUE)
)

title: stop using `error = warning` when handling errors
description:
Consider the following:

```
(function() {
  cnd <- simpleError("error")
  tryCatch(
    warning(cnd),
    error = function(e) {
      print("caught error")
    }
  )
})()
```

The error handler will catch the condition emitted via warning, e.g. this prints:

```
[1] "caught error"
```

However, we use this pattern in a couple places, e.g.

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/c06b9bfb526d52bc8a34b507854fe3c421161cb3/inst/resources/activate.R#L859

Instead, I think we should define a separate function for dropping the error classes and then using warning on that, since our intention in catching these errors is to ensure they are not propagated further up the call stack.

title: `renv::auto_load` does not work anymore
description:
Hey,
I think with this commit (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/314009b6ab456a413af03cb360239923139e57e3#diff-43c4528da3e8c329bb7bce6306f225c0b66b8e8c2fdc8d5f5f2560df86542707) a logic error has been inadvertently introduced into the autoload function, which causes the trigger for autoload to work the other way around.
If `RENV_AUTOLOAD_ENABLED=TRUE` or not set, the autoload operation is aborted instead of being performed.
This is currently causing a problem in our build pipelines and on Posit Workbench that all projects are running against the standard R library and are no longer initializing with locked packages or tracking changes.
I would be very grateful for a quick fix.
Thanks and best regards!

title: `renv::install()` fails when CRAN-like repositories are in `renv.lock`
description:
My institution uses a [`drat`](https://eddelbuettel.github.io/drat/) repository in our GitHub Enterprise to distribute packages internally. Since `renv 0.17.0` `renv::install()` seems to fail for **any** package (even CRAN packages) when our `drat` repo is in my `renv.lock`.

I did some digging and it seems like the regression may have occurred at https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/62c73d9c74117ceafec37c8e4a5c343aed149792 where a warning was upgraded to an error in [`available-packages.R`](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/62c73d9c74117ceafec37c8e4a5c343aed149792/R/available-packages.R#L58).

## reprex

I created a `drat` repo at https://ezraporter.github.io/drat to show the issue:

`renv.lock`:
``` yaml
...
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cran.rstudio.com"
      },
      {
        "Name": "OTHERAN",
        "URL": "https://ezraporter.github.io/drat"
      }
    ]
  ...
```

```r
# Fails
renv::install("dplyr")
```
<details>
<summary>Show error message</summary>

```r
Error: package 'dplyr' is not available
Traceback (most recent calls last):
15: renv::install("dplyr")
14: retrieve(packages)
13: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
12: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
11: withCallingHandlers(renv_available_packages_latest(package), 
        error = function(err) stopf("package '%s' is not available", 
            package))
10: renv_available_packages_latest(package)
 9: map(errors$data(), warning)
 8: lapply(x, f, ...)
 7: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
 6: withRestarts({
        .Internal(.signalCondition(cond, message, call))
        .Internal(.dfltWarn(message, call))
    }, muffleWarning = function() NULL)
 5: withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
 4: doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
 3: <condition-handler>(...)
 2: stopf("package '%s' is not available", package)
 1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
```
</details>

```r

utils::install.packages("dplyr")

#> ...
#> Warning: unable to access index for repository https://ezraporter.github.io/drat/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.2:
#>  cannot open URL 'https://ezraporter.github.io/drat/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.2/PACKAGES'
#> ...
```

Ideally `renv` would also be able to install and track sources for packages downloaded from `drat` repos.

In `renv 0.16.0`, this works:

```r

```

where `dummypackage` is a package in https://ezraporter.github.io/drat. `renv::snapshot()` generates the right thing in my `renv.lock`:

```yaml
...
"Packages": {
    "dummypackage": {

      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "OTHERAN", # <-- repo is tracked!

In the latest development version:

# Works

title: renv 1.0.0 check on startup can lead to long session loading time
description:
if an `.*ignore` file is missing or misspecified, loading an R project with `renv` that contains many files will take a long time because `renv` 1.0.0 checks all files at startup by default, _without a prior warning or prompt_ (see also discussion here: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1181#issuecomment-1640508295)

How I replicated the issue: I created a new R project in a new directory and created 100 000 dummy .txt files in subdirectory `data`. Opening the project hangs RStudio seemingly until the files are scanned. Adding `data` to `.gitignore` "fixes" it.

I think the user should be prompted whether they want to do the startup check if it involves a high number of files, otherwise it should be skipped. At very minimum they must be informed, as when running `renv::status()`. In a complex project it took me a while to figure out what was causing the slow loading time and at first did not realize this was related to updating renv to 1.0.0.

title: Running renv::restore() in parallel will fail
description:
I have some Airflow tasks where I launch a Kubernetes Pod and in that Pod I use `renv` to install and run code from a package.
Since the task is, essentially, "copy data from A to B for date X", there can be multiple instance of this task running in parallel for different days.

If the packages are not in the cache, `renv` will attempt to install the missing packages in all the parallel jobs. Unfortunately, only the first job to finish installing will actually be sucessful and the other jobs will fail with an error:

```
Error: target file '/renv/cache/v5/linux-ubuntu-jammy/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/kofcasts/1.2.1/51a5c034ff08245557a03533120c02e9/kofcasts' already exists
 - Installing kofcasts ...                       Traceback (most recent calls last):
 12: renv::install(package_name)
 11: renv_install_impl(records)
 10: renv_install_staged(records)
  9: renv_install_default(records)
  8: handler(package, renv_install_package(record))
  7: renv_install_package(record)
  6: renv_cache_synchronize(record, linkable = linkable)
  5: renv_cache_synchronize_impl(cache, record, linkable, path)
  4: renv_cache_copy(path, cache, overwrite = TRUE)
  3: renv_file_copy(source, target, overwrite = overwrite)
  2: renv_file_copy_dir(source, target)
  1: stop(status)
 Execution halted
```

Does this really need to be an error condition?
Ideally it would acknowledge that the desired package has been installed in the cache in the meantime and move on.

title: renv::restore() should have to option to repair broken symlinks
description:
Sometimes `renv::restore()` fails on my pipelines with the following message:

```
$ Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
Warning message:
renv took longer than expected (20 seconds) to activate the sandbox.
The sandbox can be disabled by setting:
    RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED = FALSE
within an appropriate start-up .Renviron file.
See `?renv::config` for more details. 
The following package(s) have broken symlinks into the cache:
- Matrix
- mgcv
Use `renv::repair()` to try and reinstall these packages.
The following required packages are not installed:
- Matrix
- mgcv
Packages must first be installed before renv can snapshot them.
Use `renv::dependencies()` to see where this package is used in your project.
Not interactive. Will:
Snapshot, just using the currently installed packages.
- Operation canceled.
Execution halted
```

While this might be fine when working interactively, it does not work in a Pipeline: the only option for me is to delete the workers cache and rebuild it completely.

I think `renv` should automatically repair broken symlinks. Unless there is some other reason I'm not seeing, I don't think users should be particularly interested in actively knowing that this has happened.

Like the change made to autosnapshotting (which is great), `renv::restore()` should automatically try to repair, unless explicitly disabled. A log message informing that this is happening should be enough to hint at a potential problem.

At the very least, there should be a way to auto-repair, precisely for this scenario of renv running in a pipeline or in some other non-interactive way.

title: Provide option for profiling renv startup
description:
On occasion, R can be slow to start up due to work that `renv` is doing. It would be helpful if we could define something like:

```
RENV_STARTUP_DIAGNOSTICS = TRUE
```

and use `Rprof()` to provide a summary on what `renv` was doing while the project `.Rprofile` was sourced.

title: Add option to configure a proxy server within renv::config?
description:
Hi,

in our organization we need to set a `https_proxy` in order to install/retrieve packages for a project using renv.

With `renv.config.autoloader.enabled`, however, restoring a project fails when the user is prompted during the first initialization run (typically after the git clone) with:

```
- None of the packages recorded in the lockfile are installed.
- Using `renv::restore()` to restore the project library.
Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: Y
```
There is not even an error or a warning because the installation process seems to become stuck because of the missing proxy configuration.

So what the user typically has to do instead is 

- ignoring the initial `Do you want to proceed? [Y/n]: n`
- then setting `Sys.setenv(https_proxy = our_proxy)` 
- again run `renv::restore()` which, then, works just fine.

Could it be useful to store the proxy information somewhere in the renv configuration?

Thanks
Philipp

title: renv::status() not showing reason for "The project is out-of-sync message"
description:
I'm using renv to manage packages used in creating a custom package for my company. The library is stored within the project at '~R/XXX/renv/library/'. The root and cache are located elsewhere in a shared folder on the RStudio servers.

I upgraded renv from 0.17.3 to 1.0.0, recorded the new version in the lockfile, reactived renv, and restarted my environment. Previously, when starting a new session I would receive the normal message:
```
* Project '~/R/XXX' loaded. [renv 0.17.3]
```

Now after upgrading to renv 1.0.0 I receive the following at start up:
```
- Project '~/R/XXX' loaded. [renv 1.0.0]
- The project is out-of-sync -- use `renv::status()` for details.
Warning message:
renv took longer than expected (20 seconds) to activate the sandbox.

The sandbox can be disabled by setting:

    RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED = FALSE

within an appropriate start-up .Renviron file.

See `?renv::config` for more details. 
```

`renv::status()` and `renv::restore()` reported no issues whether RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED was set to TRUE or FALSE, although startup was significantly faster when not using the sandbox. I didn't notice any delays at startup in renv 0.17.3 like I am now.

title: Error in eval(quote({ : object '..version..' not found
description:
_Edit by @kevinushey: if you're encountering this issue after updating `renv`, please run `renv::activate()` and restart the R session to re-generate the `renv` activate scripts, and resolve this issue. Thanks, and sorry for the trouble._

---

I'm experiencing this error locally and in one of my [GH Actions](https://github.com/schoulten/macro_report/actions/runs/5533292982) workflows. I'm not sure if it's due to the latest `renv` update (1.0.0) because I noticed it started happening after this commit ([#11a22a9](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/commit/11a22a908006c25fe054c4ef0ac0436b1de3edbe)).

I tried to create a reproducible example of what's happening in the workflow above. I believe the problem is installing a newer version of `renv` and activating the project without restarting the session (if I restart, the error doesn't occur). However, the [setup-renv](https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v2/setup-renv) action seems to install a new version of renv and activate the project without restarting the session. And so I'm stuck with this error.

Here's the reproducible example:

```
# console
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_version("renv", "0.16.0")
```
Create an R file with any code, for example:

```
library(ggplot2)
print(head(ggplot2::economics_long))
```

And then continue with:

```
# console
renv::init()
renv::status()
renv::snapshot() # y
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_version("renv", "1.0.0")
renv::activate()
.rs.restartR()
```

After the last command, to restart the session, this error will be displayed:
```
# Error in eval(quote({ : object '..version..' not found
```

I apologize if the issue is not with `renv` but with the action.

title: [renv 1.0.0] restore(prompt = FALSE) does not respect prompt parameter in profile with default snapshot settings
description:

title: IRkernel dependency not properly recognised
description:
I'm currently struggling to move a project of mine from my local computer to the universities jupyter lab server and I think I might have spotted a bug.

I already stumbled across #929 and that is also happening on my system, but I think the issue is not fully resolved. When I create a `.ipynb` file, `renv::status()` recognises `IRKernel` is needed, but the package `IRKernel` (upper case "K") does not exists and is not installable. The package is actually called `IRkernel` (with a lower case "k"). I can install `IRkernel` (lower case "k"), but `renv::status()` still shows the `IRKernel` (upper case "K") package as missing dependency.

title: renv::dependencies(... quiet=TRUE) errs; no NEWS
description:
``` r
renv::dependencies(path=getwd(),root=getwd(),quiet=TRUE)
#> Error in renv_dependencies_impl(path = path, root = root, progress = progress, : unused argument (quiet = TRUE)
```

The removal of this option is not mentioned in NEWS.

Called from packrat: https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/blob/main/R/dependencies.R#L182

title: inconsistent handling of Remotes in DESCRIPTION when installing vs discovering dependencies
description:
Consider a local R package with the following `DESCRIPTION` file:

```r
Package: renvdescriptiontest
Type: Package
Title: What the Package Does (Title Case)
Version: 0.1.0
Author: Who wrote it
Maintainer: The package maintainer <yourself@somewhere.net>
Description: More about what it does (maybe more than one line)
    Use four spaces when indenting paragraphs within the Description.
License: What license is it under?
Encoding: UTF-8
LazyData: true
Imports:
  glue
Remotes:
  tidyverse/glue
```

for whatever reason, the `DESCRIPTION` here indicates that we want to use the GitHub version of `glue`. If you start a fresh RStudio project (R package) *without* `renv` and then do `renv::install(".")`, the `Remotes` field in the `DESCRIPTION` is respected:

Installing renvdescriptiontest [0.1.0] ...
	OK [built from source in 0.73 seconds]
* Installed 2 packages in 4.1 seconds.

A further inconvenience is that once a CRAN package is installed, neither `renv::update(packages = "glue")` nor `renv::install(".")` will retrieve the development version of `glue` from GitHub. 

Also, I noticed that if a package is only available on GitHub then `renv::init()` will not install it. Is there perhaps a good reason for this behavior that I'm missing? :sweat_smile:

title: `renv_retrieve_git_impl` and Windows don't play well together
description:
Hi,

when using renv on Windows with a package dependency on gitlab, I encounter the following error when trying to restore a particular commit:
```r
renv::restore()
#> Cloning '****' ...
#> error: remote origin already exists.
#> Error: error cloning '****' from '*****.git' [status code 3]
```

I suspect that error message comes up because
1) renv creates a temporary folder (where the cloned repository is supposed to be placed)
2) a "cd" command is used to change the working directory to that folder
3) it is assumed that "cd" actually always changes the directory correctly
4) `git init` and friends are called.

In my case, the project folder and the temporary folder happen to live on two different "drives"[1] on my Windows machine. Windows seems to have this unexpected behavior, that if the argument to "cd" is a path in another "drive", the working directory is not changed unless a separate "<D>:" command is used to explicitly change the "working drive".
I think that in my case that leads to the working drive not to change at all, and `renv` effectively tries to execute `git init` in the actual project folder, including setting the remote origin, which in this case already exists and is set. This leads to the error above.

A possible fix would be to add the "/d" argument to "cd" on Windows, which should change the working directory regardless of the active drive.

[1] because I lack a better name: By "drive" I mean the Windows "root directories" which typically are named by capital letters, like "C:", etc.

title: renv behavior when restoring projects containing unavailable sources in lock file
description:
During a customer call, we were chatting about the expected `renv` behavior in the following scenario:

1. User creates a project with `renv` in environment **A**. Environment **A** also has an instance of Posit Package Manager and is used as the primary repo.
2. Environment **A** is decommissioned, and the users need to switch to another environment (**B**). Notably, the **A** Package Manager is no longer accessible. 
3. If a user `renv::restore()`'s an **A** project within the **B** environment, what would be the expected behavior?

**Possible Outcomes**
* `restore()` fails but prints a helpful message letting the user know the lock file source is not accessible.
* `renv` prints a message letting the user know the source is not accessible but then searches the active repositories for the correct packages/versions.
* `restore()` fails and requires the user to supply an accessible URL/source in the `repos` argument.

title: Renv and reticulate compatibility
description:
```
> renv::use_python(type = 'conda')
+ "[conda_root]/x64/condabin/conda.bat" "create" "--yes" "--prefix" "[project_root]/renv/python/condaenvs/renv-python" "python=3.7" "--quiet" "-c" "conda-forge"
Collecting package metadata (current_repodata.json): ...working... done
[...]
* Activated Python 3.7.12 [conda; ./renv/python/condaenvs/renv-python]
* Project '[project_root]' loaded. [renv 0.17.3]
> reticulate::py_config()
python:         [python_root]/x64/python.exe
libpython:     [python_root]/x64/python39.dll
pythonhome:     [python_root]/x64
version:        3.9.16 (main, Mar  8 2023, 10:39:24) [MSC v.1916 64 bit (AMD64)]
Architecture:   64bit
numpy:           [NOT FOUND]

NOTE: Python version was forced by RETICULATE_PYTHON
```

A few questions for default `renv` use:
1) Why use `[project_root]/renv/python/condaenvs/renv-python` as default? New versions of `renv` place everything in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` or [path overrides](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/paths.html).
2) Why 3.7 by default and only overridable by `RENV_CONDA_PYTHON_VERSION`??
2) It is stated that "Activated Python 3.7.12", but when you look what `reticulate` is using, it is the system python version. I have never set `RETICULATE_PYTHON`: `renv` does it on startup! I have only set `RENV_PYTHON`.
4) If I don't set `RENV_PYTHON` then it should mean that I want `renv` to ignore python. But still, `renv` sets `RETICULATE_MINICONDA_PYTHON_ENVPATH`. Why, and why this specific environment variable among a plethora of others?
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/3eb85a762ab2bbdd9aae6e0a4d6be17f9ddd42e4/R/load.R#L507-L509
 

Using `reticulate_1.20` and `renv_0.17.3`.

title: Changes to `renv.pretty.print.emitter`
description:
The vetiver package vendors all of renv, and I recently updated to the dev version of renv as outlined in #1253. I have this function that is used to report to users how their current packages are different from their model's packages (for a specific subset of packages relevant to making predictions):

```r
renv_report_actions <- function(current, model) {
    withr::local_options(
        list(renv.pretty.print.emitter = function(text, ...) {cli::cli_inform(text)})
    )
    diff <- renv$renv_lockfile_diff_packages(current, model)

    if (renv$empty(diff))
        return(invisible(NULL))

    lhs <- renv$renv_records(current)
    rhs <- renv$renv_records(model)
    renv$renv_pretty_print_records_pair(
        lhs[names(lhs) %in% names(diff)],
        rhs[names(rhs) %in% names(diff)],
        "The following package(s) do not match your model:",
        "Consider installing the same versions that your model was trained with."
    )

}
```

Everything in here works up to using `renv_pretty_print_records_pair()` (`diff`, `lhs`, and `rhs` are all correct) but then nothing is printed or returned.

The new version of renv doesn't have `renv.pretty.print.emitter` anymore and I am struggling with how to get similar output to what I had before, or actually any output at all now from `renv_pretty_print_records_pair()`. What would be an approach that gets me something similar to what I am doing currently?

title: snapshot(exclude = "myPackage") failure
description:
The 'exclude' parameter in renv::snapshot() doesn't exclude a local package.

I'm writing a shiny app as a package ("golemDeploy", built with {golem}) and am having some problems using snapshot.

There is a top-level `./app.R` file, that is required to start the app after deployment on a Connect server.
It looks like this:

```
pkgload::load_all(export_all = FALSE,helpers = FALSE,attach_testthat = FALSE)
options( "golem.app.prod" = TRUE)
golemDeploy::run_app()
```

Now, I don't want {golemDeploy} to be included in the renv.lock for this project. So I'm using `renv::snapshot(exclude = "golemDeploy")`. But snapshot fails in two different ways here:

When `golemDeploy` is not installed locally, snapshot fails because that package isn't installed (which seems odd since I've asked for that package to be excluded)

```r
> renv::snapshot(exclude = "golemDeploy")
The following required packages are not installed:

	golemDeploy

Packages must first be installed before `renv` can snapshot them.
Consider installing these packages using `renv::install()`.
Use `renv::dependencies()` to see where this package is used in your project.
```

When golemDeploy is installed locally, snapshot states that it will be updating that package in the renv.lock even though I've asked for it to be excluded. (Proceeding here means that an renv.lock is written, but golemDeploy is not included in the renv.lock, contrary to what the message implies)

```r
> # when golemDeploy is installed locally:
> renv::snapshot(exclude = "golemDeploy")
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# (Unknown Source) ===================
- golemDeploy   [0.0.0.9000 -> *]

Do you want to proceed? [y/N]:
```

(Admittedly, I can just remove the `golemDeploy::` prefix from the app.R file, but it seems like there is a bug with 'exclude' in renv::snapshot() here)

title: MRAN is getting deprecated
description:
MRAN will [shutdown on 1st of July](https://mran.microsoft.com). Therefore, I would propose to change the default value for the config `renv.config.mran.enabled` to `FALSE` and also remove the MRAN functionality completely once the service has shutdown.

In addition, MRAN is down now for a few days so that the installation from MRAN is not working, anyway.

The problem with leaving this config on by default is that renv, when installing a package, will wait for MRAN to answer and timeout only after a few seconds. This is a problem when you want to install a large amount of packages and renv will wait for the timeout for every package...

Do you agree with this assessment?

description:
```

Downloading 24 package(s) and their dependencies

In one of my scripts I have `box::use(app/helpers[foo])`, which loads a the `foo()` function from the file `app/helpers.R`.

Whenever I start a session and renv initiates, I get a warning that the package `app` is used in this project but not installed.
As `app` is a local module and not a package, it cannot be installed, instead I expect renv to not detect it as a package.


To reproduce this, you can use this:

dir.create("app")
writeLines("#' @export\nfoo <- function() 1\n", "app/helpers")

Having the latest renv version installed locally (0.17.3), I tried to restore a repo with renv 0.12.5, which is over a year old. This did not work and I got:

    * Installing renv 0.12.5 ... Done!
    * Successfully installed and loaded renv 0.12.5.

    Calls: source ... eval -> <Anonymous> -> renv_load_switch -> warningf
    Traceback (most recent calls last):
    20: source("renv/activate.R")

    14: eval(expr, p)
