title: Replace MRAN integration with PPM integration
description:
Given the impending shutdown of [MRAN](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/azure-sql-blog/microsoft-r-application-network-retirement/ba-p/3707161), we'll want to:

- Disable the existing MRAN integration in `renv`;
- Consider an alternative using PPM so we can install older binaries of packages.

Currently, `renv` maintains a database mapping package versions to the latest MRAN snapshot that provides that package. Fortunately, this shouldn't be necessary with PPM; if you try to install an archived package, PPM will quietly give you a binary from the last snapshot that had binaries available for that package.

We'll want this to be part of the next `renv` release in June, so that this can become available before the MRAN servers are officially shut down.

title: renv::install with explicit dependencies = Imports still installs Suggests
description:
If I'm trying to install "active project", suggested packages get installed even when I explicitly only request `Imports` to be installed.  The following code seems to be responsible:

```R
  # if this is the DESCRIPTION file for the active project, include
  # Suggests since they're often needed as well. such packages will be
  # considered development dependencies, except for package projects
  type <- "unknown"
  project <-
    project %||%
    renv_dependencies_state(key = "root") %||%
    renv_project_resolve()

  if (renv_path_same(file.path(project, "DESCRIPTION"), path)) {

    # collect profile-specific dependencies as well
    profile <- renv_profile_get()
    field <- if (length(profile))
      sprintf("Config/renv/profiles/%s/dependencies", profile)

    fields <- c(fields, "Suggests", field)
    type <- renv_description_type(desc = dcf)

  }
```

Basically, now if I want to really only install `Imports` packages, I have to use some renv internals to generate a list of the dependencies and then filter out the "dev" dependencies (also I have to set `Type` in description to some bogus value so the type is not "package").

This behaviour is very unintuitive and is not documented anywhere in `install`.  I think when user explicitly passes the dependencies parameter, nothing should happen to it and it should be taken as-is.

title: renv_pak_restore tries to move packages to cache instead of installing from cache
description:
I think the following code in `pak.R` function `renv_pak_restore`

```
  # attempt to link packages that have cache entries
  if (renv_cache_config_enabled(project = project)) {
    linked <- map_lgl(records, renv_cache_synchronize)
    records <- records[!linked]
  }
```

links the installed packages into the cache, not the other way around.  Looking at `renv::install`, it calls 

```R
 if (cacheable) {

    # check for cache entry and install if there
    path <- renv_cache_find(record)
    if (renv_cache_package_validate(path))
      return(renv_install_package_cache(record, path, linker))

  }
``` 

to install packages from cache.

But the code in `renv_pak_restore` is called *before* 

```R
# perform installation
  pak$pkg_install(remotes)
```

so in effect there is nothing for it to sync into the cache?

title: If a package has no requirements, renv should still record empty array
description:
There is a package called `sodium` which has no declared dependencies.  The `renv.lock` record is

```json
"sodium": {
      "Package": "sodium",
      "Version": "1.2.1",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "3606bb09e0914edd4fc8313b500dcd5e"
    }
```

Notabely, the `"Requirements"` key is missing.  This causes some problems with parsing the requirements with e.g. `records <- renv:::renv_lockfile_records(renv:::renv_lockfile_load(project = NULL))`, the entry for `sodium` is `NULL`.

I'm using these internals to achieve some "better" installation behaviour with `pak` (will report the issues if I figure out how feasable it is what I'm doing).  However, I feel like the issue here is reasonable always.

I went through `lockfile-read.R` but I don't understand where exactly the reading fails and produces NA key and NULL "body".  Following is a screenshot of the output of the above `records <- ...`

![image](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/assets/2664959/83bc23f7-922d-467a-b1f4-cd14127cc415)

title: Why aren't packages installed with pak synchronized to renv cache?
description:
I don't know all the internals but by going through the code, calling the following seems to take the `pak` installed packages (that is, `renv::install` with `renv.config.pak.enabled` set to `TRUE`) and move them to the `renv` cache.

```R
records <- renv:::renv_snapshot_libpaths(libpaths = renv:::renv_libpaths_resolve(NULL), project = renv:::renv_project_resolve(NULL))
purrr::map(records, \(x) renv:::renv_cache_synchronize(x, linkable = TRUE))
```

Wouldn't it make sense to move the installed packages to the renv cache?

title: Make pak upgrade option configurable
description:
Currently, it seems renv calls pak with this code

```R
  pak$pkg_install(
    pkg     = packages,
    lib     = lib,
    upgrade = TRUE
  )
```

I think having to always `upgrade` is a bit too "agressive".  In some cases I would like to only add packages and not upgrade what is not necessary.

Would it be possible to expose this as an option, either to `renv::install` (maybe through `...` or as some `.parameter`) or as `option` for config?

title: `install` writes DESCRIPTION that is not in valid DCF format for some packages
description:
I have noticed that a change made between versions 0.17.2 and 0.17.3 is causing `renv::install` to write DESCRIPTION files with additional blank lines for some packages. This causes R to return an error stating that the "DESCRIPTION is not in valid DCF format" when looking up the help documentation for functions in the affected packages.

The issue seems to occur when the Title or Remotes element contains a long string, unbroken by spaces, that spans the 80th character in the line.

I have prepared an example package to demonstrate the issue here: https://github.com/jistria/exampledesc

```R
# Install example package.
renv::install("jistria/exampledesc")

# Attempt to open function help documentation.
?exampledesc::example_function
# Error : file '<library path>/exampledesc/DESCRIPTION' is not in valid DCF format
```

Taking a look at the DESCRIPTION file in the installed package, in a text editor, we see that there are unexpected blank lines:

```
Package: exampledesc
Title: What the Package Does (One Line, Title Case) This Title Is

    LongerThanMost
```

The issue does not occur when the package is installed using renv 0.17.2. 

The remotes in the DESCRIPTION file are contrived for the purpose of the example. In my real package the remotes detail the location of packages on an instance of GitLab that my organisation manages, and do get that long largely due to the inclusion of the host.

title: bioconductor = TRUE doesn't actually work
description:
```
R: 4.3.0
renv: 0.17.3-51
BiocManager: 1.30.20 (already installed in system library)
OS: Pop!OS 22.04 (Ubuntu based Linux)
```

* What I see in a brand new project:

```r
renv::init(bioconductor = TRUE)
```

```
* Discovering package dependencies ... Done!
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# GitHub =============================
- renv   [* -> rstudio/renv@HEAD]

The version of R recorded in the lockfile will be updated:
- R      [* -> 4.3.0]

* Lockfile written to '~/Projects/personal/test_renv/renv.lock'.
exiting from: renv::init(bioconductor = TRUE)

Restarting R session...
````

* What I expect to see:

```
* Using Bioconductor version 3.17
```

And the `renv.lock` file does not contain a Bioconductor version either.

Debugging `renv::init`, `biocver` remains `NULL` throughout the entire function.

Loading `BiocManager` before `renv` doesn't seem to help.

I can get `renv_bioconductor_init()` to return `TRUE` after I do:

```r
renv::init()
renv::install("BiocManager")
renv:::renv_bioconductor_init()
# TRUE
```

But that doesn't help in actually getting the version of Bioconductor recorded in the lockfile.

Looking at the logic in `renv:::renv_bioconductor_init()`, I think the problem is that `BiocManager` isn't yet installed in the local `renv` library, but it can't be installed there yet because the library was just made. Shouldn't `renv` be checking that `BiocManager` is installed in the system library instead, and warning the user to do that first?

title: Export `renv:::unload()`?
description:
For some applications, we might want to use `renv::load()` to explicitly load a renv environment/profile. It would be nice to also have access to the inverse operation `renv::unload()`.
`renv::deactivate()` works but can be a bit too invasive, as it also restarts the R session along with some other side effects.

IMO, having `renv::unload()` would be useful e.g. in testing to temporarily load a renv environment, allowing something like

```r
project <- "project-path"
withr::defer(renv::unload(project))
renv::load(project)
...
```

Thank you for considering this!

title: load binary packages ahead of use
description:
Installing binary packages can often hide problems with an environment until runtime.

Take, for example, the `Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM rstudio/r-base:4.3-jammy

RUN apt-get update && apt-get -y install pkg-config

ARG REPOSITORYhttps://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest
RUN R -s -e "install.packages('rjags', repos=c(CRAN='${REPOSITORY}'))"
RUN R -s -e "library(rjags)"
```

Building this image:

```bash
docker build \
    --progress=plain \
    --no-cache -f Dockerfile.renv .
```

This example errs because the `library` statement fails to load the `rjags` package (because `jags` is missing).

```
#7 [4/4] RUN R -s -e "library(rjags)"
#7 0.385 Loading required package: coda
#7 0.427 Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘rjags’:
#7 0.427  .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rjags', details:
#7 0.427   call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
#7 0.427   error: unable to load shared object '/opt/R/4.3.0/lib/R/library/rjags/libs/rjags.so':
#7 0.427   libjags.so.4: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
#7 0.427 Execution halted
#7 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c R -s -e \"library(rjags)\"" did not complete successfully: exit code: 1
```

This same situation can be seen with renv:

```dockerfile
FROM rstudio/r-base:4.3-jammy

RUN apt-get update && apt-get -y install pkg-config

ARG REPOSITORY=https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/jammy/latest

RUN mkdir /content && echo "library(rjags)" > /content/script.R

WORKDIR /content

RUN R -s -e "install.packages('renv', repos=c(CRAN='${REPOSITORY}'))"
RUN R -s -e "renv::init(bare = TRUE, repos=c(CRAN='${REPOSITORY}'))"
RUN R -s -e "renv::install('rjags', repos=c(CRAN='${REPOSITORY}'))"
RUN R -s -e "renv::snapshot()"
RUN R -s -f "script.R"
```

The error:

```
 > [9/9] RUN R -s -f "script.R":
#0 0.537 Loading required package: coda
#0 0.580 Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘rjags’:
#0 0.580  .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rjags', details:
#0 0.580   call: dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)
#0 0.580   error: unable to load shared object '/root/.cache/R/renv/cache/v5/R-4.3/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/rjags/4-14/dc00e7bcbec8cd953930ec12fc9c8819/rjags/libs/rjags.so':
#0 0.580   libjags.so.4: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
#0 0.580 Execution halted
```

Part of this is rooted in how R handles package installation: The `R CMD install` command installs source and binary packages differently.

R CMD install source/binary switch:
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/3a15e29d1b5a94e06b99cb9315c562fd8f71bc5b/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L419-L422

R CMD install package load test (inside do_install_source):
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/3a15e29d1b5a94e06b99cb9315c562fd8f71bc5b/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L1814-L1852
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/3a15e29d1b5a94e06b99cb9315c562fd8f71bc5b/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L1854-L1861

R CMD install do_install_binary does not attempt load:
https://github.com/wch/r-source/blob/3a15e29d1b5a94e06b99cb9315c562fd8f71bc5b/src/library/tools/R/install.R#L480-L502

When first added, only to the source path (and used library, not external process):
https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/7bc912f48ad621d223bf26106d8e4ddcf405921a

Could renv attempt to validate binary packages by loading them before finalizing the installation? That would let us identify problems at restore-time rather than downstream when running the content.

title: Soft deprecate `equip()`?
improve handling of orphaned locks in available packages index
description:
`renv` uses a helper `index()` function for the available packages index, basically allowing the retrieved copy of available packages to be shared across time and across processes. This helps avoid some painful slowness when retrieving available packages is slow, especially in a session that is restarted often.

A simple reproducible example:

```
local({
  renv:::renv_scope_lock("test")
  tools:::pskill(Sys.getpid(), 9L)
})
```

You'll end up with an orphaned lock which cannot be recovered. The best option I can think of (currently) would be to spawn a separate watchdog process that waits until the R session exits, and then deletes the lockfile if it exists and was owned by that process.

Then, each process could generate a unique key (UUID?) on startup, use that key when taking ownership of a lock, and also let the watchdog know about that key so that if the watchdog sees the process exits, it could check if the lock exists with that key and remove it if so.

title: `init()` should append to `.Rprofile`
description:

Given an `.Rprofile`


This file is modified to:

```r
source("renv/activate.R")
parentDir <- dirname(getwd())
cacheDir <- file.path(parentDir, "cache")
Sys.setenv(RENV_PATHS_CACHE = cacheDir)
```

To workaround this, I'm doing something like the following:

```r
renv::init(
  bare = TRUE,
  settings = list(
  ),
  repos = c(CRAN = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest")
)

# Make sure we are using our isolated cache.
writeLines(
  c(
    "parentDir <- dirname(getwd())",
    "cacheDir <- file.path(parentDir, \"cache\")",
    "Sys.setenv(RENV_PATHS_CACHE = cacheDir)",
    "Sys.setenv(RENV_RSPM_ENABLED = 'false')",
    "source(\"renv/activate.R\")"
  ),
  ".Rprofile"
)
```

title: recommended packages and renv
description:
We have a set up where we have a validated rspm with a suite of packages. This does not include the recommended/base packages, which are pre-installed on the system.

The intention is that users should be using only this validated rpsm, with a line in their RProfile specifying their snapshot, such as:

`options("repos" = c("Validated" = "https://rspm.com/Validated-4.1/2023-05-02"))`

Currently this does not include base or recommended packages, which are in the system library. As these are typically distributed with R we thought this is appropriate.

Unfortunately this approach seems incompatible with how renv currently works. Renv will snapshot the recommended packages (if in the dependency tree), and then try to install them from rspm and fail. Ignoring these packages doesn't work, and neither does trying to add a global cache pointing at the system library (renv auto appends a system specific path to it, which doesn't seem to be a behaviour I can disable). I can't source these as local libraries as they are compiled, and renv needs tar.gz files.

It seems like my only solution here is adding the recommended packages to my rspm snapshot. This is something I can do, but it does seem like renv should be able to support my use case. 

Perhaps I am missing some setting here to enable me to do this?

title: Functions to transform Package Manager URLs from source to binary and binary to source
description:
`renv` already contains code to transform Posit Package Manager URLs for different platforms. It'd be helpful to have functions that perform the following actions on a repo URL:

- transform a binary URL, with path segments like `__linux__/bionic`, into a source URL by stripping those segments;
- transform a source URL into a binary URL by adding the appropriate segments for the platform, if any.

The functions should only operate on Package Manager URLs; all other URLs should be returned unchanged.

title: `renv` Cache Size + Deleting `source`s in Cache Safely
description:
Hey Kevin!

We've been following [the approach laid out in this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/826) for slimming down our Docker images by deleting clones of the Git repos for already-installed packages by using `rm -rf /.local/share/renv` to get rid of often multiple GB of files.

I'm working on upgrading off of `v0.13.2` and it appears that at least as of `v0.15.0` (and maybe higher), this approach doesn't work anymore. 

Nowadays, after running that `rm ...`, the _next_ (read: not the current run, but the run of our CI _after_ trying to restore the cache the first time) fails with an error that looks like the following:

```r
The following package(s) will be updated:

# GitHub =============================
- renvtest   [* -> collegevine/renv-test:renvtest]

Error in file(con, "rb") : cannot open the connection
Calls: <Anonymous> ... renv_dcf_read -> %||% -> renv_dcf_read_impl -> readBin -> file
In addition: Warning message:
In file(con, "rb") :
  cannot open file '/root/.cache/R/renv/cache/v5/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renvtest/0.0.0.9000/4add73f37c9efdc342b8496a1e42ec2f/renvtest/renvtest/DESCRIPTION': No such file or directory
Traceback (most recent calls last):
14: renv::restore()
13: renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile, rebuild)
12: retrieve(packages)
11: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
10: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
 9: renv_retrieve_successful(record, path)
 8: renv_description_read(path, subdir = subdir)
 7: filebacked(scope = "DESCRIPTION", path = path, callback = renv_description_read_impl, 
        subdir = subdir, ...)
 6: callback(path, ...)
 5: renv_dcf_read(path, ...)
 4: text %||% renv_dcf_read_impl(file, ...)
 3: renv_dcf_read_impl(file, ...)
 2: readBin(con = file, what = "raw", n = renv_file_size(file))
 1: file(con, "rb")
```

Note than in this example, `renvtest` is a minimal (no deps) package living in a private repo, which I'm installing with `renv::install("collegevine/renv-test:renvtest")` after setting my `GITHUB_PAT` environment variable.

I'm going to upload a tarball to this issue with a stable repro. To run it, you'll need to:

1. Open the `repro` project.
2. Edit the `library(renvtest)` line in `test.R` to load whatever package from a private library you choose. You can also make a private repo from the `renvtest` package in the tarball, and then open the `repro` R project in the tarball and use `renv::install("kevinushey/renv-test:renvtest")` (assuming your repo is called `renv-test` like mine is.
3. Overwrite my lockfile in `repro` with `renv::snapshot()`
4. Run `docker build --build-arg GITHUB_PAT=<< your Github PAT >> -t foo .` to build the image.
5. Run `docker run foo` to run the image, which will run the `repro.sh` to give you the same error as I'm seeing.
6. If you're curious, you can edit the Dockerfile and the lockfile to use `renv 0.13.2` and then run the build + run again, and you'll see that the package correctly restores with that version.

So on to the question: Now that I seemingly can't safely just nuke that directory, what's the best way to keep our Docker images slim after many, many CI runs that cache lots of incremental updates to many internal libraries? I'd really love to be able to avoid saving the large files, and would even more love to not need to manually cache evict often.

One note: This is actually a potentially breaking issue in production for us (and presumably others). The issue is that if our Docker images get too big, they'll build in our CI just fine, but Heroku's container boot process scales (probably sub-linearly, but unsure) with the size of the image being booted. And Heroku has a boot timeout. Which means that it's possible that if we have an image that contains an API that's supposed to be run on Heroku, that API could fail to boot seemingly at random once the image size hit some threshold, as a result of the cache getting bigger and bigger over time.

Here's the tarball with the repro that I used! I'll leave some comments in the code with pointers for what to edit.

[renv-test.zip](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/11427062/renv-test.zip)


Thanks a bunch!! And thanks so much for all of your work on `renv` too -- it's a really awesome package :)

title: renv::status() shold not give "out-of-sync" warning when additional packages have been captured with renv::snapshot(type = "all")
description:
In my project it is sometimes necessary to capture more packages in the `renv.lock` than I currently use in my existing scripts. For example, when I already know that I will use additional packages in the near future. For this I use `renv::snapshot(type = "all")`.

In `renv::status()` I get a warning that the project is out-of-sync. In my opinion this unnecessary, at least at start-up. The check should rather be if all packages versions match the lock file.

title: Change the default behavior to `RENV_PATHS_PREFIX_AUTO=TRUE`
description:
By default, `renv` creates caches that are used (in an incompatible fashion) across differing linux OSes

By setting `RENV_PATHS_PREFIX_AUTO=TRUE`, this can be remedied for different linux operating systems. We should do this by default so that starting projects on different operating systems "just works" on `renv` (modulo package rebuilding).

There may be ways to mitigate a one-time breakage with existing project options, one-time symlinks, etc.

title: `renv_settings_migrate()` only called from exported function `renv::load()`
description:
In our case, we heavily rely on `renv` for dependency management in package 
development and CI/CD with Gitlab
(more or less following the suggestions in https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/ci.html).

Up to `renv` v0.16.0 our process was to create/update the `renv/settings.dcf` 
especially for keeping the `snapshot.type = "explicit"` and for handling the list of ignored packages (e.g. those just needed for package development like pkgbuild, rcmdcheck, etc.)

Each time before we pushed new changes to Gitlab, we called `renv::snapshot()` to update the `renv.lock` file (taking into account the `renv/settings.dcf`).

With the move to `renv/settings.json`, our settings (in the dcf file) 
are not used any longer, and the automatic migration (as stated in the release 
notes) only works within `renv::load()`, which we don't use.

Would it be possible to add the automatic conversion (or a hint for it) to 
the functions `status()` and `snapshot()`, or maybe export `renv_settings_migrate`?

Thanks, Christoph

description:

At the moment, these custom packages are just saved in a folder, for example, C:\R Custom Packages\my_package_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz. My custom packages are work-specific, so they will never end up on CRAN or a public repo.

When using `renv::restore()`, I get output like

```
The following package(s) were installed from an unknown source:
```

title: [Feature Request]: Update only when binaries available across platforms/repositories
description:
A frequent challenge I find with `renv` is that, when working on a project that is collaborative across users with different operating systems, or using CI, is that a package may be updated by one user, but then not be available for another user or CI system.  For instance, one might install a package locally on OSX, and find than when the CI installs on Linux, it is not yet available via RSPM.  (Given that for the same package, one might use different repositories to get binaries for different OSs).  For a project with a large number of packages, this is not a rare event. 

I wonder if it would be possible to put some constraints on `install()` and `update()` that would only install packages up to the version that is available as binaries across operating systems for a set of repositories.

title: 0.17.2 cannot provision loaded packages from .libPaths() during hydration
description:
EDIT: This bug has been solved: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/1177#issuecomment-1483295938 A demonstration of the bug and solution can be found in https://github.com/zkamvar/renv-issue-1177 -------------- \*heavy sigh\* I'm sorry, Kevin. I really am, but I'm having yet another issue that only occurs on GitHub Actions and I _have_ been able to get it to trigger locally, but to do that, I need to [control renv projects from a renv project](https://github.com/carpentries/lesson-transition/issues/18) and I'm trying to wrap my head around how to make it minimal and understandable. ## Background I use {renv} to facilitate package discovery while avoiding surprises where people are unexpectedly thrown into a new package version that they are not prepared for by using a workflow that uses the following components: - `hydrate()` finds all the existing packages that may or may not be recored in the lockfile and places them in the library - `restore()` restores the package versions that have been recorded - `snapshot()` implicitly adds the packages that are now in the library that were not previously in the lockfile In practice, it allows people to rapidly develop lessons without worrying about how {renv} is working in the background (see https://carpentries.github.io/sandpaper/reference/dependency_management.html#details for human-language details and [`callr_manage_deps`](https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper/blob/514acae2412006eb3975469f3876af0b9b6da478/R/utils-renv.R#L217) for the underlying implementation). ### On GitHub I have created a github action that sets up the cache and system requirements for the dependencies at [carpentries/actions/setup-lesson-deps](https://github.com/carpentries/actions/blob/2016223347a996e689bc1e99b2565be8e93d4233/setup-lesson-deps/action.yaml). The action creates a DESCRIPTION from the lockfile to provision the system requirements and to install all the dependencies (via the {remotes} package). From there, The hydrate + restore + snapshot workflow is run. ## Setup The [zkamvar/automatic-robot](https://github.com/zkamvar/automatic-robot) repository is a lesson that has [a lockfile set to the R Markdown ecosystem](https://github.com/zkamvar/automatic-robot/blob/3d9e4e8a762a2d0f67f1aa9f8a7df252e93ef911/renv/profiles/lesson-requirements/renv.lock). A single commit (https://github.com/zkamvar/automatic-robot/commit/3d9e4e8a762a2d0f67f1aa9f8a7df252e93ef911) has been added to include `library("reprex")` inside of the lesson. Under normal circumstances, running `sandpaper::manage_deps()` or the above GitHub action would recognise that {reprex} has been added and make sure to install it. ## Problem The [workflow fails with {renv} 0.17.2](https://github.com/zkamvar/urban-succotash/actions/runs/4493152698/jobs/7903987389) on the [snapshot step](https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper/blob/514acae2412006eb3975469f3876af0b9b6da478/R/utils-renv.R#L280-L292) due to a validation error: ``` The following required packages are not installed: callr [required by reprex] clipr [required by reprex] rstudioapi [required by reprex] withr [required by reprex] Consider reinstalling these packages before snapshotting the lockfile. --- Backtrace: 1. sandpaper::manage_deps(path = wd, quiet = FALSE) 2. callr::r(func = callr_manage_deps, args = args, show = !quiet, … 3. callr:::get_result(output = out, options) 4. callr:::throw(callr_remote_error(remerr, output), parent = fix_msg(remerr[[3]])) --- Subprocess backtrace: 1. renv::snapshot(project = path, lockfile = renv_lock, prompt = FALSE) 2. base::stop("aborting snapshot due to pre-flight validation failure") 3. | base::.handleSimpleError(function (e) … 4. global h(simpleError(msg, call)) Execution halted ``` During the [hydrate step](https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper/blob/514acae2412006eb3975469f3876af0b9b6da478/R/utils-renv.R#L240-L258), the reprex package is detected and an attempt to install it is made: ``` Finding R package dependencies ... Done! * Discovering package dependencies ... Done! The following packages were discovered: # ~/work/_temp/Library =============== [ ... snip 30 packages ...] They will be linked into the project library. * Linking packages into the project library ... title: stuck while renv::restore() a newly deployed shiny app in a dockerized shiny server setup - azure file share as host site dir
description:
We have below setup in azure to deploy shiny apps:

- **Azure web services** to deploy shiny server containerized.
- in shiny server config we have customized the host location to a mounted azure file share. `site_dir /shinyapps;` So we can continuously deploy the shiny apps any time and it is working awesome. like put app folder in azure file share and it gets available immediately. 
-  Last piece missing was the libraries that been used in deployed app might not available on shiny server so for that we are using **`renv`** .
-  So for reproducibility we are using renv in following manner:

1.  produce renv.lock file.
2.  in app folder add .Rprofile file to restore the libraries before app starts.
       .Rprofile code
        
            require(renv) 
            options(renv.consent = TRUE)  # To start the restore process without asking the permission 
            renv::restore(prompt=FALSE)   # prompt false to stop asking for user input to procced for installation.
            source("renv/activate.R")
            renv::activate()
        
3.  Upload the application folder containing app.R , renv.lock & .Rprofile to azure file share.
4.  Now when we finally access the app through the url (eg. https://abc-rshiny.azurewebsites.net/shinyapps/team_p1/shiny-dash) it does't load and get timeout. 
5. If we check the logs for the application it looks like it gets stuck after list out all library's name. we are not able figure out the issue & resolution.

title: Capture package repository url and name
description:
I'm trying to understand an interaction that seems to happen between rspm and renv. This is for renv version 0.16.0

Apologies that I can't quite make a reprex here as this relies on using an rspm instance.

Lets say I have options(repos =c("rspm/one", "rspm/two")) and install most of my packages.

In my renv.lock file I will have those two repositories listed, and for each package it will say that the source is RSPM.

Now lets say I want to install a package from "rspm/three", but I don't want to add it to my repos options; I just want to install this particular package from this source, but in future I expect to install from rspm/one and rspm/two.

My assumption was I could go:
```
renv::install("<package>", repos = "rspm/three")
renv::snapshot()
```

But while this works for the install, the resulting lock file _does not_ contain "rspm/three", either in the list of repositories or for the individual package entry. This means that if this package only exists on "rspm/three" the install will fail for other users.

How do I ensure that this works? I could manually edit the lock file to include the repository, but I'd prefer a programattic flow for this kind of action.

title: Get Gitlab host from Global Variable
description:
Hello,

I tried setting up Renv to use a private Gitlab server following [this stackoverflow post](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62772833/use-renv-for-private-gitlab-package) and [this issue](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/476).

```
options(renv.config.gitlab.host = "https://gitlab.mycompany.de")
Sys.setenv(GITLAB_PAT = "...")
```

After reading the documentation I found, that I can use Environment Variables in .Renviron instead of options.
However, the GITLAB_PAT key works, but the GITLAB_HOST option does not seem to work as it still tries to connect to `https://gitlab.com` , even though the options work. 
Does anybody else have this issue?

title: issue with non-writable available package index
description:
**Main issue:**

`renv::install("pkgname")` hangs indefinitely on `renv` >= 0.17.0 due to my non-standard setup. 

**Details:**

I have a large `renv` cache being used by many people. It's defined using the `RENV_PATHS_ROOT` environmental variable. That location is read-only* (for most users). For `renv` prior to 0.17.0 that would result in successful installs (simply a symlink) if the package existed in the cache and an error if it did not (because it can't write there).

Now, however, it seems to hang due to `renv:::available_packages`. 

I found that if I run `options(renv.index.enabled=FALSE)` the old behavior is restored. 

I'm wondering if there could be a solution where the index will automatically be used if it can succeed (maybe just a `file.access` test or something for write-ability) and disabled otherwise? Essentially to avoid having to specify this option in every project.

I realize this is probably a very uncommon setup so understand if this isn't worth it.

\* The reason my setup is like this is because we have the `renv` cache mounted to Docker environments and for technical reasons the mounts need to be read-only. There is a separate process (where the cache is writable) to add new packages.

Thanks for the awesome package!

title: renv 0.17.1 changed package hash
description:
I upgraded to 0.17.1 this morning and when I took a snapshot, it changed the hash for the vast majority of my packages. The new hash didn't align with the package path in my cache. This was pretty unexpected. 

I tried it in two separate R environments (OS, R, RStudio and renv versions [0.16.0->0.17.1, 0.17.0->0.17.1]) and it occurred with both. 

One package example was BH. It didn't happen to R6, but it did to Rcpp and many others.

title: .onLoad from user built package failing within renv
description:
I'm trying to implement renv in projects that primarily use a custom built private package ("syhelpr") to perform a variety of tasks. The package loads perfectly fine without any renv in the project environment but fails when renv is included. Additionally, the warnings in restore() seem to occur with any renv function I run:

```
> renv::restore()
* The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.
Warning messages:
1: In value[[3L]](cond) : restarting interrupted promise evaluation
2: In value[[3L]](cond) : restarting interrupted promise evaluation
> library(syhelpr)
Loading required package: foreach
Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘syhelpr’:
 .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'syhelpr', details:
  call: loadNamespace(x)
  error: there is no package called ‘reticulate’
```

This is the code causing the failure within the syhelpr package
```
sy_init <- function() {
  library(pacman)
  pacman::p_load(
    devtools,
    here,
    odbc,
    tictoc,
    lubridate,
    fuzzyjoin,
    kableExtra,
    knitr,
    htmltools,
    tidyverse,
    dbplyr
  )
}

# python's 'uuid' module we want to use in our package
uuid <- NULL

#' Config File
#'
#' Loads common packages, configurations, db connections,
#'
#'
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname){
  sy_init()
  # delay load uuid module (will only be loaded when accessed via $)
  uuid <<- reticulate::import("uuid", delay_load = TRUE)
}
```

Further, I've tried `renv::install('reticulate')` and the same error occurs, even when I specify my repositories in the user .Rprofile and the project .Rprofile (not sure if this is redunant)
```
local({
  r <- getOption("repos")
  r["CRAN"] <- "https://cloud.r-project.org" 
  r["syapse"] <- "https://private/repository/path"
  options(repos = r)
})
```

I've read through the following issue but can't make the connection as I'm relatively new to R package development:
#https://github.com/r-lib/pillar/issues/252

title: stop 'fixing' my .gitignore :-)
description:
Is there an option to prevent various {renv} functions from re-editing my `.gitignore` files?
The specific example here is as follows:
1. I have a `cellar/` (symlink to `local/` for backwards compatibility with some of my own tooling) under my `renv/` directory in a project. I.e. these directories exist:
    ```
    <project>/renv/local/
    <project>/renv/cellar/
    ```
2. In `<project>/renv/.gitignore` there are the standard entries:
    ```
    lock/
    sandbox/
    library/
    python/
    staging/
    ```
3. In this project, I choose to store my {renv} cellar _with_ the repo. Thus I've specifically removed `cellar/` and `local/` from {renv}'s standard `.gitignore` file. (I've also tried just commenting them, but {renv} is clever and undoes my comments in the next step :-)
4. At some point during the development lifecycle, {renv} (well, I assume it's {renv}) keeps **adding** the `cellar/` and `local/` entries back into my `.gitignore` file :-|  ... this means prior to each git add/commit cycle I need to edit that file, run my git commands, and then at some point in the future {renv} reverts my changes (to `.gitignore`). (Else my package tarballs which I want to commit to the repo don't get added.)

Is there any way to tell {renv} that I'm 100% okay with the current state of my `.gitignore` file and that it should (ironically?) _ignore_ it? Perhaps a config/option that changes the silent editing behavior to warnings?

title: Project always 'out-of-sync' since renv 0.17.0
description:
After upgrading to renv 0.17.0, my renv project using `snapshot.type: explicit` keeps being "out-of-sync" without any apparent reason.

The `renv/activate.R` script (or `renv:::renv_project_synchronized_check()`) just emits the message:

```
* Project '~/REDACTED' loaded. [renv 0.17.0]
* The project is currently out-of-sync.
* Use `renv::status()` for more details.
```

- `renv::status(cache = TRUE)` doesn't show any issues (i.e. invisible output).

- `renv::snapshot(repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")` says `* The lockfile is already up to date.`.

- `renv::restore()` says `* The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.`.

What's going wrong here?

title: feature request: provide method to explicitly unlock the sandbox for teardown?
description:
I think I understand the rationale for locking the sandbox in #1090, but I'm wondering if it's possible to unlock the sandbox on `renv::deactivate()` or if there could be an explicit method to do so? 

I'm in a situation where I have to build and tear down renv environments often and the locked sandbox means that I'm often faced with situations where I have to use `sudo rm -rf` to clean up.

```json
        "R"
      ],

    },
    (... truncated ...)
```

However, immediately after trying to restore BH, I get the following error:

```
#0 32.60 Retrieving 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/survival/survival_3.5-0.tar.gz' ...
#0 40.40 	OK [downloaded 6 Mb in 7.8 seconds]
#0 40.67 Retrieving 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/BH_1.81.0-1.tar.gz' ...
#0 52.38 	OK [downloaded 13.3 Mb in 12 seconds]
#0 53.69 Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called 'BiocManager'
#0 53.69 Calls: <Anonymous> ... loadNamespace -> withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> doWithOneRestart
#0 53.70 Traceback (most recent calls last):
#0 53.70 15: renv::restore()
#0 53.70 14: renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile, rebuild)
#0 53.70 13: retrieve(packages)
#0 53.70 12: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
#0 53.70 11: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
#0 53.70 10: renv_scope_bioconductor(project = project)
#0 53.70  9: renv_bioconductor_repos(project = project, version = version)
#0 53.70  8: renv_bioconductor_repos_biocmanager(version)
#0 53.70  7: asNamespace("BiocManager")
#0 53.70  6: getNamespace(ns)
#0 53.70  5: loadNamespace(name)
#0 53.70  4: withRestarts(stop(cond), retry_loadNamespace = function() NULL)
#0 53.70  3: withOneRestart(expr, restarts[[1L]])
#0 53.70  2: doWithOneRestart(return(expr), restart)
#0 53.70  1: stop(cond)
#0 53.70 Execution halted
```

The only way I have been able to resolve it is by explicitly installing BiocManager before running `renv::restore()` in docker:

```dockerfile
COPY renv.lock renv.lock
RUN Rscript -e 'install.packages("remotes", repos="http://cran.r-project.org"); install.packages("BiocManager",repos="http://cran.r-project.org"); install.packages("renv",repos="http://cran.r-project.org"); renv::restore()'

```

Obviously, this is not really desirable - I am wondering what changed between 0.16.0 and 0.17.0 that would result in this behavior and if it is intended? 

One footnote to make here is that I do not explicitly set up the library paths as outlined in the article on the use of renv with docker (https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/docker.html): it has never been needed and I have built many functional images/containers with just running `renv::restore() `as such.

title: What part of renv infrastucture needs to be backed up to ensure reproducibility?
description:
Hi Kevin,

Our HPC administrators have advised me that the `renv/` subdirectories we have for our projects are causing the HPC backup system some grief (it basically doesn't like lots of directories with lots of small files).
Each project is its own R project with `renv/` subdirectory and we have hundreds of such projects.

I'm looking for a solution so that I continue to happily use **renv** and make life easier for our HPC admin.

One idea is to tar the `renv` directory once a project is no longer being actively analysed.
But that's a manual process to tar/untar that I can imagine might get forgotten and cause some grief to people interacting with the project or managing its backup.

I then wondered if it was sufficient to backup just the `renv.lock` file or some other small set of files?
Could you please advise the minimal set of **renv**-related files required to ensure reproducibility of an analysis.

Thanks,
Pete

title: renv.config.synchronized.check ... what does it do?
description:
In earlier versions of {renv}, my recollection is that if `renv.config.synchronized.check` was enabled, upon project startup (i.e. R startup within that project), if the lockfile and library were out-of-sync, we'd receive the customary "may be out of sync" warning.
After upgrading to 0.16.0, however, I found long scan times (#1152) and then expected warnings (because I happened to know my library and lockfile are not synchronized) but received none.

To test this behavior:
1. I created a brand new empty project and ran `renv::init()`. The lockfile thus included on the R and {renv} versions.
2. Restart R to properly activate the {renv} project.
3. I then created a R file and added the single `library(Matrix)` line, and within the R session ran `renv::install("Matrix")`. Importantly **do not** `renv::snapshot()` and ensure that `renv.config.auto.snapshot` is ` FALSE`. Double-check the `renv.lock` file to ensure that indeed {Matrix} is not included. Inspect the project's `renv/library/{R-version}/{arch}/` directory to ensure that {Matrix} is installed. At this point the library and the lockfile are out-of-sync.
4. Quit and restart R with `renv.config.synchronized.check` set to TRUE in the project's `.Rprofile`.
5. No warning :-| 

I also replaced the `.Rprofile` version with the corresponding `RENV_CONFIG_SYCHRONIZED_CHECK=TRUE` `.Renviron` setting, still no warning.

When checking if {renv} does actually believe the library and lockfile are out-of-sync explicitly via `renv::status()`, I get the familiar:
```
The following package(s) are installed but not recorded in the lockfile:
          _
  Matrix    [1.5-3]
  lattice   [0.20-45]

Use `renv::snapshot()` to add these packages to your lockfile.
```

I'm quite confused as to what `renv.config.synchronized.check` actually does these days, is the above scenario expected?
If it doesn't present us with the expected warning, the startup cost (of scanning) seems expensive -- and it's even unclear how exactly to control that scanning (#1152).

Apart from a few small sources** of confusion, I love love love using {renv} :-)




** pun intended

title: .Rprofile's `options()` vs .Renviron's `RENV_CONFIG_*`
description:
I have a large project and after recently upgrading that project's {renv} to v0.16.0 I suddenly found myself with slow R startup times again, presumably because of {renv}'s various checks.
My `.Rprofile` file in that project contains both of these settings:
```r
options("renv.config.synchronized.check" = FALSE)
options("renv.config.updates.check" = FALSE)
```
In that R session, I double-checked to make sure those were set (e.g. via `options("renv.config.synchronized.check")`) and indeed they were there.

To test whether or not those values being _used_, I commented-out those two options in the `.Rprofile` file and created an `.Renviron` file with the equivalents. Important to note that there was previously no `.Renviron` file, and the base environment from which R was called has no `RENV_*` variables.
```r
RENV_CONFIG_SYNCHRONIZED_CHECK=FALSE
RENV_CONFIG_UPDATES_CHECK=FALSE
```
Upon restarting R, voila, quick startup and immediate prompt.

This leads me to believe that somehow the `.Rprofile` options were not being respected by {renv} upon startup.
Has the behavior of these changed somehow in the past few releases?

Has a 'verbose' mode for {renv} been considered, where we can see the various code-scanning, library-scanning, and lockfile-reading steps?

Also, the documentation for the `renv.config.synchronized.check` option suggests that the lockfile is compared to the library, but not necessarily the source code.
When `status()` is run, however, _source_ is inspected, too, and it's unclear to me if there's a way to just check the library-vs-lockfile without also scanning code.

title: This project is configured to use Bioconductor '3.12', which is not compatible with R '4.0.5'.
description:
Hi, when loading an R project in terminal, I sometimes (but not always) see this message possibly prompting from `renv` package: "This project is configured to use Bioconductor '3.12', which is not compatible with R '4.0.5'. Use 'renv::init(bioconductor = TRUE)' to re-initialize this project with the latest Bioconductor release."

From [Bioconductor site](https://www.bioconductor.org/about/release-announcements/#release-versions), it says version 3.12 works with R 4.0, so I think it is natural that R '4.0.5' comes with Bioconductor 3.12, which is the version automatically determined when installing `BiocManager` package.

It is totally OK that I ignore this warning, but I would still like to find out why renv thinks Bioconductor 3.12 is not compatible with R 4.0.5.

title: renv failing on github actions with recent package update
description:
I have a R CMD ckeck workflow with `renv` suddenly failing on github actions with the errors `failed to retrieve package 'xxx'` and warning `Warning: failed to find source for 'xxx' in package repositories` or `1: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404 2: failed to find binary for 'xxx' in package repositories `. 

It is conspicuously not failing on the mac runner but is failing on the windows and all three ubuntu ones. 

I am posting this because the errors were not particularly googlable, so hopefully this will be helpful to someone else. It turns out the reason for the failures was that the package in question had just been updated a few days ago. I used `renv::install(package@1.2.3)` to go back one version and that solved the problem. 

I am also posting this in case there is another less kludgy solution to this issue, because I only half understand what I am doing here :) . My workflow is below. 




<details>
  <summary>workflow.yaml</summary>
  
```
# Workflow derived from https://github.com/r-lib/actions/tree/v2/examples
# Need help debugging build failures? Start at https://github.com/r-lib/actions#where-to-find-help
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

name: R-CMD-check

jobs:
  R-CMD-check:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.config.os }}

    name: ${{ matrix.config.os }} (${{ matrix.config.r }})

    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        config:
          - {os: macos-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: windows-latest, r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'devel', http-user-agent: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'release'}
          - {os: ubuntu-latest,   r: 'oldrel-1'}

    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      R_KEEP_PKG_SOURCE: yes

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          http-user-agent: ${{ matrix.config.http-user-agent }}
          use-public-rspm: true
          r-version: 4.1.2

      - name: Remove `.Rprofile`
        shell: bash
        run: |
          rm .Rprofile
      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/check-r-package@v2
        with:
          upload-snapshots: true
```
</details>

title: [Feature Request] renv::init() in an old project suggests old package versions
description:
If i have a 10 year old project on my system and I try to run it today, chances are that it will not run because of R and package updates.

If I run `renv::init()` renv will detect the installed versions of R, it will go through the scripts and detect the packages used in the code and if some of these packages are already in the cache then the latest version number from the cache will be stored and finally, if a package used in the old project is not in the cache, the latest version will be found online.
I hope I got it more or less right until here.

The behaviour I'd like would rather be:
`renv` detects that the project is old or this is specified by the user
`renv` suggests two modes to the user: 
 - archival snapshot only. If the intent of the user is only to get a complete `renv.lock` for reproducibility with old package versions, I think a code solution from `renv` is a possibility.
 
 - working directory. If the user wants to actually run the code:
    `renv` suggests the most compatible R version or offers to try installing old packages on the current installed R version
    `renv` offers to download package versions from the time the project was last updated

I looked into packages [groundhog](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/groundhog/index.html) and [oldr](https://github.com/duckmayr/oldr) for suggesting old package versions based on a given date.

```
# list packages needed
```

title: [Feature Request] allow user-configured remotes strategy
description:
# Motivation

`renv` currently attempts to fetch all remotes when installing packages, which introduces a behaviors that might not always be desirable: 

   - this deviates from `base::install.packages` default behavior opaquely
   - this can add unexpected packages to the local cache for soft dependencies (even when they aren't specified to be installed)
   - this will throw warnings when remotes are not accessible

The last point is particularly annoying in a private enterprise context where permissions might be required to access optional remotes.

To give a concrete example, within the context of an industry setting this is posing some hurdles. Our analysts see warnings when remotes can't be found (due to requiring authenticated access to the remote). This happens even in situations where the remote is for a dependency that does not need to be installed as specified by [`package.dependency.fields`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html#:~:text=package.dependency.fields), or when the dependency can already be satisfied by a version from a repository in `options("repos")`.

For a real-world enterprise `renv.lock` file, with a large corpus of private dependencies, this can be a barrage of warnings that can be alarming to anyone not savvy to the intricacies of remote dependency management.

# Feature Request

Introduce options for configuring when remotes should be considered. To propose some behaviors, perhaps this could be either:

- `"always"`: Remotes are always pulled, even if a non-remote source for the package is available. The remote is used if the downloaded package is the latest known version of the package. (current behavior)
- `"needed"`: Remotes are pulled only if a dependency cannot be satisfied by other sources.
- `"never"`: Never pull remotes

Ideally this option would be able to be provided to user-facing functions (`renv::install`, `renv::restore`, etc) as a parameter, or using project-level [`settings`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html), or via [`config`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/config.html) options/envvars.

---

The `"always"` behavior can be further improved following this feature request to `remotes` to allow declarative package names in remote definitions, which would allow for more selective downloading of `remotes` based on desired dependency types. (https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/741), but even without those changes this option would be helpful in cases where the publicly available version satisfies all version requirements and the remote isn't `"needed"`.

title: Issue warning when installing a package into a place that isn't `RENV_PATHS_CACHE`
description:
We have the `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` environment variable set.  Some of the packages installed to that directory by another user didn't have group write, which led to two problems:

1. When I went to install a new version of a package with `renv::install()`, it installed it to my Rproj directory without telling me it didn't install to `RENV_PATHS_CACHE`.
2. When I tried to install an existing package version in the cache, it re-downloaded and reinstalled to my Rproj directory (instead of, e.g., symlinking).  We were confused why renv kept installing packages that should've been in the cache until we realized that it was a permissions problem. 

Could `renv::install()` issue a warning when it's not able to install the package to `RENV_PATHS_CACHE`, and inform us where it's going instead?

I'm happy to be wrong on this, too--I know people don't like it when output gets too verbose...

cc @btbroderick

title: `renv_file_find()` and Docker
description:
This isn't really a bug report, nor much of a feature request, either, just a note about how an renv feature (which is nice!) doesn't play so nicely with some standard ways of using Docker.

I found myself in an odd position recently of wanting to use `renv::autoload()` to load a project renv library from a (possibly deeply-nested) project subdirectory starting-point. In development on my localhost R environment, this worked fine. When I migrated to running from within a Docker image, suddenly the auto-load behavior stopped working.

It turns out I was copying/mounting the project (root) into the `/app` directory within the Docker container (which is somewhat standard: i.e. having the 'project' or 'application' mounted at a top-level directory). The auto-loading gave up before reaching the `/app` directory, however, because of [this math](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/a921af3b9980a6cba82ebc3404c42f2a43e759fc/R/files.R#L482):
```R
  # compute number of slashes (avoid searching beyond home directory)
  slashes <- gregexpr("/", path, fixed = TRUE)[[1L]]
  n <- length(slashes) - 2L
```
Obviously on local development environments this makes sense, but when developing (or running) inside a Docker image, one _probably_ wants to go up to at least only one-level below `/`, since the application code ("project", here) would typically be mounted somewhere like `/app` or even `/root`.

Not sure what to do about this, other than make a note (this issue) for possible future reference; or possibly some optional switch to enable searching a bit farther up (with all the associated 'here-be-dragons' caveats that come from exploring that far up in the directory structure :-) ).

title: "Keep going" mode for `renv::restore()` and perhaps `renv::install()`
description:
Follow-up to #746. A perhaps more ambitious variant of #1108.

When attempting `renv::restore()` from a large `renv.lock` file, the `renv.config.install.transactional` config already avoids a lot of repeated work. Ideally, a "keep going" mode, similar to `make -k`, would attempt to install all packages that can be installed (and even avoid erroring on download failures). The first `restore()` would then be a "best effort" install, following attempts would focus on installing packages that failed with the first attempt (in combination with `renv.config.install.transactional`).

title: Avoid rechecking size of remote file in the same session
description:
When attempting `renv::restore()` from a large `renv.lock` file, the `renv.config.install.transactional` config already avoids a lot of repeated work. However, if installation of a package fails, all remote file sizes are still checked before attempting the reinstall:

```
Retrieving 'https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.1/ROCR_1.0-11.tgz' ...
	OK [file is up to date]
Retrieving 'https://mran.microsoft.com/snapshot/2022-05-02/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.1/gplots_3.1.1.tgz' ...
	OK [file is up to date]
```

I propose to (perhaps optionally) memoize the retrieval of the size of remote files. If caching works properly, iterations would become much shorter (instantaneous?).

title: Unexpected behavior cellar and github
description:
I have observed a behavior that might be an issue (at least from my perspective).

I use a package cellar as suggested in the vignette (https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/cellar.html). In short, I created a new folder  renv/cellar and stored a package.

Since this package is rather small, I would like to push it on github which is why I removed this path in the .gitignore file (renv/.gitignore).

However, everytime I activate the library (i.e., renv::activate()) the .gitignore will be updated and the cellar will be excluded. 

I would expect that removing the cellar from .gitignore will not change when using renv in a project.

title: Error in JSON text
Report installation time in logs as well
description:
This is an admittedly minor thing, but I've always found it confusing that renv logs report how long it takes to move a package into the cache, but not how long it takes to install the package.

For example, installing `nmle` here took about 10-20 seconds

```
Installing nlme [3.1-160] ...
```

and when the installation is complete it's surprising to see only 0.59ms in the logs.

```
Installing nlme [3.1-160] ...
	OK [built from source]
Moving nlme [3.1-160] into the cache ...
	OK [moved to cache in 0.59 milliseconds]
```

Could you include the installation time for packages, e.g

```
Installing nlme [3.1-160] ...
	OK [built from source in 18 seconds]
Moving nlme [3.1-160] into the cache ...
	OK [moved to cache in 0.59 milliseconds]
```

(It's even worse for a package like `sass` that takes more than a minute to compile from source on my machine but then moves into the cache in half a millisecond.)

title: Force recycle packages from cache
description:
Here is a really common scenario.

1. A new subversion of R comes out. 
2. A whole lot of packages make minor changes to keep up with the new version of R
3. New versions of these packages are released, but they are incompatible with the previous version of R
4. I create a new project, with a new `renv` library
5. I try to install a package that I've installed for a previous project, and this package has dependencies that match 2) and 3) above.
6. When installing these dependencies, `renv::install()` realises tries to download the latest versions, which fail.
7. I can explicitly request a cached version of one of these dependencies, which will work immediately by linking to the cache.
8. Occassionally, one of these dependencies will itself have a dependency that has the some problem.
9. Half an hour later, I eventually run into a dependency where the older, cached version is no longer on CRAN, and the whole process falls over, even though a perfectly fine copy of the older dependency is in the cache.

I realise that the R gods are probably trying to tell me to update R, but surely there must be a way to tell `renv::install()` to try to use packages in the cache either 1) as a first choice, or 2) as a fallback if installing the latest version fails. 

Actually, this is what I would have expected when `rebuild = FALSE`, which is the default value for this option. But `renv` still seems to be checking whether the package is on CRAN, even though it is in the cache.

title: create lockfile for entire cache
description:
Right now I find the `lockfile` argument of `renv::restore` to be very useful. I can migrate _a project_ from one cache location (or system) to another, or a new version of R for instance, simply by restoring the project's lockfile. In my renv setup, many R users are sharing the same renv cache. That means if there is a migration (or new R version) everyone needs to do their own restore in order to capture all installed packages (and rebuild them).

I think it would be nice if there was a way to create a lockfile of all packages in a cache, perhaps limited to a specific version of R. I could then restore the cache so all packages exist again. This would be particularly useful in environments where write permissions are limited for users and admins want to perform the cache migration.

title: Add feature to flag if rendered documents do not correspond to current lockfile
description:
When managing a project that creates documents with RMarkdown/quarto someone can render a document and then update packages and change the lockfile. This will lead to a project in an "invalid state" in which the code used a different environment that the one stated in the lockfile. Or someone could updated  packages, run the code and forget to update the lockfile, again leading to a mismatch. 

Currently, there's no way that I know of to tell if a project is in one of these situations. 

I imagine that this could be controlled by versioning the lockfile, perhaps just with hashes, and attaching the current version to the rendered document somehow. Perhaps as a colophon inside the document or, with hidden, machine-readable metadata embedded in the file, or using a specific file for the job. 
Then, one could compare the current lockfile hash with the document lockfile hash to see if the project is valid or not. 

EDIT: Although this wouldn't work in the situation of the lockfile being out of sync with the project library. 

Is this in scope for renv?

title: Add mechanism to force installation via GitHub API rather than git clone method
description:
In work to fix #1075, packages installed from GitHub that contain submodules now use `git` rather than the GitHub remote types. This might be necessary if the submodule is part of the package source, but it isn't always required and may cause downstream issues with deploying content to Connect that depends on packages installed with these methods.

I've set up a reprex repo at [gadenbuie/renv-git-submodules](https://github.com/gadenbuie/renv-git-submodules). In that repo, using `hadley/emo` installed via renv confuses `rsconnect::writeManifest()`.

``` r
str(renv:::renv_json_read("renv.lock")$Packages$emo)
```

    ## List of 12
    ##  $ Package       : chr "emo"
    ##  $ Version       : chr "0.0.0.9000"
    ##  $ Source        : chr "git"
    ##  $ RemoteType    : chr "git"
    ##  $ RemoteUrl     : chr "https://github.com/hadley/emo"
    ##  $ RemoteHost    : chr "api.github.com"
    ##  $ RemoteUsername: chr "hadley"

    ##  $ Hash          : chr "38cd5a58901f1ba87ca769667d557a76"
    ##  $ Requirements  :List of 8
    ##   ..$ : chr "assertthat"

    ##   ..$ : chr "magrittr"
    ##   ..$ : chr "purrr"
    ##   ..$ : chr "rlang"
    ##   ..$ : chr "stringr"

The problem that arises is that I can’t deploy content that uses emo installed with renv 0.16.0 to Connect because `rsconnect::writeManifest()` can’t determine the repository URL.

``` r
rsconnect::writeManifest(appPrimaryDoc = "example.Rmd")
```

    ## Warning in FUN(X[[i]], ...): Package 'emo 0.0.0.9000' was installed from
    ## sources; Packrat will assume this package is available from a CRAN-like

While it's probably worth raising this issue with rsconnect, I still feel that renv should provide a mechanism for overriding this choice, perhaps if installing with an explicit `github::` prefix?

description:
I'm trying to use multiple caches on windows.  The documentation here https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html#multiple-caches  doesn't mention the semi-colon option for setting the RENV_PATHS_CACHE value.

title: Consider enabling project locks by default
description:
To prevent concurrent modification within `renv` projects.

The main challenge is (given the lack of primitives available to `renv`) making sure that we have a good way of cleaning up in case the R process is unexpectedly terminated.

title: Unclear how to merge separate cache locations
description:
This is a question, possibly a feature request. 

**Problem**: I have been using renv for a while now, and I somehow have separate renv caches at two locations on my machine. Both caches include packages from R 3.6, 4.0, and 4.1, which seems rather space inefficient. I didn't set two different cache locations manually, so I assume it's the result of renv updates over the past years.

![renv caches](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61324620/195134130-f16ea7fd-76bd-4c4d-9e03-a8b95586b7a2.PNG)

The two paths are those described in the [renv paths docs](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/paths.html) [NOTE: edited to reflect comment below]:

* ~New~ Old default cache location: ```%LOCALAPPDATA%/renv```
* ~Old~ New default cache location ~(though somehow my new 4.2 caches are showing up here)~: ```%LOCALAPPDATA%/R/cache/R/renv```

I have no renviron modifications related to renv other than ```RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=FALSE```, these are the relevant parts of Sys.getenv():
```
RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED                FALSE
RENV_DEFAULT_R_ENVIRON                     <NA>
RENV_DEFAULT_R_ENVIRON_USER                <NA>
RENV_DEFAULT_R_LIBS                        <NA>
RENV_DEFAULT_R_LIBS_SITE                   C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-4.2.1/site-library
RENV_DEFAULT_R_LIBS_USER                   C:\Users\myname\AppData\Local/R/win-library/4.2
RENV_DEFAULT_R_PROFILE                     <NA>
RENV_DEFAULT_R_PROFILE_USER                <NA>
RENV_PROJECT                               C:/Users/myname/Documents/etcetc
```

**Desired outcome**: all projects refer to a package cache in one place with no duplication elsewhere.

**Question**: Is there a suggested way to merge the two caches without breaking references in all my projects? Do i just modify the RENV_PATHS_ROOT environmental variable and merge the caches myself? If i do that, do i need to manually combine the 'projects' file that's in each cache? 

If there's no way to do this programmatically, a function in renv might be nice; probably a bit out of my wheelhouse to do it in a safe way for renv but am willing to offer myself up as a tester!

title: sandbox not ignored with renv profiles
description:
In renv 0.16.0, `sandbox/*` is placed in `renv/profiles/<profile-name>/renv/.gitignore` if a given profile is loaded, so `renv/sandbox` is not ignored. I don't know if this means that the sandbox should be in the profile folder or if the .gitignore for the sandbox should be in the renv folder.

I discovered this in https://github.com/carpentries/workbench-template-rmd/pull/23 (which was automatically updated using [a custom update script run on continuous integration](https://github.com/zkamvar/vise/blob/79ac226a043e8cb8c534cd9c52f7b14a53773fae/R/update.R)).

title: Add `dependencies` argument to `renv::install()` so that Suggests deps can be ignored
description:
With `renv::settings$snapshot.type("explicit")`, `renv::install()` will install all package dependencies from the `DESCRIPTION` file, although the snapshot will only include the package listed in `renv::settings$package.dependency.fields()`, typically `Imports, Depends, LinkingTo`.

It would be helpful to have a `dependencies` argument in `renv::install()` that could be used to ignore or include `Suggests` dependencies. The default behavior of installing everything in the `DESCRIPTION` is great, but I've been running into circumstances where I only want to use `renv::install()` to install the package dependencies that are included in the snapshot.

title: renv::install() not impacted by `renv.config.repos.override` option
description: The option "renv.config.repos.override" is used to set whether renv::restore uses the lock files repo settings or the R sessions repos options. I would think having renv::install() follow this option would make sense as well, or the ability to set them.

title: renv::install()  to skip already installed packages
description:
Is there a way to run `renv::install()` on a project that uses DESCRIPTION file to keep packages dependencies, and `renv::install()` will ignore already installed packages and only install if required?

With version `0.15.5` it always installs packages if a newer version is available.

title: `renv.download.headers` is ignored during bootstrap
description:
We're using authenticated CRAN channels, so an authentication header must be provided every time a packages is installed.

The `renv.download.headers` works perfectly when using `renv::install`, however it is ignored in [bootstrap.R](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/R/bootstrap.R), so bootstrapping fails with:
```
# Bootstrapping renv 0.15.5 --------------------------------------------------
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://<internal-cran-channel>/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'https://<internal-cran-channel>/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
Warning: unable to access index for repository https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib:
  cannot open URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES'
* Downloading renv 0.15.5 ... FAILED
```

Why doesn't bootstrap.R use the same logic as download.R to install renv? Is there a way to configure the behavior of the bootstrapping phase without asking users to manually modify the activate.R file that's generated upon activation?

title: renv::use not working as expected when passing in a lockfile and setting a library path
description:
I am having a problem getting renv::use() to work correctly when attempting to supply an renv lock file and setting the library path in the call.  

Example:  renv::use(lockfile = "/home/kkrame02/mylockfile/renv.lock",
                               library  = "/home/kkrame02/test/library",
                               isolate  = TRUE,
                               verbose  = TRUE,
                               )

When I call the function the first time and check out the .libPaths() it points toward the project /home/kkrame02/mytest/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu location.  When I run the same renv:use call a second time and check the .libPaths() location it points toward the library location specified above and all subsequent runs will now point towards the library path set above.  

It appears the first time I run the code it goes to activate the project and modifies the libpath to the library folder within the projects renv folder, but after the project is activated all future calls to renv::use() by-pass that section of code and retain my library path set above.  Is this working as intended?

title: install() docs: include info/examples on installing from private repos
description: It would be helpful if the [`install()` docs](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/install.html) included info on installing from private repos (e.g., linking to https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html#authentication).

title: Disable the second repo in renv
description:
The `renv` uses two repo to host r-packages.
Example: 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52919010/190145937-b1f4af66-b0d8-4e70-81cc-3e23f490998a.png)

This creates a huge mass of problems! In some projects on different platforms, packages are installed in different repositories (directly in the `renv`-folder and in a second repo), and a package from the second repo can be written to `renv.lock`. I disabled the second repo in `.libPaths`, but the package continues to be called, although it is not in the `renv`-folder of the project. It's not clear what's going on at all.

It will be as comfortable and transparent as possible if `renv` works with only ONE repository, and not with two or more.

Request: tell me the most correct way to disable the second (and other) repository in renv, except for the first one, which leads to the `renv`-folder of the project

title: Explicit sources: Ensure that only explicit source is used
description:
I use a package that is not on CRAN and use the explicit definition in the lock file as suggested here: [https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/cellar.html#explicit-sources](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/cellar.html#explicit-sources).

The lock file looks like that:
```   
"relaimpo": { 
      "Package": "relaimpo",
      "Version": "2.2-5",
      "Source": "relaimpo_2.2-5.zip"
    }
```

It is important that the offline .zip file is used because this package has multiple versions (i.e., for US users and for non-US users).

Expected behavior: I would expect that the explict definition ensures that renv is exclusively refering to the source given and **does not** query other repositories.

Current behavior: Currently, MRAN is used to download a different package (i.e., the US version which I do not want to use) instead using the offline package.

title: Inconsistent sources when snapshotting after installing new package
description:
When installing packages and snapshotting them I've encountered that renv would updates its lock file inconsistently.

For example, `R.utils` was updated from v2.11.0 to v2.12.0 while installing a new package. In `renv.lock` the package received a multitude of new properties (i.e. `RemoteRepos`, `RemoteSha` and others), but also the `Source` property was changed from `"Repository"` to `"CRAN"`.

Strangely the `R6` package, which was not updated, also received changes. The `Source` property was changed from `"CRAN"` to `"Reposiotry"` and a lot of properties were removed.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1318997/190095055-300e9d28-561f-4467-81ac-8bcfe666cfe3.png)

I'm not sure if this is a bug or I just have a poor understanding of how dependencies work with Renv.
