title: renv::install() support for github package installs where package is using git submodules
description:
`renv::install()` does not work when a package contains git submodules. Example is `mschubert/clustermq`. 

`renv::install("mschubert/clustermq")` fails but `remotes::install_github("mschubert/clustermq")` works. 

Workaround for now: use `renv::install("git::https://github.com/mschubert/clustermq")`.

title: support binary + source packages in Nexus repositories
description:
Many thanks @kevinushey for your very quick and positive answer !

To make it simple, Nexus (aka Nexus Repository Manager, by Sonatype) is deployed by my IT teams on our company's servers.
Nexus aims at achieving two main goals:
* **Proxifying** external repositories (such as CRAN)
* **Storing** persistently packages downloaded from these repositories, for future usage (cache functionality).

In the Rprofile.site we deploy on our machines, the repository is set using the Nexus root URL for R repository (miror of CRAN). Thanks to this configuration:
* When I install an R package that nobody in my company has already installed (same package, same version, same type, architecture if binary, etc), Nexus downloads it from CRAN, serves it to me and stores it for future usage
* Afterwards, when a colleague (or myself from another machine) tries to install it, Nexus serves the package it has already stored internally.

The **architecture** of Nexus storage is **the same as the original CRAN repository**. For example :
* R source packages will be stored in /src/contrib/<PACKAGE_NAME>_<PACKAGE_VERSION>.tar.gz
* R windows binary packages will be stored in /bin/windows/contrib/<R_VERSION_X.Y>/<PACKAGE_NAME>_<PACKAGE_VERSION>.zip
* and so on.

The **main difference** with CRAN is that **older versions are kept**, and still available thanks to Nexus internal storage functionality.

### Binary packages

Here is an example for binary package `rlang` in my Nexus architecture:
```
___ bin
    |___ windows
         |___ contrib
              |___ 4.1
                   |___ rlang_1.0.3.zip
                   |___ rlang_1.0.4.zip
                   |___ rlang_1.0.5.zip
                   |___ PACKAGES
                   |___ PACKAGES.gz		 
                   |___ PACKAGES.rds
```
As said above, older versions are still available for download, even if they are not explicitly listed in PACKAGES.gz (which only includes latest version since it is the proxyfied version of CRAN’s PACKAGES.gz file):
```
Package: rlang
Version: 1.0.5
Depends: R (>= 3.4.0)
Imports: utils
Suggests: cli (>= 3.1.0), covr, crayon, fs, glue, knitr, magrittr,
        methods, pillar, rmarkdown, stats, testthat (>= 3.0.0), tibble,
        usethis, vctrs (>= 0.2.3), withr
License: MIT + file LICENSE
```
The idea would be to determine the theoretical URL and try such URL when restoring the project, if the requested package is not explicitly listed in PACKAGES.gz.
In our example, if the renv.lock file contains the record `rlang@1.0.4`, we should try URL bin/windows/contrib/4.1/rlang_1.0.4.zip.

### Source packages

The same idea could also be used for source packages, in order to take advantage of Nexus storage functionnality.
Here is an example for source package `rlang` in my Nexus architecture:

```
___ src
    |___ contrib
         |___ rlang_1.0.3.tar.gz
         |___ rlang_1.0.4.tar.gz
         |___ rlang_1.0.5.tar.gz
         |___ PACKAGES
         |___ PACKAGES.gz		 
         |___ PACKAGES.rds
```
Again, older versions are still available for download, even if they are not explicitly listed in PACKAGES.gz (which only includes latest version since it is the proxyfied version of CRAN’s PACKAGES.gz file):
```
Package: rlang
Version: 1.0.5
Depends: R (>= 3.4.0)
Imports: utils
Suggests: cli (>= 3.1.0), covr, crayon, fs, glue, knitr, magrittr,
        methods, pillar, rmarkdown, stats, testthat (>= 3.0.0), tibble,
        usethis, vctrs (>= 0.2.3), withr
Enhances: winch
License: MIT + file LICENSE
MD5sum: 0419b9b94b400f3ec1f2792ab7f228e2
NeedsCompilation: yes
```
I saw the code you wrote retrieve.R file, for `renv_retrieve_repos_archive_path()` function.
I understand (but not 100% sure) that when requested package is neither in binary PACKAGES.gz file nor in source PACKAGES.gz, this function:
* [first tries to find](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/b27db509dfb3740861bd8d7e4d8d06f4ca998eb4/R/retrieve.R#L756) the package "src/contrib/Archive/<PACKAGE_NAME>/"
* [then](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/b27db509dfb3740861bd8d7e4d8d06f4ca998eb4/R/retrieve.R#L767) in "src/contrib/" (to deal with initial request hereabove).

(If voluntary ignore the [step](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/b27db509dfb3740861bd8d7e4d8d06f4ca998eb4/R/retrieve.R#L761) related to issue #602, to keep this post as simple as possible !)

If the package has been moved to Archive subfolder in CRAN, Nexus will download it and store it with the same architecture, in folder "src/contrib/Archive/<PACKAGE_NAME>/".

At the end of the day, the same source package will be duplicated in Nexus storage : both in "src/contrib/" (initial download) and in "src/contrib/Archive/<PACKAGE_NAME>/" (second download, when package is moved to Archive in CRAN) :
```
___ src
    |___ contrib
         |___ Archive
              |___ rlang
                   |___ rlang_1.0.3.tar.gz          # redudant storage since already available
                   |___ rlang_1.0.4.tar.gz          # in Nexus outside of Archive folder
         |___ rlang_1.0.3.tar.gz
         |___ rlang_1.0.4.tar.gz
         |___ rlang_1.0.5.tar.gz
         |___ PACKAGES
         |___ PACKAGES.gz		 
         |___ PACKAGES.rds
```
If we could avoid this, this would prevent from unnecessarily increase the storage volumetry.
For Nexus’like configurations, I would suggest to try first in "src/contrib/", and then in "src/contrib/Archive/<PACKAGE_NAME>/".

### Conclusion

To put in a nutshell, my suggested sequence would be :

1. renv_retrieve_repos_binary (when binary explicitly requested by user)
2. renv_retrieve_repos_binary_older (when binary explicitly requested by user) – **new step**
3. renv_retrieve_repos_mran (when binary explicitly requested by user and MRAN enabled)
4. renv_retrieve_repos_source
5. renv_retrieve_repos_source_older – **new step**
6. renv_retrieve_repos_archive

I don't know if repository managers like Nexus are largely used by R users. If you don't want to systematically try oldest versions, a user-level configuration to trigger steps 2 and 5 could make sense:
For instance, using a new option `renv.config.retrieve.try.older` (or `RENV_CONFIG_RETRIEVE_TRY_OLDER` as  environment variable), with default to `FALSE`.

Would you have any question, please contact me.
And if you prefer that I create an new issue on Github, please tell me.
Kind regards
Arnaud

_Originally posted by @arnauddeblic in https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/595#issuecomment-1239255666_

title: How to handle two different version of R in one project?
description:
Hi, I have recently encountered an issue when using renv to manage my project. When I set up the project I only had R 4.2 installed, and the `project/renv/library` directory only had the 4.2 version, just as usual. Then I went and installed my packages under the library for R 4.2. So far so good.

Now all of a sudden another R 3.6 shows up in the same folder (`project/renv/library`), and I don't know what to do with it. If I open the project in R studio, the 4.2 version is loaded, but if I run R in the command line, the 3.6 version is loaded, which is really inconvenient and deviating from my intention to keep the environment reproducible.

I believe the 3.6 version is installed by conda because the full directory to the installed libraries is `/project/renv/library/R-3.6/x86_64-conda_cos6-linux-gn`, and I do have two conda environments on my system. I created the second environment to install a python library (MACS2) that is used by one of my R package. Perhaps R 3.6 is installed in the process? But why can't conda detect I already have R 4.2 installed? Is it because R 4.2 is managed by another conda environment? But again, I can load the second environment containing MACS2 in commandline, and my package in R-4.2 can use it normally, which make it even more confusing. So maybe conda isn't managing R version after all?

So my question is if it is safe (and how) to remove R 3.6 from my project. I also want to know how to prevent this from happening again in the future. Should I set up a new conda environment for every new r project?

title: Notify about changing R version?
description:
I notice that the change in R version in the lockfile is done silently, without any notification? It seems it would be an important information for the user?

In my case, while I had an opening message such as _Project requested R version '4.1.2' but '4.2.1' is currently being used_, running `renv::snapshot()`seems to have updated the R version to 4.1.2, yet without notifying anything?

Here was for example the message I got, which is a bit confusing since it seems to be exhaustive (i.e. informing on all changes), while maybe the biggest change is not notified?

```
> renv::snapshot()
The following package(s) have unsatisfied dependencies:

	'lobstr' requires 'cpp11 (>= 0.4.2)', but version '0.3.1' will be snapshotted

Consider updating the required dependencies as appropriate.

Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# CRAN ===============================
- lobstr   [* -> 1.1.2]

Do you want to proceed? [y/N]:
```

title: Consider masking Git provider environment variables from package install subprocesses
description:
R packages can execute code at install time. This code can access the local environment, and may not be trusted.

We [just implemented a feature in Packrat](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/682) to mask sensitive environment variables (e.g. Git service provider credentials like `GITHUB_PAT`) from package install subprocesses. Masked variables are unset before the subprocess is called and restored afterwards. This might be a good idea to do in `renv` as well.

In Packrat, the approach we decided to take was to enable masking by default for a set variables known to be used for Git provider secrets. This masking can be disabled with an option, and another option allows users to add other variables to the list of items to mask.

title: `renv/activate.R` has old `renv` version rather than `renv` version matching renv.lock of the project
description:
The reprex below creates a lock file w/renv 15.5, then installs renv 14.0 and uses renv 14.0 to create a new project, copy the renv.lock with 15.5 into it this project and initialize and restore the new project.  The activate.R ends up with `version <- 14.0` instead of `version <- 15.5` which gives us this warning when opening the new project.

```r
* Project '~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock' loaded. [renv 0.15.5]
Warning message:
renv 0.15.5 was loaded from project library, but this project is configured to use renv 0.14.0.
Use `renv::record("renv@0.15.5")` to record renv 0.15.5 in the lockfile.
Use `renv::restore(packages = "renv")` to install renv 0.14.0 into the project library. 
```

Should `renv::restore()` update `renv/activate.R`?  Or am I using a hammer when I should be using a screwdriver to programmatically setup a project using an existing, restricted `renv.lock` file, meaning it cannot be updated w/`renv::snapshot()` as suggested [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/63897210/renv-0-12-0-was-loaded-from-project-library-but-renv-0-11-0-is-recorded-in-lock)?

**reprex:**

```r
# create a lock file using latest renv
options(repos = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest")
install.packages("renv")
install.packages("rstudioapi")

# create project
rstudioapi::initializeProject("~/1_renv_question/renv15")

# initialize the project
renv::init(project = "~/1_renv_question/renv15")

# install renv 14.0
options(repos = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/2022-01-04")
install.packages("renv")
install.packages("rstudioapi")

rstudioapi::restartSession()

# create project
rstudioapi::initializeProject("~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock")

# add the renv.lock
file.copy("~/1_renv_question/renv15/renv.lock", "~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock/renv.lock")

# initialize the project
renv::init(project = "~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock", bare = TRUE, restart = FALSE)

# restore project
renv::restore(project = "~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock", prompt = FALSE)

rstudioapi::openProject("~/1_renv_question/use_renv_lock/use_renv_lock.Rproj")
```

title: Do not offer to run `renv::snapshot()` if there are packages that are used but not instaled.
description:
If there are packages recorded in the lockfile that are not longer used **and** packages that are on the lockfile and not installed, `status()` will first list the former and suggest running `renv::snapshot()` and then list the latter and suggest running `renv::restore()` to install them. 

If the user runs those commands in the order they appear, they will not install the desired packages, because the first call to `renv::snapshot()` will remove the needed packages from the lockfile too. 

I'd suggest only showing the message if the only effect of `renv::snapshot()` would be to remove those listed packages. Another alternative would be to have a separate function like `renv::remove_unused()` that has the predictable effect of only removing unused packages from the lockfile.

title: renv library doesn't work well when sharing RStudio cloud projects
description:
Using renv to manage the package library in RStudio Cloud, the status of the library is broken when sharing the project. My guess is that it has to do with the global package cache, which is only valid in the original user account. 

In any case, the user experience is that if I want to share a project that uses renv in Rtudio Cloud, the recipient has to run `renv::repair()`, which can be confusing and take a long time. Compared with the experience of not using renv, in which required packages are come installed with the project, it's much worse, particularly for teaching and short workshops. 

I don't know if this is something that could be improved from the renv side or the Rstudio cloud side. Perhaps there's a workaround? Perhaps setting the cache path inside the project?

title: Feature Request: function that tests if renv project is loaded
description:
Use-case:

When opening an .Rproj that uses renv, a message is printed like:
```r
* Project '/path/to/project/' loaded. [renv 0.15.5]
```
I can manually inspect the console output for that message, but it would be nice to add a line to my code that tests that it was successfully loaded. This would be particularly useful for cases where I'm running scripts in batch mode. Then my scripts could include something like:
```r
stopifnot(renv_is_loaded)
```
This came up because I noticed that I was running scripts in batch mode from the wrong directory, so renv was not being sourced properly.

title: changing renv/ location within project
description:
Hi,

I was not able to figure out how to configure renv to put all confi files in a subfolder og my project. I would like to store renv/... in as subfolder "stuff" where all other infrastructure and config things are collected.  I tried to solve this via project specific .Renviron file

```
RENV_PATHS_PREFIX="stuff"
RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE="./stuff/renv.lock"
```

the lock file is moved correctly, but renv still reates a renv folder at the project root directory (the library path is `.../my-project/renv/library/.infrastructure/R-4.1/x86_64-w64-mingw32`)

Is this even possible? If not, why not?

Thanks!

title: .Rprofile code: only load _activate.R_ if it exists?
description:
Hi @kevinushey & `renv` devs,
We're using `renv` throughout our apps & projects at Virga Labs, thank you all for the essential package!
I've just encountered an issue during shiny app deployment where the `renv` folder is often not included in the deployment image to reduce image size, but the _.Rprofile_ is. The line that `renv` automatically adds `source("renv/activate.R")` will cause the app to fail. 
What about adding the following to _.Rprofile_ to prevent this issue?
```r
if (file.exists("renv/activate.R"))
  source("renv/activate.R")
```

Curious to hear your thoughts!
Thanks!

title: how to create a project-related DESCRIPTION file to use explicit snapshot?
description: I would like to limit the list of packages that will end up in `renv.lock` to what i'm using in one of the files in my project. According to the `renv` vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/renv/vignettes/renv.html) it looks like i could use an explicit snapshot approach: Unfortunately the link provided in the documentation (https://r-pkgs.org/description.html) no longer works and i can't find any example of how to do this in practice. I've tried to create a DESCRIPTION file for my project using `usethis::use_description()` and editing it manually so it looks like this: ``` Type: project Title: my_project Description: data refresh pipeline for my app Imports: tidyverse, duckdb, RJDBC, aws.s3, aws.ec2metadata, httr, jsonlite, stringr Encoding: UTF-8 Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE) RoxygenNote: 7.1.2 ``` Unfortunately i get this error when trying to set the snapshot to "explicit": ``` > renv::settings$snapshot.type("explicit") 28 Jul 2022 11:53:14 [rsession-jovyan] ERROR system error 71 (Protocol error) [description=Package field not found in /home/jovyan/my_project/DESCRIPTION]; OCCURRED AT: rstudio::core::Error rstudio::core::r_util::RPackageInfo::read(const rstudio::core::FilePath&) /home/ubuntu/rstudio/src/cpp/core/r_util/RPackageInfo.cpp:85; LOGGED FROM: bool rstudio::core::r_util::isPackageDirectory(const rstudio::core::FilePath&) /home/ubuntu/rstudio/src/cpp/core/r_util/RPackageInfo.cpp:121 ``` Any idea what i'm doing wrong? is there a tutorial showing how to do this in practice?

title: renv cannot find the correct version of rtools (rtools40)
description:
Hi all !

(*disclaimer : this is the first time I submit an issue, apologies in advance for any missing or incomplete information*)

I'm attempting to restore an internal R Package with `renv::restore()`, but `renv` fails to find the correct version of rtools40. This is the error message :
```
Error in if (version < "4.0") renv_rtools_envvars_default(root) else if (version <  : 
  argument is of length zero
```
I'm running on `R@4.1.3` and `renv@0.15.5`.

I went back to the installation page of [rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools40.html), and noticed that I'm getting the same error when running the last item 
```R
install.packages("jsonlite", type = "source")
```
I looked at the definition of `renv:::renv_rtools_envvars_default()`, and found that the issue came from the function upstream [`renv_rtools_envvars()`](https://rdrr.io/cran/renv/src/R/rtools.R).
This function starts by detecting the version of rtools :
```R
version <- renv_rtools_version(root)
```

And this is where I believe there may be an issue : The function `renv_rtools_version()` is defined as 

```R
renv_rtools_version <- function(root) {

  # detect Rtools40
  mirrors <- file.path(root, "etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist.rtools")
  if (file.exists(mirrors))
    return(numeric_version("4.0"))

  # detect Rtools42
  mirrors <- file.path(root, "etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist.clang64")
  if (file.exists(mirrors))
    return(numeric_version("4.2"))

  # detect older Rtools installations
  path <- file.path(root, "VERSION.txt")
  if (!file.exists(path))
    return(NULL)

  contents <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  version <- gsub("[^[:digit:].]", "", contents)

  numeric_version(version)

}
```
However, when I look insider the installation folder of rtools40, under `rtools40\etc\pacman.d`, I'm not able to find any file named `mirrorlist.rtools`, but only a file named `rtools.mirrors` and others prefixed by `rtools.`

I reinstalled [rtools40](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) many times and on different machines, but all the installations contain the file written as `rtools.mirrors` but none as `mirrorlist.rtools`.

Thanks in advance for your help !

title: Installing binaries when collaborating across multiple operating systems
description:
When on an `renv` enabled project where collaborators or machines may be Linux or macOS, one can generally get binaries to install on Linux or macOS machines, but not both.  This is because CRAN hosts macOS binaries, and RSPM hosts Linux binaries, but in `renv.lock` individual packages are designated by a single repository, even if the package source hash would be identical across repositories. I assume similar issues arise with Windows.  I would like there to be a configuration in which the binary version of a package, hosted from either repository, can be preferred for installation on any OS.

In my setup, collaborators may be on Linux or macOS machines, and we use/commit project-level `.Rprofile` files as well as `renv.lock` files to keep our environments in sync.  The `renv`-relevant part of the `.Rprofile` is this:

```r
options(
  repos = c(RSPM = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/latest",
            CRAN = "https://cran.rstudio.com/")
  renv.config.auto.snapshot = TRUE, 
  renv.config.rspm.enabled = TRUE, 
  renv.config.cache.enabled = TRUE
)

source("renv/activate.R")
```

And so we have `renv.lock` files that look like this, but the repository source of a package (CRAN/RSPM) generally depends on whether the user who committed the change is on Linux or macOS:

```json
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "4.2.1",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "RSPM",
        "URL": "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/latest"
      },
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cran.rstudio.com"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "BH": {
      "Package": "BH",
      "Version": "1.78.0-0",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "4e348572ffcaa2fb1e610e7a941f6f3a",
      "Requirements": []
    },
...
```

I note I would expect `renv.lock` to override repository preferences in `.Rprofile` when running `renv::restore()`, and the repositories set in `.Rprofile()` to determine the source of new packages installed into the library.  Perhaps packages in `renv.lock` can have multiple `Repository` values and there can be an `renv.prefer.binary.repository = TRUE` option.

(Migrating from this post on the RStudio forum: https://community.rstudio.com/t/renv-and-rspm-for-binary-installs-on-shared-linux-mac-project/143054/2 by request of @kevinushey)

title: Issues using renv in docker image with a volume mount
description:
@kevinushey I am running RStudio Server in a docker image with a volume mount. When I log in to RStudio, `.libPaths()` links to two libaries, a `/usr/local/lib/R/site-library` which holds the custom packages installed during the docker build and a `usr/local/lib/R/library` which holds the base+recommended packages that ship with R. In order to have access to the custom packages as well, I initialize `renv` in my project directory using:

```r
renv::init(settings = list(external.libraries = "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library"))

After initialization, when I try to load packages that are compiled (e.g. `rappdirs`, `yaml` etc), I run into the following error, which I believe is because of the cache being in a volume mount with `noexec` permissions.

description:
[RStudio Public Package Manager](https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/client/) (RSPM) is an awesome service to the community, no doubt. It's main drawback compared to CRAN: [No binaries for macOS](https://docs.rstudio.com/rspm/admin/serving-binaries/#supported-operating-systems).

renv seems to have RSPM integration to [some degree](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/config.html#renv-config-rspm-enabled), which is great. But I can't figure out a sane way to **use the RSPM CRAN mirror URL (`https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest`) for Linux and Windows, and at the same time the regular CRAN URL (`https://cloud.r-project.org`) for macOS** (or the RSPM mirror only for Linux and regular CRAN also for Windows, doesn't really matter I guess).

I'm using the **explicit** snapshot type for my project (with a `DESCRIPTION` file listing immediate dependencies) and tried various different configurations to achieve the above goal. The nearest I could get is

1. setting regular CRAN, i.e.
  
    ```json
    "R": {
      "Repositories": [
        {
          "Name": "CRAN",
          "URL": "https://cloud.r-project.org"
        }
      ]
    }
    ```

    in the `renv.lock` file;

2. conditionally overwriting the `repos` option in the project's `.Rprofile` after activating renv when on Linux, i.e.

    ```r
    source("renv/activate.R")
  
    if (Sys.info()["sysname"] == "Linux") {
      options(repos =
                getOption("repos") |>
                magrittr::inset("CRAN", "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest") |>
                renv:::renv_rspm_transform())
    }
    ```

---

With the above config on Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 in my case), the weird thing is that when I e.g. do

```r
renv::purge("sp", prompt = FALSE)
```

<details><summary>Output</summary>

```

	sp 1.5-0 [Hash: 2a118bdd2db0a301711e0a9e3e3206d5]

</details>

and then do

```r
renv::repair()
```

<details><summary>Output</summary>

The following package(s) have broken symlinks into the cache:

	sp

Use `renv::repair()` to try and reinstall these packages.

* Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!

Moving sp [1.5-0] into the cache ...

the package sp is fetched from RSPM as can be seen in the output above (fine!).

But when I instead run

```r
renv::restore(clean = TRUE,
              prompt = FALSE)
```

<details><summary>Output</summary>

Use `renv::repair()` to try and reinstall these packages.

title: `renv` always applies `download.file.extra` to download command, even if `download.file.method` does not match the method in use
description:
In the `curl` and `wget` download functions, `renv` always applies the string stored in the option `download.file.extra` to the command it runs, even if the `download.file.method` specified does not match the method in use. This happens here: [`curl`](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/35af08a635dde1d225cfe1a1c36cf61067d87ee3/R/download.R#L306-L309), [`wget`](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/35af08a635dde1d225cfe1a1c36cf61067d87ee3/R/download.R#L409-L411).

Because `renv` ignores `download.file.method`, this can lead to situations where an option is applied to a download method that doesn't understand it (e.g. `wget`'s `--random-wait` passed to `curl`).

The fix should be pretty simple: in [`packrat`](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/blob/3eb97a2fa38134eec177d8f45f6e9d5120012e01/R/downloader.R#L85-L88), `download.file.method` is checked before `download.file.extra` is accessed:

```r
  # If the download method we're using matches the current option for
  # 'download.file.method', then propagate 'extra' options.
  if (!nzchar(extra) && identical(getOption("download.file.method"), method))
    extra <- getOption("download.file.extra", default = "")
```

### Reproduction

I've attached a reproducible example: [renv-download-file-extra.tar.gz](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/9075200/renv-download-file-extra.tar.gz)

This directory contains a Dockerfile and an `renv` lockfile. 

Build the docker image.

```bash
docker build -t renv-download-file-extra .
````

For each of the following example, start the image with this command, run the example, and then exit the image before running the next example.

```bash
docker run -it renv-download-file-extra
```

Example 1. You can successfully restore in the default state, which uses `curl` as the downloader.

```r
renv::restore()
```

Example 2. Just setting `wget` in R's options works. `renv` ignores this and still uses `curl`.

```r
options("download.file.method" = "wget")
renv::restore()
```

Example 3. You can also successfully restore when `wget` and `wget`-specific options are set, by also setting `wget` as `renv`'s download method.

```r
options("download.file.method" = "wget")
options("download.file.extra" = "--random-wait")
Sys.setenv("RENV_DOWNLOAD_METHOD" = "wget")
renv::restore()
```

Example 4. The restore fails if `wget` and `wget`-specific options are set, but `wget` is not set as `renv`'s downloader. In this case, `curl` is being passed the extra option `--random-wait`.

```r
options("download.file.method" = "wget")
options("download.file.extra" = "--random-wait")
renv::restore()
```

When you're done, you can remove the image with:

```bash
docker rmi -f $(docker images renv-download-file-extra -a -q)
```

title: Keep profiles in sync?
description:
Scenario: I have a development and a deployment profile. In development I have devtools and other toys, the deployment profile is lean, but should be a subset of the development profile with exactly the same versions. (A variant of #624?)

What's the best way to keep both `renv.lock` in sync? Are you planning to support cascading profiles?

title: "Dry run" restore?
description:
Is there a way to check if an `renv::restore()` is likely to succeed, without actually touching the library? Optionally, ignoring any caches?

Scenario:

- In a long-running project, I want to lift all packages to the latest and greatest
- I'm not sure the code will work after I upgrade, so I'd like to be able to revert and get my code back to a running state
- Also, I'd like to see if my collaborators will be able to restore

Some of that could be achieved with profiles, I guess. Would that be the recommended approach?

title: `record` drops requirements from lockfile
description:
Calling `record(<package>)` empties the Requirements fields of a lock file

reproducible example:
``` r
library(renv) # inside a fresh project
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'renv'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     embed, update
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:utils':
#> 
#>     history, upgrade
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     autoload, load, remove
install("cli")
#> Installing cli [3.3.0] ...
#>  OK [linked cache]
snapshot()
#> * Lockfile written to '~/deleteMe/renv.lock'.
lockfile <- renv:::renv_lockfile_read(renv::paths$lockfile())
lockfile$Packages$cli$Requirements
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "glue"

record("glue")
#> * Updated 1 record in "~/deleteMe/renv.lock".
lockfile <- renv:::renv_lockfile_read(renv::paths$lockfile())
lockfile$Packages$cli$Requirements
#> list()
```

<sup>Created on 2022-06-28 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>

I figured this is probably not intended. It happens here
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/f9cc3e0ec2f4eb0c1a729fa41f794c71c92f96e5/R/lockfile-write.R#L55-L72

In the example, `vals <- keep(record, keys)` returns an empty list.

description:

The following is a problem I [listed on rstudio community](https://community.rstudio.com/t/renv-package-management-with-mice-and-micemd/136646), where I was unable to get renv to work with mice/micemd. Reposting here as requested. My apologies for taking so long, I have been busy on another project until now. 

## Post 1 

I am having a bit of trouble using mice and micemd with renv. My code runs fine when using my global library. However, for production purposes I need a local project library. I have three scripts...

NLP and clustering - runs fine with renv
batch script sourcing 3 - runs fine until it hits problem in 3
metric builder script with mice and micemd. - displays the following error below
Error in checkForRemoteErrors(val) : **
** 5 nodes produced errors; first error: could not find function "check.deprecated"

5 nodes produced errors; first error: could not find function "check.deprecated"
This part does not always show up.
In addition: Warning messages:

** closing unused connection 37 (<-localhost.localdomain:11306)**

Because of the error I updated R and the packages mice and micemd to current on CRAN, again I get the same issue unless I am using the global library stored in the R program folder.

The packages are in my lockfile, and I used renv::isolate to make sure they are stored locally rather than linked. I also used renv::rebuild(), which resulted in an error in installing MASS, although checking the functions it seems to work fine.

I have managed to get the function to work a few times, like after a clean install of R and Rstudio, but once the other scripts and were run and packages installed the function failed in both the test example below and the batch processes. I'm not really sure where to go from here, any advice would be much appreciated?

windows 10

title: using wrong version of package, although the correct version was given - mistake on my end
Different dependencies per OS
description:
Hey Kevin!

Potentially pretty niche question / request: Our process is set up such that we each develop on MacOS, but then deploy to production with Docker (`rocker` images). In one case, we want to use `rocker/cuda` to train XGBoost on a GPU. However, this is non-trivial since the GPU-compatible versions of XGBoost aren't able to be on CRAN -- see [this issue](https://github.com/dmlc/xgboost/issues/6654).

But then there's another caveat: our local machines don't have GPUs, so we don't need to use the pre-built binary on local. But even then, there would be a problem: The binaries are OS-specific, so we'd need to have one for MacOS (local) and one for Linux (production) if we wanted to correctly set up the lockfile such that it points to a local source. AFAICT, that won't work.

So on to the question: Is there any reasonable way to get this to play nicely with `renv`? The best I could come up with was to snapshot the correct _version_ of XGBoost and then when `restore`ing the `renv` cache, just completely removing the CRAN version of XGBoost after the restore finishes and replacing it with a version we install with `R CMD INSTALL`. It's super hacky, but it seems to work.

Let me know if you've got any ideas about a better way to manage this multi-OS, multi-source issue! Thanks a bunch :)

title: renv and ACL's when using ACL'ed cache
description:
`renv` is doing a great job of retaining ACL's for all file/directory copy and move operations. 

In a situation however where there exists an ACL both on the project folder but also in the global renv cache, any package copied to the cache will inherit the ACL from the project folder but not adopt the one from the cache. 

This then creates issues when different users install the same package. `renv` will then create backup files of previous package installations and reinstall and re-add to the cache again. 

It is not clear what the rationale is to have `renv` being so restrictive with ACL's.

title: Enhancement: `renv::dependencies()` support with rpy2's `importr` in .py files
description:
As documented [here](https://rpy2.github.io/doc/latest/html/introduction.html), `rpy2` supports importing R packages in python through `rpy2.robjects.packages.importr` in the style of:

```
from rpy2.robjects.packages import importr
# import R's "base" package
base = importr('base')

# import R's "utils" package
utils = importr('utils')
```

It would be really nice to have `renv::dependencies()` detect packages imported as `importr("package")` in `.py` files similar to how `library(package)` and `require(package)` is detected in `.R` files. 

Thanks for a great package!

title: 0.15.3+ bug - Installs incorrect package when multiple packages in a github repo
description:
I can't easily add a reprex as I discovered the issue on our private github repo.

We have a github repo with multiple R packages, each in it's own folder, like:

```
repo
└───package_a
    └────  R
           | code.R
           | ...
    │   DESCRIPTION
    |   NAMESPACE
    │
└───package_b
    └────  R
           | code.R
           | ...
    │   DESCRIPTION
    |   NAMESPACE
...
```

Before renv 0.15.3 I could run:

`renv::install('github_repo/r_package_name')`

to install a package from the repo. Since 0.15.3 `renv:::renv_install_package_unpack` unpacks the tarball, sees all the DESCRIPTION files for each package and then this line:
`descpath <- descpaths[n == min(n)]`
seems to take the DESCRIPTION with the shortest filepath. This means that when I ask for any package it actually selects the package with the shortest name. (This then leads to errors further in the installation).

`renv_install_package_unpack` knows which `package` it's looking for, could it pick the relevant `descpath` in the case there are many?

title: project restart slow when using the cellar
description: When I first started using `renv`, restarting my R Session was pretty snappy, like a non-renv-based R Project. I found that once I started using the cellar and adding more and more in-house tarballs to it, each restart was rather slow. I did some profiling (using RStudio's built-in profiler tools) and it seems that each time renv is activated (each restart), renv crawls through the cellar, untars each package, then extracts the package version/description. It seems to me this untar process is what is causing the significant slow-down. I have quite a few packages in my cellar, and some are over 100MB. Is there something that can be done here to avoid so many untar calls? Thanks for any input!

title: Cache symlinks not being created
description:
Inside an ubuntu based docker container I'm installing R and using renv to manage global packages. I want to install packages from my renv.lock to `renv:::renv_libpaths_system()`. I want to use the cache to speed up build times and I want to use symlinks to the cache.

Here's what I'm doing:

- install R
- `mkdir /renv_cache` and copy cache from host into `/renv_cache`
- `ENV RENV_PATHS_CACHE /renv_cache`
- `R -e "renv::init(bare=TRUE, force=TRUE); options(renv.config.cache.symlinks = TRUE); renv::restore(prompt=FALSE, library=renv:::renv_libpaths_system(), lockfile='<path to lockfile>')"`

Here's what is happening:
- packages are being installed to `/opt/R/4.1.2/lib/R/library/` (expected and desired!)
- packages are being COPIED, not symlinked (not expected)

I'm not sure why the symlinks are not being created. Any suggestions?

title: tempdir - lib
description:

```r

  print(list.files(tmp)) # print for debug

    unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE)
  })

  path <- file.path(tmp, "cars.csv")
  write.csv(cars, file = path)

title: renv is attempting to write to R site-library folder

title: Remote parsing for git URLs fails with number in URL
description:
`renv_remotes_parse_git` works on URLs like this one:

``` r
renv:::renv_remotes_parse_git("git@github.com:rstudio/renv")
#> $spec
#> [1] "git@github.com:rstudio/renv"
#> 
#> (etc...)
```

but as soon as there's a number in the username part of the URL it chokes:

``` r
renv:::renv_remotes_parse_git("git@github.com:rstudio1/renv")
#> Error: 'git@github.com:rstudio1/renv' is not a valid remote
```

This is stopping me from cloning a repository on an enterprise installation of GitHub where my username has a number in it.

Numbers are tolerated fine in the repo part (e.g. `git@github.com:rstudio/renv1` is fine) and indeed those parts of the regex are different patterns:

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/35af08a635dde1d225cfe1a1c36cf61067d87ee3/R/remotes.R#L150-L165

I'm not sure if there's a general rule for what characters are allowed to appear in the username part, but at least the character range should be expanded from `"[/:]([-\\.a-zA-Z]+)"` to `"[/:]([-\\.a-zA-Z0-9]+)"` to reflect what's possible on GHE.

title: Renv fails to install packages under R 4.2.0 with Rtools42 on Windows
description: Renv fails to identify the Rtools42 folder when Rtools 4.2 is installed on Windows. If RENV_PATHS_RTOOLS is unset, R BUILD fails to find g++. If RENV_PATHS_RTOOLS is set, another bug prevents this from working since the `renv_paths_rtools` function throws an error.

title: Same package installed from different repos leads to spurious lockfile changes
description:
## Problem

I often end up with diffs that look like this where the only thing that changes is the repository and some metadata: 

```diff
diff --git a/renv/profiles/lesson-requirements/renv.lock b/renv/profiles/lesson-requirements/renv.lock
index 1d33a23..83d704c 100644
--- a/renv/profiles/lesson-requirements/renv.lock
+++ b/renv/profiles/lesson-requirements/renv.lock
@@ -132,7 +132,7 @@
       "Package": "knitr",
       "Version": "1.39",
       "Source": "Repository",
-      "Repository": "CRAN",
+      "Repository": "RSPM",
       "Hash": "029ab7c4badd3cf8af69016b2ba27493",
       "Requirements": [
         "evaluate",
@@ -162,7 +162,7 @@
       "Package": "renv",
       "Version": "0.15.4",
       "Source": "Repository",
-      "Repository": "CRAN",
+      "Repository": "RSPM",
       "Hash": "c1078316e1d4f70275fc1ea60c0bc431",
       "Requirements": []
     },
@@ -178,7 +178,7 @@
       "Package": "rmarkdown",
       "Version": "2.14",
       "Source": "Repository",
-      "Repository": "CRAN",
+      "Repository": "RSPM",
       "Hash": "31b60a882fabfabf6785b8599ffeb8ba",
       "Requirements": [
         "bslib",
@@ -211,10 +211,7 @@
       "Package": "stringi",
       "Version": "1.7.6",
       "Source": "Repository",
-      "Repository": "https://carpentries.r-universe.dev",
-      "RemoteUrl": "https://github.com/gagolews/stringi",
-      "RemoteRef": "v1.7.6",
-      "RemoteSha": "1a1b5115884cd68650915bb1a8ad893ee4d3f4c6",
+      "Repository": "CRAN",
       "Hash": "bba431031d30789535745a9627ac9271",
       "Requirements": []
     },

```

This occurs if I change machines or work with collaborators and I'm wondering if there is a way to add an option that would prevent the modification of a lockfile entry if the hash of the package is identical? 

## Background

Somewhat related to #785, but I'm in a situation where we are trying to distribute projects that can be worked on without the user needing to know anything about {renv} or how it works. 

To achieve this, we have a function that uses a named project and runs a [`hydrate(); restore(); snapshot()` workflow](https://carpentries.github.io/sandpaper/articles/building-with-renv.html#motivation).

Here's an example of our problem: [this diff generated from a github action shows several packages where the only field changed is "Repository" from "CRAN" -> "RSPM"](https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper-docs/commit/2edbea7d0843be6e839b7adb2953a693984cc6f6#diff-6e829793be5e3c69a05e6cd6cfdbb06dc108a8bfde1d1a36e9209b78d1850099).

A [subsequent commit two months later changed the "Repository" back from "RSPM" -> "CRAN"](https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper-docs/commit/3f3c7bff6a14958c70922989c65c32b175376f91).

I believe that I could find a workaround for this by checking and modifying the lockfile post-snap, but I'm wondering if the solution could exist in {renv}.

title: renv should not infer `quarto` R requirement from the presence of `_quarto.yml`.
description:
It looks like renv adds infers a dependency for the quarto R package if it finds `_quarto.yml` in the working directory. The presence of Quarto files shouldn't imply a Quarto dependency, since Quarto does its rendering outside of R, and the `quarto` R package is just an interface for scripting interactions with the Quarto binary.

There might be other dependencies to infer from a the `_quarto.yml`, so we probably want to leave the hook in place. Perhaps the only change needed here is to remove line 556.

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/203d222e8d540f0ab29f251986fd47a3363907d7/R/dependencies.R#L235

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/203d222e8d540f0ab29f251986fd47a3363907d7/R/dependencies.R#L554-L557

I don't think any changes is needed to the handling of `.qmd` files, only `_quarto.yml`.

It looks like `renv` does inspect at `.qmd` files like it does `.Rmd` files, but only to discover dependencies in code chunks and the YAML front matter. It doesn't look like it adds a `quarto` dependency if those files are discovered — I'd expect that to occur around here:

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/203d222e8d540f0ab29f251986fd47a3363907d7/R/dependencies.R#L582

title: Export {renv} utilities?
use_python duplicates project-local conda environment
description:
Best practice and common use of conda is to create a project-local environment for reproducibility - https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/tasks/manage-environments.html#specifying-a-location-for-an-environment - although this is not the default behavior.

In this way I end up with a /projectdir/envs/ folder containing the python interpreter along with all the required packages.
Reproducibility via version control is guaranteed by committing the environment.yml file as usual.

When using `renv::use_python(python="./envs/python.exe", type="conda")` all packages will be reinstalled into ./renv/python/condaenvs/renv-python/ folder. This is understandable when conda is used in the default mode with the conda  environment folder sitting outside the project folder (usually in the /anaconda3/envs/ folder). But again that is not the best practice and common use. It would be great if `renv::use_python(python="./envs/python.exe", type="conda")` could use the ./envs/ project-local conda environment when the interpreter sits in the same project folder to avoid duplications.

title: partial restore()s
description:
This is more of a question.

When I try a restore(), a package installation might fail and then all of the progress installing the packages is lost. For example, if I run restore() and 10 packages appear, 9 of them might successfully build and 1 will fail. But when I run restore() again, all 10 appear un-installed. (The successful packages are quick to reinstall because they are cached though.)

Is this the intended behavior of restore()? That it succeeds only when every package reinstalls successfully? (I don't care if it is. Just want to clarify.) If so, there a way to get a vector of package names from the lockfile, so I can bulk install() packages?

title: Setting the public RSPM as CRAN URL breaks MRAN
description:
Installation from MRAN fails if an URL to RStudio Package Manager is used as CRAN URL.

With the following script, openssl is downloaded from MRAN as `.tgz` :

```sh
#!/bin/sh

# run from the renv directory
R CMD INSTALL .
rm -rf test
mkdir test
cd test
R -q -e 'options(repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org/"); renv::init()'
R -q -e 'renv::snapshot()'
R -q -e 'renv::purge("openssl")'
R -q -e 'renv::install("openssl")'
```

Changing the URL to `https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/2022-04-15` or even `https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest` now gets the `.tar.gz` and attempts to build the package.

I tried older versions as far back as 0.10.0, with seemingly the same behavior. I remember seeing this working before.

We're using fixed-date snapshots to pin all packages to some consistent state. The snapshot is supposed to define the versions to be installed, but I'd still expect the binaries to be downloaded from MRAN.

This is on macOS M1, R 4.1.3 .

title: Build packages with vignettes on offline systems
description:
We started to use renv for versioning on our offline system, with multiple versioned self-hosted R package repositories (CRAN, gitlab, bioconductor, etc.) on RSPM.

According to #344 it is recommended to set the self-hosted cran repository via `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE`. However, that seems to not only overwrite repositories during [bootstrap ](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/inst/resources/activate.R#L89)but also during R package [installation ](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/R/install.R#L152)and thus does not work with multiple versioned self-hosted repositories. Using the `options('renv.repos.cran'=<cran repos>)` in the .Rprofile project file works perfectly for restoring the project. Renv correctely [bootstraps](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/inst/resources/activate.R#L105) and installs packages using the checkpoints encoded in `renv.lock`.

## Problems

When developing R packages with vignettes, I am not able to build the source package with vignettes via the Rstudio IDE. Rstudio keeps trying to renv restore the session during the `- installing the package to build vignettes` step, even though I added all renv files/folders to `.Rbuildignore`. It seems to ignore the `options('renv.repos.cran'=<cran repos>)` but still tries to restore the project (session freezes, as it is a offline system). I tested both, `R CMD build ...` and `devtools::build()` via the IDE, both did not work. However, `devtools::buil()` in a project session works fine.


## Code snippets

**.Rprofile**
```{r}
options(renv.repos.cran ='<self-hosted cran>')
source("renv/activate.R")
```

**.Rbuildignore**
```{r}
^renv$
^renv\.lock$
^\.Rprofile$
```

**Bootstrap works fine**
```{r}
# Bootstrapping renv 0.15.4 --------------------------------------------------
* Downloading renv 0.15.4 ... OK (downloaded source)
* Installing renv 0.15.4 ... Done!
* Successfully installed and loaded renv 0.15.4.
* Project '~/r_package' loaded. [renv 0.15.4]
* The project library is out of sync with the lockfile.
* Use `renv::restore()` to install packages recorded in the lockfile.
```

**Building in the session after `renv::restore()`**
```{r}
> devtools::build()
✓  checking for file ‘/home/foo/r_package/DESCRIPTION’ ...
─  preparing ‘r_package’: (651ms)
✓  checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ...
─  installing the package to build vignettes
✓  creating vignettes (5m 17s)
─  checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts (498ms)
─  checking for empty or unneeded directories
─  building r_package_0.0.1.tar.gz’
   
[1] "/home/foo/r_package_0.0.1.tar.gz"
```

**Rstudio > Build > Build Source Package**
```{r}
==> devtools::build()

✓  checking for file ‘/home/foo/r_package/DESCRIPTION’ ...
─  preparing ‘foo’: (635ms)
✓  checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ...
─  installing the package to build vignettes
         -----------------------------------
   # Bootstrapping renv 0.15.4 --------------------------------------------------

     cannot open URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES
```

Could you please help me with the correct setting for such a system, so that building via RStudio also works?

title: feature request: default permissions setting
description:
I am working in a unix-like environment with many users with varying default permissions that are used when they create files. I am trying to setup `renv` so that all users could share the same cache. For the most part this works very well, however, if someone installs a new package with read-only permissions, new versions can't be added without the original user going in and opening the permissions back up.

Would it be possible to add a `mode` argument to `install` and `update`? Or perhaps some new [configuration setting](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/config.html)? I did see this `renv.config.copy.method` and wondered if somehow a `Sys.chmod` could be added to keep the permissions open but I didn't really understand how to use this setting exactly or where it applies.

Thanks for any advice!

edit:
I tried adding this to my .Rprofile and it did not seem to work:
```r
options(renv.config.copy.method = function(src, dst) {
  Sys.chmod(paths = src, mode = "0777", use_umask = FALSE)
  file.copy(from = src, to = dst, overwrite = TRUE, recursive = TRUE, copy.mode = TRUE, copy.date = TRUE)
})
```

```

After reviewing the documentation, I realize I should have used `renv::install(packages = "data.table@1.14.0")` or `renv::update(packages = "data.table")`. Maybe this syntax could be supported? Or perhaps the `@` could be caught and a helpful error message provided?

Thanks!

title: Install package from private Gitlab repo using user/password authentication on Windows
description:
I'm successfully installing/restoring package from Gitlab private repo using Personal Access Token, however I'm wondering whether it is possible to do it using user/password authentication on Windows (this is crucial I believe). Specifically I would like to use Deploy Token, which basically works the same as username + password. I would like to pass both values as environmental variables. I know I could do `renv::install(git::https://GIT_USER:GIT_PASS@gitlab.com/username/package.git)`, but then credentials would be saved in `renv.lock` what is undesirable.

I've tried something like this
```r
Sys.setenv("GIT_USER" = "<username>")
Sys.setenv("GIT_PASS" = "<password>")
renv::install("git::https://gitlab.com/user/package.git")
```
but it's failing with `Error: failed to resolve remote`.  Issue #316 and some digging led me to the conclusion, that it doesn't work because appropriate sections of `renv_scope_git_auth` are not yet implemented for Windows, am I right? I've tested it on Linux and it works.


I've also tried this
```r
remotes::install_git(
  "https://gitlab.com/user/package.git",
  credentials = git2r::cred_env(username = "GIT_USER", password = "GIT_PASS")
)
```
which successfully installed the package, but failed on `renv::restore()`, which wasn't surprising since `renv` has no idea that it should use those credentials.

Is it any way to get around this at this moment? I think it could be useful in some cases, especially in combination with Deploy Tokens.

title: Feature request: Pin dependencies
description:
I have a few dependencies in an `renv` environment which are hard to install on the cluster but easy to install locally, such as `rgdal` and `sf`. 

Whenever we add a new package locally, `renv` is very aggressive at ensuring all dependencies are at their latest possible versions. This often results in "trivial" version bumps for our hard-to-download packages. For instance, right now we have `rgdal@1.5-28` installed on the cluster but our `renv.lock` lists `rgdal@1.5-29`. We get warnings that we should run `renv::restore()`, but this requires manually downloading `rgdal@1.5-29` which sometimes fails due to configurations. 

It would be nice to pin the difficult-to-download versions in the `renv.lock` file so they are never update, and a lower version of a new package is installed if needed.

title: Remove packages not in lock file
description:
Though `renv::restore()` is described as "to restore the state of your project from `renv.lock`", it will happily leave additional packages that have been installed but not yet added to lockfile (e.g. via `renv::snapshot()`) in the local package cache.  

Maybe this is merely a quirk of my own workflows or I'm doing something wrong, but I find this results in projects growing ever larger `renv.lock` files over time, as I switch to a different package to perform a similar function, or as I install a package for some one-off interactive testing while in an active renv project but don't actually use it.  (This balloons even faster with collaborators who may also install packages for one-off use and have no way to restore their local cache to the pristine required-packages-only described in the renv lock file.  Then eventually when they need to add a new or updated package to the lock-file they run `renv::snapshot()` and the lockfile rapidly expands to the kitchen sink).  

Is there a function that could simply remove the packages that have been installed but not added via `renv::snapshot()` (other than `renv::deactivate()`, or manually destroying the local package cache, which do not feel like the ergonomic ways to do this).  If not, would you consider adding one?  (And again apologies if I'm just missing something entirely obvious!)

title: An insuppressible message is printed at startup
description:
I recently upgraded `renv` for a project (from 0.13.1), and now each activation prints `* Project 'whatever' loaded. [renv 0.15.4]`. Wrapping `suppressPackageStartupMessages` and `suppressMessages` around `source("renv/activate.R")` doesn't work.

`capture.output` is an effective workaround, but presumably this will also silence warnings about the lockfile not being up to date, which isn't ideal.

title: Error: all repository entries must be named
description:
My organization has its own internal CRAN-like repository, and it sets the default `"repos"` option for all of us.

```r
> getOption("repos")
  CRAN 
"CENSORED/CENSORED-cran" 
                                                                            
"CENSORED/bioconductor/bioc" 
                                                                            
"CENSORED/data/annotation" 
                                                                            
"CENSORED/data/experiment" 
                                                                            
"CENSORED/workflows"
```

Not all the repos have names.

```r
> names(getOption("repos"))
[1] "CRAN" ""     ""     ""     ""    
```

When I run `renv::init()` on an empty (or small) project, I get an error (with both CRAN `renv` and 7243b4810f58d4fc11025a1eedf8e9ca8e21fe94):

```r
> renv::init()
* Initializing project ...
* Discovering package dependencies ... Done!
* Copying packages into the cache ... Done!
Error: all repository entries must be named
Traceback (most recent calls last):
5: renv::init()
4: snapshot(project = project, library = libpaths, repos = repos, 
       prompt = FALSE)
3: renv_repos_validate(repos)
2: stopf("all repository entries must be named")
1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
```

This error resolves itself when I manually give names to all entries of `getOption("repos")`.

As a workaround, I will ask my devops team to name all the repos. But would it be possible for `renv` to supply its own default names if none already exist? As a user, I almost never think about repos and would prefer them to be handled automatically.

title: renv has trouble parsing multiline yaml chunk options
description:
I was trying out {renv} with an RMarkdown document that uses yaml syntax for multiline figure captions. While it works for {knitr}, {renv} throws an error. If you parse down in the error, it's related to renv not being able to parse the yaml syntax. On the surface, this looks similar to #772, but I think the root cause is related to how the chunks in knitr are partitioned. I'm wondering if the upcoming export of `partition_chunk()` from knitr will help with this: https://github.com/yihui/knitr/pull/2083

Here's an example (text from https://stackoverflow.com/a/70665396/2752888):

```` r
  txt <- r"{But, the new syntax also allows you to use yaml syntax to specify the chunk options, and yaml allows for multiline strings. So you could do the following:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| fig.cap: >
#|   Here is my really long caption.  It'd be nice to
#|   split this and other portions across lines

print(plot(x=runif(100),y=runif(100)))
```
}"
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".Rmd")
  writeLines(txt, tmp)
````

This works in knitr

``` r
  writeLines(knitr::knit(text = txt))
#> But, the new syntax also allows you to use yaml syntax to specify the chunk options, and yaml allows for multiline strings. So you could do the following:
#> 
#> ![Here is my really long caption.  It'd be nice to split this and other portions across lines](https://i.imgur.com/3ofKiSk.png)
#> 
#> ```
#> #> NULL
#> ```
```

This does NOT work with `renv::dependencies()`

``` r
  renv::dependencies(dirname(tmp))
#> Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
#> Error in split.default(x = seq_len(nrow(x)), f = f, drop = drop, ...): group length is 0 but data length > 0
```

title: renv_python_discover should return python earliest in PATH, not latests
description:
Hi devs,

The issue I have encountered occurs when first starting an renv project that uses a python virtualenv, in a system with two installations of the same version of python available in PATH. When running for the first time running, renv attempts to create a virtualenv, but finds an unexpected python executable. I expect that the python executable in a folder found earliest on PATH (left-most) would be used, however the python executable found latest on PATH is found.

I believe the cause of this behaviour is in the code for discovering paths for installed python binaries renv_python_discover. In the function, the folders on PATH are traversed (from latest to earliest/rightmost to leftmost) and any found binaries are pushed to a 'stack'. Finally, the $data() method is called on the stack to get the list of pushed binaries. This method returns a list of pushed elements in the order they were pushed, meaning that the python executables that occur in folders earlier on PATH are at the front of the list. The function then returns the first executable with the appropriate version from the list.
 
 To fix this behaviour, some possible options are:
 - don't reverse the order of the folders on PATH in the loop where the found executables are pushed
 - change the behaviour of the $data() method of the stack to reverse the internal list so that elements pushed last are at the front of the list
 - reverse the output of the $data() method
 
 Sorry for not providing a reproducible example! 
 
 Thanks, 
 Tim

title: Support remotes syntax `local::` to reference local packages
description:
In the example given here https://remotes.r-lib.org/articles/dependencies.html#other-sources the following syntax is used to reference local packages:
```
# Local
Remotes: local::/pkgs/testthat
```

I'm aware that it's possible to reference local packages, also in DESCRIPTION files, but  I was wondering whether `renv` should also support the syntax `remotes` uses.

It should be possible to achieve this with some minor changes to `renv_remotes_resolve`:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/cac6c849a24c396f039faa95bb993587e78e5ccc/R/remotes.R#L28-L36 

I guess this can also be achieved by adding e.g., `renv_remotes_resolve_local(remote)` to

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/4e84a06688e531a14142ebf82ea30e4f414a38fa/R/remotes.R#L71-L80

although that probably also requires changes to `renv_remotes_parse`.

Either way, I'd be happy to contribute a PR if you think this makes sense!

    htmltools,

Config/testthat/edition: 3
```

When I do `renv::init(bare=TRUE)` and then `renv::snapshot(type = "explicit")` I only get: 

```
* Project '~/projects/debugme' loaded. [renv 0.15.2]
> renv::snapshot(type="explicit")
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# CRAN ===============================
- renv   [* -> 0.15.2]

```
I'm aware I'd need to add `Suggests` to the `settings.dcf`, but I'd at least expect it to find `purrr` as dependency. 
My understanding of the process is this:
- I need an extra package
- I do `usethis::use_package(<pkg>)`
- `<pkg>` is installed by `usethis`
- it's added to `DESCRIPTION` by `usethis`
- I want to snapshot the exact versions of the packages to `renv.lock` to use it e.g. in a Docker container and I try `renv::snapshot(type = "explicit")`

Does `renv`, during snapshot, look at the `DESCRIPTION`, find `purrr`, then checks the local library, find `purrr` is installed, and record that version in `renv.lock`? On the other side if I have `dplyr` in the local library, but not in `DESCRIPTION`, it would not get added to `renv.lock` because it's not in `DESCRIPTION`, no?
I read here that the `renv.lock` is the source of truth, that contradicts the role of the `DESCRIPTION` file though. 
In my understanding, `DESCRIPTION` needs to list packages, possibly lower barriers for versions, and with `renv.lock` I record the exact versions, _but_ only of the ones the `DESCRIPTION` lists, it should be the base-layer of truth.

What approaches are there to separate `Suggests` and `Imports` lockfile wise? For CI, I'd need the `Suggests` packages, but not in e.g. in production.

title: Restore env from `DESCRIPTION`
description:
Is it possible to restore the env based upon `DESCRIPTION` file? 

The use case is:
1. I create an R project and install the packages from the `DESCRIPTION` with `renv::install()`
1. Anytime I need a new package I write in the `DESCRIPTION` file and type `renv::install()` again. With the auto snapshot, this will also update the `renv.lock` file
1. I "mistakenly" install a package from the console with `renv::install('<package>')` (without including it in `DESCRIPTION`) and snapshot it. 

Now, `DESCRIPTION` and `renv.lock` have diverged, but any action on the environment will prioritize `renv.lock` while I would like to prioritize `DESCRIPTION`. 

Ideally, I would like `renv::install()` to remove all deps **not** in `DESCRIPTION`, so to keep `DESCRIPTION` and `renv.lock` aligned. Another solution is to allow `renv::restore()` to point to `DESCRIPTION`. Another note, I would suggest to make `renv::install()` a little more verbose with something like `renv::install(DESCRIPTION)`

title: wrong package version loaded from cache if version numbers are equal
description:
reprex (assuming the poorman package is not in the renv cache):
```r
renv::init()
renv::install('nathaneastwood/poorman@4750f4a0567414ee0a6c8edb35d477e8f88b2784')
renv::install('poorman@0.2.5')
```
actual behavior: The first renv::install will install poorman@0.2.5 from GitHub, the second renv::install will load the Version from GitHub from cache.
expected behavior: The second renv::install should instead check the cache for a poorman@0.2.5 installation from CRAN, and if it does not find it, install poorman@0.2.5 from CRAN (just as if the cached GitHub installation was not there, or rebuild = TRUE was passed).

Maybe this is not considered a bug in general, but for our use case it is, so an option for the expected behavior would be great. We have many people developing the same package independently via forks. As a result different versions of the same package have the same version number, but they can be differentiated by installation source (GitHub repos/forks, CRAN, CRAN-like repository, r-universe). Now these people test their changes on a shared HPC with a shared global renv cache. Some people want to install the "official" version of a package, but instead they get a development version from the global renv cache that was installed from a fork.

title: `.libPaths` is being updated when suspended session is restored
description:
I'm using RStudio Workbench, and have an renv-enabled project.  When the the project is first opened, `.libPaths` looks like this:

```r
> .libPaths()
[1] "/home/comzm/renv_test/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
[2] "/opt/R/4.0.5/lib/R/library"   
```

After awhile of inactivity, the R session will enter a suspended state (it can also be forcibly suspended from the home screen to avoid having to wait).  Then when the session is resumed, `.libPaths` looks like this:

```r
> .libPaths()
[1] "/home/comzm/renv_test/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
[2] "/opt/R/4.0.5/lib/R/library"                                  
[3] "/rlibrary/4.0"    
```

The third path is our site library that we set in `Rprofile.site` for use with non-renv-enabled projects.  It shouldn't be part of `.libPaths` in renv-enabled projects.

Restarting R correctly removes the third path from `.libPaths`.

I can see that when first opening the project or after restarting R, `.Library.site` is correctly set to `NULL`, but when resuming a suspended session, `Library.site` is set to `"/rlibrary/4.0"`.  If there is some code that runs to prevent `.Library.site` from being set, or overriding it once it is, that code doesn't seem to be triggered when resuming a suspended session.

title: In the presence of pak, renv does not symlink cached packages but builds them again from cache
description:
**Expected behaviour:**

step 1 is installing `SuppDists` as expected - download from RSPM, install it and add it to `renv` cache
step 2 detects the existence of `SuppDists` in the `renv` cache and symlinks it into the `renv` directory as it is default behaviour of `renv` without `pak`

**Actual behaviour**

step 1 is ok
step 2 the package is retrieved again from cache and installed (also evident from the timing)

**Reproducible example**

See below. Run in docker container rocker/r-ver:4.1.2 after running

```bash
apt-get update && apt-get install libxt6 libxtst6 pandoc vim
R -q -e "install.packages(c('styler','reprex'))"
```

Note 1: Example below uses admin privileges to install `renv` and `pak` but if `renv`/`pak` is already present this step can easily be omitted.
Note 2: `reprex` does not show `pak` output - I had to manually copy the pak output into the reprex output.  
Note 3: When installing `tidyverse` it is even more evident that (for binary packages) the cached (step 2) install takes the same amount of time than step 1 minus the download time. 

``` r
# Set up immutable URL from public RSPM

title: renv::activate() issue with cached library on travis
description:
With the update to v0.15, I am finding that `renv::activate(project = "path/to/project")` no longer correctly loads the project library when using a cached library on travis CI.

As recommended in the docs, we've been using 

```yaml
cache:
  directories:
  - "$HOME/.local/share/renv"
  - "$TRAVIS_BUILD_DIR/renv/library"
```

in `.travis.yml` and have not previously had any issues. However, our builds break with the update to v0.15.

It would be pretty time consuming to set up a fully reproducible example, but I'll try to summarize what I've seen in debugging.

The project structure is something like this:
````
/project
|_.Rprofile
|_.renv.lock
|_renv/
|_code/
|___script.R
````

As part of the build process, `script.R` is run from the `code` directory. `script.R` contains a call to `renv::activate`:

```r
renv::activate(project = "..")
```

If I check `.libPaths()` after this call I see

```r
"/home/travis/.cache/R/renv/library/repo-name-and-hash/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
```

But this directory does not contain project packages. It contains a folder called `renv` (which itself may contain the project packages, I'm not sure; I didn't poke around in it).

Also included in `.libPaths()` is 

```r
"/opt/R/4.1.1/lib/R/library"
```

which contains base R packages.


When I install the archived v0.14 of `renv` and run the same code `.libPaths()` shows

```r
"$TRAVIS_BUILD_DIR/renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
```

(where I've replaced the absolute path to the travis build directory with `$TRAVIS_BUILD_DIR`), which correctly loads the package library. 

In this case, `.libPaths()` also includes 

```r
"/tmp/RtmpZpPlNF/renv-system-library"
```

which contains the base R packages.


The issue seems to be isolated to using the `project` option of the call to `renv::activate` -- under v0.15 I am able to correctly load the package library if I open `R` in the `/project` folder (thereby loading `.Rprofile`, thereby calling `renv::activate()`).

I'm unable to reproduce this behavior locally on my Mac, which makes me believe it's somehow related to cache'ing on travis.

title: Windows network drive switch to project upon deactivate()
description:
I'm new to renv, so bare with me.

To test renv, I initially used a new directory on a local drive on my laptop. There I saved an R file (not an .Rproj), opened that .R file, and used renv::activate() and renv::deactivate(). This all worked pretty good locally. I then tried this on a windows network drive. When calling deactivate() in the opened .R file, Rstudio switches to the .Rproj file that is in the same directory (created when calling renv::activate() by default) in that network drive.This behaviour does not occur when on a local drive. On the local drive it just restarts the R session without switching to the .Rproj file (that was created by renv::activate()). 

Is there an option to stop renv or rstudio from switching to an .Rproj on a network drive when specifying renv::deactivate()?

system Windows 10
R version 4.1.2
Rstudio 2021.9.1.372
renv 0.15.0

(note: for this case I don't want to open the .Rproj as it was slower in performance on a network drive in conjunction with renv than just opening an .R file and renv::activate, my question is specific for why it switches to .Rproj on a network but not locally)

title: Confusing about `snapshot.type = "all"` and the R system package library
description:
**If this post is better suited for the RStudio Community, let me know and I'll post there.**

Me team and I use `snapshot.type = "all"` to capture all packages in a project library in the renv lock file. We primarily do this because a package may keep some dependencies in `Suggests`. When we install those Suggested packages to have the full features available to us, using `snapshot.type = "all"` ensures that those installed packages are recorded in the lock file (making the project portable and does not depend on any packages not listed in `renv.lock`).

An example of this is the survey package. The survey pkg lists the CompQuadForm pkg in Suggests. If CompQuadForm is installed, it is used in some p-value calculations. If it's not installed, the calculation falls back to another method. In our use case, we want to include CompQuadForm in the lock file, so whomever is running the code will restore the project's libraries and all calculations will be identical on all machines.

In the recent renv release, I am seeing that the system R library is included in `.libPaths()`. This update, coupled with `snapshot.type = "all"`, results in renv trying to snapshot every package installed on a user's system library to the project lock file.

```r
Restarting R session...

* Project 'C:/Users/SjobergD/GitHub/Writing-Function-with-the-tidyverse' loaded. [renv 0.15.1]
> .libPaths()
[1] "C:/Users/SjobergD/GitHub/my_project/renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-w64-mingw32"
[2] "C:/Program Files/R/R-4.1.1/library"    
```

What workflow should we use to 1. Capture all packages we utilize (even when there is not a direct call to a function within that package (aka the package is being used internally in another package), and 2. not capture every installed package from the system library in each project's lock file.

Thank you! 🕺🏼

title: Caching performance issue with Gitlab CI/CD
description:
Hi there,

In the documentation, there is a starter Gitlab template:

```yaml
variables:
  RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE: "http://cran.r-project.org"
  RENV_PATHS_CACHE: ${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/cache
  RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY: ${CI_PROJECT_DIR}/renv/library

cache:
  key: ${CI_JOB_NAME}
  paths:
    - ${RENV_PATHS_CACHE}
    - ${RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY}

before_script:
  - < ... other pre-deploy steps ... >
  - Rscript -e "if (!requireNamespace('renv', quietly = TRUE)) install.packages('renv')"
  - Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
```

Most of the time, the ${RENV_PATHS_CACHE} has more than > 10000 files in my projects. This leads to very long time for job completion (> 2h if not timeout before) and is not acceptable for people in my team. 

Is there any rational behind storing this element in the cache?

I would argue that only storing the renv library is enough in most cases but maybe I missed something and would be curious to know the reason. 

If storing the renv library is enough, I'd like to add a quick note in the documentation about this possible performance issue to be aware of. it might be misleading for people beginning with the template. 

Let me know your thought.

Thanks

David

title: renv 0.15.0 writes extra line breaks to DESCRIPTION files in specific cases
description:
## Problem

`renv@0.15.0` seems to write extra CR characters to the DESCRIPTION file of installed packages under the following specific conditions:

- Installing a remote package from source to a Windows machine (GitLab, GitHub, etc.)
- While within an activated `renv` **_package_** project
- And the DESCRIPTION file of the installed remote package contains indented multi-line text such as below:

    ```
    Description: An R package to do lots of cool things and make good plots
        with many cool functions and statistics. Cats are cool. Dogs are cool too.
        Big long package description here.
    ```

After the remote package is installed via `renv`, the DESCRIPTION file will contain the info appended by `renv` plus additional line breaks after indented text. The text above becomes:

```
Description: An R package to do lots of cool things and make good plots

    with many cool functions and statistics. Cats are cool. Dogs are cool too.

    Big long package description here.
```

Or, with `cat -e DESCRIPTION`:

```
Description: An R package to do lots of cool things and make good plots^M^M$
    with many cool functions and statistics. Cats are cool. Dogs are cool too.^M^M$
    Big long package description here.^M$
```

The resulting DESCRIPTION file is unreadable (incorrect DCF format) and makes the package unusable.

I suspect this issue due the change in how `renv` handles installs for package projects. `0.15.0` move package project libraries to an external dir at `tools::R_user_dir("renv", "cache")`. Again, this only happens with >= 0.15.0 and only for package projects.

## More Info

NOTE: The line endings of the source package DESCRIPTION file don't seem to matter. My source package line endings are unix but are converted to windows endings on `renv::install()`.

```

description:

library/
local/
cellar/
lock/
python/
staging/

Normally these exclusions are added to` renv/.gitignore`, they appear to be applied to the `.gitignore` file in the repository/package root in error. To reproduce:

```r
library(devtools)

install(as.package("."), upgrade = "never", reload = FALSE, quick = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
```
