When installing Mikata-project/ggthemr@4a31e0df151eacee4cbcec736411c2704f44cf4a, I receive an error that the DESCRIPTION file is empty.

Instead, there is an encoding error in the DESCRIPTION file (see https://github.com/Mikata-Project/ggthemr/issues/53).

The error message from renv_dcf_read_impl should be more descriptive, e.g. `Failed to convert DESCRIPTION (882 bytes) to Encoding X`.

title: `renv::restore()` using pak as backend?
description: I'm so excited to see the [initial support](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/news/index.html) for `pak` to install packages with `renv`! I have everything working for installing packages, but I am testing out the experience of cloning a project and restoring the packages, and running `restore()` still installs the packages one-by-one even with `RENV_CONFIG_PAK_ENABLED = TRUE` declared in the project's `.Renviron` file. Is there another way to trick `restore()` to leverage pak?

title: renv::config$cache.symlinks() now returns NULL
description:
I found a minor issue in my wrapper of {renv} where I was using `renv::config$cache.symlinks() && BOOL` to pass on to a {callr} env var so that I can turn off cache symlinks when I'm testing and still allow the user to choose this option when they are running locally (https://github.com/carpentries/sandpaper/issues/223).

The change came from https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/1709a19ff7de208642a225963dad8252556ee1fa and now `renv::config$cache.symlinks()` returns `NULL` on UNIX instead of `TRUE` or `FALSE` unless it is manually set beforehand. 

I am now wondering: how should I provision this situation?

title: Consider using {pak} to handle installing package versions
description:
renv has been fantastic for our organisation, particularly in container images. However, the time taken to restore a whole lock file when building an image can be quite annoying. Is it possible to use the {pak} package to handle this to improve speed? I hope that it wouldn't be too onerous to modify functions to suit inputs to {pak}! It'd be great if these two RStudio packages could synergise..!

Thanks for your hard work

title: `Failing to load renv from project [...], reloading previously-loaded` when loading one renv from the working directory of another via RStudio's system terminal
description:
The below behavior makes {renv} incompatible with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) for `language: r`.

[{precommit}](https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit) has recently started to use {renv} as an environment manager for [various reasons](https://lorenzwalthert.github.io/precommit/news/index.html#precommit-v020), and I am quite excited about that. However, there is a problem that this does not work when the repository in which hooks with `language: r` from pre-commit are used is at the same time a {renv} project (https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit/issues/342). After countless hours of digging, I think I was able to narrow the problem down. When 
* you have a global {renv} version installed
* two {renv} projects e.g. `~/proj1`, and `~/proj2`.
* The two {renv} repos don't use the same (and globally installed) renv version.
* and you use the RStudio project in  `~/proj1` -> open the system terminal in RStudio ->  `cd ~/proj2` -> `R --vanilla`.

You can't load the renv from `~/proj2` with `source('renv/activate.R')`.

```
> search() # just to see there are no renv shims or renv is loaded
[1] ".GlobalEnv"        "package:stats"     "package:graphics" 
[4] "package:grDevices" "package:utils"     "package:datasets" 
[7] "package:methods"   "Autoloads"         "package:base"     
> source('renv/activate.R')
Warning message:
could not load renv from project "~/.cache/pre-commit/repoop2cc2mv/renv-default"; reloading previously-loaded renv 
```
The message apparently comes from [here](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/main/R/load.R#L522). It seems like the unload of one renv version and load of another can't be performed cleanly (although there was none loaded or attached to the search path).

What sounds like a very abstractly constructed case, is apparently pretty much what happens when you run `pre-commit install --install-hooks` or `git commit` if `pre-commit install --install-hooks` was not previously called. This means in most user's workflow, pre-commit can't be used in a project where {renv} is present within RStudio (unless you do a tedious workaround outside RStudio, which has to be done repeatedly on every `precommit::autoupdate()`) because the wrong renv is loaded. 

The interesting part is that the correct renv is loaded *unless* you use the System terminal within RStudio. Outside RStudio, the correct renv is loaded. title: Opt-out of `~/.Renviron` when `.Renviron` is present
description:
Related to #876 but for `.Renviron`.  There's an option to opt-in (default opted out) for the `~/.Rprofile`, but not the `~/.Renviron`.

I have a renv project with a `.Renviron` to set project-specific environment variables.  I want this project to be as encapsulated as possible, so I don't want to "accidentally" source my `~/.Renviron`.  If I read `?Startup` correctly, R only sources the project-specific one, instead of sourcing both.  I would expect `renv`'s defaults to respect this behavior.

Not a huge deal; I was just surprised when adding `renv` to my project expanded my available environment variables.

title: Bootstrapping from cellar
description:
Somewhat related to issue https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/820

But it would also be a nice feature if renv could first attempt to bootstrap from the cellar (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/6dcd471ffb35d0c3e91563ce51fec0c46b86fefb/vignettes/cellar.Rmd) or from a user specified path to a binary copy of renv or the source so they do not have to set up a local repository just to allow bootstrapping in environments with limited internet access.

I propose checking a binary or source for the required renv version in the cellar, or checking for an environment variable and/or an `options()` setting prior to attempting to download renv ([here](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/cc7963be31ce055fb5ea1a74265648d5db76abf3/R/bootstrap.R#L8)).

This would allow the user to either include renv in the cellar or specify a path to a binary or source through an environment variable or through `options()` in the .Rprofile prior to it calling `source("renv/activate.R")`.

title: simplify bootstrap code
description:
Right now, `renv` injects a pretty large subset of code into `renv/activate.R` to try and bootstrap itself. We should try to minimize some of this if possible.

In the simplest scenario, we could try to load `renv` from the user library, and then use that to load the associated project.

When running `renv::restore()` in a CI/CI job or during `docker build` (e.g. `RUN Rscript -e "renv::restore()"`), the output is quite verbose.

title: Handling of local packages (compiled from local source)
description:
This topic originated in #789 but will be continued here. 'Local package' means a package compiled and installed from a local source directory (not by `renv`) - regardless of whether that package is also present in a repository. Even though the local package may be in a different dev state than the versions available in one of the active Repositories, @kevinushey explained (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/789#issuecomment-943673814) it is intended behaviour of `renv` to link the local package with an available Repository in `renv.lock`, if applicable. In that regard three related aspects may profit from further improvement (we could split this in more issues if needed): **1.** In the case of a **r-universe** repository there is some inconsistency in `renv.lock` (and related output of `renv::snapshot()`): - local packages get the Repository _name_ as the value for their `Repository` key. This is consistent with the case for packages installed from CRAN and their local counterparts. - packages effectively installed from a r-universe repository, get the Repository _URL_ as value for their `Repository` key
Examples (partly from #789) ```json "rlang": { "Package": "rlang", "Version": "0.99.0.9009", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "rlib", "Hash": "29e7067079a29a891ac42418806585b5" }, ``` ```json { "R": { "Version": "4.1.2", "Repositories": [ { "Name": "rlib", "URL": "https://r-lib.r-universe.dev" } ] }, "Packages": { "rlang": { "Package": "rlang", "Version": "0.4.11.9001", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "https://r-lib.r-universe.dev", "RemoteUrl": "https://github.com/r-lib/rlang", "RemoteRef": "HEAD", "RemoteSha": "26c4a878473578cf7b4c630f457a3bdfc46c8c31" } } } ``` ```json "rlang": { "Package": "rlang", "Version": "0.99.0.9009", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Hash": "29e7067079a29a891ac42418806585b5" }, ``` From https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/789#issuecomment-944047718: > Regarding how the 'inbo' r-universe is depicted in two different ways, I was referring to the difference between packages INBOtheme and n2khab in the output of `renv::init()`: > > ``` > # https://inbo.r-universe.dev ======== ## THIS LINE > - INBOtheme [* -> 0.5.9] > ``` > > versus > > ``` > # inbo =============================== ## THIS LINE > - n2khab [* -> 0.5.0.900] > ``` > > Same in the above example `renv.lock`: > > ``` > "Source": "Repository", > "Repository": "https://inbo.r-universe.dev", > ``` > > versus > > ``` > "Source": "Repository", > "Repository": "inbo", > ``` > > Sure it is not wrong, it's just not 100% consistent; I'd expect either the name or the URL in both cases.
**2.** In contrast with `renv` 0.14.0, `renv` 0.14.0-50 does no longer complain when registering a package that cannot be linked to a known Repository - instead the `Repository` gets value `null` and no further messaging occurs.
Details (copied from #789) Both below cases only have the CRAN repo enabled (`options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org/"))`). #### with `renv` 0.14.0-50 (github): This locally built package (which is not on CRAN, only in the inbo r-universe repo = disabled in this session) is now stored like: ```json "n2khab": { "Package": "n2khab", "Version": "0.5.0.900", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": null, "Hash": "9aafc0465394ce0bd93a7220c20db697" }, ``` So a local package is now always set as coming from a repository, here being the 'null' repository (before, it would have been source 'unknown', not considered as coming from a repo). In this case no warning came anymore from `snapshot()` (which now reports this package under `# Repository ========`) or `status()`. ==> **Suggestion**: should a warning not have been risen, as it was in 0.14.0? - see below #### with `renv` 0.14.0 (CRAN): Local package registered as: ```json "n2khab": { "Package": "n2khab", "Version": "0.5.0.900", "Source": "unknown", "Hash": "9aafc0465394ce0bd93a7220c20db697" }, ``` Where warnings occurred: ```r > renv::snapshot() The following package(s) were installed from an unknown source: _ n2khab [0.5.0.900] renv may be unable to restore these packages in the future. Consider reinstalling these packages from a known source (e.g. CRAN). Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile: # CRAN =============================== ... # (Unknown Source) =================== - n2khab [* -> 0.5.0.900] Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y * Lockfile written to '/.../renv.lock'. > renv::status() * The project is already synchronized with the lockfile. The following package(s) were installed from an unknown source: _ n2khab [0.5.0.900] renv may be unable to restore these packages in the future. Consider reinstalling these packages from a known source (e.g. CRAN). ```
**3.** It could be argued that `renv` should always warn the user when registering a local package, since it can be in a different state than the version available in a Repository.

title: Windows - request to use robocopy for `renv_file_move` by default
description:
We had an issue on some Windows machines where `renv::restore()` was taking an extra 8 minutes after the last `install` had completed, while on other PCs the restore completed "instantly".

We eventually tracked this down to the fact that `renv` was using `move` on those PCs while on others it was using `robocopy`.

We've worked around this by now using `options(renv.config.install.transactional = FALSE)` as proposed in https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/621

There are several advantages in using `robocopy` - including it's quicker at copying files and (particularly important for renv) by default it seems it copies junction points, rather than deep copying the underlying files - which is what `move` was doing on those PCs.

Based on what I've seen in this testing, I'd like to suggest removing this block https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/bf04c2dbcba4fe9cd9535874f04b1fdeb99b52a1/R/files.R#L213-L219 ... or to put it behind an option which defaults to `off`. 

On Windows, the code would then drop through to https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/bf04c2dbcba4fe9cd9535874f04b1fdeb99b52a1/R/files.R#L60-L78 followed by `unlink` https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/bf04c2dbcba4fe9cd9535874f04b1fdeb99b52a1/R/files.R#L226

Other possible options that could be considered:
- `robocopy` has a `/MOVE` switch which could be added (some refactoring required for this though)
- `mklink` could again be used to make the junction point in the library path instead of moving the junction point out of staging (this feels like a bigger change though)

title: option for ignore rules
description:
renv should allow callers to indicate project-level ignore rules using an in-memory option. This would let us map the packrat option ignored.directories to an renv setting, for example.

We are considering a function like the following to create renv rules from the packrat setting:

```r
# Return renv ignore patterns based on the packrat ignored.directories option.
# Each directory is returned as a rooted pattern for renv, meaning that it
# should only apply at the root directory of the project.
#
# Note: The "/data/" and "/inst/" directories are ignored by default.
ignoredDirsForRenv <- function(ignoredDirs) {
  if (length(ignoredDirs) > 0) {
    # Make sure all the directories end with a slash.
    ignoredDirs <- ifelse(
        substr(ignoredDirs, nchar(ignoredDirs), nchar(ignoredDirs)) != "/",
        paste0(ignoredDirs, "/"),
        ignoredDirs
    )
    # Make sure all the directories begin with a slash.
    ignoredDirs <- ifelse(
        substr(ignoredDirs, 1, 1) != "/",
        paste0("/", ignoredDirs),
        ignoredDirs
    )
    ignoredDirs
  }
}
```

That code would then be called like:

```r
do_some_thing <- function() {
    old_renv_ignore <- options("renv.settings.ignore.matching" = ignoredDirsForRenv(packrat::opts$ignored.directories())
    on.exit(do.call(options, old_renv_ignore), add = TRUE)
    deps <- renv::dependencies(".")
    # ...
}
```

The `renv.settings.ignore.matching` setting name is an example of what renv could use; it does not need to use this name.

title: Packages with installation controlled by env vars are hard to lock down e.g. {arrow}
description:
Just starting a conversation here. I discovered an interesting failure mode with {arrow}.

If you're installing from source, the build looks for env vars to determine what features to build: https://arrow.apache.org/docs/r/articles/install.html

If this installation is done by `{renv}` the built package is cached.

When it comes time to restore the package into `{renv}` library, the cached version is used, without consideration of environment variables in the session. This can lead to a situation where some project developers use the same lockfile to build a library and get different sets of capabilities enabled for their project library arrow versions, depending on what was baked into the cached version.

The only solution if you've accidentally cached a minimal version of {arrow} is to purge it from the cache and install it again.

Solutions:
* `{arrow}`/other packages that do this stop doing this kind of weird thing, or install full builds by default. I plan to raise a corresponding discussion to this on `{arrow}` JIRA.
* `{arrow}`/other packages that do this somehow declare what environment variables are used in build and these can be incorporated into the cache hash.
  - not suggesting `{renv}` record the env vars, merely recognise the project build environment is different and the cached version cannot be used.

title: Best Practise: Renv with R Package & Plumber
description:
//Disclaimer: I'm new to R with a background in C# & Javascript

I'm working on a sample to expose an R Package as an API with renv supporting the dependency management and reproducibility. The API itself is exposed in a docker container.

Below is my folder structure:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3485935/140648072-7914e8bd-2c30-47ac-a17e-10939b89971d.png)

The Plumber script within plumber.R is simple. It just attempts to call into the HelloWorld package.

`
helloworld::sayhello()
`

Locally i can run things like devtools::load_all() or remotes::install_local(dependencies = FALSE) to bring helloworld into scope. This is fine but it does create a bit of an interesting setup on my docker container. 


```
RUN R -e "install.packages('remotes', repos = c(CRAN = 'https://cloud.r-project.org'))"
RUN R -e "remotes::install_github('rstudio/renv')"

COPY . .

RUN  find . -type f -print0 | xargs -0 dos2unix

RUN R -e "renv::install('remotes')"
RUN R -e "renv::restore()"
RUN R -e "remotes::install_local(dependencies = FALSE)"
```


The install of remotes on the first line to pull in renv is out of scope following renv::restore() moving the package paths.

This is pointing towards me mis-understanding something fundamental here. What's the correct way to proceed here? Ideally i could pull the local package into the context via renv configuration alone or perhaps there's a different method?

title: `renv::dependencies` doesn't pick up packages specified as `base_format` in `rmarkdown` header
description:
If I open a new RStudio project and create an `rmarkdown` file with the following content, `renv::dependencies` will list my dependencies as `rmarkdown`, `renv`, and `rticles`.

```
---
title: "renv::dependencies detects packages in output format"
author: Zander

output: rticles::plos_article

---

Text.
```

If I replace that with the following content to [enable cross-referencing](https://bookdown.org/yihui/bookdown/a-single-document.html) from the `bookdown` package, `renv::dependencies` now lists `rmarkdown`, `renv`, and `bookdown`, but fails to list `rticles`. 

```
---
title: "but renv::dependencies doesn't detect packages in nested base_format"
author: Zander

output:
  bookdown::pdf_book:
    base_format: rticles::plos_article

---

Text.
```

I am for now working around this by placing a 1-line R file in my project that calls `library(rticles)`, so that `renv` doesn't try to remove `rticles` from my lock-file every time I call `renv::snapshot`.

title: Should version numbers be used in the remoteSHA field?
description:
I noticed that with recent `{renv}` dev versions the `remoteSHA` field gets set to a version number for CRAN packages.

This breaks some logic I have in `capsule` to catch a situation where packages have the same version numbers but different SHAs.

That is I assumed the presence of a SHA in the lockfile, and no sha in the local library indicates a situation where the packages have the same version with different SHAs (common with dev packages) and I throw a warning.

I can fix this, but I would question the use of a field for SHAs for version numbers. These are different concepts, and the version number is already a separate field.

title: Issue with renv::restore for local / custom packages in 0.14.0 but not 0.12.0-3
description:
I have been experiencing difficulties in using renv::restore with a local package file in version 0.14.0, the same approach works fine in a previous version 0.12.0-3. 

I can't see anything in the change log which suggests this is expected behavior due a deliberate/breaking change but maybe I've missed something.

The use case is using a renv.lock file to replicate a set of packages used on a local install in the creation of a docker image.

The problem is that when I run renv::restore renv tries to find the local package on CRAN and fails. With an older renv version, this works fine.

I can't share the actual package but an example renv.lock file would be something like:

```
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "4.1.1",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cran.rstudio.com"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "customPackage": {
      "Package": "customPackage",
      "Version": "0.1.7",
      "Source": "/path/to/package/customPackage_0.1.7.tar.gz"
    }
  }
}
```

The error will be something like:

```
Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/Archive/customPackage/customPackage_0.1.7.tar.gz' ...
Error: failed to retrieve package 'customPackage'
```

It looks like at the start of the renv::restore process it knows this isn't a CRAN package -

```
The following package(s) will be updated:
/path/to/package/customPackage_0.1.7.tar.gz ==
customPackage         [* -> 0.1.7]
```

This is being run within an Ubuntu 20.04 docker image.

title: Package not restored from S3 based repository
Ability to copy user's `.Rprofile` contents to project `.Rprofile` on activation/initialization
description:
I'm currently testing out VSCode-R for a bit of fun and am running into some problems that I believe are related to `{renv}`'s structure, namely due to the use of a project `.Rprofile`. As mentioned in #692 , it's possible to set up `renv.config.user.profile` through setting `RENV_CONFIG_USER_PROFILE = TRUE` in `.Renviron`, but I think it'd be a useful feature to be able to copy the contents of the user's `.Rprofile` to the project's, maybe through an argument like `renv::init/activate(import_rprof = TRUE)`? 

I think this would help in situations that the default `renv.config.user.profile` is trying to avoid, particularly where you may have multiple ongoing projects that aren't consistent in their `.Rprofile` requirements and you don't want to have to keep resetting `renv.config.user.profile` as you switch between projects. It might also aid reproducibility if people do have packages listed in their User's `.Rprofile`, as they wouldn't be tracked otherwise.

Not sure if this would be a simple addition, so feel free to ignore if not feasible. Thanks for the work.

description:
When `renv::install()` downloads a package, where is the tarball downloaded and extracted?
Are there environment variables or configuration settings that control this download destination?

Context: I am trying to use `renv` with a Singularity container. I say 'with' rather than 'in' because the container filesystem is read-only, so that only directories from the host filesystem that have been specifically bound to the container are writable. title: `renv::snapshot()` removes the `"Name"` of an existing Python venv
description:
When inheriting an existing `venv` with `renv::use_python(name = "./myvenv")`

The `renv.lock` file is populated correctly at `Python.Name`; e.g. below:

```
  "Python": {
    "Version": "3.8.10",
    "Type": "virtualenv",
    "Name": "./myvenv"
  },
```

But after running `renv::snapshot()`, the name is changed to null, e.g. below

```
  "Python": {
    "Version": "3.8.10",
    "Type": "virtualenv",
    "Name": null
  },
```

And this forces `renv` to create a new blank `venv` within the `renv` directory when the project is opened again. If I manually put it back to `"./myvenv"` then it works fine, but this requires a manual change after each `renv::snapshot()`.

description:

It seems that any package that was installed on machine A that was installed from source locally is being considered as if it was from CRAN. For example the latest {shinycssloaders} on CRAN is version 1.0.0 but locally I'm working on a new version so on my machine I had version 1.0.0.9000, and this is what the renv.lock file had:

title: Docker - Broken `renv` cache when starting Docker image
description:
Hi,

I use `renv` for local development and it works fine!

I successfully built a Docker image using a Dockerfile and explicitly installing `renv`
```
ENV CRAN_URI=https://cloud.r-project.org
RUN R --vanilla -e "install.packages('renv', repos = c(CRAN = '$CRAN_URI'))" && \
    R -e "renv::restore()"
```
**Failure 1**

When I try to execute the application within the container using exactly the same script as in my local environment 
```
Rscript main.R
```
the bootstrapping of `renv` starts again (why?) and I get
```
ERROR: unable to create ‘/.../renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renv’
```

**Failure 2**

When I try to execute the application within the container using a different script that the script used to run the application in local (which is quite inconvenient) 
```
Rscript --vanilla -e "renv::activate(); renv::restore()"
Rscript main.R
```
I get
```
Warning message: The project library's symlinks to the cache are all broken.
Cache root: '/root/.cache/R/renv/cache/v5/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu'.
Consider reinstalling these packages.
```
Why?

Then
```
The following package(s) are missing entries in the cache:

        backports, R.cache, R.methodsS3, R.oo, R.utils, rematch2,
        rprojroot, styler

These packages will need to be reinstalled.
```

And finally
```
Error: Object 'label' not found amongst []
Execution halted
```

**Questions**

- Why the Failure 1 and the Failure 2 happen after successful installation of R packages by `renv` during the Docker image creation?
- I read through the [Using renv with Docker](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/docker.html), but deferring `renv::restore()` to container run time or mounting external `renv` cache is not an option for me as I need a self-contained Docker image without any startup dependencies and associated delays
- Is it possible to produce a self-contained Docker image using `renv` that has all the R packages installed during the Docker image creation?

Thank you

title: Attempting to rebuild a yet-to-be-installed package gives an uninformative error
description:
Context: I've just upgraded R from V3 to V4 and am restoring my packages for my project. Things error and require a rebuild:
```
* installing *source* package ‘scales’ ...
** package ‘scales’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** using staged installation
** R
** byte-compile and prepare package for lazy loading
Error: package ‘munsell’ was installed before R 4.0.0: please re-install it
Execution halted
ERROR: lazy loading failed for package ‘scales’
* removing ‘/tmp/RtmpcYZ26h/renv-staging-710fa0f147a/scales’
```

When I try to `renv::rebuild()` a package that has yet to be installed in the "new" `renv` project library, I get the following cryptic error: 
```
renv::rebuild('munsell')

#> Error in vapply(x, `[[`, ..., FUN.VALUE = character(1)) : 
#> values must be length 1,
#> but FUN(X[[1]]) result is length 0
```

To get rid of this error, the appropriate set of steps is:
```
renv::install('munsell') # Copies the V3 version into the cache
renv::rebuild('munsell') # Reinstalls the package from scratch so it's compatible with V4
```

At minimum, it feels like the appropriate behavior on a `rebuild` call should be a more informative error, but the ideal solution is probably to simply build the package from scratch on any `rebuild` call, regardless of whether it exists in the project library already or not.

Hope that's helpful feedback! :)

title: {renv} tries to write to global package cache although it is disabled
description:
{renv} is used in pre-commit.com, `language: r` and recently, support for pre-commit.ci was [added](https://github.com/pre-commit-ci/runner-image/pull/80). However, there are strange errors occurring sometimes when multiple processes try to activate a renv (governed by `require_serial:` in the hook specs file `.pre-commit-config.yaml`). The error is:

```
failed to create directory at path '/tmp/renv'
Traceback (most recent calls last):
19: suppressWarnings({
        old <- setwd("/pc/clone/xQ5UXFOMRsuyt4tMlwQDwQ/renv-default")
        source("renv/activate.R")
        setwd(old)
        renv::load("/pc/clone/xQ5UXFOMRsuyt4tMlwQDwQ/renv-default")
    })
18: withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w) if (inherits(w, 
        classes)) tryInvokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
17: source("renv/activate.R")
16: withVisible(eval(ei, envir))
15: eval(ei, envir)
14: eval(ei, envir)
13: local(...)
12: eval.parent(substitute(eval(quote(expr), envir)))
11: eval(expr, p)
10: eval(expr, p)
 9: eval(quote(...), new.env())
 8: eval(quote(...), new.env())
 7: renv_bootstrap_load(project, libpath, version)
 6: renv::load(project)
 5: renv_load_project(project)
 4: ensure_parent_directory(projects)
 3: ensure_directory(unique(dirname(path)))
 2: stopf("failed to create directory at path '%s'", rownames(info))
 1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
Execution halted
```
E.g. in this [log](https://results.pre-commit.ci/run/github/85580810/1633372635.nQEJrJf1SgiamgC21Ssl_A). One should note that {renv} does not have the permission to write to this directory anyways in the container where the above log comes from. But the error does not occur unless parallel processing is enabled.

Not sure what is going on. We configured {renv} to not even use the global cache as it is deactivated using various env variables in https://github.com/pre-commit-ci/runner-image/blob/master/Dockerfile#L191-L195, i.e.:
```
RENV_CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLED=false 
RENV_CONFIG_CACHE_SYMLINKS=false 
RENV_PATHS_ROOT=/tmp/renv
``` 
`/tmp/renv` does not exist in the container. Creating it beforehand leads to the same error. I am not sure it would resolve the problem but `renv_load_project`, I think we should not try to create the parent directory of `projects` and write files if the global cache is disabled,  i.e.   `if (project %in% projlist)` should be extended to return `TRUE` if `RENV_CONFIG_CACHE_ENABLED` (and the corresponding option/config/R option) is set to `False`, 0, etc.

```r
renv_load_project <- function(project) {

  # record the active project in this session
  project <- renv_path_normalize(project, winslash = "/")
  Sys.setenv(RENV_PROJECT = project)

  # read project list
  projects <- renv_paths_root("projects")
  projlist <- character()
  if (file.exists(projects))
    projlist <- readLines(projects, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")

  # if the project is already recorded, nothing to do
  if (project %in% projlist) 
    return(TRUE)

  # otherwise, update the project list
  renv_scope_locale("LC_COLLATE", "C")
  projlist <- sort(c(projlist, project))
  ensure_parent_directory(projects)
  catchall(writeLines(enc2utf8(projlist), projects, useBytes = TRUE))

  TRUE

}
```

title: [FR] Configuration option to change renv.lock name
description:
Hi,

This is a simple feature request to have an option in renv to change the `renv.lock` file name.

Indeed, the `.lock` file extension is associated with some ransomware and is thus hard blacklisted by some cloud management systems, such as the one I'm using, Nextcloud: https://github.com/nextcloud/ransomware_protection/issues/60#issuecomment-777661232. This unfortunately makes `renv` unusable in my workplace.

In my case, having the sysadmins change the system security parameters is not doable.

If the name and extension of this file were changeable, this would solve the problem.

title: Managing package install reproducibility between Linux/Windows/other OSes
description:
Hi folks, I am wondering if `renv` has some feature to validate whether the packages listed in a lockfile can be downloaded for a variety of OSes (my main targets are Linux and Windows), or (even better), refuse to install packages that cannot be installed across operating systems.

As a concrete example, suppose I `renv::install("survival@3.2-13")` on a Linux box. I snapshot the environment and receive the following lockfile:

```
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "3.6.0",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cloud.r-project.org"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "Matrix": {
      "Package": "Matrix",
      "Version": "1.2-17",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "39ea11fb3ad0d759f9f1c053fd442957"
    },
    "lattice": {
      "Package": "lattice",
      "Version": "0.20-38",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "848f8c593fd1050371042d18d152e3d7"
    },
    "renv": {
      "Package": "renv",
      "Version": "0.14.0",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "30e5eba91b67f7f4d75d31de14bbfbdc"
    },
    "survival": {
      "Package": "survival",
      "Version": "3.2-13",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "6f0a0fadc63bc6570fe172770f15bbc4"
    }
  }
}
```

(Only the last entry is relevant but adding it all for reproducibility and completeness).

If I now try to initialize this environment on a Windows box, I fail out with the following errors:

```
Error installing package 'survival':
====================================

* installing to library 'C:/Users/hafiz/Desktop/renv-versioning-issue/renv/library/R-3.6/x86_64-w64-mingw32/.renv/1'
* installing *source* package 'survival' ...
** package 'survival' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** using staged installation
** libs
Warning in system(paste(cmd, "shlib-clean")) : 'make' not found
Warning in system(cmd) : 'make' not found
ERROR: compilation failed for package 'survival'
```

And rightfully so, because `make` is not on my windows machine. Maybe it's reasonable to expect users of this package to install it, but for example in my case, my Windows workstation is locked down and I cannot install common packages on the unix side arbitrarily. In this kind of case I would prefer to download the package as a binary, whenever I can.

Is there any way to specify or demand this kind of preference from `renv`? My impression is that the answer would be "no" and that there may not be a good way to implement such a preference/demand, at least in the current state of affairs. If this is the case, have others dealt with this issue, and if so, how do you manage it?

Somewhat related: #746

title: A temporary path on .libPaths() is left after renv fails to install a package
description:
Many thanks for providing this package. It has make it easier to be sure which versions I use between machines. 

When a package installation fails renv leaves a temporary directory on `.libPaths()`, which later causes confusion when installing, as the packages go to the temporary directory instead of the project library.

This happened when installing some package dependencies that depend on Bioconductor when those packages are not present. I don't remember the exact packages as I found that I could use `renv::use("package", library = .libPaths()[2])` as a workaround.

Maybe an on.exit call, `withr::with_libpaths` or similar strategies could be used to prevent this?

title: `renv` CI cache bust best practices
description:
Hey @kevinushey

We've been running into an issue in our CI, where we have an internal package that lives in a monorepo (which is about 300mb), that we update very often. This ends up leading to re-installs and re-caches of the new versions of the package often (multiple times a day). The issue is that our CI cache -- we use Circle, but AFAICT it'd be the same on GHA or anything else -- is growing by the size of the entire monorepo on every new install. It seems to me that this is happening because `renv` is downloading a tarball of the entire repo, unpacking it, installing the package, and then caching the entire repo and package instead of just caching the package and getting rid of the cruft. 

Is this mental model right? And if so, what's the best practice advice for not blowing up the size of our CI cache? RIght now it's almost 10gb because of installs over the past couple weeks, and growing fast. I can think of a bunch of ways to manually cache bust, but it'd be nice if there were a way to just clean up after myself on the install instead.

Let me know, and thanks!

title: Renv shouldn't connect to repositories on startup
description:
#### Problem
It seems that on startup renv connects to all the repositories listed in the lockfile to check their status / available packages. This makes some sense when working interactively in a single R session, but becomes troublesome when you frequently launch new R sessions. The problem is especially serious, if you have multiple repositories listed in the lockfile and they happen to be unavailable - renv will incur a long delay with multiple retries for each repository.

This problem arose in a real use case. We use the [box](https://klmr.me/box/) package to modularize a large Shiny app. Due to module caching in box, we need to run the app in a new R session each time we want to reload it. The app uses private packages available from a set of RSPM repositories, which can only be accessed via VPN. Sometimes, due to network issues or a configuration problem, the repositories cannot be accessed.

#### Proposed solution
I think renv should only connect to the repositories when it is needed, i.e. when instructed to install/update packages. This is how popular tools for creating isolated environments work in other languages, e.g. yarn in Node.js and venv in Python.

#### Notes
The problem could be alleviated by setting `renv.config.connect.timeout` to a low value, but a bug prevents it from working: [this comment](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/083dc0186c5dda77df1c78cc5c67a18c4af61b9a/R/rspm.R#L103) talks about using a shorter delay, but the code actually uses a fixed value which can be bigger than the setting provided by the user.

```r
options(repos = NULL)
renv::init()
options(repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
renv::snapshot()
```

Will result in the following error:
```
Error in mapply(renv_lockfile_diff_impl, old, new, MoreArgs = list(compare = compare),  : 
  zero-length inputs cannot be mixed with those of non-zero length
```

#### Expected behavior
Renv should either save the unnamed repository (as it does if we don't first set `repos = NULL`) or refuse to use unnamed repository with a meaningful message.

There are a growing number of packages that have dependencies listed in suggests that we utilize, and it was great to have these suggested dependencies automatically added to our lock files. 

But there were enough edge cases where we were getting unwanted snapshots. For example, we use packages from CRAN, our own internal RSPM, public GitHub, an internal Enterprise GitHub, and it happens every so often there is a package that cannot be restored. When working around this issue, we were often getting an auto snaps, locking in the more recent version of packages when we are trying to restore the previous versions.

To this end, what are you thoughts on implementing a `renv.config.ask.snapshot` option that will ask us each time the library changes if we'd like to snapshot?

Thank you!
Daniel

title: `install.packages()` shim doesn't fallback to `utils::install.packages()` correctly
description:
The idea of the renv `install.packages()` shim is to handoff to `install()` if just a single argument is passed (`pkgs`), otherwise it falls back to `utils::install.packages()`.

But it doesn't seem like the fallback is passing through optional arguments correctly. For example, this installs the INLA package (which isn't on CRAN but is hosted elsewhere) when you aren't in an renv enabled project.

```r
install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)
```

However, if you run this from an renv enabled project, then you'll get an error that it can't find INLA:

```r
> install.packages("INLA",repos=c(getOption("repos"),INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)
Installing package into ‘/Users/davis/Desktop/r/playground/temp/test-renv/renv/library/R-4.1/x86_64-apple-darwin17.0’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Warning message:
package ‘INLA’ is not available for this version of R

A version of this package for your version of R might be available elsewhere,
see the ideas at
https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Installing-packages 
```

None of the optional arguments are getting passed through to `utils::install.packages()`, so it doesn't know about the extra repo.

The shim here looks like it passes dots through correctly:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/e8ccdda601ec208e387d769076aaa16ad4f86bb6/R/shims.R#L4-L11

But the formals of that shim are actually changed to align with `install.packages()` at package load time by `renv_shim()`
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/e8ccdda601ec208e387d769076aaa16ad4f86bb6/R/shims.R#L38-L41
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/e8ccdda601ec208e387d769076aaa16ad4f86bb6/R/shims.R#L51

title: rsconnect fails to deploy app when necessary package is installed from github w/ renv in root
description:
I've been trying to debug a problem deploying a shiny app to shinyapps.io that involves a package installed from github. I believe I've narrowed the issue down to something having to do with renv (see here: https://github.com/r-lib/pillar/issues/252#issuecomment-877728907) and @klrmlr has requested that I raise it here.

# Description
Here's the gist: I have two versions of a package on github. They are identical except one has renv in the package root, and in the other I have removed renv. The package is an extremely simple MWE: it has one exported function and one dependency (dplyr). See here: https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem (the master branch has renv in the root).

When I deploy a [simple Rmd file](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/Rmd/solve.Rmd) to shinyapps.io that depends on the version of the package with renv in the project root, it fails ([log](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/rsconnect_failure.txt)). When I deploy the same Rmd file that depends on a version of the package that does NOT have renv defined in the project root ([branch](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/tree/test3)) the deploy succeeds ([log](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/rsconnect_success.txt)).

Session info is here: [session info](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/session_info_renv.txt)

# Steps to reproduce:
1. Download the `renv_test` branch of the repository (https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/tree/renv_test)
2. Open the project, and then `demo_code/R/demo_code.R`
3. Change the rsconnect username to whatever your username is
4. Run the code in `demo_code/R/demo_code.R`

# What should happen:
The first deployment (with richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem@master installed) should lead to this [failure](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/rsconnect_failure.txt); the second deployment (with richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem@test3 installed) should lead to [success](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/blob/renv_test/demo_code/rsconnect_success.txt).

You can verify that richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem@test3 only differs from richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem@master with respect to renv by looking at the [two additional commits](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/commits/test3).

To confirm that this is not a problem with the order in which I am installing the two identical packages, you can run the code in `demo_code/R/demo_code_reverse_order.R` (which fails in the same way).

I do not understand why deploying an Rmd based on [the version of the package](https://github.com/richarddmorey/shinyapps_problem/tree/master) that has renv in the root fails; as far as I can tell, once they're installed they look similar on disk. I thought it might have to do with the renv `.Rprofile` (see this [comment](https://github.com/r-lib/pillar/issues/252#issuecomment-820021550) by @krlmlr) but I'm kind of baffled to be honest.

title: renv::dependencies() skips R utility script files without file extension
renv::install(, type = "both") not supported => different behavior between utils::install.package and renv::install
description:
I work on Windows and R without Rtools, because usually do not want to go through the hassle of compilation. Therefore when installing packages, I would like to install the highest version possible without compilation needed. This behavior is implemented by utils::install.package but not by renv::install. This seems to boil down to the support for argument type = "both".

**Could renv implements support for type = "both"?**
Such that in default situation the behavior is same between utils::install.package and renv::install?

**utils::install.package**
Calling utils::install.package will default in utils::install.package(, type = "both"), because getOption("pkgType") defaults in "both". In this case, the function first analyzes which binary and source versions are available **_and_** whether compilation is needed. Based on this analysis, the highest possible version is installed. So for table below, utils::install.package acts as follows:

- Rcpp: Source version 1.0.7 is highest but **_not_** installed because compilation is needed. Therefore binary version 1.0.6 is installed.
- bslib: Source version 0.2.5.1 is highest and installed, because no compilation needed

|       | binary | source  | needs_compilation |
|-------|--------|---------|-------------------|
| Rcpp  | 1.0.6  | 1.0.7   | TRUE              |
| bslib | 0.2.4  | 0.2.5.1 | FALSE             |

**renv::install**
renv::install seems not to support for type = "both" which causes an error and different behavior compared to utils::install.package, i.e. renv::install acts as follows:
- Rcpp: Source version 1.0.7 is highest and installed. Installation fails, because compilation is needed.
- bslib: Source version 0.2.5.1 highest and installed. Installation succeeds, because no compilation needed

title: Arbitrary changes of the "Repository" field in renv.lock
description:
Finally I got around reprexing a weird problem where the "Repository" field in `renv.lock` keeps alternating between `"RSPM"` and `"CRAN"` for no obvious reason. This adds a lot of Git noise if left unchecked.

This field is set in `renv.lock` depending on the installation source. On macOS, it is reset to `"CRAN"` during `restore()`. I'll double-check what happens on Ubuntu.

``` r
packageVersion("renv")
#> [1] '0.13.2.85'

# Two repositories: test1 and test2
# test1 has a "normal" CRAN, test2 is linked to an RSPM snapshot
# During setup, we simulate a clean environment with renv::purge()
# The callr::r() call conveniently returns the result of renv::snapshot(),
#   which is the lock file as an R list. We watch the Repository component
#   for the rlang package.

renv::purge("rlang")
#> The following packages will be purged from the cache:
#> 
#>  rlang 0.4.11 [Hash: 515f341d3affe0de9e4a7f762efb0456]
#> 
#> * Removed 1 package from the cache.
dir.create("test1")
setwd("test1")

callr::r(function() {
  options(repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  renv::init()
  renv::snapshot()
  renv::install("rlang")
  writeLines("library(rlang)", "packages.R")
  renv::snapshot()
})$Packages$rlang$Repository
#> [1] "CRAN"

setwd("..")

renv::purge("rlang")
#> The following packages will be purged from the cache:
#> 
#>  rlang 0.4.11 [Hash: 515f341d3affe0de9e4a7f762efb0456]
#> 
#> * Removed 1 package from the cache.
dir.create("test2")
setwd("test2")

callr::r(function() {
  options(repos = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/2021-06-21")
  renv::init()
  renv::snapshot()
  renv::install("rlang")
  writeLines("library(rlang)", "packages.R")
  renv::snapshot()
})$Packages$rlang$Repository
#> [1] "RSPM"

setwd("..")

# The erratic behavior occurs when attempting a restore() + snapshot().
# In both repositories, the package's "Repository" entry is set to CRAN,
#   at least on macOS. This generates unnecessary VCS noise and has been
#   a source of moderate pain in the past months.

setwd("test1")
unlink("renv/library", recursive = TRUE)
callr::r(function() {
  renv::restore()
  renv::snapshot()
})$Packages$rlang$Repository
#> [1] "CRAN"

setwd("..")

setwd("test2")
unlink("renv/library", recursive = TRUE)
callr::r(function() {
  renv::restore()
  renv::snapshot()
})$Packages$rlang$Repository
#> [1] "CRAN"

setwd("..")
```

title: Document / Check for minimum required system `git` version
description:
renv requires some `git` features that are only available/only work beyond a certain release.

On ubuntu 16.04, the default `git` install is `2.7.4` .
On `git <= 2.7.4`, `renv` will fail on `git` operations with an error I can't reproduce right now (I'll try this out on a new VM soon)

On `git >= 2.21`, renv does not fail in `git` operations.

The actual minimum version is within `min > 2.7.4 && min <= 2.21`, though I don't know precisely what.

I *think* that Ubuntu 18.04's default `git --version` of `2.17.1` doesn't have problems.


the `2.7` release of `git` is ~6 years old (`2.7.4` was released march 2016), and considering `git` is a portable & widely available dependency, I don't think the minimum requirement is too onerous, but debugging the failure is tricky. 

(Even in HPC environments, if you're unable to obtain a modern `git` from modules, or build one yourself, you probably have bigger problems on your hands)

This minimum requirement should be ascertained, documented, & added to `renv_git_preflight()` s.t it's clear _why_ renv git operations are failing, & users are prompted to upgrade. 

(we could also investigate accomodating backwards compatibility, but I don't know that its worth it since no-one else seems to be raising this issue)

title: Warn/message if `snapshot()` called in an uninitialised project
description:
I recently forgot to `init()` before `snapshot()`ing and happily had my remote collaborators run `renv::restore()`, which then was surprisingly difficult to diagnose remotely - even though the issue should have been obvious to me due to the missing renv directory in the git repo. The reason, I think, is that the renv directory & renv-generated .Rprofile is mostly "commit once, forget about it", so it's hard to spot that it's missing. 

I was a bit surprise that renv let me do that without complaining, given how (usefully) explicit/talkative it is generally.

Clearly this is a silly user error, but I wonder if it might make sense to check in `snapshot()` whether the current project has in fact been initialised for renv to save others the same trouble? (Unless there is a rationale for `snapshot()` outside renv-managed projects, but then a message might still be useful.)

title: Support instructing snapshot which packages to include in the lockfile without dependency scanning
description:
My `renv` wrapper `capsule` calls

```
renv::snapshot(
      packages = detect_dependencies(dep_source_paths)
    )
```

Where `capsule::detect_dependencies` is a dependency detection function that recognises dependencies declared in ways that `renv` does not. For example it recognises the [`using::pkg()`](https://github.com/anthonynorth/using) syntax, since that package is maintained by a member of my team, but is probably a never-CRAN package.

At the moment `renv` dutifully respects the `packages` argument and compiles a lockfile containing all packages in the vector and their dependencies etc.

The issue is that `renv` still does it's own project-wide dependency scan which can be quite slow. We want to incorporate automated lockfile output as part of our build pipelines, but in our moderately sized projects adding the time cost of a full `renv` scan to the pipeline is a barrier to doing that.

The idea of snapshot mode `explicit` is what we want, but we need to be able to say 'explicitly what's in this vector I am handing you', not explicitly what's in a DESCRIPTION file in the project root. 

We don't use DESCRIPTION files anyway, for our purposes they are inferior to an .R file, which can contain whatever dependency declaration syntax we like, as well as the `conflicted` conflict resolution statements all in one place.

The interface for this behaviour could be something like 

```
renv::snapshot(
  packages = detect_dependencies(dep_source_paths),
  type = "explicit_vector"
)
```

or similar.

title: Auto-detection of available R versions?
description:
**Disclaimer**: Hi Kevin! I am aware this is a huge one but nevertheless I believe it could be a substantial user experience improvement 🙂 

**Scenario**

{renv} informs users if the current R version used differs from the one referenced in `renv.lock`. The process of installing multiple R versions differs on every OS, so do default installation paths.

**Idea**

Nevertheless, I was wondering if {renv} could potentially scan common R interpreter installation paths for major OS such as Windows, macOS and, let's say Ubuntu, for Linux.
If it finds a matching R interpreter, this one is automatically selected and somehow configured on a project basis.

**Thoughts**

While of course this does not work during the initial startup of a "wrong" R interpreter, {renv} could potentially create some softlinks / create some shims to ensure a specific R version is used during following R startups.

I cannot provide a full-fledged idea how this might work in practice but RStudio Workbench is also somehow able to encapsulate certain sessions with a specific R version which is known upfront.

I think such a behaviour is supported by project-env packages in other languages as well (no examples/proofs at hand though).

I am aware that dynamic version handling is feature of RStudio Workbench but I am also often finding myself in a terminal session with {renv} where such an auto-detection of available interpreter would be awesome to have.

title: Enable repository preference to prioritize versions available in first repository on install
description:
By default, it seems that renv gets the latest version of a package `pkg` available from any of the repositories listed in renv.lock. In the case of RSPM, we have set up  development and production sources for RSPM, both of which have our internal packages and are listed in the renv.lock during development.

Since the dev version is always larger than the production version, that version is what is installed by `renv::install("pkg")`. This can easily be worked around by using `renv::install("pkg@0.1.1")`, for example, but relies on the user understanding something about how the RSPM is set up, and how to interpret version numbers. 

Is there some setting which can be added to renv to *not* prefer the latest version, and rather prefer what is in the first repository listed?I am also open to hearing how changes in our workflow can alleviate this.

title: should renv::restore() auto-initialize a project?
description:
The following is somewhat common:

1. A user shares a project on GitHub, which itself contains an `renv.lock` lockfile, but not the `renv` auto-loader.
2. Users who download that project will want to restore the project library, and will do so with `renv::restore()`.
3. Because the project hasn't explicitly been initialized on that user's machine, `renv::restore()` will target the user library rather than the project library.

An alternative is to use `renv::init()` rather than `renv::restore()`, but to reduce user confusion we should make sure that the same actions do the right thing regardless of whether the `renv` auto-loader exists.

title: `renv` installation / remotes syntax conflict with remotes/devtools for deeper nested packages
description:
I have come across an issue (similar to #497) where I am unable to install a package using `remotes` / `devtools` syntax for GitHub based packages nested more deeply than at the top level / 1 folder down in a repository.

This is an issue for me since we use a monorepo at work, and I am sometimes not able to keep a package high up enough in the repo structure to keep `renv` happy.

I have created a [repo and instructions](https://github.com/gtm19/subsub.renv) which demonstrates that _either_ `remotes`/`devtools` OR `renv` is happy, but in short, installation like follows results in an error using `renv`, despite `remotes::install_*` being happy:

```r
desc::desc_set_remotes("github::gtm19/skeleton/subdir/subsubdir")
renv::install()
# Error: failed to resolve remote 'github::gtm19/skeleton/subdir/subsubdir' -- failed to retrieve 'https://api.github.com/repos/gtm19/skeleton/subdir' [error code 22]
# In addition: Warning message:
# curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
```

Whereas making `renv` happy then makes `remotes` / `devtools` unhappy:

```r
desc::desc_set_remotes("github::gtm19/skeleton:subdir/subsubdir")
devtools::build()
devtools::install_local("../subsub.renv_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz")

# Error: Failed to install 'subsub.renv' from local:
#  HTTP error 404.
#  Not Found

#  Did you spell the repo owner (`gtm19`) and repo name (`skeleton:subdir`) correctly?
#  - If spelling is correct, check that you have the required permissions to access the repo.
# Execution halted
```

I believe I have a fix for this which passes all existing `renv` tests. I will PR shortly.

title: Update to R 4.1 triggers many "package x was installed before R 4.0.0: please re-install it"
description:
Hi

I recently upgraded to R 4.1, which triggered issues in multiple renv projects. I get the warning message *R version change [4.0.5 -> 4.1.0]*, and many packages are now missing. 

I tried `rend::restore()`, but this quickly fails, complaining that some packages have been built with R <4. For example, I got: 

> Error: package or namespace load failed for ‘RcppZiggurat’:
>  package ‘RcppZiggurat’ was installed before R 4.0.0: please re-install it

I am able to solve the issue by running ` renv::install("RcppZiggurat",rebuild=TRUE)`, but I have to do again with the next packages, and to do ten times so far. 

Is there a more elegant way to address this? I tried using `renv::update(rebuild=TRUE)`, but it just says *All packages appear to be up-to-date.* I notice that I have `RcppZiggurat` in the newest cache (`ls ~/.local/share/renv/cache/v5/R-4.1/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/RcppZiggurat/0.1.6/`), but I guess this is just a link to the version installed on my system, that is built for R < 4? 

So what can I do? Should I hence just update/rebuild all my packages on the standard non-renv folder?

Thanks!
PS: running on Ubuntu 18.04.

title: Consider chattier message on status / snapshot
description:
If you are using a renv mode that only snapshots identified dependencies and not the entire active library, it can be hard to understand why some packages are being excluded. 

While this behavior is often what you want, users have to be proactive in finding this very helpful FAQ: https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/faq.html#why-isn-t-my-package-being-snapshotted-into-the-lockfile-

It may help if renv::status and renv::snapshot were a little chattier when the snapshot type is not all. For example, a status message might say: 

8 packages are installed in the library but will not be snapshotted because don't appear to be used. See renv::dependencies to see what packages appear to be in use. Run renv::settings$snapshot.type("all") to tell renv to track all installed packages.

This is a long message and may get annoying overtime... a tradeoff to consider. 

FWIW I really like the renv::dependencies default, I sometimes forget about it though! This ticket was prompted by the parsnip package which has dependencies that are usually not identified by renv::dependencies.

title: Robust restore()
description:
I'm currently struggling with the `restore()` of a massive lock file in two different systems:

- Linux, no control (I can only run a Shiny app), air-gapped, network-local CRAN mirror
- Windows, no (desire to) compile from sources, slow connection to the CRAN mirror

Some packages don't install out of the box. When I call `restore()`:

- all packages are downloaded
- the installation process starts, they are installed one by one
- eventually, it fails
- when I strip the failing package from the lock file, it is still installed in the next step, because of some downstream package that depends on the failing package

This makes the installation attempts unnecessarily long. How can we make `restore()` more robust in such initialization cases?

- Print upfront, which packages are going to be restored due to dependency repair (so that these can be removed from the lock file too)
- Topological sort of the packages in the lock file (so that we can restore the first n lines of the lock file, then add the next n lines, etc.)
- Offer a way to download + install package by package
- Offer a way to restore the first `n` packages (topological sort?)
- Offer a "keep going" option that attempts to restore all packages despite failures, and reports failures in the end
- ...?

description:
Occasionally a project gets into a weird state where `renv::status()` is not properly seeing packages installed in the project library.

Generally `renv` has been working fine and has been hugely helpful for me.  So this is just an occasional occurrence, and I'm not sure how to reproduce it or how best to document it.  I'm posting here regardless in case someone has suggestions of things to try or can help illustrate a specific bug.

For example in the screenshot below, I have installed several packages in the project library with only two (`renv` and `DBI`) currently in the lock file.  Yet, `status()` is showing that everything is in sync.

![Screen Shot 2021-04-30 at 9 03 18 AM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/32336739/116699738-ef006800-a993-11eb-9c95-ae80c461fd9a.png)

Stepping through in a debugger, I can see that `status()` eventually calls `renv_lockfile_create()`.  Within that function the call to `renv_snapshot_r_packages()` shows everything, but after it is piped into `renv_snapshot_filter()` only the two packages currently in the lockfile remain.  
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ffe5790161fed81226577a31231299e2be2c36ba/R/lockfile.R#L161

Is there something about the `type = "implicit"` parameter value there that is causing this issue?

description:

It would be nice if the argument `dependencies` would be exposed (like in `install.packages()`) or via `renv::settings` or `renv::config`. For local packages, I otherwise have to use {remotes} for that.

Related: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/66

title: Licensing of renv-generated infra files
description: I contributed R as a language to https://pre-commit.com, and we are [improving it currently](https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit/pull/1841) so that infrastructure generated with `renv::init()` is distributed as part of pre-commit (which is MIT licenced like renv) in certain cases and used in tests. That raises the question of the license of these files. The same question arises in any project that uses {renv} and contains artefact files such as `renv/activate.R` and friends that is public (at least I think it does). To be on the safe side here, we decided to come here and ask if it's possible to include these files in the distribution of pre-commit and how they should be licensed. I notice that in {vctrs}, certain files [were *unlicensed*](https://github.com/r-lib/vctrs/pull/1314) to make it unambiguously clear that c/p is fine. Maybe that's an approach worth taking into consideration? Thanks.

title: `renv::install()` with explicit dependencies should prioritize remote ref
description:
This is a complicated issue to describe, so I've created a [companion repository](https://github.com/gadenbuie/renv-wrong-remote-ref).

In essence, we are using explicit snapshot types with a DESCRIPTION file. Some of the packages listed in the DESCRIPTION file require package versions hosted on GitHub. Because references such as `@main` or `@master` may move, we specifically reference remote package versions by commit SHA, such as:

```
Imports:
    htmltools,
    learnr,
    parsons,
    sortable
Remotes: 
    rstudio/htmltools@11cfbf3b331387922c0144203cf6e947c8bdaee9,
    rstudio/learnr@428d9af1506447f68890724bfc619ed1f2e7cfc0,
    rstudio/parsons@42d0bfb8f23a3c8048cc4c1fbca95a0ef1e0bca3,
    rstudio/sortable@cdde09d915ee0bc73353b079c7afbed8cb70ab4a
```

However, we're finding that `renv::install()` doesn't always prioritize the version listed in `Remotes` above all other versions. In the case of [this reprex](https://github.com/gadenbuie/renv-wrong-remote-ref), sortable is installed at a different commit.

```
# GitHub =============================
- htmltools     [* -> rstudio/htmltools@11cfbf3b331387922c0144203cf6e947c8bdaee9]
- learnr        [* -> rstudio/learnr@428d9af1506447f68890724bfc619ed1f2e7cfc0]
- parsons       [* -> rstudio/parsons@42d0bfb8f23a3c8048cc4c1fbca95a0ef1e0bca3]
- sortable      [* -> rstudio/sortable]
```

The companion includes a [number of things that I've tried](https://github.com/gadenbuie/renv-wrong-remote-ref/commits/main) to force installation of the package at the specific reference, but my attempts invariably arrive at a place where a different version of one of the remote packages is installed.

title: messages are suppressed unexpectedly for embedded applications
description:
I understand that the purpose of `renv_session_quiet` is to suppress renv messages when a user runs `R --quiet`. However, it does introduce some unexpected behavior for applications that embeds R.  For example, in [radian](https://github.com/randy3k/radian), we have
```
r$> commandArgs(trailingOnly = FALSE)
[1] "radian"               "--quiet"              "--no-restore-history"
[4] "--no-readline"        "--no-save"            "--no-restore-data"
```
And the `--queit` flag has forced `renv_session_quiet` and hence `renv_load_quiet` to return `TRUE`. 


FYI, reading for `R --help`
```
  -q, --quiet           Don't print startup message
```
It does seem that renv is being a bit aggressive to suppress the messages for `R --quiet`.

title: snapshot() option to **not** remove packages from lockfile
description:
It's fairly common for me to include a package in a project, then remove some code that uses it (perhaps while experimenting a bit) and install other packages in the meantime. When taking an `snapshot()` to capture those newer packages, renv wants to _remove_ the no-longer-referenced original package. I can't find an option to `snapshot()` while protecting against deletions from the lockfile. (`type = "all"` doesn't exactly cover it, either, as it'll often add much more to the lockfile than is actually needed.)

Perhaps an additional control to snapshot to selectively list the packages to edit (where edit is insert, delete, or update)? The existing `packages=my_pkgs` argument doesn't quite cut it, either, as that'll lead to a removal of any existing lockfile entry that's **not** in `my_pkgs`.

Perhaps there's already a workflow for this (adding or updating packages selectively) of which I'm just ignorant?

title: use_python() does not find same version in interactive or non interactive mode
description:
Currently, `use_python()` does not find a version of Python installed by Windows Store when running command in the console. 
The Python version mentioned here is this one: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/p/python-38/9mssztt1n39l

I recognized this is a special version of Python but it shows the difference in `use_python()` when interactive or not.

````r
> system("where python")
C:\Users\chris\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\python.exe
[1] 0
> renv::use_python()
Please select a version of Python to use with this project: 

: 

Selection: 
````
The function used is this one
```r
> renv:::renv_python_discover()
character(0)
```

This python is correctly in PATH because `C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\WindowsApps` is in PATH
````r
> Sys.which("python")
                                                            python 
"C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\MICROS~1\\WINDOW~1\\python.exe" 
````

I believe a special handling of this could be added in `renv_python_discover()` for Windows


Also setting this version in `renv.python.root` does not work as `bin/python` and not just `python` is looked for.

It seems this is specific to `renv_python_select()` used when `interactive()` because if not **reticulate** env vars are looked up (so I could use that) or path is checked for the binary using `Sys.which()` which would work here

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ffe5790161fed81226577a31231299e2be2c36ba/R/python.R#L2-L44

When called in non interactive session, the version is found
````
> callr::r(function() renv:::renv_python_resolve())
                                                            python3 
"C:\\Users\\chris\\AppData\\Local\\MICROS~1\\WINDOW~1\\python3.exe" 
>
> renv:::renv_python_resolve()
Please select a version of Python to use with this project: 

: 

Selection: 0
Error in normalizePath(path.expand(path), winslash, mustWork) : 
  path[1]="": La syntaxe du nom de fichier, de répertoire ou de volume est incorrecte
````

So this is working for a project. 
```r
callr::r(function() renv::use_python())
```

But usually, it does not help as opening a project with Python set in the lockfile won't work.

Happy to help further if you need tests or a PR.

title: Problem moving 12.x to 13.0 - Error in startsWith(contriburl, "file:") : non-character object(s)
description:
I'm trying to debug an issue in our CI system at present.

This CI system uses a container to build our R packages. Each R package project is wrapped in its own renv environment and this system has been working well.

The CI build script basically does a `devtools::build` and then afterwards does a `install.packages` to check that the package actually is built and installable.

```
message("Building ", packageToBuild, " into ", packagePath)
built_path <- devtools::build(packageToBuild, path = packagePath, vignettes = FALSE)

message("Built path was ", built_path)

message("Build complete - now let's install the package")
built_packages <- list.files(path = packagePath, pattern = "*.tar.gz", full.names = TRUE)
message("Found built packages: ", built_packages)
message("Installing...")
install.packages(built_packages, repos=NULL, type="source")
message("Installed... but did it really... let's check if it worked")
```

This code has been working well under 12.x.

However, after upgrading renv to 13.0 (or later - have tried 13.1 and 13.2), then we see an error of `Error in startsWith(contriburl, "file:") : non-character object(s)`

```
Built path was /__w/180/a/package/P.DetailReport_0.4.34.tar.gz
Build complete - now let's install the package
Found built packages: /__w/180/a/package/P.DetailReport_0.4.34.tar.gz
Installing...
Installing package into ‘/__w/180/s/P.DetailReport/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu’
(as ‘lib’ is unspecified)
Error in startsWith(contriburl, "file:") : non-character object(s)
Calls: install.packages ... delegate -> eval -> eval -> <Anonymous> -> startsWith
Execution halted
```

Looking around it feels like this might be caused in a base R `available.packages` call somewhere - see  `localcran <- startsWith(repos, "file:")` in https://svn.r-project.org/R/trunk/src/library/utils/R/packages.R 

I've fixed our build to use `renv::install` instead - that succeeds without the error - but thought I'd report this as it might help others who come across a similar problem...

I've looked through the release notes on https://rstudio.github.io/renv/news/index.html and not seen what might have caused this.... but am still reading...

```r
desc <- file.path(boot, "DESCRIPTION")

sapply(boot, file.exists)
#> C:/Users/davzim/Documents/projects/the-project/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-w64-mingw32/boot
```

title: Unable to restore old versions of Git packages from RSPM
description:
When renv restores an old version of a Git package from RSPM, it tries to download the package from a URL like `/src/contrib/Archive/testit/testit_b2df32d0149ab2f7f4aeb78c2325fce0285a254f.tar.gz` (with the `RemoteSha` as the version) instead of `/src/contrib/Archive/testit/testit_0.11.tar.gz`:
```r
> renv::restore()
The following package(s) will be updated:

# RSPM ===============================
- testit   [* -> 0.11]

* Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
Retrieving 'https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/bionic/latest/src/contrib/Archive/testit/testit_b2df32d0149ab2f7f4aeb78c2325fce0285a254f.tar.gz' ...
Error: failed to retrieve package 'testit'
In addition: Warning messages:
1: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 500  
2: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 500  
```

Restoring current versions of Git packages from RSPM does work fine however.

From talking to @kevinushey, this is a conflict from RSPM adding a `RemoteSha` field to Git packages, while still being served from a CRAN-like repo.

To reproduce this without an RSPM instance, you can use this script:

```r
# To reproduce the issue, create a renv project with an older version of
# a Git package from RSPM (testit 0.11)
proj_dir <- tempdir()
writeLines('{
  "R": {
    "Version": "3.6.3",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/latest"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "renv": {
      "Package": "renv",
      "Version": "0.13.2",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "RSPM",
      "Hash": "079cb1f03ff972b30401ed05623cbe92"
    },
    "testit": {
      "Package": "testit",
      "Version": "0.11",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "RSPM",
      "RemoteSha": "b2df32d0149ab2f7f4aeb78c2325fce0285a254f",
      "Hash": "54334635456f745dce584a8cc53d7900"
    }
  }
}', file.path(proj_dir, "renv.lock"))

setwd(proj_dir)
renv::activate()
# * Project '/tmp/Rtmp9sARgj' loaded. [renv 0.13.2]

renv::restore()
# The following package(s) will be updated:
#
# # RSPM ===============================
# - testit   [* -> 0.11]
#
# * Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
# Retrieving 'https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/__linux__/bionic/latest/src/contrib/Archive/testit/testit_b2df32d0149ab2f7f4aeb78c2325fce0285a254f.tar.gz' ...
# Error: failed to retrieve package 'testit'

# curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 500
```

title: Custom Pkg Management + Remote Servers
description:
I am in the setting where I have a custom R package that is used in dozens of repos, on dozens of remote machines. I am using .Renv because when I upgrade a package or install a new package from CRAN to one of these repos on my local, I want to be able to push a new lock file, and have it be used in all the repos. However, with my own package, I would like to be able to deploy a small change (say I update the NAMESPACE file) without having to go through the following process: 

1. Cut a new release of the package
2. devtools::install_github(package_name, ref = packageversion)
3. renv::snapshot() 
4. commit and push the lockfile to the new repos

Ideally I would push my new package to master branch, and when I renv::restore() on a remote server it would realize that the package hash has changed, and it would re install / build the package from the master branch in the github repo. However, this is not the case. Is it possible to force this behavior?

title: Managing `renv.lock` for Github Actions when installing packages from internal RStudio Package Manager
description:
In our Github Actions, we use `renv::restore()` to restore and cache the package dependencies. When installing and snapshotting packages installed from an internal RStudio Package Manager (inaccessible on Github), what is the best way to manage the `renv.lock` file so that the same package dependencies can be installed from a secondary source/repository?

As an example, this following script modifies the `renv.lock` to install internal packages from Github instead of RSPM. Are there issues with this approach, or is there a better way to handling this?

```library(rjson)
internals <- c("package1","package2")
lockfile <- rjson::fromJSON(file = "renv.lock")
packages <- lockfile$Packages
lockfile$Packages <- packages[!(names(packages) %in% internals)]
fileConn<-file("renv.scrubbed.lock")
writeLines(rjson::toJSON(lockfile), fileConn)
close(fileConn)
for(package in internals){
    devtools::install_github(paste0("LKS-CHART/",package))
}
renv::restore(lockfile = "renv.scrubbed.lock")
```

Thank you!

title: proposal: extend settings and allow additional libraries to be recorded
description:
I would have another proposal for discussion

our example use case:

we have a custom library (custom tool, which helps us to manage our projects - for example, it contains some helper functions used during the build on our build server, or it contains some functions used to deploy to our custom and secured CRAN deployment)

We don't reference this library anywhere in the code, but we use it and we want it to be tracked using RENV.

One option would be to record the package in the "Suggests" section of DESCRIPTION, but we have a single-repo for multiple R packages managed as a single RENV project. For this reason, RENV is not scanning DESCRIPTION in these sub-folders, so this does not work.

What I'd propose for these custom scenarios is to add a configuration option in 
https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html

called additional.packages and every package mentioned here would be tracked by RENV.


What do you think abouyt this improvement?
