title: Proposal: make renv:::project public or add a public method for getting dependencies defined in renv.lock
description:
Hi, would it be possible to make **renv:::project** public or somehow make available any option to get info about packages and their versions recorded in _renv.lock_ file?

Our use case is that we build and deploy internal snapshot  (ie. unstable versions under development) packages with version string as 99.99.99.9000 and what we are doing when we want to build a package is that we check all its (also transient) dependencies with 99.99.99.9000 version string and forcibly reinstalls them. And we don't want to increase the versions every time we make a change to these snapshot packages because we have a pretty wide dependency graph. 

So we are accessing _renv:::project$data()$Packages_ for getting information about packages recorded in renv.lock_, then we detect all snapshot versions and reinstalls them with _renv.install("xxxxxx@99.99.99.9000", rebuild = TRUE)_.

SO what I'd propose is to export _renv:::project_. Or is there any other safe alternative to get the information about dependencies other than using internal API or parsing the JSON lock file directly?

temp <- tempfile()

title: Custom repos overwritten by renv in .profile

I am running on RStudio Server Pro with renv 0.12.5. When I try to use custom repositories via the *.Rprofile* I am finding the 'renv' script overwrites the provided values.

local({

  r["CRAN"] <- "https://cran.rstudio.com/"
  r["rspm_ext"] <- "https://customlocation.com"
  options(repos = r)
})

source("renv/activate.R")

  r <- getOption("repos")
  r["CRAN"] <- "https://cran.rstudio.com/"
  r["rspm_ext"] <- "https://customlocation.com"

title: system library that is installed doesn't appear in Packages/System Library
description:
I installed a variety of libraries at the system level.  When I run R on the command-line, I can call `library(here)`, for example, and it will reference the system here lib.  Also, when I start a regular R project, the system libs that I installed are all there.  However, when I open a project in RStudio Server with renv they do not appear.  I only see what look like a core set of system libs.

I'm guessing this is probably intentional, so that external (non-core) system libs are not modified on the fly, potentially corrupting the environment.  On the other hand, we create instances that data scientists use and would like them to use the same set of base libraries.

It sounds like the simple solution is just to snapshot what were system libs into renv as well- does that sound right?

Apologies if this is not so much an issue as a comment.

title: Feature request: function to batch-install all packages "used in the project, but not installed"
description:
Thanks to the commit https://github.com/rstudio/renv/commit/7bd669b40dea4c3bb1ce61731701159d7aef6fb7, now renv correctly detects newly required packages (i.e. after init), and gives message: *The following package(s) are used in the project, but are not installed:*. Is it possible to have a function to install those newly added packages in batch?

The current workflow is either:

1. Install all of them manually with `renv::install()`.
2. Install all of them automatically with `renv::hydrate()`. 

The problem with 1) is that this is quite cumbersome, and against the usual workflow in R (install a package once forever, no need to install again in every new project, just call with `library`). 

The problem with 2) is that this will also update all other installed packages to their latest version! This goes against a conservative approach, that would update packages only when needed, or only after testing. Updating packages and installing newly required are two distinct steps, that could ideally be called separately?

Thanks!

title: install packages from lockfile to normal .libPaths() library
description: It would be great if there would be a way to install all packages from a given lockfile into the standard .libPaths() library. This would facilitate faster renv::restore() when renv::restore() is being called repeatedly in complex pipelines (e.g. distributing to a HPC cluster).

title: renv::restore upgrading dependencies already in renv.lock file
description:
I'm doing a renv::restore (renv version 0.12.5) on a project and the following two dependencies keep getting upgraded:

* knitr from 1.30 (lockfile) to 1.31 (latest)
* xfun from 1.18 (lockfile) to 1.20 (latest)

This then causes one of the other libraries to fail as the dependency is setup as `knitr (== 1.30)` in the DESCRIPTION file

I've tried setting `renv.setting.package.dependency.fields` to FALSE but it continues to upgrade knitr and xfun.
I've not looked to see if xfun is a dependency of knitr.

I end up having to purge knitr 1.31 and xfun 1.20 from the global cache and then manually install them to match the renv.lock file and then I can do a restore to get the other packages.

I know that this isn't probably enough to figure it out - I'm just failing to see where the dependencies are being updated. I see installs followed up by a version difference with an output of "the following dependencies were 'fixed'".

title: document how renv::use_python affects RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV
description:
Two related issues:
- The help file here (https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/use_python.html) states that "On load, set the RETICULATE_PYTHON environment variable, so that the reticulate package can automatically use the requested copy of Python as appropriate," This could be more clear that this effectively *supersedes* any RETICULATE_PYTHON value set in .Renviron (ie while the value in .Renviron is left as-is, it is silently ignored)
- when `renv::use_python(name=)` is specified, presumably renv::use_python does the same for RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV that the python argument does for RETICULATE_PYTHON. Adding to this information to the help file would be good.

title: renv::install fails to install archived versions from company internal CRAN-like repo since renv version 0.12.4
description:
Dear renv developers,

thank you for this very versatile and helpful package. It is a game changer to our package handling in R projects.

# Summary

I am facing a bug when downloading and installing an old package version from our company internal CRAN-like repository. Everything worked as intended until renv `0.12.3`. However, I run into an error as soon as I upgrade to any renv version from `0.12.4` onwards, including the latest dev-version.

# Assumption on the origin of the bug

I hypothesise that auth via the `renv.download.headers` option is not considered correctly when installing archived versions from private repos with `renv::install`.

I suppose that the bug may have been introduced in the following change stemming from the changelog details for `0.12.4`: 
> renv::install(<pkg>) will now install the latest-available version of that package from local sources, if that package is available and newer than any package available on the active package repositories. (#591)

# Setup

- We have a company internal R package called `MY-PACKAGE` hosted on our company internal R package distribution server `https://company-repo-url` (the same problem arises with all of our packages)
- The latest version of `MY-PACKAGE` is `0.4.8`. I aim to install `0.4.6`, e.g. via `renv::install("MY-PACKAGE@0.4.6")` or during a call to `renv::restore()` when `0.4.6` is recorded in the lockfile and has not been cached yet.
- Auth via `renv.download.headers` option (as described in your [vignette](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html#authentication-with-custom-headers-1))

# Working behaviour with `0.12.3`

r$> renv::install("MY-PACKAGE@0.4.6")

title: snapshot() overwrites python/environment specified via use_python()
description:
I've created my own local conda environment and would like to use this pre-created environment.
``` r
renv::use_python(python="/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/bin/python3.8", type="conda", name="/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/envs/rgee5")
```
returns:
``` r
* Activated Python 3.8.5 [conda; /var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/envs/rgee5]
* Project '/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5' loaded. [renv 0.12.5]
```

Inspecting the lockfile I see my specified version of python
```
"Python": {
    "Version": "3.8.5",
    "Type": "conda",
    "Name": "/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/envs/rgee5"
  }
```

If I run `renv_python_conda_snapshot` (which is called deep inside of `snapshot`)
``` r
renv:::renv_python_conda_snapshot("/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5", "/var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/envs/rgee5/bin/python")
```
then inspect environment.yml, i see at the bottom it's using the correct conda environment:
``` bash
cat environment.yml
```
the final line is:
```
prefix: /var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/miniconda/envs/rgee5
```
This is correct.


_________________________

However, if I use `renv::snapshot`:

the lockfile gets changed to:

```
  "Python": {
    "Version": "3.9.1",
    "Type": "conda",
    "Name": null
  }
```

and the bottom of environment.yml reads:
```
prefix: /var/local/QUTE/Transfer/Michael/rgee5/renv/python/condaenvs/renv-python
```

This environment which comes out of nowhere arises from the contents of `renv:::renv_python_conda_snapshot`:
```

        "conda", version)
```

since lockfile$Python$Name is now null, renv_python_envpath gets used instead of the python environment I originally specified

something inside of snapshot() is altering the python environment even though it was already specified.

title: How to prevent stealth copying from user library?
description:
Hi Kevin 👋 

We faced a strange scenario this morning while upgrading a RSP container from 18.04 to 20.04. During this process we realized that renv somehow copies binaries from the local user library even though all configs were set not to do this. Do we overlook something or is this a bug?

## Scenario

- `stringi` installed in user library (no renv) from binary on Ubuntu 18.04 (RSP) some days ago
- `RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/opt/renv/cache`
- `RENV_PATHS_BINARY=/opt/renv/binary`
- `RENV_PATHS_SOURCE=/opt/renv/source`

→ Upgrade RSP/OS to 20.04 (RSP running in a container with the home dirs mounted)

→ Delete renv/cache, renv/binary, renv/source to start fresh

→ `renv::init()` in project (new session)

→ `renv::install("stringi")`

Now instead of downloading a new binary, renv copies the local binary (console log says: `copied binary`) from the user library.

Then `library("stringi")` fails because it tries to link against `libicu60` (bionic) but the container has `libicu66` (focal).

## Questions

- Is there a way to prevent {renv} from copying from the user library? It would be great if we could restrict this to the paths set with `RENV_PATHS_*`. To make this clear, this does not relate to `renv.config.user.library` but where renv gets cached packages from.

  ```r
   .libPaths()
  [1] "/home/someuser/project/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"
  [2] "/tmp/Rtmpn3oKZp/renv-system-library"
   ```

- Because renv does not report where it copies the binary from it took us long to realize that renv did not copy it from RENV_PATHS_BINARY but from the users local library. Maybe a verbosity setting could help here to tell where it got the binary from?

- Installing `stringi` again into the user library and then letting renv pick it up solved the issue. This prooves the assumption that renv copied the pkg from the user library.

- renv states in the log "copied local binary". Where does this binary come from in this scenario? AFAIK there are only installed packages in the user library but not the downloaded binaries (binaries <-> installed packages). Only renv stores and caches the pkg binaries (?) but we deleted all binaries in `RENV_PATHS_BINARY` and `~/.local/share/renv`.

title: capture source package with renv in package root
description:
I have an R package `{mypkg}` and I want to create a virtual environment where this (built) package and its dependencies are available. So I thought I could, in the root of the sources of `{mypkg}` 
```r
renv::settings$snapshot.type("explicit") # Just from DESCRIPTION
renv::settings$package.dependency.fields("Imports")
renv::init()
```
I am not sure why `{mypkg}` does not end up captured with `{renv}` in both the lockfile and the library. This makes it (apparently) impossible to use it in non-dev workflows (e.g. without calling `devtools::load_all()`)
```r
library(mypkg)
#> Error in library(gli.clu) : there is no package called ‘gli.clu’
```
In particular, I want to share my code with other people, so they could clone the repo and use `renv::restore()` and then `library(mypkg)` without the requirements of the `{devtools}` toolchain. Next, I tried `renv::install(".")`, beacuse in the help file for `renv::install()`, I saw `renv::install("~/path/to/package")`. This didn't do what I wanted either.
```r
renv::install(".")
#> Error in if (is.character(url) && grepl("/__[^_]+__/", url)) type <- "binary" : 
#>  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

Last attempt was `remotes::install_local()`, which installed the package properly, but:
* then I did not know how to add it to the lockfile, the following attempt also did not do it:
```r
renv::settings$snapshot.type("custom")
options(renv.snapshot.filter = function(proj_dir) {
  desc_deps <- desc::desc_get_deps() # probably needed recursive deps here but...
  c(
    desc_deps[desc_deps$type == "Imports",]$package,
    unlist(read.dcf('DESCRIPTION', 'Package'))
  )
})
```
* was really slow (probably because it had to copy `renv/` at that point (I could move the folder outside the package sources as I found out in the [documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/packages.html#r-cmd-build-and-the-project-library-1) though, but I think it's better to make `{remotes}` respect `.Rbuildignore`, e.g. as suggested in https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/107.

***

Given my understanding and challenges, I think when `renv::init()` is called in a package directory, it should also install that package and make it available on `renv::restore()`, potentially add it to the lock file (maybe this requires to extend the lockfile specs for this particular case). Alternatives are that at least `renv::install(".")` would install the package properly and there is a way to add it to the lockfile. Putting a library statement in some random file should not be the solution to this I think, in particular not since for this to work, I couldn't use 
```r
renv::settings$snapshot.type("explicit") # Just from DESCRIPTION
renv::settings$package.dependency.fields("Imports")
```
Anymore (I think) and all dev deps would have to be installed. I found https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/624, which is related.

Context: I am trying to add  renv as a [supported language](https://pre-commit.com/#supported-languages) for https://pre-commit.com (partly tracked in https://github.com/lorenzwalthert/precommit/issues/215).

title: Feature request: Multiple cache directories
description:
Would it be possible to support multiple cache directories?

For example, `Sys.setenv("RENV_PATHS_CACHE" = "~/.local/share/renv/cache1;~/.local/share/renv/cache2")`, could indicate that both `~/.local/share/renv/cache1` and `~/.local/share/renv/cache2` are directories where renv looks for cached packages. When adding a new package to the cache, renv would use the first writeable path.

My use case is the following: our software consists of multiple modules (basically R packages with a user interface). Each of these modules has its own dependencies, and we supply a default set of R packages through an installer. Right now, we are making these modules more modular so that we can update them independently. During an update, the package dependencies may change. To efficiently reuse available packages, I'd like to use renv with its excellent caching feature.
Now here's the problem. The R packages shipped by default end up in the installation folder of a user. We do not have write access there after installing (at least on macOS and on Linux with flatpak). In our own local folder (inside Appdata, ~/.local/share, etc.) we do have write access. My goal is to create a second cache directory in our local folder. That way, we can 1) efficiently reuse the R packages in the installation folder and 2) reuse R packages installed while updating modules.

The changes required to make this work are rather minimal, at least in the small example that I tested locally. I'd be more than happy to open a PR if you think this could be useful.

title: FR: distinguish between runtime and developer packages
description:
This has been a recurring struggle for me since I've started to use renv.

My project/package needs, say:
- data.table
- DBI
- lubridate

But to do any work on it I inevitably need:
- devtools
- testthat
- roxygen2
- styler
- lintr

If I'm using my `renv.lock`, say, to create a Docker image to deploy the application, I really only want to include the runtime dependencies, in particular because `devtools` brings along an enormous chain of recursive dependencies that bloat the image. But if I don't include devtools et al in the lockfile, then, well ... my project library won't have devtools after`renv::restore()`. Even if I manually `renv::install()` (but don't record) it, I'd have to tell everyone else working on my project to do that to, and we wouldn't necessarily have the same version of everything, thus leading to spurious changes in e.g. test behaviour (testthat 2 vs 3), documentation files (roxygen 6 vs 7), etc.

Do you think it would be possible to record both types of packages, but somehow in different tiers -- something like `[packages]` vs `[dev-packages]` in Pipenv?

(And if not -- might you have any wisdom?)

title: "deploying" an environment to a cluster
description:

I'm working with somewhat of a unique situation: I start a script on a server that involves data processing. This script is in a project that uses renv for package versioning. Later in that script, I send some files (that result from the data processing) to a cluster along with a signal to run some code on that cluster.  I'd like the package versions loaded on the cluster to be the same versions that the renv lockfile specifies. I'd prefer not to have the same git repo both on the local server and the remote cluster because that involves ensuring that the repos are always in sync.

So is there any way to "deploy" a lockfile to a new directory (such that that in that new directory a local library is created and all the specified package versions are installed/hopefully copied from a local library) without having to copy the entire project directory from the local server to the cluster? I guess I'm asking is: what is the cleanest way to initialize a new project (and install packages) from just an existing lockfile?

title: other thoughts for embedding lockfile in a script
description:
- New function called `use()`, that takes a list of packages to use for a script. `renv` will then install the requested packages to a temporary library, copying or linking from the cache as appropriate.
- `embed()` will read the project lockfile, and generate a call to `use()` that can be embedded in the R script. (basically, a compact version of the lockfile encoded for the R script)
- Users can then just `source()` the file, and `renv` will automagically install those packages for them.

title: activate.R installs file from source; option for install from binary

title: consider encoding version of pandoc used into lockfile?
description: For projects using `rmarkdown`, since having an appropriate version of `pandoc` available is required by `rmarkdown` in most workflows.

title: Avoid using junctions in the temporary directory
description:
On Windows, the base library is mirrored in the temporary directory using junctions ("sandbox" in the code), in `file.path(tempdir(), "renv-system-library")`. This creates a problem in the following situation:

- The user works in RStudio
- They reboot their machine while RStudio is open
- A service (configured or third-party) purges `%TEMP%\` and incorrectly deletes the contained junctions recursively before reboot.

After reboot, the user finds a base library full with empty directories where the base packages should be, yielding a non-usable R installation. (Sorry, no reprex :upside_down_face:.)

Can we generate the sandbox in a subdirectory of `./renv/` to work around this problem?

CC @pat-s.

title: restore() ignores library argument?
description:
Hi, I've found that in renv 0.12.5, the `library` argument in `renv::restore()` works differently than it did in renv 0.12.3. Before, a `restore()` would've always restored packages into the `library` directory if specified. But now, renv seems to ignore the `library` directory in certain cases.

I'm not sure if this is a bug or if it's intended, but I didn't see anything in the changelog about it.

Here's a minimal example to demo this:

```r
# Create a minimal lockfile with just renv in the snapshot
proj_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "project")
dir.create(proj_dir)
renv::snapshot(project = proj_dir, prompt = FALSE)

# Restore the lockfile into an empty package library
temp_lib <- file.path(tempdir(), "lib")
dir.create(temp_lib)
renv::restore(project = proj_dir, library = temp_lib, prompt = FALSE)

# The renv package should have been restored into the package library
library(renv, lib.loc = temp_lib)
```

In renv 0.12.3, this is what I get. The renv package is snapshotted and restored into the specified package library:
```r
> proj_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "project")
> dir.create(proj_dir)
> renv::snapshot(project = proj_dir, prompt = FALSE)
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

# CRAN ===============================
- renv   [* -> 0.12.3]

* Lockfile written to '/tmp/RtmpYMfHi0/project/renv.lock'.

> temp_lib <- file.path(tempdir(), "lib")
> dir.create(temp_lib)
> renv::restore(project = proj_dir, library = temp_lib, prompt = FALSE)
The following package(s) will be updated:

# CRAN ===============================
- renv   [* -> 0.12.3]

Installing renv [0.12.3] ...
	OK [copied local binary]
Copying renv [0.12.3] into the cache ...
	OK [copied 61 files in 0.01 seconds]
The dependency tree was repaired during package installation:
       _
  renv   [0.12.3]

Call `renv::snapshot()` to capture these dependencies in the lockfile.

> library(renv, lib.loc = temp_lib)
```

However in renv 0.12.5, the restore doesn't do anything. It's like the `library` argument was ignored, and my default libraries were used anyway:
```r
> proj_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "project")
> dir.create(proj_dir)
> renv::snapshot(project = proj_dir, prompt = FALSE)
The following package(s) will be updated in the lockfile:

> renv::restore(project = proj_dir, library = temp_lib, prompt = FALSE)
* The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.

> library(renv, lib.loc = temp_lib)
Error in library(renv, lib.loc = temp_lib) :

title: Support for Artifactory
description:
There is a similar issue logged for packrat as well - https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/583

Artifactory does not store archived versions in a CRAN-like way - see
* https://www.jfrog.com/jira/browse/RTFACT-17392
* https://www.jfrog.com/jira/browse/RTFACT-21144

The last issue from Artifactory looks like they have changed this in their code but I'm not clear on what version this fix is included in.

I thought about re-implementing this PR from remotes - https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/pull/441 - thinking that will also fix renv but now I don't believe that that is true (since renv only Suggests remotes)

title: add: Example using docker-compose
description:
Hi all,

Thanks for the work in this awesome package. I use it instead of packrat and it has been wonderful.

# Suggestion - add example of docker-compose setup

While the documentation has some examples on using renv with docker, I must admit that I had some trouble converting the 
usage for a docker-compose setup.

Since it is common to use docker with several containers working together (e.g., one with R, another with Python and yet another with SQL), I think to have such an example in the docs would be useful.

This is a basic template I used that sufficed for my needs, and may inspire you.

docker-compose.yml:

```yml
version: '3'

services:

  r_temp:
   build:
     context: ./working_container
     dockerfile: Dockerfile
   env_file: .env  
   volumes:
      - "${RENV_PATHS_CACHE_HOST}:${RENV_PATHS_CACHE}"
   command:  
     #this is a setup for Emacs or CLI usage
     sh -c "R -e 'options(renv.consent = TRUE);renv::restore(lockfile= \"$renv_lock\");' && tail -f /dev/null"
    # for Rstudio substitute "tail..." by 
    # /usr/lib/rstudio-server/bin/rserver --server-daemonize=0
```
./wroking_container/Dockerfile:
```yml
FROM rocker/verse:3.6.1

# create container folder for packages
RUN mkdir -p ~/.local/share/renv/

# install renv
RUN R -e 'install.packages("renv")'

CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```
env file:

```yml
# the path to an renv cache on the host machine
RENV_PATHS_CACHE_HOST=/path/to/host/cache

# the path to the cache within the container
RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/root/.local/share/renv/

# path for renv lockfile used by the container
renv_lock=/path/to/renv.lock
```

title: Renv assumes CRAN-like placement for older versions of package
description:
Related to https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/209

We're using the Nexus Package Manager for internal R-package-repositories. The Nexus package manager implements the minimum requirements for a R-repository, but does not place older versions in contrib/Archive, as is the case with CRAN. Instead, all versions are placed in /scr/contrib

Thus, installation of older versions with renv::install fails:

```r
install.packages("internalpackage@3.0.0")

Retrieving 'https://nexus/repository/internal/src/contrib/Archive/internalpackage/internalpackage_3.0.0.tar.gz' ...
Error: failed to retrieve package 'internalpackage'
In addition: Warning messages:
1: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404 Not Found 
```

As per https://issues.sonatype.org/browse/NEXUS-25130, a "monkey-patch" has been suggested by the Nexus community:
``` r
library(renv)

# see: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/master/R/retrieve.R 
utils::assignInNamespace(
  "renv_retrieve_repos_archive", 
  function(record) 
  {
    name <- sprintf("%s_%s.tar.gz", record$Package, record$Version)
    for (repo in getOption("repos")) {
      archive_repo <- file.path(repo, "src/contrib/Archive", record$Package)
      status <- renv:::catch(renv:::renv_retrieve_repos_impl(record, "source", name, archive_repo))
    
      if (identical(status, TRUE))
        return(TRUE)

      nxrm3_repo <- file.path(repo, "src/contrib")
      status <- renv:::catch(renv:::renv_retrieve_repos_impl(record, "source", name, nxrm3_repo))
      if (identical(status, TRUE))
        return(TRUE)
      }  
      return(FALSE)
  }, 
  "renv")
```

Since contrib/Archive is not a requirement for R-repositories per se, could this hard-coded logic be changed (https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/ff7aa1ed8de5b48cb1138ee567029eeb9a6fe1bd/R/retrieve.R#L529)?

Thank you

title: renv and multi-package projects
description:
We are using renv for a product that is made up of multiple packages - call them A and B.
The issue we are facing is that A depends on B.
We deploy released versions "x.y.z" to a WORK repository.
We use local sources when building development versions "x.y.z.9000".

For our workflow, we tried setting up A with a renv setting of ignored.packages = B thinking that we would manually manage the dependent package version. However this doesn't work since A's environment needs B's dependent packages. So we can't ignore B because that ignores all of B's dependencies.

The only way that I can think to make this work is for the renv of A to depend on a Local B.
But then I always have to build the local B even if I'm only working on A.

Also when I install from local sources
```
renv::install('B@1.0.0.9000')
```
that works but then when I snapshot it - it thinks that the repository is WORK.
And renv::upgrade does not see local sources as a later version of the WORK versions.

I really don't want to have to do a deploy of B in order to use it for A changes.

I'm at a loss for how best to make this work and looking for ideas...

title: GitLab refs with slash not working
description:
# Problem
Trying to specify a Remote on a GitLab server with a slash in the `ref`, e.g. `gitlab@host::user/repo/@feature/foo` fails during  `renv::restore()`.

# Reason
The `ref` is not encoded using `URLencode` as `id` is:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/7fdff02b7148f850ae65e0fdda130594373b64b7/R/remotes.R#L382-L385

# Proposal
Add `ref <- URLencode(ref, reserved = TRUE)`.

title: Dcoumentation: mention renv::hydrate() as main step in the worklow?
description:
I feel the use of `renv::hydrate()` is not documented enough in the renv documentation? As a newcomer, I had to dig a lot to understand it is a fundamental function that I am likely to use very often! 

The documentation seems to be based on a workflow where any time a user would need a new library (new to the project, not to the system), she would manually install it with `install.packages()`. But this is rather a rare case, most of the time one is just using `library()` in a script to load a new package (again, new here refers to new to the project). In that case, `renv::status()` will not detect anything, and then the user won't be able to load that package! After a lot of trial-and-error, I believe the right function is `renv::hydrate()` in that case. As a newcomer, I tried first `restore`,  `refresh`, `clean`, `record`.

Is it correct that after adding a new `library()` call the right function is `renv::hydrate()`? If yes, this would be worth adding in the main workflow. 

I suggest adding in the _Workflow_ section of https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html:

1. Call renv::init() to initialize a new project-local environment with a private R library,
2. Work in the project as normal, installing and removing new R packages as they are needed in the project,
3. Call renv::snapshot() to save the state of the project library to the lockfile (called renv.lock),
4. Continue working on your project, installing and updating R packages as needed. **If you want to use packages that are in your system library but not yet in your project library, use `library(pkg)` in your script and then `renv::hydrate()`**

title: renv::status throws warning for reused knitr chunks
description:
I recently introduced a knitr chunk with [reused chunks](https://yihui.org/knitr/demo/reference/) in my Rnw document, and noted that `renv::status()` throws a warning (that looks like an error). Apparently, renv does not consider reused chunks valid R code ;-)

Example:
```{r}
<<'chunk1', eval=FALSE>>
a <- 1+1
@

<<'chunk2'>>=
<<chunk1>>
a+1
@ 
```

Run `renv::status()`:
```{r}
> renv::status()
WARNING: One or more problems were discovered while enumerating dependencies.

/solarchemist/thesis/300-text.Rnw
----------------------------------------------------------

ERROR 1: <text>:6:1: unexpected input
6: <<
   ^

Please see `?renv::dependencies` for more information.
Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: 
```

There are at least a couple of ways for the user to proceed, in spite of this error-looking warning (it's just a warning):

+ simply choose `y` to proceed at the prompt, or
+ [add `renv.ignore=TRUE` to the chunk options](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/421#issuecomment-689007228) of the chunk containing the reused chunks.

`renv` v0.11.0 on R 3.6.2, Ubuntu 18.04.5.

title: Possible to define compilation staging folder outside of the project
description:
Hi @kevinushey,

Thanks for such a great package - our team is getting a lot of use from it!

Would it be possible to allow renv users to compile packages outside of the current defined location: `*\renv\staging\.*`?

**Why?**
Our IT are starting to roll-out CarbonBlack (security software that limits what staff can install) and they've whitelisted certain locations where packages can be installed / compiled. 

`renv` works fine with symbolic links to these whitelisted library folder locations, however, when setting up (restoring) a renv project, for packages that require compilation, this compilation occurs within the `project\renv\staging\.*` folder which isn't allowed.

I believe it's as simple as allowing the `root` path to be manually declared in the following function (in `install.R`):

```R
renv_install_staged_library <- function(library) {

  project <- renv_project(default = NULL)

  root <- if (is.null(project))
    file.path(library[[1]], ".renv")
  else
    file.path(project, "renv/staging")

  renv_install_staged_library_impl(root)

}
```

title: Package development with renv and build-time \Sexpr in documentation

When doing an R CMD build (via various entry points) - the build process sees the build-time \Sexpr and tries to install the package in order to complete the help pages. This package installation fails when it cannot find the Import: packages.

title: renv 'time' caches incorrect package list
description:
I am behind a corporate proxy through which I need to access the internet. To use `renv`, I set the `HTTP_PROXY` and `HTTPS_PROXY` env variables and this allows me to install packages correctly:

``` r
Sys.setenv("HTTP_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>", "HTTPS_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>")
renv::install("data.table")
#> Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/4.0/data.table_1.13.2.zip' ...
#>  OK [downloaded 2.5 Mb in 1.3 secs]
#> Installing data.table [1.13.2] ...
#>  OK [installed binary]
```

The following situation is, however, unexpected:

1. Install a package before setting the proxy server (this fails as expected).
2. Set the proxy env variables.
3. Install the package again, which fails (unexpected).

``` r
renv::install("data.table")
#> Warning: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib"
#> Warning: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/4.0"
#> Error: package 'data.table' is not available
Sys.setenv("HTTP_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>", "HTTPS_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>")
renv::install("data.table")
#> Error: package 'data.table' is not available
```

After some debugging I found that `renv` seems to inadvertently cache the result from the first call to `renv::install()`. I am using R 4.0.2 and `renv` 0.12.3.

Edit:
I think the following code allows to reproduce the issue when not behind a proxy:

``` r
Sys.setenv("HTTP_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>", "HTTPS_PROXY" = "<proxy_server>")

title: <project-root>/renv/local requires full tar.gz path, not just package name ... is this expected?
description:
Hi, I'm trying to bundle some custom packages with a project, and I've following the instructions in the [_Installing from Local Sources_](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/local-sources.html) article. My interpretation of the documentation suggests that for package `mypkg` placed in `./renv/local/` (relative to the project's root) one can install it using:
```R
renv::install("mypkg")
```
... and that, upon failing to locate `mypkg` on CRAN (and any other registered other remotes) search locally in the `./renv/local/` directory **OR** `${RENV_PATHS_LOCAL}` (the latter of which I'm trying to avoid for maximum portability with colleagues).

This doesn't appear to be the case, however, as I'm finding I need to specify the exact path to the tarball, as in:
```R
renv::install("./renv/local/mypkg_0.0.0.9000.tar.gz")
```
(Similarly `renv::install("./renv/local/mypkg")` doesn't work, either.)

Is this behavior expected? Or should `renv::install` use the fallback search path (or the environment variable) and standard 'packagename-only' semantics?

EDIT: `renv` v0.12.0

title: renv::status() queries dependencies and sanity of package cache
description:
According to [`?status`](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/status.html), its job is to

> Report differences between the project's lockfile and the current state of the project's library (if any).

Both actions take too long in our use case. There's no progress, R just appears to hang. We have `snapshot.type: all` in our `settings.dcf` .

- Querying dependencies takes too much time when renv is used in a large monorepo or in `~` . We can work around the enumeration of dependencies by adding `*` to `.renvignore` . 

- Checking the R package cache in `renv_status_check_cache()` takes too much time if the cache is on a network drive. There seems to be no workaround.

Questions:

- Why are we querying dependencies?

- Would you be open to check the cache only in a dedicated `cache_status()` function, or to add a `cache = FALSE` (or even `cache = TRUE`) argument to `status()`?

CC @pat-s.

title: lockfile example issue
description:
The `lockfile()` example is not run, so there is a subtle issue that gets through the checks.  Since the function is not exported, [this example](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/master/R/lockfile-api.R#L109) doesn't work:

```
lock <- lockfile("renv.lock")
```

I believe it should be:
```
lock <- renv:::lockfile("renv.lock")
```

I'm happy to submit a PR for this if you're open to it.

title: Setting `renv.lock` location globally?
description:
In a project with a monorepo setting the following structure exists:

```
$DRIVE (network drive)
  - renv/RENV_CACHE
  - renv/RENV_BINARY
  - renv/RENV_SOURCE
  - renv.lock
  - renv/activate.R
  
$LOCAL 
   - project1
   - project2
   - projectX
```

Idea: All projects should share the same `renv.lock` file by default which should live in `$DRIVE`.

The issue we are facing is that the `lockfile` argument in all {renv} functions points to the project directory and can not be set via an env var.

Hence, for every call to `renv::snapshot()` or `renv::restore()` from within a project, `lockfile` needs to be set explicitly, otherwise an `renv.lock` file will be created in the project directory.
This is not a longterm solution and currently we are working around the problem by redefining customized {renv} functions with hardcoded paths for `lockfile` pointing to `$DRIVE`.

(We are accounting for the location of `$DRIVE/renv/activate.R` in the global `.Rprofile`)

Would it be possible to define a global env var `RENV_PATHS_LOCKFILE` similar to the already existing `RENV_PATHS_*` ones?

title: RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT leads to conflicts
description:
I’m using `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT` to use ‘renv’ during package development, and this works quite well. However, I often have projects (most throw-away, some bigger) with identical names. This even happens during package development, because I occasionally check out multiple copies of a project when working on multiple branches simultaneously (Git purists might say this is bad practice, but it’s fairly common, and sometimes just practical).

Unfortunately this causes conflicts since the libraries in `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT` are identified only by a single folder name rather than by a complete path. That is, a library for a project `X` is located at the path `$RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT/‹X›/%v/%p`.

I suggest changing this by replacing the `‹X›` by a slug of the whole path to `X`. Obviously this means that moving the project to a different location in the file system renders the library path stale (I don’t see that as a big problem).

As an example for slugging the paths, Vim uses `%` in place of `/` for undo and swap files (for reasons unknown to me, Vim doesn’t seem to escape `%` in the original path though, so `foo/bar` and `foo%bar` still conflict, despite this being trivially solvable).

title: renv and containers
description:

I want to be able to use the container as non-root user as well for HPC portability, e.g., using singularity. 

My fist impression was to only modify RENV_PATHS_CACHE to some shared location in the container (/usr/share/renv) and 
the use `renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)`. 
This would install the cache in a location that can later be accessed by other users as well. I then run into problems with shared libraries not being found. 
I can circumvene that by setting the RENV_PATHS_ROOT to the current working directory (which is writable). renv complains about broken symlinks but restores the packages all-right from the cache. 

I guess, ideally I would want to use the information in renv.lock to install all packages on the system level is there any functionality in renv that could help me do that?
Alternatively, how do I safely restore an renv to the host project folder when the cache is inside of  a container?

edit: the julia package manager allows multiple 'depots', this allos me to append the depot that I have in the container to the user depot. Whatever is not found in the current users depot is then taken from the container.

title: Provide a means to initalize a renv project without using the global package library
description:
Using renv enables me to have a separate library for each of my projects, completely avoiding the use of any user or system library. In this light, it seems strange to me that in order to install renv, I need to use the global package library. We deploy R in containers in our institution and don't know what the users do besides that. For example, our users could have a user library for other projects and different versions of R, that does not distinguish between R versions from following some barely-understood blog tutorial. Or they could use different containers with the same R versions but different libcs (e.g. Alpine vs Debian...)

When I was explaining renv to my biologist users, it took them a good portion of thinking to learn about the package library, and to understand `init`, `snapshot`, and `restore`. I then have to go on to troubleshoot problems with mismatching R internals or missing user libraries (for example, on our system, `install.packages` tries to install packages to the folder `NA`...) just for the one-time-task of initializing an renv project. It is unnessecarily cumbersome to explain users that with renv they don't need to care about different libraries for different R versions coming in conflict, but in order to install it they need to know the state of their user or system library. 

It is almost there: renv already has the means to install itself as part of hydrating. So why not provide a script that installs the latest CRAN version of renv directly into a new package library?

Currently this can be achived by executing

```r
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rstudio/renv/(COMMIT ON CRAN)/renv/activate.R"
```

However, this is a bit cumbersome and by replacing `(COMMIT ON CRAN)` with `master` users might get an unstable version. 

So why not create a script with an easy-to-remember link that points to the latest CRAN `renv/activate.R`, like for example `https://rstudio.github.io/renv/install.R`?

title: Provide some equivalent to npm package.json's postinstall scripts / add "scripts" field to lockfile
description:
I'm interested in automating initialization of certain git hooks to enforce commit style on my repos. 

In javascript, a pattern for achieving this is to use the package.json's "scripts" field, with a postinstall script. See https://typicode.github.io/husky/#/ 

This would make sense for renv, if a project has conventions/toolings, it would be nice to have a way to bootstrap toolings, & to help enforce these.

title: Installation fails with 'main' as the default branch name on `renv::install()`
description:
GitHub has announced that the default branch name of the repository will change from `master` to `main`.
https://github.blog/changelog/2020-10-01-the-default-branch-for-newly-created-repositories-is-now-main/
This causes the installation of the new package repository to fail.

```r
renv::install("uribo/tororomecab")
#> Error: failed to parse remote 'uribo/tororomecab' -- download failed [error code 22]
#> In addition: Warning messages:
#> 1: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 422 Unprocessable Entity 
#> 2: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 422 Unprocessable Entity 
```

I was able to install it by specifying the branch as follows. 

```r
renv::install("uribo/tororomecab@main")
```

However, I feel that it would be better to support both master and main by default to prevent the same problem.

title: Allow isolated projects to read from cache / copy into isolated library
description:
Related to #555 

Would be helpful to have a way to override the project's settings.dcf at runtime, or provide use.cache as an argument to restore and eliminate any ambiguity. Since `isolate()` modifies the settings.dcf file, other processes activating the same project (but using differently library paths - HPC-style usecase) will not be able to use the cache. In other words, is there a way to make the cache setting a property of the library path rather than a property of the renv project?

Perhaps a way to say "Use the cache, but copy instead of symlink" during restore would be sufficient, effectively isolating w/o disabling the cache

title: Clarify isolate() usage
description:
My understanding from the documentation for `isolate()` is that it should create a copy of the cache and install packages from that copy into the activated renv.  However, the source code for `isolate()` just seems to disable the cache (vs copying the cache), and running `restore()` after `isolate()` results in a otherwise-cached packages being install from CRAN.  

Curious if there was a regression somewhere which prevented the cache from getting copied, or if my interpretation of the docs is incorrect?

title: Create a renv environment from a crated function
description:
The R package https://github.com/r-lib/carrier can be used to create standalone functions. However, it does not manage package dependencies. For this reason, deployment of R functions in arbitrary environments (e.g. deployment of crate functions in mlflow) is not that straight-forward because the user has to manage dependencies manually. I think it would be a great addition to connect renv and carrier, creating a `renv.lockfile` from a crated function: 

```r
fn <- carrier::crate(function(x) styler::style_text(x))
renv::init(bare = TRUE)
renv::snapshot(fn) # make snapshot an S3 generic to handle project (directories) / single files and crated functions
```
(The API change is just a suggestion, maybe there are better ways to implement this)

Then, to execute the function anywhere, one could just 
```r
renv::restore()
renv::activate()
fn <- readRDS('path/to/crated/function.Rds')
fn(...)
```

I assume most of the functionality to do this already exists in renv, but I could not find them in the exposed API.

This is similar to two existing renv issues that aim at using renv for low(er) level dependency management than an average user: 
* https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/443
* https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/507


I also filed an issue in r-lib/carrier at some point: https://github.com/r-lib/carrier/issues/5

title: Error if missing package version
description:
Hi

I was getting the following error from most **renv** functions (`renv::status()`, `renv::snapshot()`...):

```
Error in if (eval(cond, envir = environment(dot))) return(eval(expr, envir = environment(dot))) : 
  argument is of length zero
```

Using `traceback()` and `debug()` I was able to track it down to the `renv:::renv_lockfile_diff_record()` function, particularly these lines: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/5831de0bd139ce4f7cb41c08111a24a601e6d983/R/lockfile-diff.R#L50-L55

Eventually, I worked out that one of the entries in my `renv.lock` file was missing a version number:

```json
    "reticulate": {
      "Package": "reticulate",
      "Source": "Repository",
    },
```

This was causing the comparison between `before$Version` and `after$Version` to fail. The easy fix was to manually edit `renv.lock` to add the version.

I'm not sure how I managed to have an entry without a version but thought I should report the issue in case somebody else manages to do the same thing.

My suggestion would be to add a check somewhere and give a more informative error if there is no version. I would be happy to help with a PR for that but I'm not sure if it is best to do it in this function or somewhere upstream?

title: Can't snapshot my own project
description:

Previously this wasn't a problem, but in trying to upgrade my renv and dependency versions, renv now wants to remove my package from the lockfile. description:
Hi Kevin,

I am starting to use `{renv}` more and more to make sure my `R`-centric projects are truly self-contained and reproducible. But I have a specific project that also happens to also use `python` quite a bit and I'm looking for a little guidance on best practices for setting up a `virtualenv` using `{renv}` with the least amount of friction.

As an example, I have a `virtualenv` which lives in the default location on my Mac (`/Users/matt/.virtualenvs/r-reticulate`). This virtualenv is the one I generally bind to when using `{reticulate}` because I have installed all of the `python` packages I need in that envrionment. So when I am ready to use python in my `renv`-initialized project, I call `renv::use_python("/Users/matt/.virtualenvs/r-reticulate/bin/python")` and point it toward the python binary found in this virtualenv. This creates a `virtualenv` in the `renv/` directory, but that newly created virtual environment doesn't contain any packages.

I guess my expectation was that since I define my `python` dependencies in my `R` scripts via `alias <- import("package")` declarations, that I maybe expected the virtualenv would be set up in a similar way to how the `R` library is set up, such that `renv` would detect my `import`s and make sure they are included in the `renv/python/virtualenvs` that was created.

So it seems like I have two options to get the new virtual environment up to speed, __(1)__ start installing `python` packages with `reticulate::virtualenv_install()` and they will now be installed in my `renv/python/virtualenv/renv-python...`, or __(2)__ I can export the `requirements.txt` from the `/Users/matt/.virtualenvs/r-reticulate` and restore them. Both of these are a little more manual than I was hoping.

Any suggestions? Is my mental model of how python is managed by `renv` completely misguided?

Thanks for your help!

title: sandbox creation can be very slow when using networked filesystems
description:
Summarized from https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/7818.

When an `renv` project is loaded, `renv` will (by default) attempt to sandbox the system library, thereby isolating the project from any non-system packages that may have been installed into the system library. This is done by either linking or copying those system packages into a temporary library directory in the R session's temporary directory.

Linking can fail, and copying can be slow, if the project happens to live on a different drive than the R session itself lives on. We should consider whether we could alleviate this issue in some way.

The sandbox can be disabled with:

```
RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED = FALSE
```

in an appropriate startup `.Renviron` file, but it would be good if the out-of-the-box behavior here was better.

cc: @gwd666

title: How to properly load the renv project from a Windows batch file?
description:
I have an R script that I want to run with a Windows batch file.
This file is located in a subfolder of the project_root (where renv/ renv.lock and .Rprofile are located).

This is how I got it to work:

```cmd
CALL "C:\Program Files\R\R-4.0.2\bin\Rscript.exe" -e "renv::load('c:/project_root'); source('c:/project_root/subfolder/script_name.R')"
```

However `renv::load()` is not supposed to be called directly according to the function documentation:

```
# load a project -- note that this is normally done automatically
# when the R session is started in an renv project after calling
# renv::activate()
```

Is the use of `renv::load()` justified in this case?
If not, what is the proper way to activate the renv project if I run my scripts exclusively through a batch.cmd file?

title: Installing from fixed RSPM snapshots only
description:
When trying to install from a fixed RSPM snapshot only, {renv} updates the "Repository" field for some packages in `renv.lock` from RSPM to some CRAN refs, even though no CRAN repo is listed in `options(repo = )`.

I assume this happens due to cache linking? I.e. if the installed matched version requested was installed from CRAN on the local machine, it will be used instead of downloading the RSPM binary?

However, if a different user now calls `renv::restore()`, restoring will fail because there is no CRAN repo configured which `renv.lock` refers to.

It would be nice if only entries which are listed in `options(repo = )` were allowed to be valid entries for the "Repository" metadata field in `renv.lock`.


The following `.Rprofile` can be used to mimic this situation in a project:

```r
source("renv/activate.R")
options(renv.config.auto.snapshot = TRUE)
options(repos = structure(c(
  RSPM = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/cran/301"
)))
```

title: ##[error]Error: package was installed before R 4.0.0: please re-install it ; package caching after major R update
description:
I got this error after I updated R locally from 3.6.2 to 4.0.2, updated the project/renv files locally, and ran the project on a github runner with the updated R version. Didn't make any sense, because I updated all the packages and reinitialized the project.  

![restore-fail-r402-upgrade](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25374582/92415500-385f2700-f127-11ea-99b8-8e0cb682a2d7.png)

I tried different fixes and different packages would have that same error during restoration on the runner. It also seemed like the packages that were erroring were packages that needed building from source. Not sure if that's true or not.  

Finally, I figured out that the package caching github action was the cause. Removed the package caching step from the workflow yaml, and the run finished successfully. Good news is that my project doesn't fail with an updated R and updated packages on github actions, and I happened to update after RStudio package binaries became publicly available. Bad news is that I probably can't utilize package caching for at least a week. With gh action caches being deleted after a week of not being accessed, I (hopefully) should be able insert the caching step back into the workflow and not have an issue.  

Mainly just wanted to post this in case anyone else runs into this issue, but I also like to know if there's any way to speed up this up. I haven't been able to find any way to reset the cache through github, but my understanding is that the package caching is keyed by the hashes in the lockfile. Been looking through `renv` functions, and I was wondering if `rehash`  would create new hashes and essentially reset the github cache for me.

title: Workflow for restoring Bioconductor packages when updating to new R version
description:
I've read #244 and #495 and don't think either answer my question directly. I'm trying to update one of my projects to use the newest version of R. Naturally, the first console messages I see are:
```
* The project and lockfile are out of sync -- use `renv::status()` for more details.
Warning message:
Project requested R version '3.5.3' but '4.0.2' is currently being used 
Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘rmarkdown’
Error in loadNamespace(name) : there is no package called ‘rmarkdown’
```
The Bioconductor version for R-3.5 is 3.8, whereas the version for R-4.0 is 3.11. What I expect `renv::restore()` to do automatically is detect that I'm using R 4.0.2 and have a prompt to modify the following part of the lock file so that it uses the repositories from `BiocManager::repositories()` (in this case under 3.11).
```
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "3.5.3",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "BioCsoft",
        "URL": "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/bioc"
      },
      {
        "Name": "BioCann",
        "URL": "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/data/annotation"
      },
      {
        "Name": "BioCexp",
        "URL": "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/data/experiment"
      },
      {
        "Name": "BioCworkflows",
        "URL": "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/workflows"
      },
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cran.rstudio.com"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Bioconductor": {
    "Version": "3.8"
  },
```
But it doesn't, and I get the following error:
```
Error: failed to determine Bioconductor repositories
In addition: Warning messages:
1: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/data/annotation/bin/windows/contrib/4.0" 
2: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/workflows/bin/windows/contrib/4.0" 
3: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/data/experiment/bin/windows/contrib/4.0" 
4: could not retrieve available packages for url "https://bioconductor.org/packages/3.8/bioc/bin/windows/contrib/4.0" 
```
I know that the Bioconductor package versions depend on the Bioconductor version itself, but I was hoping there's a way to make this migration as smooth as possible and minimize the number of packages used in my `renv` that need to have an updated version. The Bioconductor packages will definitely change, and maybe some of the other ones depending on whether there are `Depends: R (>= 4.0)` fields, for example.

My current workflow:

1. Run `options(repos = BiocManager::repositories())`
2. Run `renv::install(vector_of_bioc_packages)` so that the release versions of the Bioconductor packages get installed
3. Manually `renv::restore(packages = package_name)` one by one until they are all restore. I can't just do `renv::restore()` since I'll get the error `Error: failed to determine Bioconductor repositories`, and I can't use `renv::snapshot()` to update the part of the lockfile that tells `renv` what version of bioconductor I'm using since it'll remove all the packages I have yet to restore.

Is there a better way to do this?

title: Add package license information to lockfile?

title: untar() can fail strangely on Windows causing confusing error message in `renv::restore()`
description:
I had a problem with `renv::restore()` because `untar()` used tar.exe from Git for Windows.
That version of tar needs paths like `/C/myfile.tar.gz` instead of `C:/myfile.tar.gz` and throws the error message

    /usr/bin/tar: Cannot connect to C: resolve failed

While the problem _can_ be fixed locally using `Sys.setenv(TAR = ...)` to another version of tar, the error is far from obvious, because `renv` stops with the error file not found (as it tries to download the same tarball from another repo which may not contain the package in question).

If `renv:::renv_archive_list_impl` used a specific version of `tar` (maybe installed with `renv::equip()`?) or used `tar = "internal"`, the error would not occur.

CMD tail -f /dev/null

zoo
```

title: renv::restore() fails to determine Bioconductor repositories
description:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to make a custom docker image, using a base rstudio image. My strategy is to call an R script within the my docker container that executes "renv::restore()". It correctly identifies which packages need to be updated, however it ends up giving me this error messsage:

```
Error: failed to determine Bioconductor repositories
Traceback (most recent calls last):
9: renv::restore()
8: renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile)
7: renv_retrieve(packages)
6: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
5: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
4: renv_scope_bioconductor()
3: renv_bioconductor_repos()
2: stopf("failed to determine Bioconductor repositories")
1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
Execution halted
```

My renv.lock files looks like this ( see  below ).
Any idea on what might be happening ?
Best,
-M.

title: During `renv::restore()`, installing packages aren't able to see previously-installed packages
description:
Within docker image which has its own compilation of R, `renv::install()` and `renv::restore()` will raise errors where packages to be installed can't see their already-installed dependencies. How should I go about debugging the error below? For example: ```R renv::install('gdata') # Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/# gdata_2.18.0.tar.gz' ... # OK [downloaded 1 Mb in 0.3 secs] # Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib/# gtools_3.8.2.tar.gz' ... # OK [downloaded 192.9 Kb in 0.2 secs] # Installing gtools [3.8.2] ... # OK [built from source] # Installing gdata [2.18.0] ... # FAILED # Error installing package 'gdata': # ================================= # # * installing *source* package ‘gdata’ ... # ** package ‘gdata’ successfully unpacked and MD5 # sums checked # ** using staged installation # ** R # ** data # ** inst # ** byte-compile and prepare package for lazy # loading # Error in loadNamespace(j <- i[[1L]], c(lib.loc, .# libPaths()), versionCheck = vI[[j]]) : # there is no package called ‘gtools’ # Calls: ... loadNamespace -> # withRestarts -> withOneRestart -> # doWithOneRestart # Execution halted #ERROR: lazy loading failed for package 'gdata' #* removing '/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/.renv/1/gdata' #Error: install of package 'gdata' failed #Traceback (most recent calls last): #14: renv::restore() #13: renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile) #12: renv_install(records, library) #11: renv_install_staged(records, library) #10: renv_install_default(records, library) # 9: handler(package, renv_install_impl(record)) # 8: renv_install_impl(record) # 7: withCallingHandlers#(renv_install_package_local(record), error = function(e) { # vwritef("\tFAILED") # writef(e$output) # }) # 6: renv_install_package_local(record) # 5: renv_install_package_local_impl(package, path, library) # 4: r_cmd_install(package, path, library) # 3: r_exec(package, args, "install") # 2: r_exec_error(package, output, label) # 1: stop(error) #Execution halted ``` Quick diagnostics: ``` renv version: 0.11.0 .Library: [1] "/usr/local/lib/R/library" .libPaths(): [1] "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/local/lib/R/library" $RENV_PATHS_CACHE: [1] "" renv:::renv_paths_cache(): [1] "/root/.local/share/renv/cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu" renv::settings$use.cache(): [1] TRUE repos: $CRAN [1] "https://cloud.r-project.org" $R_LIBS_USER: [1] "/foo/renv/library/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu:/tmp/Rtmpcgk3sE/renv-system-library" ```
The test script ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash mkdir /foo && cd $_ Rscript -e 'renv::consent(provided = T); renv::init()' # omitting doesn't change the outcome Rscript -e 'renv::install("gdata")' ```
script to print the diagnostics as well ```sh echo " ------ status ------ " Rscript -e 'renv::status()' echo printf '.Library: ' Rscript -e 'print(.Library)' printf '.libPaths(): ' Rscript -e 'print(.libPaths())' printf '$RENV_PATHS_CACHE: ' Rscript -e 'print(Sys.getenv("RENV_PATHS_CACHE"))' printf 'renv:::renv_paths_cache(): ' Rscript -e 'print(renv:::renv_paths_cache())' printf 'renv::settings$use.cache(): ' Rscript -e 'renv::settings$use.cache()' printf 'repos: ' Rscript -e ' lockfile <- renv:::renv_lockfile_read("renv.lock"); print(lockfile$R$Repositories) ' ```
`renv::restore()`ing with the equivalent `renv.lock` produces the same error.
equivalent renv.lock ```json { "R": { "Version": "3.6.3", "Repositories": [ { "Name": "CRAN", "URL": "https://cloud.r-project.org" } ] }, "Packages": { "gdata": { "Package": "gdata", "Version": "2.18.0", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Hash": "465ccb84427f5fe2c54f8620666db131" }, "gmodels": { "Package": "gmodels", "Version": "2.18.1", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Hash": "beb8ca96406a2828f25e49ab17001c39" }, "gtools": { "Package": "gtools", "Version": "3.8.2", "Source": "Repository", "Repository": "CRAN", "Hash": "0a749b4458d19a54acae93c64e3e7c85" } } } ```
Docker image code ``` ├── Dockerfile ├── ami.json # for packer └── scripts ├── 01_install_build_utils.sh ├── 02_install_r.sh # ... other installs unrelated to R └── 08_install_r_dependencies.sh # test.sh stands in for this script ```
Dockerfile ```dockerfile FROM ubuntu:20.04 ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive # note that each script guarantees that /tmp/ is empty, as is the apt cache COPY ./scripts/01_install_r.sh /tmp/install_r.sh RUN /tmp/install_r.sh COPY ./scripts/02_install_renv.sh /tmp/install_renv.sh RUN /tmp/install_renv.sh ```

title: purge() should also remove downloaded source files
description:
I tried to install a complicated package from source from CRAN, and it didn't work:

```
> renv::restore(packages = 'sf')
Retrieving 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/sf_0.9-5.tar.gz ...
	OK [downloaded 8 Mb in 0.2 secs]
# ERROR!
# lots of output from the source install complaining about sys reqs
```

Makes sense. Let me try to avoid the compilation and install a binary from RSPM instead:

```
> renv::restore('sf', repos = c(RSPM = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/latest"))
Retrieving 'https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/__linux__/xenial/latest/src/contrib/sf_0.9-5.tar.gz ...
	OK [file is up to date]
# Same error and lots of output from the source install
```

It seems that it did _not_ try to download the binary file, but rather reused the the source file from CRAN, and thus had the same errors.

To get it to work, I first tried `renv::purge('sf')`, but it didn't change anything. Eventually I figured out to manually:
```
unlink(file.path(renv::paths$root(), 'source', 'repository', 'sf'), recursive = T, force = T)
```

And then running `renv:restore` with RSPM actually downloaded and (successfully) installed the binary. 

(Sorry that the example here is more recreated from memory than an actual reprex, hopefully it's clear enough).

Should running `purge(<pkg>)` also clean up source files, such that it actually resets the global cache to a state where you had never installed `<pkg>` to begin with?

title: suggestion: mention that renv will not update lockfile unless installed package has explicit reference in repo
description:
Ran into a thing that confused me for a bit this week. I had a missing package inside an `renv` project that I installed with `renv::install`, which worked fine (I now had access to the package). But, when I ran `renv::status()` it said that my project was up to date with the lockfile, even though the new package was installed inside the project library but was not listed in the lockfile. After some trial and error, I realized that `renv` only noticed that the new package was there and should be updated in the lockfile if it was explicitly referenced somewhere in the repo (e.g. `library(newpackage)` or `newpackage::function()`). 

That makes sense in that you wouldn't want a lockfile filled with packages that aren't referenced anywhere in a repository. But, this behavior did confuse me for a while since the [documentation](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html#workflow) doesn't mention this behavior clearly, and just says that you should install / uninstall packages normally; I thought there was an error with `renv` so kept trying to reinstall it, reinstall the troublesome package etc, until I realized that I needed to install the package *and* reference it somewhere in the repository. 

If you agree with the need, I'm happy to submit a pull request to the documentation explaining this?

title: Feature request: snapshot a local document template package into the lockfile
description:
How can I snapshot a local document template package into the lockfile? I am using CRAN's `renv` 0.11.0 on Windows 10:

```
> sessionInfo()
R version 4.0.2 (2020-06-22)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 10 x64 (build 18362)

Matrix products: default

locale:
[1] LC_COLLATE=English_United States.1252  LC_CTYPE=English_United States.1252   
[3] LC_MONETARY=English_United States.1252 LC_NUMERIC=C                          
[5] LC_TIME=English_United States.1252    

attached base packages:
[1] stats     graphics  grDevices utils     datasets  methods   base     

loaded via a namespace (and not attached):
 [1] compiler_4.0.2  htmltools_0.5.0 tools_4.0.2     yaml_2.2.1      tinytex_0.24

[11] rlang_0.4.7     evaluate_0.14  
```

I created a local document template package by following Chester Imay's instructions [here](http://ismayc.github.io/ecots2k16/template_pkg/). The instructions worked fine except that you must also add a description line in template.yaml. There are complementary instructions from the `bookdown` manual [here](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown/document-templates.html).

According to the `renv` [FAQ](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/faq.html#why-isnt-my-package-being-snapshotted-into-the-lockfile), you encourage feasible feature requests, This feature request seems highly feasible to me given the importance and ease of using a local document template package. 

I could not figure out to snapshot the source version of the package, therefore I built a binary package version with:
`devtools::build(pkg = "basictemplate", binary = TRUE)`

I installed the binary template package, which by default is named `basictemplate_0.0.0.9000.zip`, with:
`renv::install("V://Testing//renv//local//basictemplate_0.0.0.9000.zip", type="binary")`

I can only snapshot the package with:
`renv::settings$snapshot.type("all")`
and then from the renv.lock copy-paste the basictemplate portion:
```
      "basictemplate": {
      "Package": "basictemplate",
      "Version": "0.0.0.9000",
      "Source": "Local",
      "Hash": "4edabaa51dfcdfe93edb5db45309c490"
    },
```
into the another renv.lock file. As an aside, should the "hash" change when I update the skeleton.Rmd? 

But this manual method is convoluted. Can you please provide a simpler and more automated way to snapshot a local document template package? It does not matter to me if the template package is source or binary but it has to be a local package (unless there is an easy other "private" solution based on the Chester Imay example data). Perhaps a new feature is not required, perhaps better documentation is sufficient.

title: Diagnose connectivity errors
description:

title: create lockfile from subset of package requirements
description:
For my workflow I try to disregard the global package library as soon as renv gets involved. As soon as a project switches to renv, it is tied to a stable RSPM snapshot and should get all packages from there, no matter what I might have installed in the global package library (which I tend to keep up-to-date-ish).

For users who have very few (or just one) project they're working on and who want to switch to renv, the current implementation (=consulting the local library) is better, because this avoid surprises when switching to renv. My objective is to minimize the set of package universes I'm using across all my projects, this is more important than exact replication of the current state of the package library. I might install GitHub packages on a case-by-case basis.

Ideally, for starting use of renv in a particular project, I'd do a variant of:

- `init(bare = TRUE, repos = c(RSPM = "https://packagemanager.rstudio.com/all/301"))` (bare-bones infrastructure with empty library and repo pointing to latest snapshot I've used in other projects)
- `record()` (auto-detect and record dependencies)
- `restore()` (to check if `restore()` will work on my colleague's machines)
- Run tests on the project (to check if any problems arise from potentially different package versions)

From time to time, I'd lift a project to a more recent RSPM snapshot:

- Edit `renv.lock`
- `update()`

Does this make sense?

_Originally posted by @krlmlr in https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/469#issuecomment-668976971_

title: `renv::update("renv")` gives invalid update instructions that result in cURL error 22 - Unprocessable entity
description:
I was updating renv today. This resulted in 

* Instructions to record a non-existent renv version in the lockfile
* An cURL error 22 / HTTP error 422 (Unprocessable entity) instead of a more helpful error message.

I used `update` to update renv. That installed the latest commit on the master branch which is `5831de0b` at the time of this writing.

That commit bumped the version number to 0.11.0-21, but no tag named like that exists in the repository, yet. 

This lead to invalid post-install instructions. After installing the new renv version and restarting R, I get the instructions to record renv in the version `0.11.0-21` in the lockfile. But this tag does not exist yet, and calling that command gives the error

```
# Error: failed to parse remote 'rstudio/renv@0.11.0-21' -- download failed [error code 22]
```

**Proposals**:
1. `renv::update()` should download the latest version that has a version tag, instead of the master branch
2. When a non-existent version is requested via the `renv::update("PACKAGE@VERSION")` syntax, the "Error 22"/"Unprocessable Entity"-Warning should be replaced by something more related to the missing version. 

Code and output below:

```
renv::update("renv")
# * Checking for updated packages ... Done!
# The following package(s) will be updated:
# 
# # GitHub =============================
# - renv   [rstudio/renv: f85f2f7b -> 5831de0b]
# 
# Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y
# Retrieving 'https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/renv/tarball/5831de0bd139ce4f7cb41c08111a24a601e6d983' ...
# 	OK [downloaded 333.5 Kb in 0.9 secs]
# Installing renv [0.11.0-21] ...
# 	OK [built from source]
# The following package(s) have been updated:
# 
# 	renv [installed version 0.11.0-21 != loaded version 0.9.3-4]
# 
# Consider restarting the R session and loading the newly-installed packages.
# 
# Warning message:
# GITHUB_PAT is unset. Updates may fail due to GitHub's API rate limit.
# 
# To increase your GitHub API rate limit:
# - Use `usethis::browse_github_pat()` to create a Personal Access Token (PAT).
# - Use `usethis::edit_r_environ()` and add the token as `GITHUB_PAT`. 
```

I then cleared my RStudio environment and restarted my R session. I got the following message from renv:

```
# * Project '~/' loaded. [renv 0.11.0-21]
# Warning message:
# renv 0.11.0-21 was loaded from project library, but renv 0.9.3-4 is recorded in lockfile.
# Use `renv::record("rstudio/renv@0.11.0-21")` to record this version in the lockfile.
# Use `renv::restore(packages = "renv")` to install renv 0.9.3-4 into the project library. 
# * The project may be out of sync -- use `renv::status()` for more details.
```

(My project is called `~` because my RStudio runs inside a singularity container that maps my project directory onto the folder `/proj` which is also set as the home directory. So in my case running renv in the home directory is intended.)

Following the instructions by renv got me an error: 
```
renv::record("rstudio/renv@0.11.0-21")
# Error: failed to parse remote 'rstudio/renv@0.11.0-21' -- download failed [error code 22]
# In addition: Warning messages:
# 1: curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 422 Unprocessable Entity

```

title: Separate libraries for different linux distributions
description:
There are some environments where the same directory might be shared by multiple linux operating systems (i.e. RSP with Launcher, where a session can be started on a Centos docker image or a Bionic docker image).

It would be nice if `renv` environments were more specific in their library storage than `x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library`, which is universal across many of the linux operating systems. Instead, it should have directories that correspond to distribution / etc. 

Even if this is not the "default," it would be nice if this were behavior that were possible as an "opt in."

Perhaps related to #253

title: Add a way to "recover" from the "wrong" repository
description:
I have had it happen several times where I:

- am restoring an environment and want to be sure to use binary packages from RSPM
- start `renv::restore()`
- see packages downloading from `cran.rstudio.com` or some other repo with no binaries
- CTRL+C to abort
- fix the repository URL
- restart `renv::restore()`
- `renv` _still_ installs the downloaded packages from the first pass (i.e. source bundles) and does not go back to retrieve them

It would be great if there were a way to gracefully "abort" and "re-restore" from a fresh state.

title: Add an easy way to switch python versions
description:
When multiple python virtualenvs have been associated with an renv environment, it would be ideal to be able to 

- list the python virtualenvs
- easily switch between them

title: option to use system-installed R packages during `init`
description:
When using `renv::hydrate` we can use already downloaded/built local packages and this is much faster (in our network and in particular with our firewalls and virus checkers) than downloading new copies.

Is there a way to get `renv::init` (and other methods?) to use local packages too? This would have significant speed benefits for us (which would lead to much better perceived usability by users)

As with other issues, we'd be happy to investigate this further, including helping with PRs - but wanted to discuss first... especially as we know there may already be options we just haven't seen.

Thanks

 )
