Happy to assist with PRs on this - but thought we'd start with an issue....

title: CI vignette: add Bitbucket, review steps
description:
It may be helpful to some to include in the CI vignette an example for [bitbucket pipelines](https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/get-started-with-bitbucket-pipelines/).

Here's a prototype similar to the ones provided for other services:

```
pipelines:
  default:
    - step:
        caches:
          - renvlib
          - renvcache
        script:
          - Rscript -e "if (!requireNamespace('renv', quietly = TRUE)) install.packages('renv')"
          - Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
          - [your next actions here]

definitions:
  caches:
    renvlib: renv/library
    renvcache: ~/.local/share/renv
```

In actual pipelines that I've written, however, I skipped the `if (!requireNamespace('renv', quietly = TRUE)) install.packages('renv')` step which you have as an example in all of them. Somewhat related to our discussion regarding the collaboration vignette (#366 ), it seems to me that:

- if you checked in `.Rprofile` and `renv/activate.R` , the `if` will always be FALSE, because that will bootstrap everything
- if you *didn't* check those in, then `renv` won't be active yet, so while things may work, you'll be targeting your normal `.libPaths()[[1]]` instead of `renv/library` (right?)

This was a little confusing to me.

title: Feature request: method to check library vs lockfile, regardless of project
description:
My lockfile has packages I want even though they aren't obvious dependencies of my project. This means that if I turn on the `synchronized.check`, I'll always get:
```
* The project and lockfile are out of sync -- use `renv::status()` for more details.
```
even if the **library** and **lockfile** are in sync:
```
> renv::status()
The following package(s) are no longer used in this project:
                _
  KernSmooth      [2.23-17]
   . . . # but no actual mismatches

> renv::restore()
* The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.
```

That's fine in of itself. The option is now FALSE by default anyway. And maybe I should have used some non-default snapshot type that I haven't bothered to figure out. But what I would really like, and what seems useful anyway, is an option to check if the **library** and **lockfile** are in sync, ideally on load, but without attempting to actually restore. 

Basically:
- just activating `renv` (i.e., `source('renv/activate.R')`) won't run `renv::restore()` or otherwise guarantee that my project library is in line with the lockfile
- I don't necessarily want to force myself or my team to run `restore()` at load, e.g. by adding `renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)` to the `.Rprofile` right after `source(renv/activate.R)`
- But I do want to KNOW if I probably need to run `renv::restore()`, ideally via an automatic check at load

An option similar to `synchronized.check` could work, but even wrapping some of the checks that happen inside `renv::restore()` into its own exported function so that I can check myself would be helpful, e.g. I could manually make my .Rprofile something like:
```
source('renv/activate.R')
if (renv::needs_restore()) { # doesn't seem to be an easy way to do this yet
  message("Warning: the library is out of sync with the lockfile. You may need to run renv::restore()")
}
```

```
Error: package 'dropletUtils' is not available
Traceback (most recent calls last):
8: install.packages("dropletUtils")
7: install(pkgs)
6: renv_retrieve(packages)
5: handler(package, renv_retrieve_impl(package))
4: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
3: renv_available_packages_latest(record$Package)
2: stopf("package '%s' is not available", package)
1: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
```
This appears to be because `renv::install()` does not automatically configure the package repositories as `biocLite` or `BiocManager::install()` do.

I haven't tried to rehydrate a `renv` containing a Bioconductor package yet, but I wonder if this would also run into similar problems.

I was able to work around this by first installing `BiocManager` and then running `options(repos = BiocManager::repositories())` as suggested in #81.

Is it reasonable to implement a solution where the repositories are configured automatically when a Bioconductor package install is attempted?  As a newer user of `renv`, when the documentation stated it supported installing from Bioconductor, I was confused when `renv::install()` failed and I had to search for a workarround.

title: Restore should consider uncached system/user library packages
description:
When initializing an renv environment in a fresh R setup, `hydrate` recycles packages from e.g. user or system libraries (i.e. puts them to the cache). This seems particular useful with heavily prepackaged Docker images such as [rocker/tidyverse](https://hub.docker.com/r/rocker/tidyverse/). However, these packages are reported with CRAN sources in the lock file, as mentioned [here](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/257).

So when restoring the renv in another fresh R setup (same conditions and version, e.g. by using the same Docker image), all locked packages will be installed from CRAN. Although many of them could have been recycled from the local libraries again, which would save time and data transfer volume. This kind of defeats the purpose of more extended prepackaged Docker images.

Would it be possible for `restore` to draw packages from local sources first (if version/hashes match) similar to as `hydrate` does? Or to have a function that puts local packages into the cache which could be run before `restore`? 

My current workaround is to use `hydrate` to populate the cache with local packages (but which then already downloads everything else, not necessarily in the finally required version) and then `restore` to make sure each package is in the right version. But this is also redundant and not time and data transfer friendly.

title: hydrate uses cache, install doesn't
description:
Not sure if this is by design and I'm missing something, or whether this is a bug, but it appears that `hydrate` uses the local cache whereas `install` doesn't.

To explain I'll describe how I noticed this. Normally I'll write a script/Rmarkdown etc first, and that will have a call such as `library(Rcpp)`. I then use `hydrate` to pull `Rcpp` into the project library before actually running the code, it all works perfectly and picks up the `Rcpp` that exists in the local `renv` cache.

However, if I try to use `install` first instead, then it completely ignores the cache and tries to download `Rcpp`. I only noticed this because of the downloading issue on Windows behind corporate proxy, so I got an error that the package is not available (and that the relevant urls aren't) rather than it just being downloaded instead. But if the package is already in my local cache, I don't believe it should even be trying to download the package - so that shouldn't be an issue unless I'm trying to install something completely new.

The problem is a nuisance at the moment (and I'm pretty sure I didn't have this before 0.11.0 - but I can't remember 100 %) is that I can't open a new notebook in a new project. When I do RStudio warns some packages are needed, then it tries to install them but fails. If I click don't install (so I could manually do them after) it just fails outright, so it's not like I can even open a new notebook and then tell `hydrate` to go do it instead. 

Ok so I can manually fudge a way to get `hydrate` to pull them in and/or fix the download/proxy issue, but I shouldn't really need to - I think - because these packages are all in the cache and it should pull the relevant ones in for the notebook. Like I said, I never noticed this problem before so it seems like the downloading/cache issues are both new to me.

Output from some commands that might help:

```
> renv:::renv_paths_cache()
[1] "C:/Users/XXX/AppData/Local/renv/cache/v5/R-4.0/x86_64-w64-mingw32"

> .Library
[1] "C:\\Users\\XXX\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\RtmpULev1w/renv-system-library"

> .libPaths()
[1] "C:/ProjectName/renv/library/R-4.0/x86_64-w64-mingw32" "C:/Users/XXX/AppData/Local/Temp/RtmpULev1w/renv-system-library" 
```

Edit: I checked the `use.cache` option and it was `NULL`, so changed it and then re-initialised, but that didn't change anything:

```
> getOption("renv.settings.use.cache")
NULL
> options("renv.settings.use.cache" = TRUE)
```

Edit 2: I can get around this by removing `renv` from the project, opening a notebook, then re-introducing `renv`, then `hydrate` will pull (almost) everything required. Except it doesn't pull in `Rcpp` or `rprojroot` automatically so I have to make a temporary script with a `library` call for those.

Weirdly, if I remove that script and then use `clean` I get the following packages listed as unusused, first `translations` then:

```
backports, Rcpp, renv, rprojroot
```

So something really weird is going on as `renv` thinks it doesn't need itself, plus those other packages which are needed to use a notebook - it even pulled in `backports` when I hydrated after saving a notebook template! I'm sure this was never an issue with previous versions and (I think) I haven't done something really dumb recently - though I can't swear to it!

title: Use renv for private GitLab package on local server
description:
Hi there. Following up on a question I [posted on Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62772833/use-renv-for-private-gitlab-package/62803742?noredirect=1#comment111092291_62803742): I'd like to use `renv` to manage some packages hosted on a private local GitLab account. By local I mean hosted on a local server with GitLab on. I use RStudio Server Pro to develop packages and other users can install packages from GitLab by running:

`devtools::install_git( 
  url = "http://my-gitlab-server/r-projects/package.git",
  credentials = git2r::cred_user_pass("user", "pass")
)`

When I use `renv::init()` the package source is unknown and after help from Kevin Ushey (KU) the `DESCRIPTION` file of the package I'm trying to install as `RemoteType: git2r`. Following this I tried to use `renv::install()` to install the package after saving a `GITLAB_PAT` in a `.Renviron` file in the project root folder. I got the error:

`download failed [error code 22]`

I'm not sure how to use `renv::install` correctly in this scenario. KU suggested to try `renv::install("gitlab::user/project")` but I'm not sure this makes sense when the package is hosted on `http://my-gitlab-server`. I did try various combinations of strings to install:

- `renv::install("gitlab::user/project")`
- `renv::install("gitlab::http://my-gitlab-server/r-projects/package.git")`
- `renv::install("gitlab::my-gitlab-server/r-projects/package.git")`
- etc.

But all resulted in the same error and KU suggested raising an issue. Perhaps there is a better or different way to go about this?

title: Libraries not available after renv::init
description:
Suppose I create a new R project, and do renv::init() to record the state of the packages. Afterwards, if I type library(devtools) in the R console, I get an error saying there is no such library. library(devtools) works fine before renv::init()

This is sort of a big deal, because I have to use devtools::install_version in order to install an older version of a library.

title: Feature Request: Allow direct query of the package dependency graph
description:
When `renv` discovers dependencies, it does so by searching the source code for implicit dependencies, and the description for implicit dependencies. 

If I have this correctly (Correct me if I'm wrong):

It then recursively searches through its dependencies, using their DESCRIPTIONs to build a graph (or tree) of all of its required dependencies.

When this traversal is done, it uses it for whatever purpose we've asked it to (initializing the project, cleaning out unused deps, reporting the status, whatever). 

I am wondering if we could have a user-side function that allows us to access this dependency graph, ideally in a format that may be consumed by existing network graph tools such as [visNetwork](https://github.com/datastorm-open/visNetwork), [igraph](http://igraph.org/r/) , or whatever other network graph tools exist. 

A few solutions appear to be floating around for graphing this, like miniCran, pkggraph, but a lot of them seem to be highly CRAN focussed, and limited in what they can actually do.

description:
For example, `rearthdata` requires `rnaturalearthhires` for some tasks, which is typically installed from rOpenSci with `install.packages("rnaturalearthhires", repos = "http://packages.ropensci.org", type = "source")`, but if I use `install.packages` instead of `renv::install`, `renv::snapshot` seems unable to see the library.

Perhaps related: #449, concerning the installation of repositories from BitBucket.

title: hydrate() without updating packages
description:
Not sure if I'm missing something obvious, but it seems to me there's no way to `hydrate()` a project without also updating packages from the main R library. I'll try to expand on that explanation as it might not be clear.

Let's say I am working on a project using renv for package management. I then switch to a non-project R session, do some basic stuff, update some packages (ones which happen to be used in the project I was working on), then go back to the project.

Now, let's say I now need some new packages in the project so write the necessary code and then call `hydrate()` to get them pulled in from my main R library. The problem is, when I do this, `hydrate()` also updates the existing packages in my project library with the updates from my main R library - which I might not want to do.

I realise I could avoid this by bringing in the new packages to the project using `renv::install()` instead, but then I have to manually type them out, whereas `hydrate()` is just so bloody convenient!

Unless I'm missing something, it would be great to include an option such as `hydrate(update = FALSE)` to only bring in new packages and avoid pulling in the updates from the main R library for other packages used.

Hopefully that makes sense??

title: Replace references to deprecated flag `--slave` with `-s` or `--no-echo`
description:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/3cb0f1516d73b0b31596484a8cb54ee0e53282c8/R/session.R#L10

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/9fbf93e7023679fc2f6ae7bdb74e6cee565b1702/tests/testthat/test-activate.R#L21

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/4e91e2f7c039f631dbce8bc565c3286c1e979baa/R/repos.R#L32

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/8216d005e5ce24f5254b03f95345041681c9c789/tests/testthat/test-profiles.R#L23

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/31073ae174e828c0c6be31b66b7532216073df86/R/run.R#L92

https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/3e92b4fc2278bf969505c94bb68a266f1eb964ad/vignettes/docker.Rmd#L136

From R 4.0.1 forward, `--slave` is deprecated: https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/NEWS.html

https://github.com/wch/r-source/commit/f1ff49e74593341c74c20de9517f31a22c8bcb04

`-s` is an undocumented alias for the flag formerly `--slave` now `--no-echo` and thus ensures backwards compatibility. Alternatively, going forward, we could trap for the R version to be called and choose `-s` or `--no-echo` as needed.

title: Docker with renv using rocker/rstudio
description:
Hi, I was following the best practices for docker with renv from [here](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/docker.html#running-docker-containers-with-renv). I am not sure what I'm doing wrong but it does not seem that I am able to use the rocker/rstudio image in order to use this best practice for running containers. Here is some supporting information:

- Docker version 19.03.8, build afacb8b
- Dockerfile for building an image using **renv**
```
FROM rocker/rstudio:3.6.3-ubuntu18.04
RUN apt-get upgrade -y && \
apt-get update -y && \
apt-get install -y tzdata
RUN R -e 'install.packages("remotes")'
RUN R -e "remotes::install_github('rstudio/renv@0.10.0-45')"
```
- Docker run command
```
docker run -d --rm -it --name renv `
-e ROOT=TRUE `
-e DISABLE_AUTH=TRUE `
-e RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/renv/cache `
-p 8787:8787 `
-v C:\Users\other\docker\renv\cache:/renv/cache `
renv:latest
```

Some issues I tried to work through with no luck

1. The environment variable **RENV_PATHS_CACHE** does not pass through to Rstudio
- In a shell **outside of RStudio** I am able to run `printenv` and view the env var, but using `Sys.getenv()` in Rstudio console the variable does not get picked up. Additionally, if I use the Terminal within Rstudio and run `printenv` I am unable to see the variable as *rstudio* user or as *root*.
- Manually executing `Sys.setenv(RENV_PATHS_CACHE = /renv/cache)` has worked, but again, its manual

2. I'm unable to run `renv::restore()` as a post-command for the run command above
- I think this is because of how the base image of rocker/rstudio is designed
- I was able to begin running post-commands once I added `ENTRYPOINT ['R']` as the last command to Dockerfile, but then I have to manually run `/init` which kickstarts Rstudio



Thanks for your help.

title: Temporarily disabling search for dependencies
description:
Can there be an option to temporarily disabling dependencies search at startup and while installing new packages? I am looking for an option that disables all {renv} tests at startup, but sets the link to the internal {renv} libraries.  
 
I am working with big projects with multiple files to search in. I would like to avoid {renv} to search for dependencies each time I add a new package and each time I open a new session with `system()`.  

Indeed, the main problem is while using {future}. Setting a `mulitprocess` plan takes forever to setup all separate processes. I would like to be able to add an option in the `.Rprofile` so that {renv} only sets up the internal `.libPaths` with the correct symlink to the cache and nothing else.

title: `files` option to `renv::snaphsot()` to indicate which files to scan for dependencies.
description:
My use case is to generate a new lock file with a small subset of packages needed for production to be used in production docker. Something like `renv::snapshot(files = "init.R", lockfile = "docker/production/renv.lock")`. Basically as a simple alternative to #253. 

Alternatively, I thought I could use  `dependencies.R` with snapshot type `explicit`, but it's currently ignored. 

I think it would be good to allow `dependencies.R` to be used as alternative to `DESCRIPTION` regardless. First, to avoid duplicating `library(xyz)` calls in a non-package project.  Second, to potentially avoid confusing some other tools which might assume that it's a package project just based on the presence of the DESCRIPTION file.

title: devtools::check() don't find dependencies attached by imported ones
description:
## Preamble

I need to use `{Hmisc}` into a package I am developing.

Because I use packages as companions for analyses, I am developing those packages using `{renv}` too for reproducibility (including a `.Buildignore`d `analyses/` folder). 

I think that the real main cause of the issue remains in the Hmisc package (which attach other packages on load) on the other hand, the problem happens when using `{renv}` only. 

## General description of the Issue


description:
Hi, thanks for renv! I'm seeing an issue when trying to migrate from Packrat. Versions are different between lockfiles:

```r
renv::migrate(packrat="lockfile")
```

title: Rtools40
description:
Some of the packages in my lock file require compilation (I could have avoided it during renv::init() I guess) and Rtools is needed for it. I did not know that R4.0.0 requires a new version of Rtools so some packages could not be compiled and the whole restore() process just stopped with a simple error message like "package could not be complied".
Would it make sense to first check whether Rtools is needed, and if yes, to check whether it is installed?

title: Unable to install non-default branch of package from GitLab
description:
Installing packages from GitLab always returns the version on the default branch, regardless of whether you specify a different branch. 

I believe the problem is caused by this line:
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/3c86e40c8e09f2e26fcfae3c953a60ac96c29aec/R/retrieve.R#L220

For packages from GitLab, `record$RemoteSha` is always `NULL`. 

Substituting `record$RemoteSha` with `record$RemoteRef` resolves the issue.

title: Default to PPM on Linux
description:
Similar to how renv uses MRAN to provide historical binaries for Mac and Windows, now that RSPM is publicly available at packagemanager.rstudio.com it should be possible:

1. For renv to default to PPM for installing binaries on Linux for new package installs during init, hydrate, or install
2. For renv to default to PPM for installing binaries on Linux for historical packages during restore

One easy way to do this might simply be to prefer packagemanager.rstudio.com over cran.rstudio.com automatically, with an opt-out setting. The previous renv+RSPM work will ensure that the appropriate binary suffix is added to the repo URL, while maintaining a cross platform compatible repo URL in the lock file. 

 The only downside to be aware of is that sometimes PPM will lag CRAN on brand new package releases, up to a few days.

title: Renv outputs to stdout instead of stderr
description:
I have noticed that recent renv 10.0 started printing to stdout instead of stderr. 

```
* Project '/opt/program' loaded. [renv 0.10.0]
```

I don't think this is ok. Output of the program is normally consumed by other tools, so renv messages get intermingled with the program output. `message` or `warning` should be used instead.

title: On trusty, renv tries to use RSPM binaries and fails
description:
On trusty, `renv` tries to be smart and use the RSPM binary URL. However, it fails in the URL construction for some reason. It is also worth noting that RSPM does not have support for "trusty" here, even if the URL was created properly.

The same is probably true for Ubuntu 20.04 or other unsupported linux variants, I would suspect, but support for that is on the way, at least.
```
> options("repos" = c(RSPM = "http://path/all/latest"))
> install.packages(c("vctrs", "rlang"))
Error: package 'vctrs' is not available
In addition: Warning message:
could not retrieve available packages for url 'http://path/all/__linux__//latest/src/contrib'
```

title: Following XDG_CACHE_HOME specification
description:
Currently, on Linux, `renv` uses the environment variable `XDG_DATA_HOME` for setting the `renv` global storage path. Unless the `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` environment variable is set, it seems that the default is to store the cache in the `$RENV_PATHS_ROOT/renv/cache`, which ultimately uses `$XDG_DATA_HOME/renv/cache` (if that variable is set).

For completeness and simplicity of configuration, it would be nice if you could use `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` to set the location of the cache directory when `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` is not set.

In any case, thanks for maintaining this great package! It's made analyses done in R much more reproducible 😄.

Here's the full [XDG specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir-spec/basedir-spec-latest.html) for anyone who is interested.

title: preserve lockfile records for other OS during snapshot
description: If you're working with `renv` on Windows, and are snapshotting within a project that contains a record for e.g. `doMC` (only available for Unix), the existing record should be preserved as-is and not removed (at least by default).

title: If I delete my local cache (c:/users/d/appdata/local/renv) then strange things happen
description:
I tried adding renv to an existing project (`renv::init()` on an existing project) and checked it into git. I wanted to try to mimic what would happen to a different person on a different machine, so I deleted my project locally, re-cloned from git (which means I didn't have the `renv/library/` anymore), deleted the local cache, and tried using renv. 

Things did not work well. I know we're not expected to delete that folder, but the problems I ran into seem like they shouldn't happen.

When I ran `renv::init()` it told me that this project already has a lock file and asked me what to do. So I thought "ok, maybe I need to use `restore()` instead of `init()`. So to make sure I get a fresh start, I again deleted the local cache and again deleted the project locally and again re-cloned from git.

Now I ran `renv::restore()`. I received the "Welcome to renv! It looks like this is your first time..." message, which makes sense since I deleted the cache. When I said "y" I want to proceed, I got a message 

```
The library is already synchronized with the lockfile.
```

Strange. I looked inside `renv/library/` and the only package in there was `renv`. So it did not work. After restarting my RStudio session and again running `renv::restore()`, now it actually attempted to install the packages locally.

Also, I kept running into this issue https://github.com/rstudio/rstudio/issues/6799

I know I'm doing things I shouldn't be doing 🙈

title: init() on an initialized project: allow an option to "cancel"
description:
When wanting to update your local library, it's not unreasonable to accidentally call `init()` instead of `restore()`

```
> renv::init()
This project already has a lockfile. What would you like to do? 

1: Restore the project from the lockfile.
2: Discard the lockfile and re-initialize the project.
3: Activate the project without snapshotting or installing any packages.
```

There should be an additional option "4: Cancel" to exit this

title: A way to "check out repository versions"
description:
The use case here is that (even using `renv`), the project library can be an unexpected mashup of random GitHub versions, CRAN versions, etc. of packages.

I would like a way to `renv::checkout_repo()` or something where all of my packages either (1) have the latest version retrieved from my repository and installed or (2) stay the way they are (i.e. if not found on CRAN) and are notified about. (maybe an option to throw these packages out?)

This is especially useful when using frozen repositories (i.e. RSPM) and checking out a point in time, or when trying to emulate the build environment for CI (which typically installs the latest from a repository into a clean environment). `renv::update()` seems to get close here, but it reaches out often to git repositories.

One noteworthy point here is that I want to be careful to (1) use the `renv` cache if I have the version already, (2) populate the `renv` cache if I don't.

This would have the added benefit of being able to "move from frozen repository to frozen repository within RSPM" in a reliable way.

title: Different linux distros/versions are not distinguished in the cache
description:
I am trying to migrate my project across to singularity containers on my work's HPC.

I am running R from a singuarity container.

When running singularity from our HPC, the host system's `/home` , and `/project` directories are mounted to the container.

My work's HPC is Centos 6.9, the container image is Ubuntu 16.04 (Newest version of Ubuntu that the HPC's kernel can run). 

In the past, to set the path to `renv::cache`, I would set the following in `~/.Renviron`: 

```
RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/project/STEMI/software/renv/cache
```

# The problem

My problem is this:

When I attempt to run some package (For example here's something that uses igraph), I run into errors like this:

```
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :  unable to load shared object '/project/RDS-FHS-STEMI-RW/software/renv/cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/igraph/1.2.4.2/fffa635f747cd07ffc56bc13a23701e4/igraph/libs/igraph.so':
   libRlapack.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory 
```

Digging into this, I perform the following from within both the host and container


```r
# HOST
renv:::renv_paths_cache()

#> [1] "/project/RDS-FHS-STEMI-RW/software/renv/cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"

La_library()

#> [1] "/usr/local/R/3.6.3/lib64/R/lib/libRlapack.so"
```

```r
# CONTAINER
renv:::renv_paths_cache()

#> [1] "/project/RDS-FHS-STEMI-RW/software/renv/cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu"

La_library()
#> [1] "/usr/lib/lapack/liblapack.so.3.6.0" 
```

So what I'm seeing is that both container and host are looking at the same cache - I'd be okay with that, except that they also can't really distinguish whose system is whose, and packages built on the HPC host system are going to reference shared objects dependendant on the host systems environment. 

The following article explains how to achieve exactly the same setup I already have, but with Docker:
https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/docker.html#running-docker-containers-with-renv 

You state:

> Note that the platform and R version in use are appended to the requested cache directory. This ensures that a single directory can act a base of cached packages for multiple different platforms and R versions.

The thing is- Ubuntu 16.04 and Centos 6.9 (Legacy HPC Magic Edition) are VERY different platforms, and they should probably not share any cache whatsoever - 

That being said, I would like my container to leverage the cache, and I'd still like my host system to be able to do the same, if possible.

How can I trick, force, or politely ask renv to use a different cache when in my container?

title: Improve `.gitignore` handling
description:
Hello everyone,

While trying to apply `renv` to some of my projects, I ran into an issue when invoking `renv::init()` in one of them. Surprisingly, the automatic dependency discovery implemented in `renv::dependencies()` did not work correctly. After deleting file after file to identify the cause of the problem and resolve the complications, I came across [this section](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/dependencies.html#ignoring-files) in the `renv::dependencies` documentation dealing with automatically skipped scripts occurring in `.gitignore` files. As it seems, `renv` does not correctly process patterns for explicitly included files (marked by `!`), which are tracked by `git`.

Below is a shell script, which shows the difference between a failed dependency discovery and a correctly initialized project. To run the script only renv is required to be installed. I tested both the current `renv` release on CRAN and the up-to-date GitHub master branch - both resulting in the same result.

Workaround for now would be not to rely on `!` in `.gitignore`files though I doubt that this is intended behaviour.

Hope this helps for implementing a fix 😃 Love the package already 👍

Greetings

Christian

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env sh

# renv does not discover dependencies in script.R
mkdir renv-failing
cat > renv-failing/script.R <<EOF
library(tidyverse)
EOF
cat > renv-failing/.gitignore <<EOF
# also fails for *.R /* /*.R
*
!script.R
EOF
cd renv-failing
Rscript -e 'renv::init()'
cd ..

# renv correctly discovers all dependencies
mkdir renv-working
cat > renv-working/script.R <<EOF
library(tidyverse)
EOF
cd renv-working
Rscript -e 'renv::init()'
cd ..
```

title: load external package that is in global library
description:
Hi, 

this could relate to #132 but I believe it is an adjacent use case. 

## Context

We use RStudio Server Pro in our company where I configured some internal R packages to connect to our internal DB. Theses packages are only available inside these servers and can't be installed by the user. They are installed in a server-wide library with other strandard packages. That allow us to provide specific packages versions for new users. (following something similary to [shared baselines strategy](https://environments.rstudio.com/shared.html)). 

## Issue

The issue we encountered with our users is that they can't use renv with a project that is using one of these specific internal packages. It is unlucky because renv has proven to be useful for collaboration and deployment inside the company where these packages are always available. 

In packrat, there was an option called [`external.packages`](https://rstudio.github.io/packrat/commands.html#externalpackages) that allow to have a project external package loaded. I believe this is used also [in RStudio Connect: to have external packages for content](https://docs.rstudio.com/connect/admin/r/package-management/#external-package-installation)
I don't think there is such an option already in renv. Or Maybe I missed it...

## Current situation 

Currently the workaround is to use `external.librairies` [settings](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/settings.html) but we get all the drawbacks described only to have access to one packages. In this situations the renv project get access to all the packages.

We could also isolate in a specific  library path to only provide access to those to renv. Seems a bit tedious to do r-admin stuff to solve this. 

Otherwise, I guess we could deploy our internal package directly into the global renv cache we set up on the servers so that they are available for other without any installation. Obviously this would work only if this global cache is used. And this would work only for packages that don't require specific access right. yes, we have also internal packages that are deployed in specific library path with linux access right. I guess for those, the `external.libraries` setting would work just fine. 

## Follow-up

What could be the best way to handle this in your opinion ? 
Is something like `external.packages` considered for renv ? 
Is there any other similar use case out there ? 

Thank you.

title: How to install binaries from local sources on Linux (RcppParallel_5.0.0.tgz not being detected)

Hi Kevin et al, 
I've been trying to install some packages whose dependency trees include RcppParallel on my work's HPC. 

# Overview

After hitting a tonne of compilation issues bc of TBB, it seemed like I'd have to somehow just remove the dependency.
Fortunately, it turns out that for the most recent evironment module version of R, `R/3.6.3`, the sysadmins have actually built TBB for us. 

I searched for my system's RcppParallel install, living here: `/usr/local/R/3.6.3/lib64/R/library/RcppParallel` , and I was able to copy it into `~/extlib`, and point `renv::settings$external_libraries()` at `~/extlib`. 

This appeared to have given me access to `RcppParallel` from within my projects, but I don't particularly relish the thought of having to maintain and document such a setup in order for the project to function portably.

When i try to `restore()` it looks like renv will still prefer a project local install for `RcppParallel` from CRAN, so I'd probably have to ignore the package or something. 

# Current Problem

I thought a more elegant solution might be to use tar this static copy of the library, and set up [Local Sources](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/local-sources.html) in order to force R to install the local binary if working from the HPC, but in other environments use CRAN. 

So far this doesn't appear to be working, and renv seems to default to fetching a source tarball from cran.

# Reprex

## In R

```r
renv:::renv_paths_local()
#> [1] "/home/mstr3336/.local/share/renv/local"
renv::settings$external.libraries()
#> character(0)
```

## Bash

```bash
cd ~/.local/share/renv/local
ls
```
```
RcppParallel
```
```bash
 ls RcppParallel/
```
```
RcppParallel_5.0.0.tgz
```

title: Docker FAQ notes
description:
I read with interest the [FAQ](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/docker.html) on using `renv` with Docker, perhaps I should've read it before going through what I've gone through!

In our case one of the objectives in our use of Docker is to get a repeatable build process.  There  are obvious advantages in locking your operating system, R itself and the R packages to defined versions.  Assuming those things are stable then you can change your code and get a consistency in the behavior of the container as you, test fix bugs or make other improvements.

We do things a little different than is noted in your FAQ, our `Dockerfile` uses a multi-stage build such that we do the build work in one container which functionally takes a base OS (containing R) copies our `renv`-enabled app into it and runs `renv::restore()` on it.  `renv` will bootstrap itself to the version in the lockfile: that is useful behavior.  After the restore we run `renv::settings$use.cache(FALSE)` to copy the global cache into the local project.  There is probably a different way to do this but I don't believe that a global cache has much of a benefit in this case, I can't see the point in holding all the packages outside of the project folder in a Docker container.

Once the build container has done that we copy the app from the build container into a new one, add an entry point and that becomes our actual container which does the work.

There are downsides to this approach: you have to do a lot of work - and consume a lot of time - before you can figure out if you've got a working container.

Interested in any comments on this.

title: Custom location of renv/library folder
description:
First of, nice package!

I am trying to use renv in combination with package development (under Windows) to share package configurations among developers, but due to the renv/library folder, commands like

As a workaround, I can clone my git repo (which does not contain renv/library) somewhere else to check & build it. So to save this step, renv would require an option to put the renv/library folder somewhere else, e.g. just outside the package root.
Sorry, if that is already possible, but I could not find anything in the docs to make renv work like this.

Thanks!
Roman

```r
pkgs <- list.files(.libPaths()[1], full.names = TRUE)

}
```

title: Use of renv without .Rprofile on startup
description:
I am using renv in a cluster environment and as a result want to find a way to have `renv` bootstrap itself without the use of a `.Rprofile` file since the initialization of R will not be occurring in the project directory nor will it always be by the same user.

So far my solution has been to call either `renv::activate("/path/to/renv/lib")` or `renv::load("/path/to/renv/lib")` at the beginning of the script that is using the `renv` library.  I worry though that doing this after R's normal startup process (where default packages are attached) might cause some issues with system versions of packages being loaded  during startup rather than the`renv` library version of those packages.

Is there a better way to do this, or does `renv` really need to be loaded via `.Rprofile` in order to function appropriately?

description: Within the 'Collaborating with renv' article, it briefly mentions using either init() or restore() to automatically install all required packages. Please could the article clarify whether there is a difference in behaviour in this situation. For example, if calling init(), will renv regenerate the infrastructure? (This is precisely what I don't want since I've added to the project .Rprofile file and I don't want it overwritten by a re-initialisation).

title: better heuristics in RSPM detection?
description:
Right now, `renv` attempts to automatically detect RSPM repository URLs, and transform source URLs to binary URLs on Linux as appropriate. However, I'm not sure if `renv` can do this automagically and always correctly.

The main challenge here is, given a repository URL, `renv` needs to try and determine if it refers to an RSPM repository. There are some heuristics:

- Does this have the format `<url>/<name>/<id>`? If so, we might be able to infer this is RSPM. Can we expect that all RSPM URLs will have this format? Do we need to worry about proxies that subvert this format in some way?

- Does that repository respond to the `<url>/__api__/status` endpoint? (Note: this also runs into issues with proxies subverting the format above)

Ultimately though, it seems like if we can't get this right all the time then users might need some way of telling `renv` that "yes, you should treat this like an RSPM repository".

@slopp, what are your thoughts?

title: binary downloads from RSPM should go to separate folder
description:
Right now, packages downloaded from a CRAN repository get downloaded to a common location, e.g.

```
~/.local/share/renv/<type>/repository
```

However, because binaries served from RSPM are binary packages masquerading as source packages, they end up with `<type> = "source"` above. They should be downloaded to a separate `binary` location.

title: renv::init() uses local library package version
description:
I'm not sure there is anything to be done here, but this was counter-intuitive to me. I just kept thinking "but I've installed 0.9.3...".

## Steps to reproduce
Install an older version of renv from Github in your user library. Create a new project. Run `renv::init()`. As expected, it will use the version from your library. Run `renv::upgrade()` in the the project. It now uses 0.9.3. Now, delete all renv related files, and run `renv::init()`. You're back to the older Github version. That's because it's using the version from the user library.

## Expected behavior
I guess I'd like `renv::upgrade()` to ask me if I'd also like to update my user library or something. Maybe `renv::init()` checks if later versions are available on CRAN and prompts. In my mind, if I'm starting a new project, I always want to use the latest version of renv (I know others may not be in agree on this point).

Like I said, not sure there's anything to be done, but it took me a few minutes to get it sorted out. This seems like it'll be less and less of an issue as renv matures and renv upgrade frequency decreases.

Edit: With RStudio 1.3, the outdated version of renv is detected in the user library and the user is prompted to install a newer version.

title: Allow 'source' to be specified for renv::restore()
description:
For Docker images, it would be useful to generate separate layers for R packages from CRAN, Bioconductor, and github.  A `source` parameter for `renv::restore()` would be valuable for large builds (e.g. 300 packages) where a complete rebuild might otherwise be required from a single error (typically in a github package), e.g.

```
RUN R -e 'renv::restore(source = "CRAN")'
RUN R -e 'renv::restore(source = "Bioconductor")'
RUN R -e 'renv::restore(source = "GitHub")'
```

This would allow the relatively error-free packages to install first and be cached by Docker.  Any errors in the relatively more error-prone github packages then wouldn't require a complete rebuild and would accelerate troubleshooting.

title: Warn on missing dependencies / Auto-restore
description:

https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/packages.html#r-cmd-build-and-the-project-library
> By default, when building a package tarball, R will copy all files within the package directory to a temporary build directory before building the package. Unfortunately, this also implies copying the renv library. When that library is large, this can dramatically increase the amount of time it takes to build your package.
This was already posted here also https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/245

To illustrate, I am working on a package for my company where without renv it takes **992ms** against more than **3min** as reported by `devtools::install()`

As a workaround to install a dev version, one can use `devtools::install(build = FALSE)` or `devtools::install(quick = TRUE)` that does not build. However, when this package will be build it will took some time. 

To follow the advice given in the documentation, do you think there could be room for some helpers functions and workflow to have a dev mode in renv in order to use a `~/.renv` folder for globally storing library for package developpement ? 

In Python, `virtualenvwrapper `does this by default. See [Location of Environments](https://virtualenvwrapper.readthedocs.io/en/latest/install.html#location-of-environments) with is `$HOME/.virtualenvs`. Then creating a new virtualenv for a project is done by `mkvirtualenv env1` and it will be created there by default. 

As development environment in R, I always found the [`devtools::dev_mode()`](https://devtools.r-lib.org/reference/dev_mode.html) interesting. Coupling this logic with `renv` project would be very nice for package development. 

Do you have any other feedback on using renv for package development  ?

I am thinking of helpers function to set up a dev mode use of renv, that would default to create a project library outside of the project in a global folder, using the package name in DESCRIPTION or a define renv project name that would be then store in renv files somewhere. 

I am willing to dig into this or prototype something if you this is useful or in your scope. 

What is your opinion on this ?

title: Global .Rprofile which requires a package
description:
I'm interested in settings `options(rlang::entrace)` in my global .Rprofile. For a project using renv, this will error if rlang isn't in the project library. That's the correct thing to do. 

Next, I install rlang in the project library. I restart R, my .Rprofile still has `options(error = rlang::entrace)`, yet `getOption("error")` returns `NULL`. The expected behavior is to return a call to `rlang::entrace`. 

The weird thing is that all my even though the error option isn't set, all my other options defined in .Rprofile are.

# How to reproduce

Create a new project. Run `renv::init()`. Set `RENV_CONFIG_USER_PROFILE=TRUE` in .Renviron. Add `options(error = rlang::entrace)` to global .Rprofile, along with another option, such as `options(digits = 10)`, to verify the .Rprofile is being run. 

Restart R, receive an error because rlang is not installed. Install rlang into the project, restart R. `getOption('error')` returns `NULL`.

If you run `renv::deactive()`, we'll get the expected return value of `getOption("error")`. 
# session info
Using the latest from Github, 57eb5398 (0.9.3-6)

title: Surfacing consistent information when dependencies() uncovers problems
description:
It seems that `dependencies()` only sometimes reports a warning when it uncovers errors in R code that prevent it from detecting dependencies, which can lead to hard-to-diagnose issues using renv. For example, take a project with the following file, and renv initialized:

```r
library("tidyverse")
test <- data.frame(a = 1 b = 2) # note missing comma
```

The first time I call `dependencies()` I see a warning message about the syntax error, and renv is returned as the only dependency. If I call `dependencies()` again, I don't see any warning, and just get renv as the single dependency. If I then edit anything in the file, save, and call `dependencies()` again, I see the warning again. 

In practice, what I experienced is I tried to snapshot a project that I had unwittingly introduced a syntax error into. This resulted in renv wanting to remove all packages from the lockfile. I puzzled about this for a while, and as part of trying to figure it out I called `dependencies()`. But since it had been called by `snapshot()` already, there was no warning message.

Is it intentional that `dependencies()` behaves this way? It would have helped me figure out the problem sooner if `dependencies()` always warned about issues it uncovers (and even better, if that warning came through `snapshot()` as well), but not sure if there's other reasoning behind this behavior.

title: generate lockfile from DESCRIPTION + (environment)
description:
Something like:

```R
renv::resolve(packages, remotes, ..., project)
```

which would generate a lockfile `renv.lock`.

- `packages`: The packages to resolve. When `NULL`, draw the packages as declared in the project `DESCRIPTION` file (if any).
- `remotes`: Remote specifications, giving requirements around package versions.

When `packages` is NULL or empty, the dependency list is drawn from the project's DESCRIPTION file.

title: Generate citation list
description: Suppose I'm working on a paper and using renv in my project. I'd love to be able to do something like `renv::cite()` and pass an argument for whether I want plain or bibtex citation and get a list of citations of all packages I've used, along with the correct version numbers. I could copy and paste this, maybe directly include it in an R Markdown file in the project? I'm not sure, but the basic print to the console or write out to a file functionality would be very welcome at the first stage! It might even have the positive effect of people getting in the habit of citing packages.

title: renv::restore() freezes when installing stringi
description: When running renv::restore(), the whole process gets blocked on stringi. What can be the issue?

title: use more evocative names for snapshot type
description:
"packrat" and "simple" are strange names. Alternate suggestions:

Type | Description
--- | ---
explicit | Managed explicitly by user in DESCRIPTION.
implicit | Inferred by runtime dependency detection.
all | Include all packages in project library.

title: allow users to ignore packages with unknown source during restore
description: This would allow `renv::restore()` to succeed with lockfiles containing packages that aren't otherwise retrievable.

title: encourage use of DESCRIPTION file for explicit dependency tracking
description: `renv::status()` could report packages which are mentioned in the lockfile, but not in the project `DESCRIPTION` file.

title: Differences in permissions in package installation
description:
Hi,

I'm running a docker container strictly based on rocker/verse:3.6.1 image.
If i exec into the container as root and run `R --slave -e "install.packages('here')"` I'll get the following result for `ls -l /usr/local/lib/R/site-library | grep here`
drwxrwxr-x 6 root staff ... here
However if I run `R --slave -e "renv::install('here')"` then I'll get
drwxr-xr-x 6 root staff ... here
This results in not being able to reinstall the package from the RStudio session while being rstudio user.

Strangely if I change the user from root to rstudio with `su rstudio` then both of the mentioned installation commands return the same result
drwxrwxr-x 6 rstudio staff ... here

To sum it up, somehow there is a difference in package folder permissions between `install.packages` and `renv::install` only while being the root user. This has a major impact during the Docker image build. I'm aware that I could mount the cache to the Docker container, however there are some functionalities and packages I would like to have already embedded inside the image.

The simple workaround could be to just run extra chmod command during the build, after the package installation.

However there must be a reason why this difference exists and maybe you would like to investigate it further.

description:

```R
```

title: Allow ordering library sources in hydrate
description:
Hi,

the hydrate function manual says, that it

>will attempt to discover R packages from the following sources (in order):
The user library,
The site library,
The system library,
The renv cache.

Let's say I have the checkmate package version 1.9.0 installed in one of my user/site/system libraries. At the same time I have checkmate version 1.9.1 and 1.9.4 (the latest) living simultaneously inside the renv cache. When I initialize a new project, and install the checkmate package, I'll get the 1.9.4 version in my project library. However if I write some script that contains `library(checkmate)` and run the hydrate function, then my 1.9.4 package version will be overwritten by the 1.9.0 version (which will also be copied to the cache).

Alternatively could the hydrate function look for packages in all four places, but populate the project library with the latest version found, instead of the version that gets found first?

title: renv bootstrapping with cache
description:
I am building a handful of test Docker images and scripts that use `renv` to prepare environments. I am adjusting or removing the `renv`-generated `.Rprofile` and `renv/activate.R` files to avoid private installs of `renv`. This issue is trying to determine how to best bootstrap `renv` in shared multi-project environments (such as a Docker image that may be used for multiple Shiny applications).

In my working directory, I have `cache` and `content` subdirectories. The `cache` directory starts empty. The `content` directory contains a simple R Markdown document and the `.Rprofile`, `renv.lock`, and `renv/activate.R` created by `renv` initialization and snapshotting.

Bootstrapping `renv` installs the package into the `renv/library/....` and does not take advantage of the cache. This means that each project that uses `renv` installs its own copy of the package.

In my case, I have a same-version of `renv` in the environment. The `renv/activate.R` does not see this copy of `renv` because it is not a loaded namespace. I am attempting to restore outside an active R session with:

```bash
export RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/cache
R -e 'renv::restore(repos = c(CRAN=Sys.getenv("R_REPOSITORY")))'
# Failed to find installation of renv -- attempting to bootstrap...
# * Installing renv 0.9.2 ... Done!
# Successfully installed and loaded renv 0.9.2.
```

This `renv` is in `renv/library` but not the cache. Everything besides `renv` is a symlink from `renv/library/...` into `/cache/...`.

```bash
ls -ld renv/library/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renv
drwxr-xr-x 13 USER USER 416 Jan 22 22:39 renv/library/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renv
ls -ld /cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renv
ls: cannot access '/cache/v5/R-3.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/renv': No such file or directory
```

The system-installed `renv` is used if the `.Rprofile` is changed to:

```r
library(renv)
source("renv/activate.R")
```

Alternatively, I can bypass `renv/activate.R` entirely if I ditch the `.Rprofile` and explicitly call `renv::load()`:

```bash
R --slave -e 'renv::load(); renv::restore(repos = c(CRAN=Sys.getenv("R_REPOSITORY")))'
```

What is the recommended way to bootstrap `renv` into environments? Should `renv/activate.R` attempt to load `renv` from the system library if the namespace is not already loaded? Should `renv` come from the cache (is this even possible with such a lightweight `renv/activate.R`)?

title: renv tests all fail for users with uid >32767
description:
This took me a while to understand but I think I have found what's going on now.

Steps to reproduce:
* Run the renv tests with a user whose uid is > 32767.
* All tests fail.

What's happening:
* R's internal `utils::tar` command produces a warning when used with uids > 32767 (https://stackoverflow.com/questions/30599326/warning-message-during-building-an-r-package-invalid-uid-value-replaced-by-that)
* renv uses `utils::tar` during test setup 
  https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/83fa169e6d49559a072e350267a427df1c8ac634/R/tests.R#L128
* renv sets options(warn = 2) during testing, converting warnings to an error
  https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/83fa169e6d49559a072e350267a427df1c8ac634/R/tests.R#L97
* According to the stackoverflow discussion above, the use of this internal tar command can be bypassed by providing a system tar in an environment variable like `R_BUILD_TAR`. This workaround can be used to avoid the warning when building/installing packages, and `utils::tar` itself also checks Sys.getenv("tar"). But renv calls `utils::tar` directly with the argument `tar = internal` and so overrides those choices.
* Therefore renv tests fail if your uid is too large.

I can think of two ways that we might be able to resolve this:
* Don't force the use of tar = "internal", allowing the use of the system tar instead of the internal R implementation.
* Don't convert warnings to errors.

Any other ideas?

title: Loading Renviron manually looses expansion identifer for R_LIBS_*
description:
On our mutualized servers, we use `R_LIBS_SITE` to configure a site library. As we need to take care of multiple R versions, we use the expansion identifier as describe in `?.libPaths()`
Something like that in `~/Renviron` 
```
R_LIBS_SITE=/applis/R/site-library/%p/%V
```

It seems when using a `renv` project, the ` ~/.Renviron` file is manually imported in `renv_load_renviron` using `readRenviron`. Issue is this function does not do the identifier expansion as it is done when R load the environ file. 

Outside of renv project I get : 
```r
> Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_SITE")
[1] "/applis/R/site-library/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/3.6.2"
```
but inside renv project
```r
> Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_SITE")
[1] "/applis/R/site-library/%p/%V"
```

This means the environment variable can't be read anymore. 

This could be a very special case but I think it is worth underlying this behavior. 
I did not find an R function that does the % identifier expansion. Not sure it is possible... 
You may already have encounter this and know how to solve this.

It is a bit annoying that renv behavior superseed this by overwriting the env variable. However, I can find some workaround by not using this environment variable anymore or by setting at the server level if possible as `Renviron.site` is correctly loaded by R, not read by renv.

I don't know if other R environment variables, other than `R_LIBS_*` have this feature and could be impacted. 

Anyway, `%` identifier can't be used in environ file that `renv` will load.

## Step to reproduce

1. create a project with renv
2. Have a `~/.Renviron` with `R_LIBS_SITE` set up
3. compare `Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_SITE")` when renv activated and when deactivated

title: Handling packages in Suggests of a dependency
description:
How does **renv** handle packages in the `Suggests` field of a dependency?
It seems these aren't captured by `renv::snapshot()`.

Below is an example; it uses Bioconductor, which I hope isn't a confounder, but this is where I first noticed the issue.
Starting a new project in RStudio and then running

```R
renv::init()
renv::install("BiocManager")
renv::install("bioc::scPipe")
```

Then, creating an R file in the project, `test.R`, with the following:

```R
library(scPipe)
```

Then, running `renv::snapshot()`.
This yields the attached `renv.lock` ([renv.lock.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/4028407/renv.lock.txt), I had to change the extension to be able to attached the file to this issue).

`renv::snapshot()` skips the packages in `Suggests` of **scPipe** (namely, **Rsubread**, **knitr**, **rmarkdown**, **testthat**; see https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/scPipe.html).
Some of the **scPipe** functionality uses these packages, e.g., `scPipe::create_processed_report()` calls `rmarkdown::render()` (`scPipe::create_processed_report()` isn't an essential function to the package, which is why I believe **rmarkdown** is only in `Suggests` of **scPipe**) .

So, if my analysis code calls `scPipe::create_processed_report()`, for example, then **renv** doesn't 'see' the **rmarkdown** dependency and so it is not included in the lockfile.
Is there currently a way to force **renv** to record those packages in `Suggests` of a dependency?
I thought `renv::dependencies(dev = TRUE)` might do it, but I think I misunderstood this option.
FWIW I've not thought through the implications of recording packages in `Suggests` by default, but an option would be much appreciated.

title: renv github dependencies don't work with rsconnect::deployApp
description:
I have a large existing application I am converting to using Renv. Mostly it's gone great, but there are a couple of direct github dependencies. Locally, it's no problem. Renv installs and restores them fine. However, when I attempt to deploy with rsconnect::deployApp, they fail.

I created a simple repo to demo the problem with full documentation: 

- https://github.com/generalui/renv-rsconnect-github

In short, I have a tiny app which deploys, but when I run the following:

```R
renv::install("th86/concordanceIndex”)
```

And starting using the library in the source (e.g. `concordanceIndex::concordanceIndex`), the deploy fails:

```R
> rsconnect::deployApp()
Preparing to deploy application...
Update application currently deployed at
https://iatlas-test.shinyapps.io/084-single-file/? [Y/n] y
DONE
Uploading bundle for application: 1597446...Warning in FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  Unable to find repository URL for package concordanceIndex
DONE
Deploying bundle: 2688358 for application: 1597446 ...
Waiting for task: 678405041
  building: Building image: 2935776
  building: Building package: concordanceIndex
################################ Begin Task Log ################################ 
################################# End Task Log ################################# 
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 678405042 failed: Error building image: Error fetching concordanceIndex (0.1) source. <CRANPackageSource repo='http://cran.rstudio.org'> unable to satisfy package: concordanceIndex (0.1)
In addition: Warning message:
In FUN(X[[i]], ...) :
  Package 'concordanceIndex 0.1' was installed from sources; Packrat will assume this package is available from a CRAN-like repository during future restores
```

Versions:

- R: 3.6.2 (2019-12-12)
- RStudio: 1.2.5019
- renv: 0.9.2-13
- rsconnect: 0.8.16-9000

I have a workaround at the moment from the doc on this page: https://docs.rstudio.com/shinyapps.io/getting-started.html

```R
renv::install('devtools')
devtools::install_github("th86/concordanceIndex", force=TRUE)
```

However, whatever devtools::install_github does isn't reflected in changes in my repository. Every time someone checks out my repository, they have to manually run devtools::install_github for every github dependency. 

The original renv::install + renv::snapshot should be all I need to use a github dependency, right?

title: Support authentication for private CRAN-like repositories
description:
I would like to use renv with an internal repository that requires authentication.
I can already install package from the repo using install.packages:

```install.packages("pkgName", repos = "https://repo.url", headers = c("Authorization" = Sys.getenv("AUTH_HEADER")))```

I would really appreciate it, if I could specify the authentication header somewhere, like the GITHUB_PAT and that this would then be picked up when installing packages from that CRAN-like repository.

title: Downloading files w/o curl
description:
Hi

I have had trouble restoring on Windows Server. Unlike Windows 10 there is no `curl` on Windows Server. 

The function `renv_download_impl` *should* figure this out with `renv_donwload_file_method`, but it returns `curl` even though `curl` is not available. 

My log looks something like this:

> Querying repositories for available binary packages ... Done! 
> ...
> Error: failed to retrieve package <name>
> ...
> InternetOpenUrl failed: 'The requested header was not found' 

The first query is listed as successful, but it doesn't receive anything. However, the problem is not discovered until `renv` tries to download the first (source) package and fails. 

One suggestion is more information when setting the download method. It took quite a bit of digging to realize that the download method was not set correctly.

title: Option to force renv/.gitignore (and other ignore-file) construction?
description:
I use a project structure where the R 'project' (i.e. directory) itself sits in a subdirectory within a parent git repository. So, for example, the repo itself might be called `top-level`, and it'll contain its own `.gitignore`. Then within, `top-level`, there'll be R projects (`app1`, `app2`, etc), and from there each has its own `renv` structure. This results in a directory structure a bit like so:
```
/top-level/.git/*
/top-level/.gitignore
/top-level/app1/main.R
/top-level/app1/renv.lock
/top-level/app1/renv/*
/top-level/app2/main.R
/top-level/app2/renv.lock
/top-level/app2/renv/*
```
When initializing `renv` from within any of the `app`s, no `.gitignore` file is created and placed in the `renv` directory.
After poking-around a bit it appears the `.gitignore` file will only be created _if_ a non-empty `.gitignore` is found in the same directory in which the `renv` directory itself will live.
I can probably create some dummy indicators to 'simulate' each `app` as being its own git repo, but perhaps it'd be easier to have an option where we can _force_ ignore-file construction regardless of the detected directory structure?

description:
If on 2 git branches live different verisions of `renv` and the user moved from one branch to another without restarting the R session, the `renv` from the old git branch will be used throughout. This can lead to very confusing bugs and errors.

I am using drake in tandem with renv. I've decided to wrap the meat of my project in an R package, exposed to drake through `expose_imports()`. When changes require updating the package, I would expect `renv::install(mypkg)` to work, as long as I had bumped the package version. Instead, I get

What's weird about this behavior is based on the renv.lock contents, I'm not sure why the first doesn't work.

```
    "mypkg": {

      "Source": "Local",
      "RemoteType": "local",

    }
```
I've also set RENV_PATHS_LOCAL to "S://Projects" or "file://S://Projects" in an attempt to fix it.

```
renv::update('mypkg')

#  attempt to set an attribute on NULL
```

One thing I noticed is `renv_snapshot_r_packages()` is returning `mypkg$Source` as "unknown", rather than "Local", so it isn't picking up that "RemoteURL" in the renv.lock as I expected.

I'm on the latest dev version, and had the same issues with the version on CRAN.

Another edit: I see you've addressed essentially this at #250. I agree with the conclusion there, but I find the behavior quite surprising. At the very least, a more informative error message or an explanation in [this vignette](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/local-sources.html) about this behavior would be very welcome. I'd be happy to submit a PR for whichever is the desired route.

title: renv::restore() only creates base Python install from renv.lock without add-on libraries i n environment.yml
description:
Two issues, as outlined below.

Below are steps taken to attempt to create a reproducible R and Python environments with `renv`:

1. in an RStudio project, call `renv::init()`
2. call `renv::use_python()`, pointing to existing Python interpreter in conda virtual environment
3. confirmed correct Python.exe used with `reticulate::py_config()` 
4. __Issue 1__:  `renv::init()` correctly captures R environment, but doesn't capture all the supplementary Python libraries in the conda virtual environment
5. manually installed missing Python libraries into new virtual environment created by `renv::use_python()`
6. call `renv::snapshot()` to capture R and Python environments via `renv.lock` and `environment.yml`
7. on a separate machine, git cloned repository containing `renv.lock` and `environment.yml`, and call `renv::restore()`
8. __Issue 2__: full R environment reproduced, but only base Python environment is restored; is user expected to manually run `conda env create -f environment.yml` on the restored  Python environment to install missing libraries from base Python?

title: Provide loading utility similar to `pacman::p_load`
description:
Would be nice if renv cold provide a way to attach a list of packages, (and install+attach if packages are missing). It should load all project specific packages at once when called with no arguments.

My team is currently using `pacman::p_load` a lot, and that's the only function we use from that package. Would be great if we could get rid of that dependency. To my mind such an utility is a natural complement to the existing trio `renv::install`, `renv::remove`, `renv::update`.

As a concrete workflow, if my packages are already declared in DESCRIPTION then I could do `renv::load_packages` and load all of them in the order they are specified in that file. 

Not sure about the name though. The current `renv::load` is a too-nice-of-a-name reserved for an semi-internal function. So maybe (if you agree with the proposal) the current `renv::load` could be renamed into `load_project` and the name could be used for this new feature.

title: Bioconductor packages via `install.packages` are not restored
description:
Hello, thank you for `renv`, really hope that it will take environment management problem away.

I have a little bit strange setup for `packrat` that appears to not work with `renv`.
I have a project with CRAN and Bioconductor dependencies, but I install all of them via `install.packages` by first setting the repos with `setRepositories()`.
This works for `renv` too, but the recorded `renv.lock` file states that Bioconductor packages were installed via Bioconductor, so restoring them fails on the other machine.

I guess since `renv` has now support for Bioconductor, I should use that (and I'll try), but I thought this is probably not the intended behaviour.
Thank you

title: Make `renv::status` output available to programs
description:
Currently `renv::status` prints a lot but outputs very little. I think the common way to design the reporter is in the `print` method - let `renv::status` do all the work but printer do the reporting. 

Particularly, concerning #255 I don't see how to grab the packages listed for purge and re-install them in bulk.

title: Allow explicit list of packages to snapshot with `renv::snapshot`
description:
It's occasionally necessary to snapshot some packages but to restore another set of packages. `restore` already has `packages` argument. I think it would be nice to add this argument to the `snapshot` as well. 

I just had the following use case:

 1) I am using the most recent version of `renv` 
 2) I pull a PR from a collaborator which rolls back a bunch of packages, but uses a different version of `renv`. 
 3) I want to restore the packages that my colaborator wants to restore, but to snapshot the new version of `renv`. 

Would be nice if I could do `renv::snapshot(packages="renv")` and then `renv::restore()`. Currently I have to either restore the package list selectively (all without renv), or restore all then upgrade renv and then snapshot. 

More generally the exclusion argument begs itself here. For a consistent API, all 3 core functions `update`,  `snapshot`, and `restore` could have `include_packages` and `exclude_packages` arguments. With these, I wouldn't know what would one need more in order to manipulate `renv.lock`. 

Somewhat related #157

title: shouldn't renv narrow to project packages when snapshot type is `packrat`?
description:
If I add `library(blabla)` to my project files `renv::status` does not detect it. The other way around, when I install a package which is not loaded by the project, `renv:status` will report it and `renv::snapshot()` will shove it into the `renv.lock`. 

It looks to me that, when snapshot type is packrat, renv should differentiate between used and unused packages in the library, and snapshot only the used ones. What do you think?

The motivation behind this is somewhat similar to what has been discussed in #121. I want to share with collaborators only the state of the relevant packages, not all the mambo-jumbo that I play with while experimenting and learning locally. 

I know there is `settings::ignored.packages`, but we are after is more like `used.packages`. Is there a way to achieve this currently?

title: blogdown dependencies not found
description:
I am trying to use renv for a blogdown project and by default the blogdown dependency is not found. 

Example of a new blogdown project: 
``` r
dir.create(tmp_dir <- tempfile())
options(blogdown.open_sample = FALSE)
blogdown::new_site(dir = tmp_dir, serve = FALSE)
renv::dependencies(tmp_dir)
#> Finding R package dependencies ... Done!
#>                                                                                                        Source
#> 1 C:/Users/dervieuxchr/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp6Jhg7h/file43b03cac44f2/content/post/2015-07-23-r-rmarkdown.Rmd

#>     Package Require Version   Dev
#> 1 rmarkdown                 FALSE
#> 2     knitr                 FALSE
#> 3 rmarkdown                 FALSE
unlink(tmp_dir)
```

blogdown is not found - I think it should be because at least in a default blogdown project, you have a `index.Rmd` with 

and `renv` is parsing Rmd file. However, the internal function does not look at `site` field.

Minimal reprex: 
``` r
dir.create(tmp_dir <- tempfile())
xfun::write_utf8(c(
  "---",
  "site: blogdown:::blogdown_site",
  "---"

renv:::renv_dependencies_discover_rmd_yaml_header(file.path(tmp_dir, "index.Rmd"))

#> 1 rmarkdown                 FALSE
unlink(tmp_dir)
```

Maybe it should look at this field ? 

Or detect that we are in a blogdown project ? 

What do you think ?

title: add a use_renv_ignore to help maintain `.renvignore` file ?

I find this functions in usethis really useful to help maintain `*ignore` files from R

title: Company internal CRAN-like repo
description:
Hi, 

From within an `renv` project, I have found that if I want to install from my companies internal CRAN-like repo (that requires authentication that is somehow managed automatically), I need to run:
`install.packages("custompkg", type = "source")`
If I don't specify `type = source`, it tries unsuccessfully to find a windows binary to install from (as they are not hosted).
However, if I am not in an `renv` project, I can run
`install.packages("custompkg")`
and it installs fine.

The real problems comes when creating a snapshot and then trying to restore.
This [issue](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/120#issue-474858634) tells me why my package ends up as an "unknown" source.
I then edit the lock file to specify a repo, and then it tries to access the "Archive" location when running `renv::restore()`
```
Retrieving 'http://internalCRAN/src/contrib/Archive/custompkg/custompkg_1.5.1.tar.gz' ...
Error: failed to retrieve package 'custompkg'
In addition: Warning messages:
1: could not retrieve available packages for url "http://internalCRAN/src/contrib" 
2: could not retrieve available packages for url "http://internalCRAN/bin/windows/contrib/3.5" 
3: In downloader(url, destfile, type, request, headers) :
  curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404 Not Found
4: In downloader(url, destfile, type, request, headers) :
  curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404 Not Found
5: In downloader(url, destfile, type, request, headers) :
  curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 401 Unauthorized
6: In downloader(url, destfile, type, request, headers) :
  curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 401 Unauthorized
```
So, I created the Archive directory in our companies CRAN and placed the tar.gz files into that location, but I get the same error and warnings.

Do you have any ideas on how to make this work?

At the moment, I am resigned to using the "unknown" source method of copying the required tar.gz files and setting up a local directory where they can be installed from.
But I would like to be able to install directly from our internal CRAN-like repo directly from within a `renv::restore()`

Thanks,
Ben

title: permit automatic upgrade of some packages?
description:
From https://community.rstudio.com/t/error-message-installing-nlme-with-restore-command/45246.

---

In some cases, `renv::restore()` may fail on Windows or macOS because:

1. One of the packages recorded in the lockfile is no longer current; hence
2. That package must be installed from archive sources, but
3. The user's machine does not have the necessary tools to build the package.

We should consider accommodating such cases by instead choosing to download the latest available binary.

title: Documentation improvement on local source package
description:
While trying to configure all renv paths for a RStudio server cluster, I stumble upon soemthing not clear in the documentation about where local source packages should be

### In the vignette 

https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/local-sources.html
Only `RENV_PATHS_LOCAL` is mentioned and, if unset, it is a folder parent of  `RENV_PATHS_ROOT` 

### In the paths help page 

https://rstudio.github.io/renv/reference/paths.html#local-sources

It says that local source can be put into the project folder

```
<project>/renv/local/<package>_<version>.<ext>
<project>/renv/local/<package>/<package>_<version>.<ext>
```

it seems to be here in the code
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/cfbbf9e9868f1a22a4d6748785ac15382b2feb59/R/retrieve.R#L280

FWIW, I think this should be added to the local source vignettes.

title: Activation loads grDevices and doesn't inhibit the message
description: In my build targets I see an extra `Loading required package: grDevices` due to loading of `renv/activate.R`. Placing the activation into `suppressPackageStartupMessages` block solves the problem but I think this should be taken care on the renv side. In fact I don't think it should load/attach any packages (if this is possible of course).

title: Add ability to `renv::restore` to restore only a subset of packages from the library
description:
Would be nice to be able to restore only a subset of the library. Boils down to the new `packages` argument to `renv::restore`. But I am not sure how well this would play with `renv::status`. 

The primary use case is to use with docker in production which commonly requires only a small subset of all packages used. 

It might be useful in interactive contexts as well, such as when for collaborators wants to quickly use/test only part of the functionality of the project. 

This one is narrower than #253 but would quickly address a major use case.

title: renv::activate/deactivate clobber .Rprofile
description:
Renv treats .Rprofile pretty harshly. 

First, it removes all the indentation. 

Second, `renv::deactivate()` removes the `source("renv/activate.R")` and then `renv::activate()` adds it to the end of the file. This is not right in most of the use cases except of the very basic one. One would normally want to run some custom code/setup after renv/activation. 

Looks to me that right approach would be to simply comment/comment the `source("renv/activate.R")` and let it to the user to decide where it should be located.
