title: How to deal with different versions of R?
description:
Thank you for writing `renv`! I am excited to use it to make my code more future-proof and reproducible.

`renv` solves package management; my question is what is the best practice for handling different R versions?

For example, on my local computer, I have `3.5.2`, but on a remote computer, I have `3.2.3`, and I get the following message when trying to restore a project built from the local machine.

```
Project requested R version '3.5.2' but '3.2.3' is currently being used
```

In python, there are `pyenv` or `conda` which allows one to use multiple python versions in an isolated environment. 
Is there an equivalent system that allows multiple versions of R?
If not, what's the current recommendation?

title: Multiple named renv profiles?
description:
I might be missing something but it seems that currently renv doesn't allow for multiple named "profiles" to co-exist. 

I often work simultaneously with multiple versions of R and dependency packages. Would be really great if renv.lock could store multiple profiles, dev, test, deploy etc. 

Even more so, for the interactive use one of them could be chosen automatically depending on the version of R.  Currently, if I start with a different version of R, I am getting an incompatibility error and the renv is not loaded. What would be the easiest way to accommodate multiple R versions right now? Thanks!

title: R CMD build significantly slower
description:
When I build a package that makes use of  `renv`, it takes much longer to build the package than without `renv`, even though the `renv` folder is in `.Rbuildignore`:

```
v  checking for file 'C:\pkg/DESCRIPTION' (810ms)
-  preparing 'pkg': (1m 22s)
v  checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... 
-  checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts (35.3s)
-  checking for empty or unneeded directories
-  building 'pkg_1.0.0.tar.gz'
```

When I temporarily move the `renv` folder out of the root package folder, package build is much faster:
```
v  checking for file 'C:\pkg/DESCRIPTION' (763ms)
-  preparing 'pkg': (5.2s)
v  checking DESCRIPTION meta-information ... 
-  checking for LF line-endings in source and make files and shell scripts (3.6s)
-  checking for empty or unneeded directories
-  building 'pkg_1.0.0.tar.gz'
```

This is probably due to `R CMD build` copying all directories/files first and then removing any that are in `.Rbuildignore`, as explained [here](https://community.rstudio.com/t/r-cmd-check-preparing-package/27151).

Do you have any suggestions how to speed up package building when using `renv`?

title: Can't install Bioconductor packages
Working in a shared renv in two machines
description:
The way our work is set-up is that sometimes we work on a project on a server (for compute-heavy tasks), others in the locally mounted project folder (quick plotting etc). In effect we access the same `renv` from two different locations. Both OSs are unix-based (LInux on the server side, and OSX or linux on client side). 

My expectation was that, assuming that the R version is the same on the server and client, we could load `renv `on either and carry on with the work having the same version of all libraries. So as a test I created an `renv` locally, did some work on it, and then logged into the server. There the renv was recognize by the R session, however there was warning:

```R
 Project '/lustre/projects/bioinfo/domingue/scripts/motifs' loaded. [renv 0.8.3]
Warning message:
The following package(s) are missing entries in the cache:

        acepack, annotate, AnnotationDbi, AnnotationFilter, ape,
        argparser, backports, bamsignals, base64enc, beachmat,
        beeswarm, bezier, BH, bibtex, Biobase, BiocGenerics,
        BiocManager, BiocNeighbors, BiocParallel, BiocSingular,
        biomaRt, Biostrings, biovizBase, bit, bit64, bitops, blob,
        BSgenome, callr, caTools, checkmate, cluster,
        clusterProfiler, codetools, colorspace, corescf, covr,
        cowplot, crosstalk, cummeRbund, curl, data.table, DBI,
        DelayedArray, DelayedMatrixStats, DESeq2, devtools,
        dichromat, digest, DO.db, docopt, DOSE, dplyr, dqrng, DT,
        ellipsis, enrichplot, ensembldb, europepmc, fansi, farver,
        fastcluster, fastmap, fastmatch, fdrtool, fgsea,
        fitdistrplus, FNN, forcats, foreach, foreign, formatR,
```

After a quick search, it seems that the libraries are missing because the packages are symlinked in `renv`, which is expected.

title: Lockfile generation on Windows not specific to project or package
description:
I am not sure this is an issue specific to renv or the way that packages are being installed or viewed as active in Windows. I have a couple packages that I've created recently. When using `renv::init()` on these packages, the entirety of the packages in `~\AppData\Local\renv\cache\v4\R-3.6\x86_64-w64-mingw32` are written into the lockfile and shortcuts copied to the renv project folder, regardless of whether they are specified in the DESCRIPTION or loaded into the current R session.

I've recreated this with a simple R project: https://github.com/Aryllen/test-renv-windows. This project was created in a new directory, then `renv::init()` was run to initialize the package workspace. The lockfile generated shows every package in my local AppData directory and, while not uploaded, the renv package library within this project directory has shortcuts for every one of these packages. The behavior I expected was to create a clean slate package workspace that only has the packages currently active in the R session (at that time of creation only base R was active). This happens for both projects and R packages with DESCRIPTION files for the dependencies. 

However, my colleague who uses a Mac does not seem to have this problem. We were trying to recreate a different issue and she created this example branch: https://github.com/karawoo/renv-restore-windows-test/tree/test-20191107. The lockfile only has the packages loaded in Script.R and their dependencies, which is the expected behavior.

**System:**
- Windows 10 Pro
- RStudio 1.2.5019
- R 3.6.1
- renv 8.2

On potentially a similar note, when using `renv::restore()` the packages are installed into the same AppData directory and I get warnings for every package installed saying that the directory is not for a project. There is a snippet below.

title: Module Dependencies
description:
This is a future-looking feature request. At the moment, dependencies expressed in patterns such as modules (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/modules/vignettes/modulesInR.html) are incorrectly identified. The consequences is that, unless one set snapshot type to simple, dependencies only used in these types of modules do not end up in the lock file (I am assuming during the dependency discovery phase it believes it's not needed).

Realize this is complex and renv::settings$snapshot.type("simple") is an easy workaround. Thanks

List of actions

title: Documentation improvement
description:
Just sharing thoughts following new experience with `renv`

Currently, `renv` is not on CRAN and I am testing it in our offline servers by installing it manually (no access to GITHUB).

From the current documentation of `renv::upgrade`

> By default, this function will attempt to install the latest version of renv as available on the active R package repositories. If you'd instead like to try out a development version of renv, you can explicitly request a different version of renv and that version of the package will be downloaded and installed from GitHub. Use version = "master" to install the latest development version of renv, as from the renv project's GitHub page. 

I was under the impression that if not find on CRAN (which is currently the case), `renv` would say FALSE or "already up to date" if I ask to `upgrade`. However, that is not the default behavior I observed, and indeed it is not the default behavior in the code.  

`renv::upgrade` will look into my internal CRAN mirror, not find it, **then** look for a version Github, and at last R will hang until timeout as it can't access the web. 

I think the documentation could be improved to say what is the default behavior. 

I also open the issue if someone look for this during development phase.
Because once a first version will be one CRAN, this would not be an issue I guess. Unless for outdated or curated cran mirror where `renv` would not be available and `upgrade` would still try to look on github even if not asked to. 

This type of issue falls under "offline mode" category for renv - best scenario would be an option to deactivate all features requiring internet access. But like with remotes or pak, this is not always easy and this helps only a few of us who are still on offline environment 🤷‍♂

title: option to add full library to git
description:
I will preface this with saying this is an esoteric request, but very much informed by my day-to-day with legacy enterprise processes!  

Currently renv automatically creates `renv/.gitignore` with the `library` directory added so that it's ignored by Git.  For 99% of the time I fully support that 😄 .  However for some of my app deployments, I need to actually add the full package library to the Git repo for the project.  So my first attempt is to simply edit the `renv/.gitignore` and remove `library/` rmyself.  However if I close the project and resume again, renv automatically adds that line back.  Would there be a way for a user to opt-out of this automatic behavior, as crazy as it may sound?

title: `reticulate` no longer able to find the Python binary
description:
When using `renv` in combination with `reticulate`, the latter is no longer able to find the Python binary. I suspect this is because `renv` sets the environment variable "RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV" to an empty string. The current workaround I employ is to first unset that variable:

```r
Sys.unsetenv("RETICULATE_PYTHON_ENV")
library(reticulate)
use_virtualenv("../venv", required = TRUE)
```

PS. I filed this issue as requested by @kevinushey (see https://twitter.com/kevin_ushey/status/1183869321992269824).

PPS. This package is amazing. Thank you.

title: Failing to restore MASS weirdness
description:
Tonight I found I couldn't restore this lockfile:

```
{
  "R": {
    "Version": "3.6.1",
    "Repositories": [
      {
        "Name": "CRAN",
        "URL": "https://cloud.r-project.org"
      }
    ]
  },
  "Packages": {
    "MASS": {
      "Package": "MASS",
      "Version": "7.3-51.4",
      "Source": "Repository",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "Hash": "a489ad42493fa9bfac8f3e3a3bc7d4ca"
    }
  }
}
```

I traced the error to this weird `entry` being returned from `renv_available_packages_entry()`:
```
> entry
       Package  Version    Priority
MASS      MASS 7.3-51.4 recommended
MASS.1    MASS 7.3-51.4 recommended
                                               Depends Imports LinkingTo
MASS   R (>= 3.1.0), grDevices, graphics, stats, utils methods      <NA>
MASS.1   R (>= 4.0), grDevices, graphics, stats, utils methods      <NA>
                            Suggests Enhances       License License_is_FOSS
MASS   lattice, nlme, nnet, survival     <NA> GPL-2 | GPL-3            <NA>
MASS.1 lattice, nlme, nnet, survival     <NA> GPL-2 | GPL-3            <NA>
       License_restricts_use OS_type Archs                           MD5sum
MASS                    <NA>    <NA>  <NA> de47a9821cf202349ea173f56efa2719
MASS.1                  <NA>    <NA>  <NA> f17515b8329376b6ed9fe99de63ff2ce
       NeedsCompilation              Path
MASS                yes              <NA>
MASS.1              yes 4.0.0/Recommended
                                    Repository   Type Name
MASS   https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib source CRAN
MASS.1 https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib source CRAN
```

Eventually this lead to `download()` being called with `url = c("https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/MASS_7.3-51.4.tar.gz", "https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/MASS_7.3-51.4.tar.gz")`, which failed, leading to `renv` checking archive which also failed. 

The WEIRD thing is by the time I had done all this tracing and wrote up the issue, the problem was gone. When I checked `available.packages()` there was only 1 entry for MASS. I guess someone made a mistake publishing the package? Just letting you know in case you want to make `renv` robust to this.

title: renv::restore() always looking in repository archive
description:
I am using renv_0.7.0-17 and am running into problems that when using with git, where if I upgrade some packages and then commit the lock file, when I pull that from another machine and then renv::restore(), it always wants to hit the repo in the Archive directory.
Sometimes, the version of a package is the latest, so it is in the main CRAN repo structure and not Archive, so the restore fails.
One example is upgrading "cli" from 1.0.1 -> 1.1.0

title: option to disable warning on missing dependencies when snapshotting?
description:
I've been experimenting with using snapshots of `type = "custom"`, where I supply a function in `renv.snapshot.filter` that only returns my project's direct dependencies, ignoring recursive dependencies.

This seems like a nice way to capture the versions of my direct dependencies in a minimal lockfile. Currently this process results in a large screen of recursive dependencies that I should `Consider re-installing these packages before snapshotting the lockfile.`. This occurs even with `force = TRUE`.

It would be nice to have the option to disable the messages relating to recursive dependencies not included in the snapshot. Or it might make sense not to warn when `renv.snapshot.filter` is in use since this implies advanced usage.

title: `future` and `.libPaths()`
description:
Ran into an interesting bug with the `future` package and `.libPaths()` and was pointed your way to double check you have the case covered with `renv`.

--------------------------------

Issue:  https://github.com/HenrikBengtsson/future/issues/219

`future` Bug Repro:

1. Make a custom lib path to use a package in that libpath. 
2. `future` PSOCK cluster is used.
3. In a future call, try to use package in custom libpath.
* Error: Fails to find package as custom libpath is not passed through.


--------------------

Work around:

* Set `R_LIBS` to the custom libpath

I can see in the code `R_LIBS` is being set here: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/24ed969635376879ca16655d2d6a289eaa0e676b/R/R.R#L12 . 

Didn't know if there were other situations where this might be useful, but I thought I'd pass along the odd situation.  (Feel free to close if this is already covered.)

cc @jcheng5

title: installing packages slow outside C:/ on Windows
description:
I have secondary drives that I usually do my project work on. If I create a project under C:/ everything works fine -- however, when I try to use renv with a project on any other drive, I run into a bunch of strange behaviour:

Package installation hangs for long periods of time after everything is seemingly done: the more packagese there are, the worse it gets. After large installations, like e.g. `install.packages("tidyverse")`, the R session hangs for several minutes.

Once installation eventually finishes, the packages are available, but don't get picked up by `renv::snapshot()` for updating the lock file. For example:

``` r
library(glue)
#> Error in library(glue) : there is no package called ‘glue’
install.packages("glue")
#> * Querying repositories for available binary packages ... Done!
#> * Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
#> Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/3.6/glue_1.3.1.zip' ...
#> 	OK [file is up to date]
#> Installing glue [1.3.1] from CRAN ...
#> 	OK (installed binary)
```

This step took ~10s to finish after the "OK" print. Then:

``` r
renv::snapshot()
#> * The lockfile is already up to date.
renv::status()
#> * The project is already synchronized with the lockfile.
library(glue)
#> 
#> Restarting R session...
#> 
#> * Project 'S:/tmp/bar' loaded. [renv 0.7.0-112]
renv::clean()
#> * No stale lockfiles were found.
#> * No temporary directories were found in the project library.
#> * No non-system packages were discovered in the system library.
#> The following packages are installed in the project library,
#> but appear to be no longer used in your project.
#> 
#> 	glue
#> 
#> These packages will be removed.
#> 
#> Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y
#> * Removing package(s) from project library ...
#> Removing package 'glue' ... Done!
#> * The project has been cleaned.
```

I thought maybe it might be a cache thing, so I tried setting `RENV_PATHS_CACHE` to point to a directory on the same drive that the project was on: this seemingly had no effect.

title: `renv` for R package checking
description:
I am thinking about using _renv_ for isolated R pkg checking on CI providers.

My current approach is as follows:

1. `renv::init(bare = TRUE)` to avoid copying unneeded dependencies from the main R lib
2. `renv::install()` to scrape deps from the DESCRIPTION file
3. R CMD build and R CMD check

However when at step 3, I face the following problem 

```r
==> R CMD check *.tar.gz

* checking whether package ‘tic.package’ can be installed ... ERROR
Installation failed.
```

with 

```
Error in file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) : 
  cannot open the connection
Calls: source -> file
In addition: Warning message:
In file(filename, "r", encoding = encoding) :
  cannot open file 'renv/activate.R': No such file or directory
Execution halted
```

Inspecting the tarball that makes sense since there is no `renv` directory in `00_pkg_src/pkg` since it is listed in `.Rbuildignore`.
However, during R CMD check the `.Rprofile` kicks in and makes R search for that directory which does not exist and hence it fails.

If I change `.Rbuildignore` from

```
^renv$
```

```
^renv/library
^renv/settings
```

everything works since now `renv/activate.R` is within the tarball. Also I get no complains about unwanted files during the check.

However, when restarting the session, `^renv$` is automatically re-added to `.Rbuildignore` which breaks my approach. 

Would it be possible to avoid that behavior of readding `^renv$`? Or even easier, set my own logic for `.Rbuildignore`?

title: renv sometimes fails to restore project library
description:

title: Notes on renv + CI (specifically, travis) ... and bookdown
description:
Notes on my experience wiring renv into the STAT 545 reboot based in https://github.com/rstudio-education/stat545.

I think this could be used to expand the new [short vignette re: CI/CD](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/ci.html). I'm envisioning some some high-level guidance about what to cache (or not) and why, then examples of concrete config files / snippets for important providers. I am also only doing this for a bookdown site right now, so I didn't explore the variant for an R package. Another major point that needs coverage -- maybe it's own vignette? -- is the interaction between renv and `DESCRIPTION`.

---

Here's the current `.travis.yml`:

https://github.com/rstudio-education/stat545/blob/master/.travis.yml

Below I comment on certain features and will inline bits that exist / don't exist as of https://github.com/rstudio-education/stat545/commit/f1feb7f06a2bb2fb3c0379bbc72909e04e0b3f3f. Obviously the file can and probably will continue to evolve.

---

What to put in the CI's cache?

``` yaml
language: r
cache:
  directories:
  - _bookdown_files
  - $HOME/.npm
  - $HOME/.local/share/renv
  - $TRAVIS_BUILD_DIR/renv/library
```

Notice the **absence** of the usual `packages: true` here. If the renv-using project is structured properly / in the default way, the usual R package library will not be used. I decided it was best to not cache it, because this will make any use of it more visible and painful and will encourage scrutiny.

`$HOME/.local/share/renv` is [renv's global package cache](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/renv.html#cache). This is the default location for Linux.

`$TRAVIS_BUILD_DIR/renv/library` is the project-specific private library. @jimhester has suggested that I **not** cache this and I think I agree? I almost deleted this line, but it's still there because I want to discuss. If we don't cache this, then every build will rebuild the private library, from the global package cache, triggered by `renv::restore()`. This is fast (~30s for this project) because it's just recreating symlinks. However, I feel like the log will be more informative if we **do** cache the private library, because it makes _changes_ to the library more visible. If we are constantly rebuilding the whole thing, you can't see change. Thoughts?

`_bookdown_files` and `$HOME/.npm` relate to bookdown and Netlify's cli, respectively.

---

Where to install packages from?

I also wanted to get Linux binaries from RSPM. That's what `RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE` is about here:

```
env:
  global:
    - NETLIFY_SITE_ID=6b6a38b6-7523-4555-965a-fa5cdc9f7157
    # NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN set in travis settings
    - RENV_CONFIG_REPOS_OVERRIDE=https://demo.rstudiopm.com/all/__linux__/xenial/latest
```

This setting only appeared in renv v0.7.0-50 and that's a direct result of the stat545 experiment. The usual mechanisms of setting the CRAN repository don't work because renv generally consults the repository indicated in the lock file for this.

Using binaries makes a big difference: if we install from CRAN, it takes 35-40 mins to build & deploy. Using Linux binaries from RSPM brings this down to 13 mins for the first build and to ~6 mins for subsequent builds (that's the benefit of the travis-caching the renv global package cache).

---

Prepare the private library.

``` yams
before_install:
  - export COMMIT_MSG=$(echo "$TRAVIS_COMMIT_MESSAGE" | head -n1)
  - export DEPLOY_MSG="${TRAVIS_COMMIT:0:7} ${COMMIT_MSG:0:50}"
  - Rscript -e "renv::restore()"
```

The `renv::restore()` line is the one that makes sure the private project library is ready to go. We do this in `before_install`, so it precedes the step where the base r-travis script installs the dependencies discovered from `DESCRIPTION`. I think we expect the `install` step to always be a no-op here (right?). Because you shouldn't be discovering the need to install or upgrade anything based on `DESCRIPTION` that wasn't already embodied in the lock file.

The `export` commands are just preparing some decent messages for the Netlify log.

The fix could be to make `snapshot()` return the path to the lock file, or for `restore()` to support the snapshot object produced by `snapshot()`.

title: https protocol pre-pended twice during restore
description:

```r
> renv::restore()
The following package(s) will be installed:
       _                       
  renv   [0.7.0-17 -> 0.7.0-17]
```

description:
[5.txt](https://github.com/rstudio/renv/files/3529400/5.txt)
Hi @kevinushey,

Some further findings from the pipeline I've got set up. I seem to be having problems with a number of packages that have been migrated from the packrat cache to the renv cache. 

The migrate works fine in the it makes the correct lock file but then when it is trying to restore it seems to fail due to DLL's not found. From reading online this is usually due to a corrupt install and the suggestion is to delete and reinstall. title: Funcky project structure: a follow up
description:
This is a follow up to the discussion we were having [here](https://community.rstudio.com/t/packrat-bundles-with-different-r-versions-suggestions-and-alternatives/32988), but since the thread got closed I decided to continue here.

The basic issue I was having can be summed up as:

- How to make `renv` work in a situation where src, analysis and the renv itself exists in diverse locations?

Tested solution using tips from  @cderv and @kevinushey :

- Place the renv infrastructure in PRJ_SCRIPTS, for the  purposes of version control- this is where .git lives
- Initialize the project in PRJ_SCRIPTS without attempting dependency discovery and installation – that is, we manually install the packages your project requires – with `renv::init(bare = TRUE)`
- Find / install libraries manually with `renv::dependencies()` and renv::hydrate() function, which will also attempt to save time by copying packages from your user library (rather than re-installing from CRAN) as appropriate. Code used:

```R
pkg_src <- c("./", "../prj_data")
pkgs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pkg_src, renv::dependencies))$Package
renv::hydrate(pkgs)
```

- Restore project in the analysis folder with `renv::load(project = "../prj_scripts")`. In a final setting this line needs to be present in the `.Rprofile` inside the analysis folder.

While on the analysis folder I installed some packages to see:
1. where the source would end up
2. if they would be registered in the lockfile

the answer is that they are stored in the PRJ_SCRIPTS, as expected / desired, and registered in that folder's lockfile:
>  Lockfile written to '/projects/sandbox/prj_scripts/renv.lock'

In the end this looks less complicated that I initially though. Let me know if I am missing something or something else you would like me to test.

title: renv behind a corporate Proxy. Improve documentation?
description:
Like in https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/64 we have an awful man in the middle Proxy using Windows logins (SSPI) and the ntlm authentication protocol. A good  explanation is found in this [stackoverflow answer]( https://stackoverflow.com/a/1277196). To make matter worse, the bundled curl is removed from our windows image. 

`renv::install()` fails:

```
> renv::install("xtable")
Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/3.5/xtable_1.8-4.zip' ...
Warning message:
In (function (url, destfile, method, quiet = FALSE, mode = "w",  :
  URL 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/3.5/xtable_1.8-4.zip': status was 'HTTP response code said error'
```

I found a simple solution in the end, but it was cumbersome to find all the pieces of information:

•	Install curl with `renv::equip()`
•	Create following _curlrc in `Sys.getenv("HOME")` or `Sys.getenv("R_USER")`

```
--proxy "your.proxy.dns:port"
--proxy-ntlm
--proxy-user ":"
--insecure
```

The double quotes are important. `:` is interpreted as separator. See https://github.com/curl/curl/issues/3738#issuecomment-480379380

```
> renv::install("xtable")
Retrieving 'https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/contrib/3.5/xtable_1.8-4.zip' ...
	OK [downloaded 688.3 Kb in 1.9 secs]
Installing xtable [1.8-4] from CRAN ...
	OK (installed binary)
* Copying 'xtable' into the cache ... Done!
```

title: Suggestion: An alternate workflow for reproducible environments
description:
Hey, over the last few months my work team has been trying to use `renv` and competing packages to make our DS pipelines easily reproducible and deployable in the cloud. We haven't really been able to create a jank-free experience that I had hoped for which is essentially:

* Git clone the project
* Run a command to build the project environment (download dependencies)
* Run the project

## Issues with `renv` workflow

We have faced two major challenges:
1. Depending on internal packages stored in Azure dev ops repositories.
2. Trying to stop our 'dev dependencies' from polluting the project environment.

With respect to 1, some work was done on `renv` to support that and I think the problems we have now might be particular to our cyber-security setup here at work. 😢

With respect to 2, The issue comes because while we can specify certain packages in `ignored.packages`, their dependencies are not ignored and thus the environment is polluted. Example dev dependencies are `styler`, `lintr`, `rlanguageserver` and many other tools that people use on an individual basis to make their R dev experience more comfortable.

There's a related problem in that often in development of a pipeline, you *trial* the use of a package, before later deciding not to use it. Those can pollute the environment in certain `renv` workflows if people are not vigilant.

## Proposed alternative

What we have come to realise is that while we have a need to create these dependency environments, we do not actually need to run our code within them *reproducibly* **and** *interactively*.

This is partly because our workflow uses `drake` heavily to orchestrate our pipelines. So while we build our functions interactively, we run the pipeline in a non-interactive mode - actually in another R session - using `drake::r_make()`. This is kind of similar to running projects in RStudio's job mode.

So we almost never need to 'switch' our interactive-mode package library to be the project-local one. To use the project-local library,  we can just use a simple wrapper for `r_make` e.g. `r_make_with_library()` or some such. Jobs users could have something similar.

It would be great if we could leverage some of the tools in `renv` to define/build/restore the project-local library without attaching the machinery that assumes we always want to use it for interactive use - that being the `.Rprofile` and associated `renv` bootstrapping.

This approach conveniently sidesteps all possible issues related to challenge 2. Our interactive environment is our 'dev' environment and contain anything, while our project-local environment is our 'prod' and contains only the packages on which the pipeline depends.

## Possible drawbacks

This kind of workflow requires the user to remain aware of the fact that their dev environnent could potentially generate different results to the prod one. So they'll want to be running their pipeline frequently in prod mode with the local library. The great thing about working with `drake` is this is fairly painless, and you're guaranteed to catch an issue introduced by code that works in one but not the other pretty much immediately.

The user would also presumably need some kind of way to switch into a prod environment for debugging these kinds of issues - knowingly sacrificing some of their dev creature comforts while doing so.

They'll also probably want some functions to diff the versions of packages in dev and prod libraries so they can make informed decisions about upgrading.

## Summary

This is a proposal for `renv` to support an alternative reproducible environment workflow that does not assume all work takes place inside the project-local library. Removing this assumption allows users to freely use dev environments packed with dependencies that make interactive development convenient, whilst keeping a well defined prod environment they can run their project in.

title: package deps not installed when using remotes::install_github()
description:
This is loosely related to #77 with respect to the system's R library being a part of `.libPaths()` inside an `renv` project (maybe) but I've encountered this perplexing issue illustrated by this workflow:

* I want to install an updated version of a package (for example Shiny) in my renv project.
* An (earlier) version of the package already exists in the system R library.
* renv::snapshot()` shows that a few dependencies of Shiny are not installed.

Interestingly, this does not seem to happen when I am installing packages from CRAN.  This is becoming a bit of a problem because I have to then manually install the package dependencies one-by-one in the renv project to get rid of that message.  Hope this makes sense, but I have the workflow below:

### Initialize renv in project

```r
renv::init()
```

### Install remotes package

```r
install.packages("remotes")
```

### Install updated version of Shiny from GitHub

* Within the default R system library, shiny `1.3.2` is already installed

```r
remotes::install_github("rstudio/shiny")
```

```
> remotes::install_github("rstudio/shiny")
Downloading GitHub repo rstudio/shiny@master
These packages have more recent versions available.
Which would you like to update?

1: All                             
2: CRAN packages only              
3: None                            
4: mime   (0.6    -> 0.7   ) [CRAN]
5: digest (0.6.19 -> 0.6.20) [CRAN]
6: rlang  (0.3.4  -> 0.4.0 ) [CRAN]
```

Adam

title: implement mechanism for excluding certain packages from cache
description:
For example, someone might be working on a project with some packages which need to be compiled with special flags (e.g. for debugging, or special optimizations, and so on). However, we don't want these packages to enter the cache as one likely would not want the package to be used in other projects (or worse, to inadvertently be used in other projects when the 'default' build of the package is expected)

Fortunately, it's unlikely that the hashes of a locally compiled-from-source package would collide with that of a package retrieved from a remote source, because the `Remote*` fields are used when building the hash.

Unfortunately, there's no way for us to tell the difference between a package compiled from source with different sets of compilation flags -- the onus would be on the user to do something like change the Version in the DESCRIPTION, or similar.

I think the right solution is to ensure that we only cache packages which have a known source. If we cannot figure out where a particular package has come from, then we don't cache the package.

(note: in theory this does affect packages installed from remotes, since the user could change their R Makevars and so on between installations of packages from source)

title: renv::restore() fails when Bioconductor packages are included in lockfile
description:
## Overview

After generating a snapshot of a project which includes some bioconductor dependencies, an attempt to restore the project using the corresponding `renv.lockfile` results in an error along the following lines:

```r
* Project '~/renv-debug' loaded. [renv 0.4.0-21]
> renv::restore()
The following package(s) will be installed:
                _           
  AnnotationDbi   [1.44.0]  
  BH              [1.69.0-1]
  Biobase         [2.42.0]  
  BiocGenerics    [0.28.0]  
  BiocManager     [1.30.4]  
  BiocVersion     [3.8.0]   
  DBI             [1.0.0]   
  GO.db           [3.7.0]   
  IRanges         [2.16.0]  
  RSQLite         [2.1.1]   
  S4Vectors       [0.20.1]  
  bit             [1.1-14]  
  bit64           [0.9-7]   
  blob            [1.1.1]   
  pkgconfig       [2.0.2]   
  plogr           [0.2.0]   

Do you want to proceed? [y/N]: y
* Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
Error: failed to determine Bioconductor repositories
Traceback (most recent calls first):
  10: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
   9: stopf("failed to determine Bioconductor repositories")
   8: renv_bioconductor_repos()
   7: unique(c(renv_bioconductor_repos(), repos))
   6: options(repos = unique(c(renv_bioconductor_repos(), repos)))
   5: renv_retrieve_bioconductor(record)
   4: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
   3: renv_retrieve(packages)
   2: renv_restore_run_actions(project, diff, current, lockfile)
   1: renv::restore()
```

## To Reproduce

1. Create a conda environment with R 3.5.1:

```sh
conda env -n debug -c defaults r-base=3.5.1
conda activate debug
```

2. Install / initialize renv

From R:

```r
install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('rstudio/renv')
renv::init()
quit()
```

3. Install bioconductor package (e.g. "GO.db")

Re-launch R and run:

```r
renv::install('BiocManager')
BiocManager::install('GO.db')
renv::snapshot()
```

title: Add documentation on interacting with packages from Bioconductor
description:
From a quick look at the good, it appears that renv has some support for working with packages hosted on Bioconductor.

Attempting to initialize an environment containing such packages fails, however:

```
* Discovering package dependencies ... Done!
* Copying packages into the cache ... Done!
* Resolving missing dependencies  ... 
* Querying repositories for available source packages ... Done!
Retrieving 'http://lib.stat.cmu.edu/R/CRAN/src/contrib/foreach_1.4.4.tar.gz' ...
        OK [file is up to date]
Retrieving 'http://lib.stat.cmu.edu/R/CRAN/src/contrib/codetools_0.2-16.tar.gz' ...
        OK [file is up to date]
Retrieving 'http://lib.stat.cmu.edu/R/CRAN/src/contrib/iterators_1.0.10.tar.gz' ...
        OK [file is up to date]
Error: failed to retrieve package 'limma' (missing record)
Traceback (most recent calls first):
  9: stop(sprintf(fmt, ...), call. = call.)
  8: stopf(fmt, package)
  7: renv_retrieve_missing_record(package)
  6: records[[package]] %||% renv_retrieve_missing_record(package)
  5: renv_retrieve_impl(package)
  4: renv_retrieve(packages)
  3: renv_hydrate_resolve_missing(project, na)
  2: hydrate(project = project, library = library)
  1: renv::init()
```

Attempting to install the package via `renv::install()` results in a similar failure.

A work-around is to first install any needed packages manually using `BiocManager::install()`, and _then_ call `renv::init()`, at which point renv is able to detect the locally-installed packages and use them.

Is this something that should be supported? And if so, would it be possible to update the docs to indicate how? Otherwise, a note in the README.md on expected behavior / advice for working with Bioconductor, etc. packages might be helpful to include.

title: evaluate how renv and Conda environments can be used together
description:
Currently, renv scans the directory and picks up an libraries that appear to be used and attempts to install them.

In some cases, however, packages are installed from non-standard sources like Github, and therefor renv won't know what to do.

If it wouldn't add to much complexity, it might be useful to provide a mechanism through which users could explicitly list some additional sources to use.

This could take the form of some renv-specific comment insert in the files, e.g.

```r
# renv-src: https://github.com/stephenturner/annotables
# renv-src: https://github.com/slowkow/tftargets
```

Or, alternatively, something like conda's `environment.yml` could be use to manually specify the precise requirements for a project, including packages installed via GIthub, etc.

(On an unrelated note -- have you considered modifying `renv::hydrate()` so that it follows sourced files in a project? e.g. In some projects with a shared codebase, I do something like `source('../shared/libraries.R')`. Since it is outside of the main project directory, however, these files get missed by `hydrate`.)

title: should 'local' package tarballs always be used?
description:
Related to https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/43.

Suppose we have a package installed from CRAN, e.g.

```
[R/Package/Matrix]
Package=Matrix
Version=1.2-17
Source=CRAN
Hash=b10030fd8c964dbecd79719236d4a668
```

Now, suppose a local tarball for that package is available, at e.g.

```
<project>/renv/local/Matrix/Matrix_1.2-17.tar.gz
```

Should we consider installing from that tarball directly, skipping the attempt to download and install from CRAN? Should we consider doing this for all package sources? This would effectively allow 'local' sources to act as an override for packages which aren't otherwise retrievable (ie: it could be an escape hatch)

title: Docker builds and renv
description:
Hi there,

Installing packages via renv on a docker image is a bit finicky, the renv::restore() command takes a long time for larger projects (say > 100 libraries), if there is a failure at some point the entire RUN R -e "renv::restore()" command is nullified and has to be performed again. Is it possible to make renv more robust when restoring libraries on a Docker images? For example, could there be a way to (partially) cache the renv installations, as one would see when using the RUN R -e "install.packages('xxx')" lines repeatedly?

Best regards,

Michael

title: should `renv_download_curl()` inherit local config from _curlrc/.curlrc?
description:
At my work we have an awful man in the middle proxy which decrypts all traffic by substituting the certificates on all secure connections. We work around this by disabling certificate verification for git and other services. 

We can do the same for `curl` using the `insecure` option in the `curlrc` but since `renv` does not read this config and in fact provides its own, all attempted package installations fail due to certificate errors with curl.

edit relevant function is: renv_download_curl, https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/master/R/download.R#L87

title: Option to disable dependency search in `init()`
description:
I think the option to disable the scraping of dependencies in `packrat` is really useful and should make its way over to `renv::init()`.

For new projects, the point is moot. But when you have been working on something a little while, and are ready to make it transportable, I like the workflow of:

1. Init empty project-local library and restart R session
2. Manually install what I think my dependencies are into my project-local library
3. Run project and see what breaks
4. Fix broken things by either changing code or installing additional libraries
5. Snapshot

It's a nice opportunity to catch things that might have slipped through the net like stray usage of `::`. Nearly every time I've used the automated scraping I've picked up stuff by accident. I just now watched a colleague do the same thing playing around with `renv`, so I know it's not just me :).

To save the user some labor, you could have a function that returns a character vector of all the detected dependencies. They can then evaluate that and choose whether to install them all.

title: project package are not linked at first install in the cache
description:
For a new project, if a package is not already cached, it will be installed in the cache but not linked to the project library. It will be copied from temp library where it was installed.

This is because, when a package is not in cache `renv_install_package_local` is used. I understand that 
* Package is downloaded in cache (`binary` folder on windows)
* Package is installed in a temporary library  (`templib <- tempfile("renv-templib-")`) 
* Cache is synchronize with `renv_cache_synchronize`: Temp installation is copy into cache.
Not move and linked because `library == renv_paths_library()` is FALSE (one is temp lib the other is project lib)
* Then the package is moved from temp lib to project lib
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/4c29ee4a1b016812f64cf602ed1b425fae7061aa/R/install.R#L69-L73

At the end here, the package is not a linked folder to cache library but installed in the project.
I would have expected the package to be linked from the cache to the project library. 

Seems like what this does 
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/4c29ee4a1b016812f64cf602ed1b425fae7061aa/R/cache.R#L136-L138
but it is not activated in this case.

title: upgrade does not work with a version number
description:
The doc says 
> his implies that you can call (for example) renv::upgrade(remote = "0.1.0-75) to request the installation of that particular version of renv if so required.

But 
```r
> renv::upgrade(remote = "0.2.0-59")
Error in unclass(numeric_version(rhs))[[1]] : subscript out of bounds
Call `rlang::last_error()` to see a backtrace
```
This is because there is no version in records
https://github.com/rstudio/renv/blob/494ce53b8593a84eb2305ea7728008b097c8566b/R/upgrade.R#L30-L35
``` r
renv:::renv_remotes_parse("0.2.0-59")
#> $Package
#> [1] "0.2.0-59"
#> 
#> $Version
#> NULL
#> 
#> $Source
#> [1] "CRAN"
```

so `request` is NULL and `version_compare(current, request) == 0` throws the error

It is like Package and Version field are not correct. I would expect
```r
#> $Package
#> [1] "renv"
#> 
#> $Version
#> [1] "0.2.0-59"
#> 
#> $Source
#> [1] "Github"
```

Currently from the code, I don't think it is possible to install a specific renv version like documented. I understand that the call should be something like that `rstudio/renv@0.2.0-59` to be understand as a github remote
```r
 renv:::renv_remotes_parse("rstudio/renv@0.2.0-59")
```
But even like that it is not ok because 0.2.0-59 is a tag name and `renv_remotes_parse_github` only knows how to handle branch reference (`git/refs/heads/`)
* https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/renv/git/refs/heads/0.2.0-59 does not exist
* https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/renv/git/refs/tags/0.2.0-59 does exist

Github API makes a difference here between commit / branch and tag. You would need to test both or use another approach like download the tarball and read DESCRIPTION inside 
`https://api.github.com/repos/rstudio/renv/tarball/<any git ref>`

Currently, `renv::upgrade` only works to upgrade from master or branch but not from a version number.

title: Enhancement: Check installed and pack.lock package version at session start
description:
I was playing with renv a bit and I find it pleasant to use - specially I like that renv::install() automatically updates renv.lock, since one can easily forget to call snapshot.

One cool feature that could be added would be a check of installed package versions and versions in renv.lock when R session is started. So if versions for some package are different, then user would be asked to run renv::restore() (or there could be [y/N] prompt to call restore).

**Use case:**
For example there are multiple people working on the same project and then someone updates/downgrades some library and pushes changes to git. Then other guys might pull changes but they would not notice package changes and project would break for them. With this check everyone would know right away that some package version was changed and that they should update their local packages.

title: think about Python + reticulate integration
description:
What information about the selected version of Python do we need to capture? Some options:

- The path to the Python executable,
- The version of the Python interpreter used,
- The name, or path, to a virtual environment / Conda environment.

Where do we want to capture this? Within the project options? Or as part of the lockfile? Or both?

The primary benefit of capturing these things in the lockfile is that an `renv::restore()` using just a project lockfile could then attempt to find the path to an appropriate Python executable, and then use that (+ a `requirements.txt`) to restore the Python packages in e.g. a virtual environment.

However, capturing paths may not be useful since there's no guarantee that `/usr/local/bin/python` on one system and `/usr/local/bin/python` on another system are the same.

We could enforce (or at least encourage) the use of virtual environments by name, since it would be easier to orchestrate -- e.g. "virtual environment 'tensorflow-1.13' uses Python x.y.z and these tensorflow packages", and that concept would be uniform across different machines.

The 'reproducible' solution would involve enforcing the use of virtual environments, and capturing Python by version. Then we could (in theory) attempt to find or download that particular version of Python, create a virtual environment using that Python, and then restore any packages recorded in `requirements.txt`.

Ultimately, I think we want to make sure it's easy for users to collaborate on the same repository, which does imply being able to easily reproduce the environment on different machines.

We should also have some provisioning for automatically selecting a project-local virtual environment called `r-reticulate`.

Some API proposals:

```r
# init could take a 'python' parameter
renv::init(python = "/usr/bin/python")

# renv could activate a version of Python post-hoc
renv::settings$python("/usr/bin/python")
```

title: Allow shared build cache package installation to avoid duplication
description:
In multi-tenant servers (i.e. RStudio pro products), it might be beneficial to have "build awareness" in relation to #3 (when using a shared cache).

I.e. 5 users request to build the same package version at the same time. It would be nice to see if it's possible for `renv` to have hooks or some type of awareness into that build pipeline so that redundancy can be reduced. 

Honestly, part of this may be just awareness / extensibility and potential dependence on an arbitrary package installation client (which might provide this build awareness). I just wanted to document the idea in case it affects the development process at all.

For instance - on Connect (packrat), if 5 users attempt to install the same package at the same time, they will all build from source concurrently. Each one, as it completes, will update the cache with its completed version. This (1) is redundant and (2) burns up the CPU. Binary packages could resolve much of the issue, but in any case where binaries are not available, some additional client awareness would be useful.

title: Possible to "create" renvs at a path other than home directory?
description:
I feel like I am seeing some type of weirdness with renvs that are tried with a path.
``` r
library(reprex)
renv::init()
#> * Virtual environment 'reprex548277d89f6' activated -- please restart the R session.
renv::activate()
#> * Virtual environment 'reprex548277d89f6' activated -- please restart the R session.
text <- "blahblah2"
renv::create(paste0("/", text))
system("ls ~/.renv/environment", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "blah" "tmp"

system("ls ./", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "renv"                   "reprex_reprex.R"       
#> [3] "reprex_reprex.spin.R"   "reprex_reprex.spin.Rmd"

renv::deactivate()
#> * Virtual environment deactivated -- please restart the R session.
renv::create(paste0("/tmp/", text))
system("ls ~/.renv/environment", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "blah" "tmp"
system("ls ~/.renv/environment/tmp/", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "blah"
renv::create(paste0("./", text))
#> Error: Local virtual environment './blahblah2' already exists.
system("ls ~/.renv/environment", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "blah" "tmp"

system("ls ./", intern = TRUE)
#> [1] "renv"                   "reprex_reprex.R"       
#> [3] "reprex_reprex.spin.R"   "reprex_reprex.spin.Rmd"
```

<sup>Created on 2019-01-03 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.2.1)</sup>

I think this relates to my [preferences in `virtualenv`](https://github.com/rstudio/reticulate/issues/393) :smile: 

Not sure if `renv::init()` is the only way you can get a `renv` within a project, and whether any project would ever be justified in having more than one `renv` locally.

The other use case to wonder about here is whether you could put `renv`s or the cache at a shared location. This is something that I know [some users were interested in](https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/pull/357) for packrat.
